ಪದದ ಪ್ರಯೋಗವಿದೆ. ಪ್ರಕೃತವಾದ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಅದೇ ಅರ್ಥವು ಸಹಜವಾದರೂ ಸಹ ಅಗ್ನಿಯ ಸಮೀಪ
en: When the oblations called Devasū are offered, this Ṛk अनमीवास इळया (*anamīvāsa iḷayā*) is to be recited as the puronuvākyā mantra addressed to Mitra; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अनमीवास इळया मदंतः प्र स मित्र मर्तो अस्तु प्रयस्वान् (*anamīvāsa iḷayā madaṃtaḥ pra sa mitra marto astu prayasvān*) (Ā. 4-11).

In this mantra the favour of Āditya, in the form of Mitra, is prayed for. Neither wealth of food nor wealth of cattle is sought. Even where life is prosperous and contented, the prayer is for good understanding, that one may be a doer of good acts and follow the good path. The epithets अनमीवासः (*anamīvāsaḥ*) and इळॆया मदंतः (*iḷèyā madaṃtaḥ*) also show the good state of the worshipper.

On the nature of Iḷā. The word इळया (*iḷayā*) is here explained as "food". The particular deity denoted by the word इळा (*iḷā*) was described earlier, when the deities of the Āprī hymns were treated [Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, part 11, p. 264]. But the other meanings suggested by this word were not explained there. The uses of this word, which in many contexts give room for doubt, must be examined for what meanings they indicate in which contexts.

The Nirukta author lists the word इळा (*iḷā*) among the names of the earth (Ni. 1-1), among the names of speech (1-11), and among the names of food (2-7). Here it is explained as food. Food may be either earthly wealth of food, or else a particular divine power that is the original cause of this food.

In places such as येषामिळा धृतहस्ता दुरोण आ अपि प्राता निषीदति । (*yeṣāmiḷā dhṛtahastā duroṇa ā api prātā niṣīdati |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-16-8), the goddess in the form of food, characterised as the oblation, अन्नरूपा हविर्लक्षणा देवी निषीदति । (*annarūpā havirlakṣaṇā devī niṣīdati |*): since the goddess in the form of food is described as sitting with butter in her hands, a particular power is indicated. There is room for the doubt whether the goddess Iḷā praised in the Āprī hymns is different from this Iḷā in the form of food; but if all the Śruti passages are examined closely, identity is what appears.
यज्ञे चेद्वै मावकल्पयिष्यसि बहुः प्रजया पशुभिर्भविष्यसि । (*yajñe cedvai māvakalpayiṣyasi bahuḥ prajayā paśubhirbhaviṣyasi |*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-19)⟨NOTE:202⟩

This assurance — "if you perform the sacrifice with my help, the sacrificer will be endowed with wealth of food, of cattle and of offspring" — was spoken by the goddess Iḷā. Who is this Iḷā? What is her connection with the sacrifice? These matters are explained in detail in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. Although, in reality, the Iḷā described in many passages of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā and the Iḷā described in the Śatapatha are the same, particular usages give room for doubt. In some contexts the word इळॆ (*iḷè*) is used in the masculine; and in places such as इति त्वा देवा इम आहुरैळॆ .... .... (*iti tvā devā ima āhuraiḷè .... ....*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-95-18), Aila (Purūravas) raises the doubt whether he is a son of Iḷā (fem. इळॆ (*iḷè*)) or of Iḷa; so there is room for such doubt as well. If the Śruti passages are closely examined, there is no room for such doubts. To know in what context the above-quoted sentence यज्ञे चेद्वै मावकल्पयिष्यसि (*yajñe cedvai māvakalpayiṣyasi*) was spoken and what its real meaning is, the story of the Śatapatha must be known. In this narrative the origin, power and nature of Iḷā are fully understood. Thereafter one can understand that the Iḷā praised in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā has this same nature. Moreover, one can examine the appropriateness of the use of इळा (*iḷā*) in the present mantra concerning Mitra.
The origin of Iḷā and her earthly nature.

मनवे ह वै प्रातः .... .... .... .... तदप्येतदुत्तरस्य गिरेर्मनोरवसर्पणमित्यौघो ह ताः सर्वाः प्रजा निरुवाहाधेह मनुरेवैकः परिशिशिषे । (*manave ha vai prātaḥ .... .... .... .... tadapyetaduttarasya girermanoravasarpaṇamityaugho ha tāḥ sarvāḥ prajā niruvāhādheha manurevaikaḥ pariśiśiṣe |*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-1 to 6)

Manu reared a fish in the water brought for washing, and with the help of that fish crossed the great flood, and sat practising austerity at the place famed as Manu's mountain. When the flood had swept away all other creatures and he alone sat there in that tranquil setting practising austerity, the wish for offspring arose in him.

सोऽर्चञ्चाम्यंश्चकार प्रजाकामः । तत्रापि पाकयज्ञेनेजे स धृतं दधि मस्त्वामिक्षामित्यप्सु जुहवांचकार ततः संवत्सरे योषित्संबभूव सा ह पिब्बमानेवोदेयाय तस्यै ह स्म धृतं पदे संतिष्ठते तया मित्रावरुणौ संजग्माते ॥ (*so 'rcañcāmyaṃścakāra prajākāmaḥ | tatrāpi pākayajñeneje sa dhṛtaṃ dadhi mastvāmikṣāmityapsu juhavāṃcakāra tataḥ saṃvatsare yoṣitsaṃbabhūva sā ha pibbamānevodeyāya tasyai ha sma dhṛtaṃ pade saṃtiṣṭhate tayā mitrāvaruṇau saṃjagmāte ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-7)

Desiring offspring, Manu stayed silent, practising austerity and engaged in worship of the gods. At this time he performed a pāka-yajña and, in the rite belonging to it, offered butter, curds, whey ("Whey" printed) and āmikṣā ("Curds" printed) into the water. Within a year a woman came into being. When she arose, firm of limb (पिब्बमान (*pibbamāna*) = "firm", with limbs), she appeared with butter on her feet.
(The epithet धृतहस्ता (*dhṛtahastā*), 7-16-8, in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā was mentioned above.) At that time Mitra and Varuṇa met her.

ताग्ंहोचतुः कासीति । मनोर्दुहितेत्यावयोर्ब्रूष्टेति नेति होवाच य एव मामजीजनत तस्यॆवाहमस्मीति तस्यामपित्वमीषाते तद्वा जज्ञा तद्वा न जज्ञावतित्त्वेवेयाय सा मनुमाजगाम ॥ (*tāgṃhocatuḥ kāsīti | manorduhitetyāvayorbrūṣṭeti neti hovāca ya eva māmajījanata tasyèvāhamasmīti tasyāmapitvamīṣāte tadvā jajñā tadvā na jajñāvatittveveyāya sā manumājagāma ‖*)

When they asked who she was, she said, "I am Manu's daughter." When they pressed, "Say that you are ours," she said, "Certainly not; I belong to him who begot me; I am his daughter." They wished to have a share in her. Then she signified neither consent nor refusal, but went to her father Manu and joined him.

ताग्ं ह मनुरुवाच कासीति । तव दुहितेति कथं भगवति मम दुहितेति या अमूरस्त्वाहुतीरहौषीर्घृतं दधि मस्तामिक्षां ततो मामजीजनथाः साशीरस्मि तां मा यज्ञेवकल्पय यज्ञे चेद्वै मावकल्पयिष्यसि बहुः प्रजया पशुभिर्भविष्यसि याममुया कां चाशिषमाशासिष्यसे सा ते सर्वा समर्थिष्यत इति तामेशन्मध्ये यज्ञस्यावाकल्पयनमध्यग्ग् हैतद्यक्षस्य यदंतरा प्रयाजानुयाजान् ॥ (*tāgṃ ha manuruvāca kāsīti | tava duhiteti kathaṃ bhagavati mama duhiteti yā amūrastvāhutīrahauṣīrghṛtaṃ dadhi mastāmikṣāṃ tato māmajījanathāḥ sāśīrasmi tāṃ mā yajñevakalpaya yajñe cedvai māvakalpayiṣyasi bahuḥ prajayā paśubhirbhaviṣyasi yāmamuyā kāṃ cāśiṣamāśāsiṣyase sā te sarvā samarthiṣyata iti tāmeśanmadhye yajñasyāvākalpayanamadhyagg haitadyakṣasya yadaṃtarā prayājānuyājān ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-9)

Then Manu too asked who she was. "Your daughter," she said. "O revered one, how are you my daughter?" he said. She replied: "By the oblations of butter, curds, whey and āmikṣā that you offered in the water, in the rite belonging to the pāka-yajña, I was produced; I am a blessing (āśīḥ) for all your undertakings. In sacrificial acts, if you seek my help and perform your rites together with me, you will be possessed of cattle, sons and all wealth. Whatever desires you have, you will obtain them all." On this assurance Manu obtained her help during the sacrificial acts performed in the middle, between the Prayājas and the Anuyājas.

तयर्चञ्चाम्यंश्चचार प्रजाकामः । तयेमां प्रजातिं प्रजज्ञे येयं मनोः प्रजातियाम्वेनया कां चाशिषमाशास्त्र सास्मै सर्वा समार्थ्यत॥ (*tayarcañcāmyaṃścacāra prajākāmaḥ | tayemāṃ prajātiṃ prajajñe yeyaṃ manoḥ prajātiyāmvenayā kāṃ cāśiṣamāśāstra sāsmai sarvā samārthyata‖*)

With her help, worshipping and practising austerity, desiring a son, he remained absorbed in meditation. Through her he created this human progeny. Whatever gracious blessings of hers were to be obtained, he obtained them all and fulfilled his desires.

सैषा निदानेन यदिडा । स यो ह्येवं विद्वानिडया चरत्येताग्ं हैव प्रजातिं प्रजायते यां मनुः प्राजायत याम्वेनया कां चाशिषमाशास्त्रे सास्मै सर्वा समृध्यते ॥ (*saiṣā nidānena yadiḍā | sa yo hyevaṃ vidvāniḍayā caratyetāgṃ haiva prajātiṃ prajāyate yāṃ manuḥ prājāyata yāmvenayā kāṃ cāśiṣamāśāstre sāsmai sarvā samṛdhyate ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-11)

This excellent woman is Iḍā in every respect. Whoever, knowing this truth, performs the rite together with Iḍā, increases this human progeny; through her he obtains all blessings and fulfils all his desires. (In इडया चरति (*iḍayā carati*) there are two meanings: one, "with the woman in the form of Iḍā"; the other, "with the pāka-yajña having the nature of Iḍā".)
Up to here the origin and nature of Iḍā as history have been explained; now the nature of Iḍā in the form of the sacrifice is explained. Iḍā is praised as the animal, Iḍā as food, Iḍā as everything.

सा वै पंचावत्ता भवति । पशवो वा इडा पांक्ता वै पशवः तस्मात्पंचावत्ता भवति । स समवदायेडां । पूर्वार्धं पुरोडाशस्य प्रशीर्य पुरस्ताद्भुवायै निदधाति ताग्ं होत्रे प्रदाय दक्षिणात्येति ॥ (*sā vai paṃcāvattā bhavati | paśavo vā iḍā pāṃktā vai paśavaḥ tasmātpaṃcāvattā bhavati | sa samavadāyeḍāṃ | pūrvārdhaṃ puroḍāśasya praśīrya purastādbhuvāyai nidadhāti tāgṃ hotre pradāya dakṣiṇātyeti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-12, 13)

Iḍā is of the nature of the animal. The animal has five chief parts; therefore Iḍā too is to be divided into five parts. (By sentences such as यो वै यज्ञं हविष्पंक्तिं वेद हविष्पंकिना यज्ञेन राध्नोति (*yo vai yajñaṃ haviṣpaṃktiṃ veda haviṣpaṃkinā yajñena rādhnoti*) etc., the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa explains these five kinds also, in four or five ways: Ai. Brā. 8-24.) The Adhvaryu divides Iḍā into five portions and places the forward part of the puroḍāśa on the barhis. Then he hands Iḍā to the Hotṛ. The division into five is made by these three acts: upastaraṇa, abhighāraṇa and sviṣṭakṛt.
Having thus stated the procedure belonging to the sacrificial process, the other-worldly power-nature of Iḍā is told next.

अथोपाग्ंशूपह्वयेते । एतद्ध वै मनुर्विभयां चकारेदं वै मे कनिष्ठं यज्ञस्य यदियमिडा पाकयज्जिया यद्वै म इह रक्षाग्‌सि याज्ञं न (*athopāgṃśūpahvayete | etaddha vai manurvibhayāṃ cakāredaṃ vai me kaniṣṭhaṃ yajñasya yadiyamiḍā pākayajjiyā yadvai ma iha rakṣāgsi yājñaṃ na*)

हन्युरिति तामेतत्पुरा रक्षोभ्यः पुरा रक्षोभ्य इत्येवोपागंशूपाह्वयत तथो एवैनमेष एतत्पुरा .... .... पह्वयते ॥ (*hanyuriti tāmetatpurā rakṣobhyaḥ purā rakṣobhya ityevopāgaṃśūpāhvayata tatho evainameṣa etatpurā .... .... pahvayate ‖*)

On this occasion the Hotṛ calls Iḍā in a soft voice. Even so, Manu [thought]: "This act, which is a limb of the sacrifice, is not so firm. Therefore, before the fear of the demons draws near, Iḍā must be protected." Declaring just this wish, he calls her.

स उपह्वयते । उपहूतग्ं रथंतरग्ं सह पृथिव्योपमां वामदेव्यग्ं सहांतरिक्षेण ह्वयतामुपहूतं वामदेव्यग्ं सहांतरिक्षेण ह्वयतामुपहूतं बृहत्सह दिवोप मां बृहत्सह दिवा ह्वयतामिति तदेतामेनै तदुपह्वयमान इमांश्च लोकानुपह्वयत एतानि च सामानि ॥ (*sa upahvayate | upahūtagṃ rathaṃtaragṃ saha pṛthivyopamāṃ vāmadevyagṃ sahāṃtarikṣeṇa hvayatāmupahūtaṃ vāmadevyagṃ sahāṃtarikṣeṇa hvayatāmupahūtaṃ bṛhatsaha divopa māṃ bṛhatsaha divā hvayatāmiti tadetāmenai tadupahvayamāna imāṃśca lokānupahvayata etāni ca sāmāni ‖*)

Next he recites the mantras that praise Iḍā. If Iḍā is praised with these mantras, the three worlds beginning with the earth are praised and called for protection. How? By calling the earth together with the Rathantara sāman, the atmosphere together with the Vāmadevya, and the heaven-world together with the Bṛhat, he has called for protection Iḍā herself, who pervades the three worlds. In this way the invocation of the goddess Iḍā, in the form of praise, indicates her special powers.

उपहूता गावः सहर्षभा इति । पशवो वा इडा .... .... उपहूतेडा ततुरिरिति तदेनां प्रत्यक्षमुपह्वयते ततुरिरिति सर्वग् हैषा पाप्मानं तरति तस्मा दाह ततुरिरिति ॥ (*upahūtā gāvaḥ saharṣabhā iti | paśavo vā iḍā .... .... upahūteḍā tatuririti tadenāṃ pratyakṣamupahvayate tatuririti sarvag haiṣā pāpmānaṃ tarati tasmā dāha tatuririti ‖*)

The goddess Iḍā herself is of the nature of cattle. She is therefore called with the prayer that she appear together with the bull, and, since Iḍā herself brings about the quieting of all sin, that she come to the sacrifice in a form that gives victory.

उपहूतः सखा भक्ष इति । प्राणा वै सखा भक्षस्तप्राणमुपह्वयतउपहूतग्ं हेगिति तच्छरीरमुपह्वयते । (*upahūtaḥ sakhā bhakṣa iti | prāṇā vai sakhā bhakṣastaprāṇamupahvayataupahūtagṃ hegiti taccharīramupahvayate |*) (Śa. Brā. 1.8-1-2)

Iḍā is the dearest friend. Iḍā is the food that is the vital breath. Friend and food are forms of the vital breath and nothing else. The invocation, in the form of a prayer, is made to Iḍā, who is of the nature of the vital breath.

मानवी धृतपदीति । मनुर्ह्येतामग्रेऽजनयत तस्मादाह मानवीति धृतपदीति यदेवास्यै धृतं पदे समतिष्ठत तस्मादाह धृतपदीति ॥ (*mānavī dhṛtapadīti | manurhyetāmagre 'janayata tasmādāha mānavīti dhṛtapadīti yadevāsyai dhṛtaṃ pade samatiṣṭhata tasmādāha dhṛtapadīti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-26)

Thus the goddess Iḍā, described above as of the nature of a cow, bestower of victory, of the nature of food and of the vital breath, is famed as the daughter of Manu. Because ghee clung to her foot, the name Dhṛtapadī also became famous for her.

उत मैत्रावरुणीति । यदेव मित्रावरुणाभ्याग्ं समगच्छत स एव मैत्रावरुणो न्यंगो ब्रह्मा देवकृतोपहूतेति ब्रह्मा ह्येषां देवकृतोपहूता दैव्या अध्वरव उपहूता मनुष्या इति तद्दैवांश्चैवाध्वरूनुपह्वयते ये च मानुषा वत्सा वै दैव्याअध्वरवोऽथ य इतरे ते मानुषाः॥ (*uta maitrāvaruṇīti | yadeva mitrāvaruṇābhyāgṃ samagacchata sa eva maitrāvaruṇo nyaṃgo brahmā devakṛtopahūteti brahmā hyeṣāṃ devakṛtopahūtā daivyā adhvarava upahūtā manuṣyā iti taddaivāṃścaivādhvarūnupahvayate ye ca mānuṣā vatsā vai daivyāadhvaravo 'tha ya itare te mānuṣāḥ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-27)

Iḍā, so described, has shown her relation also to Mitra and Varuṇa. Since, as soon as she was born of Manu, she appeared to Mitra and Varuṇa, she may also be called of the nature of Maitrāvaruṇa. Because she is made by the gods, she is also called Brahma. She is also the Adhvaru connected with the gods. The Adhvarus connected with the gods are like calves to Iḍā, who is of the nature of a cow. All, gods and men alike, obtain food only through Iḍā's favour. That Iḍā is the giver of food and herself of the nature of food. This Iḍā, famed as Maitrāvaruṇī and of the nature of food, is the one indicated in the Ṛk at hand. The meaning is that this food is itself of the nature of Brahma.
The milk of the cow that is Iḍā.

स होवाच । इडैव मे मानव्यग्निहोत्री वायुव्यो वत्सः सजूरुपसृष्टा विराट् संयोजनमाश्विनं दुह्यमानं वैश्वदेवं दुग्धं वायव्यमाह्रियमाणमाग्नेयमधिश्रितमैंद्राग्नमवज्योत्यमानं वारुणमद्भिः प्रत्यानीतं वायव्यमुद्वास्यमानं द्यावापृथिव्यमुद्वासितमाश्विनमुन्नीयमानं वैश्वदेवमुन्नीतं महादेवायोद्यतं वायव्यग्ं ह्रियमाणं वैष्णवं निगृहीतः ॥ (*sa hovāca | iḍaiva me mānavyagnihotrī vāyuvyo vatsaḥ sajūrupasṛṣṭā virāṭ saṃyojanamāśvinaṃ duhyamānaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ dugdhaṃ vāyavyamāhriyamāṇamāgneyamadhiśritamaiṃdrāgnamavajyotyamānaṃ vāruṇamadbhiḥ pratyānītaṃ vāyavyamudvāsyamānaṃ dyāvāpṛthivyamudvāsitamāśvinamunnīyamānaṃ vaiśvadevamunnītaṃ mahādevāyodyataṃ vāyavyagṃ hriyamāṇaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ nigṛhītaḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 11-5-3-5)

"Iḍā, daughter of Manu, is my cow of the Agnihotra. The principle of Vāyu is the calf. The relation of the two is Virāj." [Here Sāyaṇa explains: वायुना संश्रितः द्यौः (*vāyunā saṃśritaḥ dyauḥ*), the connection of Vāyu with the atmosphere.] "When the calf joins this cow, after the drinking of the milk, at the time of milking it belongs to the Aśvins; after the milk has been drawn, to the Viśvedevas; when it is brought from the cow-pen, to Vāyu; when it is placed on the fire, to Agni; when it shines, to Indra and Agni; when it is brought out,

to Heaven and Earth; at the time of removal, to the Aśvins; when it is raised up, to Mahādeva; when it is made ready for the Āhavanīya, to Viṣṇu." So Uddālaka explained. In such a context one should understand Iḍā to be a special power that propounds a very hidden principle.

The nature of this cow that is Iḍā, the greatness of this milk that is to be offered at the times of the Pāka-yajña and the like, and the wealth of food, in the form of Iḍā, that comes to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice with her help, are described in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā as follows.

पाकयज्ञं वा अन्वाहिताग्नेः पशव उप तिष्ठंत इडा खलु वै पाकयज्ञस्यॆषांतरा प्रयाजानूयाजान् यजमानस्य लोकेवहिता तामाह्रियमाणामभि मंत्रयेत सुरूपवर्षवर्ण एहीति पशवो वा इडा पशूनेवोपश्वयते यज्ञं वै देवा अदुह्रन् यज्योऽसुराग्ं अदुहत्तेऽसुरा यज्ञदुग्धाः पराभवन् (*pākayajñaṃ vā anvāhitāgneḥ paśava upa tiṣṭhaṃta iḍā khalu vai pākayajñasyèṣāṃtarā prayājānūyājān yajamānasya lokevahitā tāmāhriyamāṇāmabhi maṃtrayeta surūpavarṣavarṇa ehīti paśavo vā iḍā paśūnevopaśvayate yajñaṃ vai devā aduhran yajyo 'surāgṃ aduhatte 'surā yajñadugdhāḥ parābhavan*) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 1-7-1-1) ⟨NOTE:203⟩

Wealth of cattle comes to one who has established the fire for the Pāka-yajña. Iḍā herself is this Pāka-yajña. She is placed between the Prayājas and the Anuyājas. Then one should pray, "O goddess of fair form and of the colour of the rain, be gracious." Since Iḍā is cattle, by this invocation cattle themselves are called. The gods called the sacrifice; the sacrifice called the Asuras. Therefore the Asuras suffered defeat.

यो वै यज्ञस्य दोहं विद्वान् यजतेऽप्यन्यं यजमानं दुहे सा मे सत्याशीरस्य यज्ञस्य भूयादित्याहैष वै यज्ञस्य दोहस्तेनैवैनं दुहे प्रत्ता वै गौर्दुहे प्रत्तेडा यजमानाय दुह एते वा इडाय्कॆ स्तना इडोपहूतेति वायुर्वत्सो यर्हि होतेडामुपह्वयेत तर्हि यजमानो होतारमीक्षमाणो वायुं मनसा ध्यायेत् । (*yo vai yajñasya dohaṃ vidvān yajate 'pyanyaṃ yajamānaṃ duhe sā me satyāśīrasya yajñasya bhūyādityāhaiṣa vai yajñasya dohastenaivainaṃ duhe prattā vai gaurduhe pratteḍā yajamānāya duha ete vā iḍāykè stanā iḍopahūteti vāyurvatso yarhi hoteḍāmupahvayeta tarhi yajamāno hotāramīkṣamāṇo vāyuṃ manasā dhyāyet |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-7-1-2)

Whoever knows this principle and the way of calling the sacrifice, the sacrifice in the form of Iḍā calls another sacrificer to help him. The sacrificer's reciting, "May the blessing of this sacrifice be fulfilled for me," is itself the milking of the sacrifice. The cow gives her consent to this milking. Since this same prayer is addressed to Iḍā, it is the cow in the form of Iḍā that has been called. [The response इडोपहूता (*iḍopahūtā*) shows the order followed by the gods, and उपहूतेडा (*upahūteḍā*) that of the Asuras. This is a point to be noted in the sacrificial procedure.] Before the worship that calls this cow,
the calf must be joined to the cow. When the sacrificer prays addressing Iḍā, he should look at the Hotṛ's face and meditate on Vāyu.

मात्रे वत्समुपाव सृजति सर्वेण वै यज्ञेन देवास्सुवर्गं लोकमायन्हाकयज्ञेन मनुरश्रामृत्सेडा मनुमुपावर्तत तां देवासुरा व्यह्वयंत प्रतीचीं देवाः पराचीमसुरास्सा देवानुपावर्तत पशवो वै तद्देवानवृणत पशवोऽसुरानजहुर्यं कामयेतापशुस्स्यादिति पराचीं तस्यॆडामुप द्वयेतापशुरेव भवति ॥ (*mātre vatsamupāva sṛjati sarveṇa vai yajñena devāssuvargaṃ lokamāyanhākayajñena manuraśrāmṛtseḍā manumupāvartata tāṃ devāsurā vyahvayaṃta pratīcīṃ devāḥ parācīmasurāssā devānupāvartata paśavo vai taddevānavṛṇata paśavo 'surānajahuryaṃ kāmayetāpaśussyāditi parācīṃ tasyèḍāmupa dvayetāpaśureva bhavati ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-7-1-3)

While meditating on Vāyu he lets the calf go to the cow. It was by the help of this complete sacrifice that the gods obtained heaven. Manu too toiled for this sacrifice. Iḍā went to Manu. When gods and Asuras came to resort to this same Iḍā, the gods called her face to face and the Asuras with face turned away. Iḍā went to the gods and joined them. Therefore the gods obtained wealth of cattle; the Asuras did not obtain it. If a sacrificer wishes that someone remain without cattle, and one calls Iḍā on that man's behalf standing with face turned away, then that sacrificer becomes without cattle.

यं कामयेत पशुमान्त्स्यादिति प्रतीचीं तस्येडामुपह्वयेत पशुमानेव भवति ब्रह्मवादिनो वदंति स त्वा इडामुप ह्वयेत य इडामुपहूयात्मानमिडायामुपह्वयेतॆति सा नः प्रिया सुप्रतूर्तिर्मघोनीत्याहेडामेवोपहूयात्मानमिडायमुपह्वयते व्यस्तमिव वा एतद्यज्ञस्य यदिडा सामि प्राश्नंति ॥ (*yaṃ kāmayeta paśumāntsyāditi pratīcīṃ tasyeḍāmupahvayeta paśumāneva bhavati brahmavādino vadaṃti sa tvā iḍāmupa hvayeta ya iḍāmupahūyātmānamiḍāyāmupahvayetèti sā naḥ priyā supratūrtirmaghonītyāheḍāmevopahūyātmānamiḍāyamupahvayate vyastamiva vā etadyajñasya yadiḍā sāmi prāśnaṃti ‖*) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 1-7-1-4) ⟨NOTE:204⟩

If the sacrificer is to obtain wealth of cattle, one must stand face to face and call Iḍā with prayer on his behalf. At once that sacrificer obtains wealth of cattle. When calling Iḍā with prayer, the praiser sees unity between himself and Iḍā; the knowers of the principle say that he has made his own nature one with Iḍā. He prays: "May Iḍā be for my share the doer of what is dear, the giver of victory, and the giver of abundant wealth." Iḍā is, as it were, somewhat broken in the middle of the sacrifice. By saying that in it the meaning is enjoyed, and so on, her protective nature and her power to break the Asuras and others are described. And Iḍā's capacity to protect the world is explained still more fully.

सग्ग श्रवा ह सौवर्चनसस्तु मिंजमौपोदितिमुवाच यत्सत्रिणाग्ंहोता भूः कामिडामुपाह्वथा इति तामुपाह्व इति होवाचॆ या प्राणेन देवान्हा- धार व्यानेन मनुष्यानपानेन पितृनिति छिनत्ती सा न छिनत्ती ३ इति छिनत्तीति होवाच शरीरं वा अस्यै तदुपाह्वथा इति होवाच गौर्वै अस्यै शरीरं। (*sagga śravā ha sauvarcanasastu miṃjamaupoditimuvāca yatsatriṇāgṃhotā bhūḥ kāmiḍāmupāhvathā iti tāmupāhva iti hovācè yā prāṇena devānhā- dhāra vyānena manuṣyānapānena pitṛniti chinattī sā na chinattī 3 iti chinattīti hovāca śarīraṃ vā asyai tadupāhvathā iti hovāca gaurvai asyai śarīraṃ|*) (Śai. Saṃ. 1-7-2-1) ⟨NOTE:205⟩

Saṃśravas, son of Suvarcanas, asked Tumiñja Aupoditi: "When were you Hotṛ to those who perform a sattra sacrifice? In which form of Iḍā did you pray, praising her?" Aupoditi answered: "I prayed to that Iḍā who sustains the gods with the prāṇa breath, men with the vyāna breath, and the fathers with the apāna breath." To the question whether she is one who divides or one who does not divide, he answered that she is one who divides. "Then did you praise her body?" he asked. The body of that Iḍā is the cow.

गां वाव तौ तत्परवदतां या यज्ञे दीयते सा प्राणेन देवान्दाधार यया मनुष्या जीवंति सा व्यानेन मनुष्यान् यां पितृभ्यो घ्निंति सापानेन पित्र्यन् य एवं वेद पशुमान्भवत्यथ वै तामुपाह्व इति होवाच या प्रजाः प्रभवंतीः प्रत्याभवतीति ॥ (*gāṃ vāva tau tatparavadatāṃ yā yajñe dīyate sā prāṇena devāndādhāra yayā manuṣyā jīvaṃti sā vyānena manuṣyān yāṃ pitṛbhyo ghniṃti sāpānena pitryan ya evaṃ veda paśumānbhavatyatha vai tāmupāhva iti hovāca yā prajāḥ prabhavaṃtīḥ pratyābhavatīti ‖*) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 1-7-2-2) ⟨NOTE:206⟩

The two of them, eager to know the meaning of the principle, were discussing that cow in the form of Iḍā. This Iḍā, offered for the sake of the sacrifice, sustains the gods in the form of prāṇa. She by whose support men live, those men she sustains with vyāna and is the cause of their growth; the fathers, for whose sake they slay her, she sustains with apāna. He who knows all these principles is possessed of wealth of cattle. Aupoditi answered: "I have prayed to that Iḍā who is the cause of the increase of creatures."

अन्नं वा अस्यैतदुपाह्वथा इति होवाचौषधयो वा अन्या अन्नमौपधयो वै प्रजाः प्रभवंतीः प्रत्या भवंति य एवं वेदान्नादो भवत्यथ वै तामुपाह्व इति होवाच या प्रजाः पराभवंतीरनुगृह्णांति प्रता,भवंतीर्गृह्णांतीति प्रतिष्ठां वा अस्यै तदुपाह्वथा इति होवाच ॥ (*annaṃ vā asyaitadupāhvathā iti hovācauṣadhayo vā anyā annamaupadhayo vai prajāḥ prabhavaṃtīḥ pratyā bhavaṃti ya evaṃ vedānnādo bhavatyatha vai tāmupāhva iti hovāca yā prajāḥ parābhavaṃtīranugṛhṇāṃti pratā,bhavaṃtīrgṛhṇāṃtīti pratiṣṭhāṃ vā asyai tadupāhvathā iti hovāca ‖*) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 1-7 2 3) ⟨NOTE:207⟩

Then it amounts to praying for Iḍā's food. This food is itself in the form of herbs. If creatures prosper, they obtain these herbs that are of the nature of food. When Saṃśravas said that one who knows this principle eats food, Aupoditi said again: "I have prayed to Iḍā, who lifts up those fallen into misfortune and shows favour to them when they prosper." He replied that then he has obtained her complete support.

इयं ना अस्यॆ प्रतिष्ठेयं वै प्रजाः पराभवंतीरनु गृह्णाति प्रत्याभवंतीर्गृह्णातिय एवं वेद प्रत्येक तिष्ठत्यथ वै तामुपाह्व इति होवाच यस्यॆ निक्रमणे धृतं प्रजास्संजीवंतीः पिबंति त्रि छिनत्ति सा न छिनत्ती ३ इति न छिनत्तीति होवाच प्र तु जनयतीत्येष वा इडामुपाह्वथा इति होवाच वृष्टिर्वा इडा वृष्टैः वै निक्रमणे धृतं प्रजास्संजीवंतीः पिबंति य एवं वेद प्रैव जायतेऽन्नादो भवति॥ (*iyaṃ nā asyè pratiṣṭheyaṃ vai prajāḥ parābhavaṃtīranu gṛhṇāti pratyābhavaṃtīrgṛhṇātiya evaṃ veda pratyeka tiṣṭhatyatha vai tāmupāhva iti hovāca yasyè nikramaṇe dhṛtaṃ prajāssaṃjīvaṃtīḥ pibaṃti tri chinatti sā na chinattī 3 iti na chinattīti hovāca pra tu janayatītyeṣa vā iḍāmupāhvathā iti hovāca vṛṣṭirvā iḍā vṛṣṭaiḥ vai nikramaṇe dhṛtaṃ prajāssaṃjīvaṃtīḥ pibaṃti ya evaṃ veda praiva jāyate 'nnādo bhavati‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-7-2-4)

This earth, the support of all and of the nature of Iḍā, is the one who lifts up those fallen into misfortune and favours those who are to grow. He who knows this principle obtains a complete and firm support for his existence and growth. When again he was asked whether this Iḍā is one who divides or one who does not, whether she is a divider or not, he said: she does not divide, but becomes the cause of increase. This Iḍā of great power is the rain. Relying on this rain, creatures drink ghee, the support of their life. For this satisfaction Iḍā, Dhṛtapadī, is the cause. The praiser who relies on her obtains all wealth and wealth of progeny: so is the greatness of Iḍā described. In the explanations above she is praised as a goddess pervading the universe; as the giver of support to gods, men and all; as the earth, support of all; as the giver of satisfaction to all worlds in the form of food; as the friend in distress; as having power to punish the wicked and protect the good; and as the very form of rain, the support of the life of the world. Ghee, the support of the world's life, is what is to be obtained through her favour. The Iḷā whom the Ṛk Saṃhitā praises as धृतहस्ता (*dhṛtahastā*) is praised in the Śatapatha and other texts as धृतपदी (*dhṛtapadī*). In the Ṛk at hand, which praises Mitra, Iḷā in the form of food is indicated, and the relation between Mitra and Iḷā is told. That she is of the nature of Maitrāvaruṇa has been stated above and its meaning explained. Since in the Ṛk at hand the word इळा (*iḷā*) is taken to mean food, only one aspect of Iḷā's nature is set forth.

अनमीवासः (*anamīvāsaḥ*)—the word अमीव (*amīva*) is formed from the word अम (*ama*), which gives the sense of disease (अम रोगे (*ama roge*)). अनमीवासः (*anamīvāsaḥ*) shows its negation: it means "free from disease". The word अमीव (*amīva*) is also used in the sense of "enemy". अमीवहन् (*amīvahan*) is an epithet of Indra and others, meaning "destroyer of enemies".
उपक्षियंतः (*upakṣiyaṃtaḥ*)—when the preverb उप (*upa*) joins the root क्षि (*kṣi*), the meaning is "dwell nearby". The word is used in this sense on many occasions. For example,

Likewise in यस्य ते अग्ने अन्ये अग्नय उपक्षितो वया इव । (*yasya te agne anye agnaya upakṣito vayā iva |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-19-33), the word उपक्षितः (*upakṣitaḥ*) is used to convey that the other fires also dwell near the chief Agni. In the present Ṛk too that meaning is natural; yet the purport is that one stays near Agni and carries out the sacrificial rite.

kn: ಅಯಂ ಮಿತ್ರೋ ನಮಸ್ಯಃ ಸುಶೇವೋ ರಾಜಾ ಸುಕ್ಷೇತ್ರೋ ಅಜನಿಷ್ಟ
ತಸ್ಯ ವಯಂ ಸುಮತೌ ಯಜ್ಞಿಯಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಭದ್ರೇ ಸೌಮನಸೇ ಸ್ಯಾಮ ॥೪॥
ref: अ॒यं मि॒त्रो न॑म॒स्य॑ः सु॒शेवो॒ राजा॑ सुक्ष॒त्रो अ॑जनिष्ट वे॒धाः।
तस्य॑ व॒यं सु॑म॒तौ य॒ज्ञिय॒स्यापि॑ भ॒द्रे सौ॑मन॒से स्या॑म

kn: ಅಯಂ । ಮಿತ್ರಃ । ನಮಸ್ಯಃ । ಸುಶೇವಃ ರಾಜಾ । ಸುಕ್ಷತ್ರಃ । ಅಜನಿಷ್ಟ । ವೇಧಾಃ ।
ತಸ್ಯ । ವಯಂ । ಸುಮತೌ । ಯಜ್ಞಿಯಸ್ಯ । ಅಪಿ । ಭದ್ರೇ । ಸೌಮನಸೇ । ಸ್ಯಾಮ ॥ ೪ ॥

ಅಯಂ ಪೂರ್ವಮಂತ್ರೇ ಪ್ರತಿಪಾದಿತೋ ಮಿತ್ರಃ ಸೂರ್ಯೋ ನಮಸ್ಯಃ ಸರ್ವರ್ನಮಸ್ಕರಣೀಯಃ ಸುಶೇವಃ ಶೋಭನಸುಖಃ । ಸುಖೇನ ಸೇವ್ಯ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ । ರಾಜಾ ಸರ್ವಸ್ಯ ಜಗತಃ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಪ್ರದಾನೇನ ಸ್ವಾಮೀ ಸುಕ್ಷತ್ರಃ । ಕ್ಷತ್ರಶಬ್ದೇನ ಬಲಮುಚ್ಯತೇ । ಶೋಭನಬಲೋಪೇತೋ ವೇಧಾಃ
ಸರ್ವಸ್ಯ ಜಗತೋ ವಿಧಾತಾ । ಏವಂಗುಣೋಪೇತಃ ಸೂರ್ಯೋಽಜನಿಷ್ಟ । ಪ್ರಾದುರಭೂತ್ । ತಸ್ಯೈವಂವಿಧಗುಣೋಪೇತಸ್ಯ ಯಜ್ಞಿಯಸ್ಯ ಯಜ್ಞಾರ್ಹಸ್ಯ ಸೂರಸ್ಯ ಸುಮತೌ ಶೋಭನಾಯಾಂ ಬುದ್ಧ್ಯಾಂ
ಭದ್ರೇ ಕಲ್ಯಾಣಕಾರಿಣಿ ಸೌಮನಸೇ ಸೌಮನಸ್ಯೆಪಿ ಯಜಮಾನಾ ವಯಂ ಸ್ಯಾಮ । ಭವೇಮ ॥
ನಮಸ್ಯಃ ನಮಸಿ ಸಾಧುಃ । ತತ್ರ ಸಾಧುರಿತಿ ಯತ್ । ತಿತ್ಸ್ವರಿತಃ । ಅಜನಿಷ್ಟ । ಜನೀ ಪ್ರಾದುರ್ಭಾವ
ಇತ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಲುಜಿ ಸಿಚಿ ರೂಪಂ । ಸೌಮನಸೇ । ಸುಮನಸ ಇದಮಿತ್ಯರ್ಥೇ ತಸ್ಯೇದಮಿತ್ಯಣ್ । ಪ್ರತ್ಯಯಸ್ವರಃ ॥

en: This Mitra, the Sun set forth in the previous mantra, is नमस्यः (*namasyaḥ*), to be bowed to by all; सुशेवः (*suśevaḥ*), one of good happiness, that is, easily served; राजा (*rājā*), lord of the whole world through giving light; सुक्षत्रः (*sukṣatraḥ*), for the word क्षत्र (*kṣatra*) denotes strength, so one endowed with good strength; वेधाः (*vedhāḥ*), the ordainer of the whole world. The Sun, endowed with such qualities, has been born, that is, has appeared. May we, the sacrificers, be in the good intention (सुमतौ (*sumatau*)) and the auspicious, welfare-bringing benevolence (सौमनसे (*saumanase*)) of that Sun, who is so endowed and worthy of sacrifice. ⟨NOTE:208⟩
notes: ಸುಕ್ಷೇತ್ರೋ in Saṃhitā, ಸುಕ್ಷತ್ರಃ in Pada and bhāṣya; Pratipadārtha has ಸುಕ್ಷೇತ್ರಃ

kn: ಅಯಂ ಮಿತ್ರಃ—ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ತುತನಾಗಿರುವ ಮಿತ್ರನು । ನಮಸ್ಯಃ—ಪೂಜ್ಯನಾಗಿಯೂ । ಸುಶೇವಃ—
ವಾದುದೂ । ಭದ್ರೇ—ಕಲ್ಯಾಣಾತ್ಮಕವಾದುದೂ ಆದ । ಸೌಮನಸೇ—ಹಿತಕರವಾದುದೂ ಆದ ಬುದ್ಧಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ।
en: - अयं मित्रः (*ayaṃ mitraḥ*)—this Mitra who is praised here
- सुमतौ (*sumatau*)—in the mind that is gracious

kn: ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ತುತನಾಗಿರುವ ಮಿತ್ರನು ಪೂಜ್ಯನಾಗಿಯೂ, ಸುಖದಿಂದ ಸೇವಿಸಲ್ಪಡುವವನಾಗಿಯೂ, ಸಕಲಜಗ
ತ್ತಿಗೂ ಒಡೆಯನಾಗಿಯೂ ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠವಾದ ಬಲವುಳ್ಳವನಾಗಿಯೂ ಜಗತ್ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಕರ್ತನಾಗಿಯೂ ಉತ್ಪನ್ನನಾಗಿದ್ದಾನೆ.
ಇಂತಹ ಪೂಜಾರ್ಹನಾದ ಸೂರ‍್ಯನ ಅನುಗ್ರಹಾತ್ಮಕವಾದುದೂ ಕಲ್ಯಾಣಾತ್ಮಕವಾದುದೂ ಆದ ಬುದ್ಧಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಯಜ
en: Here the Mitra who is praised has been born worshipful, served with ease, lord of the whole world, possessed of excellent strength and creator of the world. May we sacrificers be in the gracious and auspicious mind of this worshipful Sun.

kn: This Mitra has been engendered adorable and to be served, the sovereign (over all), endowed with vigour, the creator (of the universe); may we ever be in the good favour, in the auspicious approbation, of this adorable (Aditya).
en: This Mitra has been engendered adorable and to be served, the sovereign (over all), endowed with vigour, the creator (of the universe); may we ever be in the good favour, in the auspicious approbation, of this adorable (Aditya).

kn: ಮಿತ್ರಪರವಾದ ಈ ಮಂತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ರಾಜಾ, ಸುಕ್ಷೇತ್ರಃ ಎಂಬ ಎರಡು ವಿಶೇಷಣಗಳೂ ಮಿತ್ರನ ಗುಣಗಳನ್ನು
ತಿಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ದಿವ್ಯಶಕ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ, ಕ್ಷತ್ರ ಎಂದು ಎರಡು ವಿಧವಾಗಿ ವರ್ಣಿಸಿರುವಾಗ ಶ್ರುತಿವಾಕ್ಯಗಳಲ್ಲಿ
ಮಿತ್ರನನ್ನು ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಶಕ್ತಿದ್ಯೋತಕವಾದ ದೇವನೆಂದೂ, ವರುಣನನ್ನು ಕ್ಷತ್ರಶಕ್ತಿದ್ಯೋತಕವಾದ ದೇವನೆಂದೂ
ಕ್ರತುದಕ್ಷೌ ಹ ವಾಅಸ್ಯ ಮಿತ್ರಾವರುಣ್ .... .... ಸ ದಕ್ಷೋ ಮಿತ್ರ ಏವ ಕ್ರತುರ್ವರುಣೋ
ದಕ್ಷೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮೈವ ಮಿತ್ರಃ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಂ ವರುಣೋಽಭಿಗಂತೈವ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಕರ್ತಾ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಿಯಃ ॥
ಮಿತ್ರನು ಇಚ್ಛಾ (ಸಂಕಲ್ಪ) ಶಕ್ತಿಸ್ವರೂಪನು; ವರುಣನು ಕ್ರಿಯಾಶಕ್ತಿರೂಪನು. ಮಿತ್ರನು ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಸ್ವರೂಪನು,
ವರುಣನು ಕ್ಷತ್ರಸ್ವರೂಪನು ; ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವು ಸಂಕಲ್ಪಾತ್ಮಕವಾದ ಇಚ್ಛೆಯನ್ನೂ, ಕ್ಷತ್ರವು ಆ ಸಂಕಲ್ಪವನ್ನು ಕಾರ್ಯ
ರೂಪಕ್ಕೆ ತರುವ ಶಕ್ತಿಯನ್ನೂ ಹೊಂದಿರುವುದೆಯೆಂದು ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಕ್ಷತ್ರಗಳ ಸಂಬಂಧವನ್ನೂ, ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವನ್ನೂ ತಿಳಿಸಿದೆ.
ಹೀಗಿರುವಾಗ ಪ್ರಕೃತವಾದ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಸುಕ್ಷತ್ರಃ ಎಂಬ ವಿಶೇಷಣವು ಮಿತ್ರಪರವಾಗಿ ಹೇಗೆ ಹೊಂದಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ
ಎಂಬ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗೂ ಅವಕಾಶವಿದೆ. ಆದರೆ ಸಾಯಣರು ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಶಬ್ದಕ್ಕೆ ಬಲವೆಂಬ ಅರ್ಥವೆಂದೂ ರಾಜಾ ಎಂಬ
ವಿಶೇಷಣಕ್ಕೆ ಸ್ವಯಂಪ್ರಕಾಶನೂ, ಜಗತ್ಪಕಾಶಕನೂ ಆದ ಜ್ಯೋತೀರೂಪನೆಂದೂ ತಾತ್ಪರವನ್ನು ಹೇಳಿದ್ದಾರೆ.
ಆದರೆ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಶಬ್ದಕ್ಕೆ ಕೇವಲ ಭೌತಿಕಶಕ್ತಿಯೆಂದರ್ಥವಲ್ಲ. ಇತರ ವಿಶೇಷಣಗಳೊಡನೆ ಇದನ್ನೂ ಸೇರಿ
ಸಿರುವುದರಿಂದ ಮಿತ್ರನ ಅಸಾಧಾರಣವಾದ ಗುಣಗಳನ್ನು ತಿಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಮಿತ್ರನೆಂದರೆ ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಮಿತ್ರಾತ್ಮಕನಾದ
ದೈವಂ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಂ ಯಾಚೇದಿತ್ಯಾಹುರಾದಿತ್ಯೋ ವೈ ದೈವಂ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಮಾದಿತ್ಯ ಏಷಾಂ
ಜಗಚ್ಛಕ್ಷುವಾದ ಈ ಆದಿತ್ಯನೇ ಕ್ಷತ್ರದ ಸತ್ವವು. ಈ ಮಹಿಮೆಯನ್ನು ಉಪಾಸನಮಾಡುವುದರಿಂದ ಯಜ್ಞಕರ್ತನು
ಕ್ಷತ್ರರೂಪದ ಆದಿತ್ಯಶಕ್ತಿಯ ರಕ್ಷಣೆಯಿಂದ ತಾನೂ ಪ್ರಭುತ್ವವನ್ನು ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತಾನೆ ಎಂದು ಆದಿತ್ಯನ ಸ್ವರೂಪ
ವನ್ನು ಸ್ತುತಿಸಿದೆ. ಈ ಕ್ಷತ್ರದ ಶಕ್ತಿಯು ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವನ್ನೂ ರಕ್ಷಿಸುವ ಶಕ್ತಿಯಿದೆ.
ಕ್ಷತ್ರಂ ತದಪಿ ವಿಜೇಯಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಯತ್ಪಾತಿ ಶಾಶ್ವತಂ ।
ಶಾಶ್ವತವಾದ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವನ್ನು ರಕ್ಷಿಸುವ ಶಕ್ತಿಯು ಯಾವುದಕ್ಕಿದೆಯೋ ಅದೇ ಕ್ಷತ್ರವೆಂದು ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧವಾಗಿದೆ. ಈ
ಆದುದರಿಂದಲೇ ರಾಜಸೂಯಾದಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣನೂ ಸಹ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಿಯನಿಗಿಂತ ಕೆಳಗಿನ ಸ್ಥಾನದಲ್ಲಿಯೇ ಕುಳಿತುಕೊಳ್ಳು
ತಚ್ಛೈಯೋರೂಪಮತ್ಯಸೃಜತ ಧರ್ಮಂ ತದೇತತ್ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಸ್ಯ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಂ ಯದ್ಧರ್ಮಸ್ತಸ್ಮಾದ್ಧರ್ಮಾತ್ಪರಂ ।
ಈ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಶಕ್ತಿಯೇ ವಿಶ್ವನಿಯಮನರೂಪವು. ವಿಶ್ವಧರ್ಮವೇ ಇದಾದುದರಿಂದ ಇದರ ರಕ್ಷಣೆಯನ್ನು ಪಡೆದವನು
ದುರ್ಬಲನಾದರೂ ಸಹ ಪ್ರಬಲನೊಂದಿಗೆ ಸಾಮ್ಯರಕ್ಷಣೆಯನ್ನು ಹೊಂದಬಹುದು. ಈ ಕ್ಷತ್ರವೇ ಸತ್ಯಸ್ವರೂಪವು.
ಯಾವುದು ಕ್ಷತ್ರವೋ ಅದೇ ಧರ್ಮವು. ಯಾವುದು ಧರ್ಮವೋ ಅದೇ ಕ್ಷತ್ರವು. ಆದುದರಿಂದ ಲೋಕದ
ಶ್ರೇಯಸ್ಸಿಗೆ ಕಾರಣವಾದ ಈ ಕ್ಷತ್ರವು ಆದಿತ್ಯನ ವಿಶ್ವನಿಯಮನದ ಶಕ್ತಿಯನ್ನೂ, ಶ್ರೇಯಸ್ಸನ್ನುಂಟುಮಾಡತಕ್ಕ
ದ್ದೆಂದೂ, ನೀತಿಪಾಲಕವೆಂದೂ ವರ್ಣಿತವಾಗಿದೆ. ನೈತಿಕವ್ಯವಹಾರದಲ್ಲಿ ಅತ್ಯಾದರವಿರುವುದರಿಂದಲೇ ಪ್ರಕೃತವಾದ
ಮಂತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ—ಭದ್ರೇ ಸೌಮನಸೇ ಸ್ಯಾಮ ಎಂದು ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠವಾದ ವ್ಯವಹಾರಕ್ಕೆ ಬೇಕಾದ ಶುದ್ಧ ಬುದ್ದಿಯನ್ನು
ಅಪೇಕ್ಷಿಸಿ ಪ್ರಾರ್ಥಿಸಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಿದೆ. ಆದುದರಿಂದ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಪದವು ಮಿತ್ರಶಬ್ದಕ್ಕೆ ವಿಶೇಷಣವಾಗಿರುವಾಗಲೆಲ್ಲಾ ಈ ತಾತ್ಪರ್ಯ
ಮಿತ್ರಃ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಂ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಪತಿಃ । ಕ್ಷತ್ರಮಸ್ಮಿನ್ಯಜ್ಞೇ ಮಯಿ ದಧಾತು ।
ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ವಾಕ್ಯಗಳಲ್ಲೆಲ್ಲಾ ಮಿತ್ರನನ್ನು ಕ್ಷತ್ರಪತಿಯೆಂದು ಕರೆದಿರುವುದೂ ಸಹ ಈ ಅರ್ಥದಲ್ಲೇ. ಜಗತ್ಪ್ರಕಾಶಕ
ನಾದುದರಿಂದ ರಾಜಾ ಎಂಬ ವಿಶೇಷಣವೂ ಇರುತ್ತದೆ. ಈ ವಿಶೇಷಣವು ಮಿತ್ರರೂಪನಾದ ಆದಿತ್ಯನ ಜಗತ್ಪ್ರಭುತ್ವ
ಅಸಾವಾದಿತ್ಯ ಏಕವಿಗ್ಂಶಸ್ತದ್ದೈವಂ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಗ್ಂ ಸಾ ಶ್ರೀಸ್ತದಾಧಿಪತ್ಯಂ ತದ್ಬ್ರಧ್ನಸ್ಯ
ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಿಸುವ ಈ ದಿವ್ಯಪ್ರಭುವೇ ಕ್ಷತ್ರರೂಪದ ಶಕ್ತಿಯು. ಲೋಕಪ್ರಕಾಶಕವೂ, ಲೋಕಕ್ಕೆ ಶ್ರೇಯಃ
ಕಾರಕವೂ ಆದ ಈ ಪ್ರಭಾರೂಪವಾದ ಆದಿತ್ಯನ ಉಪಾಸನವನ್ನು ಮಾಡುವುದರಿಂದ ಪ್ರಭಾಯುತವಾದ ಸ್ವರಾಜ್ಯವು
ಲಭಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿಯಾಗಿ ವರ್ಣಿತವಾಗಿರುವ ಆದಿತ್ಯನ ಸ್ವರೂಪವು ಪ್ರಕೃತವಾದ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ವರ್ಣಿತವಾಗಿ
ಅವನ ಅನುಗ್ರಹದಿಂದ ಲಭಿಸತಕ್ಕ ಸೌಮನಸ್ಯವನ್ನೂ ಕಲ್ಯಾಣಕಾರಕವಾದ ಸದ್ಬುದ್ಧಿಯನ್ನೂ ಪ್ರಾರ್ಥಿಸಿದೆ.
en: In this mantra addressed to Mitra, the two epithets राजा (*rājā*) and सुक्षेत्रः (*sukṣetraḥ*) show Mitra's qualities. When divine power is described as of two kinds, Brahma and Kṣatra, the Śruti passages praise Mitra as the deity signifying the Brahma-power and Varuṇa as the deity signifying the Kṣatra-power.

क्रतुदक्षौ ह वाअस्य मित्रावरुण् .... .... स दक्षो मित्र एव क्रतुर्वरुणो दक्षो ब्रह्मैव मित्रः क्षत्रं वरुणोऽभिगंतैव ब्रह्म कर्ता क्षत्रियः ॥ (*kratudakṣau ha vāasya mitrāvaruṇ .... .... sa dakṣo mitra eva kraturvaruṇo dakṣo brahmaiva mitraḥ kṣatraṃ varuṇo 'bhigaṃtaiva brahma kartā kṣatriyaḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 4-1-4-1)

Mitra is of the nature of the power of will (resolve); Varuṇa is of the nature of the power of action. Mitra is of the nature of Brahma, Varuṇa of Kṣatra; Brahma holds the will in the form of resolve, and Kṣatra the power that brings that resolve into the form of action: thus the relation and the difference between Brahma and Kṣatra are shown. This being so, the question arises how the epithet सुक्षत्रः (*sukṣatraḥ*) in the present Ṛk fits Mitra. But Sāyaṇa has said that here the word क्षत्र (*kṣatra*) means strength, and that the epithet राजा (*rājā*) means the self-luminous one who illumines the world, of the form of light.

But the word क्षत्र (*kṣatra*) does not mean merely physical power. Since it is joined here with the other epithets, it shows Mitra's extraordinary qualities. Mitra here means Āditya, who is of the nature of Mitra.
दैवं क्षत्रं याचेदित्याहुरादित्यो वै दैवं क्षत्रमादित्य एषां भूतनामधिपतिः ॥ (*daivaṃ kṣatraṃ yācedityāhurādityo vai daivaṃ kṣatramāditya eṣāṃ bhūtanāmadhipatiḥ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 7-20)

This Āditya, the eye of the world, is the very essence of Kṣatra. By meditating on this greatness the sacrificer, through the protection of the Kṣatra-form power of Āditya, himself attains lordship: thus the nature of Āditya is praised. This power of Kṣatra has also the power to protect Brahma.
क्षत्रं तदपि विजेयं ब्रह्म यत्पाति शाश्वतं (*kṣatraṃ tadapi vijeyaṃ brahma yatpāti śāśvataṃ*) (Bṛ. De. 5-126)
That which has the power to protect the eternal Brahma is renowned as Kṣatra. By this great power all other powers must be protected.
तस्माक्षत्रात्परं नास्ति तस्माद्ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियमधस्तात् उपास्ते । (*tasmākṣatrātparaṃ nāsti tasmādbrāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyamadhastāt upāste |*) (Bṛ. U. 1-4-11)
That is why, in the Rājasūya and the like, even the Brāhmaṇa sits at a lower place than the Kṣatriya. This is divine power.
तच्छैयोरूपमत्यसृजत धर्मं तदेतत् क्षत्रस्य क्षत्रं यद्धर्मस्तस्माद्धर्मात्परं । (*tacchaiyorūpamatyasṛjata dharmaṃ tadetat kṣatrasya kṣatraṃ yaddharmastasmāddharmātparaṃ |*) (Bṛ. U. 1-4-24)

This Kṣatra-power is itself the regulation of the universe. Since it is the very law (dharma) of the universe, one who has obtained its protection, though weak, may obtain protection equal to that of the strong. This Kṣatra is of the nature of truth. What is Kṣatra is Dharma; what is Dharma is Kṣatra. Therefore this Kṣatra, the cause of the welfare of the world, is described as Āditya's power of regulating the universe, as productive of welfare, and as the upholder of right conduct. It is because of the great regard for moral conduct that in the present mantra, with भद्रे सौमनसे स्याम (*bhadre saumanase syāma*), the pure mind needed for excellent conduct is desired and prayed for. Therefore, whenever the word क्षत्र (*kṣatra*) stands as an epithet of the word मित्र (*mitra*), this purport is to be stated.
मित्रः क्षत्रं क्षत्रपतिः । क्षत्रमस्मिन्यज्ञे मयि दधातु । (*mitraḥ kṣatraṃ kṣatrapatiḥ | kṣatramasminyajñe mayi dadhātu |*) (Śa. Brā. 11-4-3-10)

In all such sentences too, Mitra is called lord of Kṣatra in this sense. Because he illumines the world, the epithet राजा (*rājā*) also occurs. This epithet shows the world-lordship of Āditya, who is of the form of Mitra.

असावादित्य एकविग्ंशस्तद्दैवं क्षत्रग्ं सा श्रीस्तदाधिपत्यं तद्ब्रध्नस्य विष्टपं तत्स्वाराज्यमश्नुते ॥ (*asāvāditya ekavigṃśastaddaivaṃ kṣatragṃ sā śrīstadādhipatyaṃ tadbradhnasya viṣṭapaṃ tatsvārājyamaśnute ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 13-1-7-3)

This divine lord shining in the atmosphere is the power in the form of Kṣatra. By worshipping this Āditya, of the form of radiance, who illumines the world and brings welfare to it, a radiant sovereignty of one's own is obtained. This nature of Āditya, thus described, is described also in the present Ṛk, and the benevolence and the auspicious good mind to be gained through his grace are prayed for.

kn: ತಸ್ಮಾ ಏತತ್ಪನ್ಯತಮಾಯ ಜುಷ್ಟಮಗ್ನೌ ಮಿತ್ರಾಯ ಹವಿರಾ ಜುಹೋತ ॥
ref: म॒हाँ आ॑दि॒त्यो नम॑सोप॒सद्यो॑ यात॒यज्ज॑नो गृण॒ते सु॒शेव॑ः।
तस्मा॑ ए॒तत्पन्य॑तमाय॒ जुष्ट॑म॒ग्नौ मि॒त्राय॑ ह॒विरा जु॑होत

kn: ಮಹಾನ್ । ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ । ನಮಸಾ । ಉಪಸದ್ಯಃ । ಯಾತಯತ್ಜನಃ । ಗೃಣತೇ । ಸುಶೇವಃ ।
ತಸ್ಮೈ । ಏತತ್ । ಪನ್ಯತಮಾಯ । ಜುಷ್ಟಂ । ಅಗ್ನೌ । ಮಿತ್ರಾಯ । ಹವಿಃ । ಆ । ಜುಹೋತ ॥ ೫ ॥
ಯೋಽಯಮಾದಿತ್ಯೋ ಮಹಾನ್ ಅತ ಏವ ನಮಸಾ ನಮಸ್ಕಾರೇಣೋಪಸದ್ಯಃ ಸರ್ವೈರುಪಸದನೀಯೋ ಯಾತಯಜ್ಜನಃ । ಪ್ರಾತಃ ಪ್ರಾತಃ ಸ್ವಸ್ವಕರ್ಮಣಿ ಪ್ರವರ್ತನೀಯಾ ಜನಾ ಯೇನೇತಿ ಸ
ತಥೋಕ್ತಃ । ಗೃಣತೇ ಸ್ತೋತ್ರಂ ಕುರ್ವತೇ ಜನಾಯ ಸುಶೇವಶ್ಚ ಭವತಿ ತಸ್ಮೈ ಪನ್ಯತಮಾಯ ಸ್ತುತ್ಯತಮಾಯ ಮಿತ್ರಾಯಾದಿತ್ಯಾಯ ಜುಷ್ಟಂ ಪ್ರೀತಿವಿಷಯಮೇತದ್ಧವಿರಗ್ನಾವಾ ಜುಹೋತ । ಜುಹುತ ॥
ಯಾತಯಜ್ಜನಃ । ಯತೀ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನ ಇತ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಣ್ಯಂತಸ್ಯ ಶತರಿ ರೂಪಂ । ಬಹುವ್ರೀಹೌ ಪೂರ್ವಪದ-
ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಸ್ವರೇ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೇ ಮರುದ್ವೃದ್ಧಾದಿತ್ವಾತ್ಪೂರ್ವಪದಾಂತೋದಾತ್ತತ್ವಂ । ಗೃಣತೇ । ಗ್ಯ ಶಬ್ದೇ ।
ಶತುರನುಮ ಇತಿ ವಿಭಕ್ತೇರುದಾತ್ತತ್ವಂ । ಪನ್ಯತಮಾಯ । ಪನತೇರಘ್ನ್ಯಾದಿತ್ವಾದ್ಯತ್ । ಯತೋಽನಾವ ಇತ್ಯಾದ್ಯುದಾತ್ತತ್ವಂ । ಜುಷ್ಟಂ । ನಿತ್ಯಂ ಮಂತ್ರ ಇತ್ಯಾದ್ಯುದಾತ್ತತ್ವಂ ॥

en: This Āditya is great, and therefore नमसा उपसद्यः (*namasā upasadyaḥ*), to be approached by all with homage. He is यातयज्जनः (*yātayajjanaḥ*): he by whom people are set, morning after morning, to their respective works. He is सुशेवः (*suśevaḥ*), a giver of happiness, to the man who praises him. To that most praiseworthy (पन्यतमाय (*panyatamāya*), स्तुत्यतमाय (*stutyatamāya*)) Mitra, the Āditya, offer (आ जुहोत (*ā juhota*), that is जुहुत (*juhuta*)) this oblation, the object of his delight (जुष्टं (*juṣṭaṃ*)), in the fire. The block then begins the grammatical remarks on यातयज्जनः (*yātayajjanaḥ*).
The block consists only of grammatical remarks (formation and accent of यातयज्जनः (*yātayajjanaḥ*), गृणते (*gṛṇate*), पन्यतमाय (*panyatamāya*), जुष्टं (*juṣṭaṃ*)); it adds nothing to the sense.

kn: ನಾಗಿಯೂ ಇದ್ದಾನೆ । ಪನ್ಯತಮಾಯ—ಸ್ತುತ್ಯತಮನೂ । ಮಿತ್ರಾಯೆ—ಮಿತ್ರರೂಪನೂ ಆದ । ತಸ್ಯೈ—
ಆ ಆದಿತ್ಯನನ್ನುದ್ದೇಶಿಸಿ । ಜುಷ್ಟಂ—ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಸೇವಿಸಲು ಯೋಗ್ಯವಾದ । ಏತತ್ ಹವಿಃ—ಈ ಹವಿಸ್ಸನ್ನು ।
en: - यातयज्जनः (*yātayajjanaḥ*)—one who impels people to their respective works
- मित्रायॆ (*mitrāyè*)—and of the form of Mitra ⟨NOTE:210⟩
- जुष्टं (*juṣṭaṃ*)—fit to be enjoyed with love
- आ जुहोत (*ā juhota*)—offer as an oblation
notes: ಉಪಸನ್ನಃ in Pratipadārtha; Saṃhitā/Pada have ಉಪಸದ್ಯಃ
ಮಿತ್ರಾಯೆ printed for ಮಿತ್ರಾಯ
ತಸ್ಯೈ printed; Saṃhitā/Pada ತಸ್ಮೈ

kn: ಜನರನ್ನು ಅವರವರ ಕರ್ಮಕ್ಕೆ ಪ್ರೇರಿಸುವವನಾಗಿಯೂ, ಸ್ತುತಿಕರ್ತನಾದ ಯಜಮಾನನಿಗೆ ಸುಖಕಾರಕನಾಗಿಯೂ
ಇದ್ದಾನೆ. ಸ್ತುತ್ಯತಮನೂ, ಮಿತ್ರರೂಪನೂ ಆದ ಈ ಆದಿತ್ಯನನ್ನುದ್ದೇಶಿಸಿ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಸೇವಿಸಲು ಯೋಗ್ಯ
en: Āditya is of great nature, approached with homage, the impeller of people to their respective works, and a giver of happiness to the sacrificer who praises him. To this Āditya, most praiseworthy and of the form of Mitra, offer in the fire, as an oblation, this offering fit to be enjoyed with love.

kn: The great Aditya, the animator of men to exertion, is to be appro-
ached with reverenee : he is the giver of happiness to him who praises him :
offer with fire the acceptable libation to that most glorifiable Mitra.
en: The great Aditya, the animator of men to exertion, is to be approached with reverence : he is the giver of happiness to him who praises him : offer with fire the acceptable libation to that most glorifiable Mitra.

kn: ಅಭಿಪ್ಲವನೆಂಬ ಯಾಗದ ಐದನೆಯ ದಿವಸದಲ್ಲಿ ವೈಶ್ವದೇವಶಸ್ತ್ರಮಂತ್ರ ಪಠನಮಾಡುವಾದ ಈ ಸೂಕ್ತದ
ಇಂದ್ರ ಋಭುಭಿಃ ಎಂದು ಮೊದಲಾಗುವ ಮೂರು ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳನ್ನು ಋಭುದೇವತಾಕವಾದ ತೃಚವನ್ನಾಗಿ
ಪಠಿಸಬೇಕೆಂದು ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನಶೌತಸೂತ್ರದ-ಧೃತವತೀ ಭುವನಾನಾಮಭಿಶ್ರಿಯೇಂದ್ರ ಋಭುಭಿರ್ವಾಜವದ್ಧಿರಿತಿ ತೆಚೌ ಎಂಬ ಸೂತ್ರದಿಂದ ವಿವೃತವಾಗಿರುವುದು. (ಆ. ೭ ೭) ಮತ್ತು ಈ ಸೂಕ್ತದ ಮೊದಲನೆಯ
ಋಕ್ಕನ್ನು ತೃತೀಯಸವನದಲ್ಲಿ ಹೋತೃವು ಪಠಿಸುವ ಪ್ರಸ್ಥಿತಯಾಜ್ಯಾಮಂತ್ರನ್ನಾಗಿ ಪಠಿಸಬೇಕೆಂದು ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನ
ಸೂತ್ರದ-ಇಂದ್ರ ಋಭುಭಿರ್ವಾಜವದ್ಧಿಃ ಸಮುಕ್ಷಿತಮಿಂದ್ರಾವರುಣಾ ಸುತಪಾವಿಮಂ ಸುತಂ ಎಂಬ
ಜಗತ್ಪೇರಕನಾದ ಆದಿತ್ಯನ ಪೂಜ್ಯತೆಯನ್ನು ಈ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ತುತಿಸಿದೆ. ಆದದರಿಂದಲೇ ಪನ್ಯತಮಾಯ
ಆದಿತ್ಯನಿಗೆ ಪನಸ್ಯತಿ, ಪನಾಯತೇ ಎಂಬ ಪದಗಳು ಅರ್ಚತಿಕರ್ಮನಾಮಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಪಠಿತವಾಗಿವೆ. (ನಿ. ೩-೧೯)
ಅಭೀಶೂನಾಂ ಮಹಿಮಾನಂ ಪನಾಯತ (ಋ. ಸಂ. ೬-೭೫-೬) ಇತ್ಯಾದ್ಯುದಾಹರಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹಿಂದೆ
ಪನಿತಾರಃ. ವಿಪಸ್ಯವಃ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಪದಗಳ ತಾತ್ಪರ್ಯವನ್ನು ವಿವರಿಸಿದೆ. ಪೂಜ್ಯತೆಯನ್ನು ತಿಳಿಸುವ ಪದಗಳಾಗಿವೆ.
ಸುಶೇವಃ— ಶೇವಶಬ್ದವು ಸುಖನಾಮಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಪಠಿತವಾಗಿದೆ. (ನಿ. ೩-೬) ಪ್ರೀತಿಪಾತ್ರವಾದುದೂ, ಸುಖ
ನ ಹಿ ಗ್ರಭಾಯಮಾಣಃ ಸುಶೇವೋಽನ್ಯೋದರ್ಯಃ (ಋ. ಸಂ. ೭-೪-೮) ಇತರರ ಹೊಟ್ಟೆಯಲ್ಲಿ
ಹುಟ್ಟಿದವನು ಸುಶೇವನಾದರೂ ಸ್ವೀಕೃತನಾಗಲು ಅರ್ಹನಲ್ಲ ಎಂಬ ಈ ವಾಕ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂತೋಷಕಾರಕನೆಂಬರ್ಥ.
ಪ್ರತಿ ಮೇ ಸ್ತೋಮಮದಿತಿರ್ಜಗೃಭ್ಯಾತ್ ಸೂನುಂ ನ ಮಾತಾ ಹೃದ್ಯಂ ಸುಶೇವಂ ।
ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಸ್ಥಳಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅತ್ಯಂತಪ್ರೀತಿಪಾತ್ರವಾದ ಎಂಬರ್ಥದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಯೋಗಿಸಿದೆ. ಇವುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಮೊದಲನೆಯ
ಉದಾಹರಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತೆಯು ಸುಶೇವನಾದ ಸೂನುವನ್ನು ಆಲಂಗಿಸುವಂತೆ ಎನ್ನುವಾಗ ಮಾತೃಪುತ್ರ ಸಂಬಂಧ
ವನ್ನೂ, ಎರಡನೆಯ ಉದಾಹರಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸುಶೇವಳಾದ ಪೃಥಿವಿಯನ್ನು ಎನ್ನುವಾಗ ಮಾತರಂ ಎಂಬ ವಿಶೇಷಣ
ವಿರುವುದರಿಂದ ಪುತ್ರರಿಗೂ, ಮಾತೃವಿಗೂ ಇರುವ ಸಂಬಂಧವನ್ನೂ ತಿಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಹೃದ್ಯವಾದ, ರಮ್ಯವಾದ,
ಸಂತೋಷಜನಕವಾದ ವಸ್ತುಗಳನ್ನು ವರ್ಣಿಸುವಾಗ ಈ ವಿಶೇಷಣವಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಇವುಗಳ ನಿಷೇಧಾರ್ಥವನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸು
ವಾಗಲೂ ಸಹ ಇದರ ಪ್ರಯೋಗವನ್ನು ನೋಡಬಹುದು. ಉದಾಹರಣೆಗೆ, ಅತ್ರಾ ಜಹಾಮ ಯೇ ಅಸನ್ನಶೇವಾಃ (೧೦-೫೩-೮) ನಾವು ನಮಗೆ ಬೇಡದಿರುವವರನ್ನೆಲ್ಲಾ ಇಲ್ಲೇ ಬಿಟ್ಟುಬಿಡುತ್ತೇವೆ ಎಂಬಲ್ಲಿ ಅಶೇವಪದಕ್ಕೆ
ಶತ್ರುಗಳ ಈ ಆಯುಧವು ಅಥವಾ ಆಯುಧದಂತೆ ಹಿಂಸಾಕಾರಕವಾದ ಈ ದಾರಿದ್ರ್ಯವು ಅಶೇವವಾದುದರಿಂದ
ನಮ್ಮಿಂದ ದೂರವಾಗಿರಲಿ ಎಂದರೆ ನಾಶವಾಗಲಿ ಎಂಬಲ್ಲಿ ಅಶೇವಶಬ್ದಕ್ಕೆ ಅಸುಖಕಾರಿ, ಹಿಂಸಾಕಾರಿ ಎಂಬರ್ಥ
ವಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಹೀಗೆ ಸುಶೇವ ಮತ್ತು ಅಶೇವ ಎಂಬ ಪದಗಳ ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳಿವೆ.
en: On the fifth day of the sacrifice called Abhiplava, when the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras are recited, the three Ṛks of this sūkta beginning इंद्र ऋभुभिः (*iṃdra ṛbhubhiḥ*) are to be recited as a tṛca addressed to the Ṛbhus. This is set out in Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra by the sūtra धृतवती भुवनानामभिश्रियेंद्र ऋभुभिर्वाजवद्धिरिति तॆचौ (*dhṛtavatī bhuvanānāmabhiśriyeṃdra ṛbhubhirvājavaddhiriti tècau*) (Ā. 7 7). And the first Ṛk of this sūkta is to be recited by the Hotṛ at the third pressing as the prasthita-yājyā mantra; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana sūtra इंद्र ऋभुभिर्वाजवद्धिः समुक्षितमिंद्रावरुणा सुतपाविमं सुतं (*iṃdra ṛbhubhirvājavaddhiḥ samukṣitamiṃdrāvaruṇā sutapāvimaṃ sutaṃ*) (Ā. 5-5).
In this Ṛk the worshipfulness of Āditya, the impeller of the world, is praised. That is why he is described by the epithet पन्यतमाय (*panyatamāya*).

पन्यतमाय (*panyatamāya*)—स्तुत्यतमाय (*stutyatamāya*): to Āditya, who is the most excellent among those worthy of praise and who is of the form of Mitra. The words पनस्यति (*panasyati*) and पनायते (*panāyate*) are read among the names of the act of worship (Ni. 3-19). With examples such as अभीशूनां महिमानं पनायत (*abhīśūnāṃ mahimānaṃ panāyata*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-75-6), the purport of the words पनितारः (*panitāraḥ*), विपस्यवः (*vipasyavaḥ*) and the like was explained earlier; they are words expressing worshipfulness. In the present place too it indicates the worshipfulness of Āditya.
सुशेवः (*suśevaḥ*)—The word शेव (*śeva*) is read among the names of happiness (Ni. 3-6). It is used in the senses of "the object of love", "what produces happiness" and the like.

न हि ग्रभायमाणः सुशेवोऽन्योदर्यः (*na hi grabhāyamāṇaḥ suśevo 'nyodaryaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-4-8): in this sentence, which means that one born of another's womb, though सुशेव (*suśeva*), is not fit to be accepted, the meaning is "the giver of delight".
प्रति मे स्तोममदितिर्जगृभ्यात् सूनुं न माता हृद्यं सुशेवं (*prati me stomamaditirjagṛbhyāt sūnuṃ na mātā hṛdyaṃ suśevaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-42-2)
उपसर्प मातरं भूमिमेतामुरुव्यचसं पृथिवीं सुशेवां (*upasarpa mātaraṃ bhūmimetāmuruvyacasaṃ pṛthivīṃ suśevāṃ*) (10-18-10)

In such places it is used in the sense of "very dear". Of these, in the first example, where it is said that as a mother embraces her son who is सुशेव (*suśeva*), the relation of mother and son is shown; in the second, where it speaks of the earth who is सुशेवा (*suśevā*), since the epithet मातरं (*mātaraṃ*) is present, the relation between sons and the mother is shown. This epithet occurs in describing things that are pleasing, charming and productive of delight. Its use may also be seen where the negation of these is to be shown. For example, in अत्रा जहाम ये असन्नशेवाः (*atrā jahāma ye asannaśevāḥ*) (10-53-8), "we leave behind here all those who are not wanted by us", the word अशेव (*aśeva*) comes to mean "not to be regarded".
व्येतु विद्युद्विषामशेवा युयोत विष्णुग्रपस्तनूनां (*vyetu vidyudviṣāmaśevā yuyota viṣṇugrapastanūnāṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-34-13)

Here, "may this weapon of the enemies, or this poverty, harmful like a weapon, being अशेव (*aśeva*), be far from us, that is, be destroyed": the word अशेव (*aśeva*) has the sense "not productive of happiness, harmful". Thus there are uses of the words सुशेव (*suśeva*) and अशेव (*aśeva*).

ಚರ್ಷಣೀಧೃತೋ ಮನುಷ್ಯಾಣಾಂ ವೃಷ್ಟಿಪ್ರದಾನೇನ ಧಾರಕಸ್ಯ ಮಿತ್ರಸ್ಯ ದೇವಸ್ಯ ಸಂಜಂಧ್ಯವೋಽನ್ನಂ ಸಾನಸಿ ಸರ್ವೈಃ ಸಂಭಜನೀಯಂ ದ್ಯುಮ್ನಂ ತದೀಯಂ ಧನಂ ಚ ಚಿತ್ರಶ್ರವಸ್ತಮಂ । ಅತಿಶಯೇನ ಚಾಯನೀಯಕೀರ್ತಿಯುಕ್ತಂ ॥ ಸಾನಸಿ । ಸನೋತೇಃ ಸಾನಸಿಪರ್ಣಸೀತ್ಯಾದಿನಾಸಿಚ್ ಪ್ರತ್ಯಯಾಂತತ್ವೇನ ನಿಪಾತನಾದುಪಧಾವೃದ್ಧಿಃ । ಚಿತ್ತಾದಂತೋದಾತ್ತಃ । ಸ್ವಮೋರಿತಿ ಸ್ವಮೋರ್ಲುಕ್ ॥

en: In the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha and in the Daśarātra, when the stomas are the seventeen-fold, the twenty-one-fold and so on, verses numbering five, seven and so on are to be inserted (āvāpa) at the place of insertion in the hotṛ-type śastras. Among them, in the Maitrāvaruṇa śastra the four verses beginning मित्रस्य चर्षन्णीधृत (*mitrasya carṣanṇīdhṛta*) are meant for insertion. This is stated in the sūtra मित्रस्य चर्षन्णीधृत इति चितस्रो मैत्र्यः (*mitrasya carṣanṇīdhṛta iti citasro maitryaḥ*) (Ā. 7-5).

Of the divine Mitra, who upholds men by giving rain, the food (avaḥ) is to be shared by all (sānasi), and his wealth (dyumna) is also most endowed with wonderful, hearable fame. On सानसि (*sānasi*) he gives a derivation: the affix is formed by the rule for words ending in -asi, and the penultimate vowel is lengthened. The word has acute accent on its final syllable because of चित्तादंतोदात्तः (*cittādaṃtodāttaḥ*); the loss of the case-ending is by the rule on sū and am.

en: In the sacrifices called Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha and Daśarātra, when the seventeen-fold and twenty-one-fold stomas are recited, the priests of the hotṛ group recite verses of five, seven and similar numbers as insertion (āvapanīya) mantras among the śastra mantras they must recite. Then, when the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa recites his śastra mantra, four verses beginning मित्रस्य चर्षणीधृतः (*mitrasya carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ*) (the 6th, 7th, 8th and 9th verses of this sūkta) are to be used as insertions. This is set out in the Āśvalāyana-śrautasūtra by the sūtra मित्रस्य चर्षणीधृत इति चतस्रो मैत्र्यः (*mitrasya carṣaṇīdhṛta iti catasro maitryaḥ*) (Ā. 7-5).

By the epithet चर्षणीधृतः (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ*) Mitra, the support of the universe, is praised. If one examines the greatness of this epithet, the power of Mitra, that is of the Āditya in the form of Mitra, becomes clear. In this verse Sāyaṇa has said that the word चर्षणीधृतः (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ*) means मनुष्याणां धारकस्य (*manuṣyāṇāṃ dhārakasya*), "the one who holds up human beings". Earlier, when explaining the sense of words such as पंचकृष्टयः (*paṃcakṛṣṭayaḥ*) and पंचजनाः (*paṃcajanāḥ*), quotations from authorities such as the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa and the Bṛhaddevatā were cited, and it was shown that these words do not mean merely earthly human beings but include gods, humans and all. By sentences such as गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा.... (*gaṃdharvāḥ pitaro devā....*) (Bṛ. De. 7-68) or चक्षुःशोत्रं मनो वाक् (*cakṣuḥśotraṃ mano vāk*) (7-71), this wider sense is established (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, Part 12, pp. 378-381). In the Ṛk Saṃhitā too, sentences such as पंच जना मम होत्रं जुषंतां (*paṃca janā mama hotraṃ juṣaṃtāṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-53-5) support the sense "gods and others". Therefore in the present verse the word चर्षणीधृतः (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ*) indicates Mitra's upholding of the whole universe.

ಮಿತ್ರಃ ಸಪ್ರಥಾಃ ಪ್ರಥಃ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಿಃ ಕೀರ್ತಿಃ । ತತ್ಸಹಿತಃ ಶ್ರವೋಭಿವೃಷ್ಟಿದ್ವಾರೋತ್ಪಾದಿತೈರನ್ನೈಃ ಪೃಥಿವೀಮಪ್ಯಭಿಭವತಿ । ಬಹ್ವನ್ನಯುಕ್ತಾಂ ಕರೋತೀತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ॥ ಸಪ್ರಥಾಃ । ಪ್ರಥ ಪ್ರಖ್ಯಾನೇ । ಅಸುನ್ ।

en: When the time of the morning homa has passed, there is a Maitra offering (iṣṭi); in it the verse अभि यो महिन (*abhi yo mahina*) is the anuvākyā. It is stated in the sūtra अभि यो महिना दिवं प्र स मित्र मर्तो अस्तु प्रयस्वान् (*abhi yo mahinā divaṃ pra sa mitra marto astu prayasvān*) (Ā. 3-12).

Mitra, who by his own greatness (mahinā) overcomes (abhi babhūva) the heaven, that is the atmosphere, that Mitra, with fame (saprathāḥ: प्रथः प्रसिद्धिः कीर्तिः (*prathaḥ prasiddhiḥ kīrtiḥ*), "praise is renown, fame"), overcomes also the earth with food produced by way of rain; that is, he makes it rich in food. On सप्रथाः (*saprathāḥ*): the root प्रथ (*pratha*) is in the sense of renown; the affix asun; sa is substituted for saha.
- अभि बभूव (*abhi babhūva*)—has overcome and pervaded (that same Mitra)

kn: ಮಿತ್ರನು ತನ್ನ ಮಾಹಾತ್ಮ್ಯದಿಂದ ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷವನ್ನು ಆಕ್ರಮಿಸಿ ವ್ಯಾಪಿಸಿರುವಂತೆಯೇ ಪೃಥಿವಿಯನ್ನೂ ಸಹ
ತನ್ನ ಕೀರ್ತಿಯಿಂದಲೂ, ಅನ್ನದಿಂದಲೂ ಕೂಡಿಕೊಂಡು ವ್ಯಾಪಿಸಿ ನಿಂತಿದ್ದಾನೆ.
en: Just as Mitra has overcome and pervaded the atmosphere by his greatness, so he stands pervading the earth also, joined with his fame and with food.

kn: The renowned Mitra, who by his might presides over heaven, is he
who presides over the earth by (the gift of) food.
en: The renowned Mitra, who by his might presides over heaven, is he who presides over the earth by (the gift of) food.

kn: ಮೈತ್ರೇಷ್ಟಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಾತಃಕಾಲದ ಹೋಮವನ್ನು ಮಾಡುವಾಗ ಕಾಲಾತೀತವಾಗಿದ್ದರೆ ಅದರ ಪ್ರಾಯಶ್ಚಿ
ತ್ತಾರ್ಥವಾಗಿ ಮಾಡುವ ಹೋಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಭಿ ಯೋ ಮಹಿನಾ ಎಂಬ ಈ ಋಕ್ಕನ್ನು ಅನುವಾಕ್ಯಾಮಂತ್ರವನ್ನಾಗಿ
ಉಪಯೋಗಿಸಬೇಕೆಂದು ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನಶೌತಸೂತ್ರದ—ಅಭಿ ಯೇ ಮಹಿನಾ ದಿವಂ ಪ್ರಸಮಿತ್ರ ಮರ್ತೋ
ಈ ಸೂಕ್ತದಲ್ಲಿ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಸಹ ಮಿತ್ರರೂಪನಾದ ಆದಿತ್ಯನ ಸ್ತುತಿಯಿದೆ. ಅದರಲ್ಲೂ ೬, ೭
ಮತ್ತು ೮ನೇ ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಮಿತ್ರನ ಒಂದು ಮುಖ್ಯವಾದ ವ್ಯಾಪಕಗುಣವನ್ನು ವಿವರಿಸಿ ತಿಳಿಸಿದೆ. ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಹಿಂದಿನ
ಎಂದರೆ ೬ನೇ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಮಿತ್ರಸ್ಯ ಚರ್ಷಣೀಧೃತಃ ಎಂದು ವರ್ಣಿಸಿದೆ. ಆ ಋಕ್ಕಿನ ವಿಶೇಷವಿಷಯಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಚರ್ಷಣಿ
ಶಬ್ದವು ಕೇವಲ ಪೃಥ್ವೀಸ್ಥವಾದ ಮಾನವರೆಂದು ಮಾತ್ರ ಅರ್ಥವಾಗಿರದೆ, ದೇವಮಾನವಾದಿ ಸಕಲರನ್ನೂ ಸೂಚಿಸ
ತಕ್ಕ ವ್ಯಾಪಕಧರ್ಮವುಳ್ಳ ಪದವೆಂದು ತಿಳಿಸಿದೆ. ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಮುಂದಿನ ಎಂದರೆ ೮ನೇ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಸಹ ಪಂಚ ಜನಾಃ
ಅಭಿ ಬಭೂವ—ಭೂಧಾತುವು ಅಭಿ ಎಂಬ ಉಪಸರ್ಗದೊಡನೆ ಸೇರಿದರೆ ಸಾಧಾರಣವಾಗಿ ಸೋಲಿಸು,
ಆಕ್ರಮಿಸು ಎಂಬರ್ಥವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರಕೃತವಾದ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷವನ್ನೆಲ್ಲಾ ತನ್ನ ಪ್ರಭುತ್ವದಿಂದ ತನ್ನ
ಅಭೀ ಷೂ ಣಃ ಸಖೀನಾಮವಿತಾ ಜರಿತ್ಕೃಣಾಂ । ಶತಂ ಭವಾಸ್ಕೃತಿಭಿಃ ॥
ಎಂಬಲ್ಲಿ ಎಲೈ ಇಂದ್ರನೇ, ನೀನು ಸ್ತೋತೃಗಳಿಗೆ ಅಭಿ ಭವಾಸಿ ಅಭಿಮುಖನಾಗು ಎಂಬ ತಾತ್ಪರವಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಇತರ
ಕಡೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಗ್ರಹಮಾಡಿ ಸೋಲಿಸು ಎಂದು ತಾತ್ಪರವಾಗಿರುವ ಈ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಅನುಗ್ರಹಾತ್ಮಕವಾದ ಆಗಮನವಿರಲಿ
ಎಂದು ಪ್ರಾರ್ಥಿಸಿದೆ. ಪ್ರಕೃತವಾದ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಸಹ ಮಿತ್ರನು ಅನುಗ್ರಹರೂಪವಾಗಿಯೇ ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷವನ್ನೆಲ್ಲಾ
ಸಪ್ರಥಾಃ—ಪ್ರಥಃ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಿಃ ಕೀರ್ತಿಃ । ತತ್ಸಹಿತಃ । ಪ್ರಥವೆಂದರೆ ಕೀರ್ತಿ, ಸಪ್ರಥವೆಂದರೆ ಕೀರ್ತಿ
ಯುಕ್ತನೆಂದರ್ಥ. ಪ್ರಥಶಬ್ದಕ್ಕೆ ಮೂಲಾರ್ಥವು ವಿಸ್ತ್ರತವಾಗಿ ಹರಡುವುದು ಎಂದರ್ಥ. ವ್ಯಕ್ತಿಯ ಗುಣವು
ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಕಡೆಯೂ ವಿಸ್ತ್ರತವಾಗಿ ಹರಡುವುದರಿಂದ ಎಲ್ಲೆಲ್ಲೂ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧವಾಗುವುದು. ಎಂದರೆ ಕೀರ್ತಿಯೆಂಬುದರಲ್ಲಿ
ತಾತ್ಪರ್ಯ. ನಿರುಕ್ತಕಾರರೂ ಸಹ ಇದೇ ರೀತಿ ವಿವರಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಸಪ್ರಥಾಃ ಸರ್ವತಃ ಪೃಥುಃ । ಸುತ್ತಲೂ
ವಿಸ್ತ್ರತವಾಗಿ ಹರಡಿರುವುದೆಂದರ್ಥವೆಂದು ತೋರಿಸಿ ತ್ವಮಗ್ನೇ ಸಪ್ರಥಾ ಅಸಿ .... .... (ಋ. ಸಂ. ೫-೧೩-೪)
ಎಂಬ ಋಕ್ಕನ್ನುದಾಹರಿಸಿ ಈ ಪದಕ್ಕಿರುವ ಅರ್ಥವೈಶಿಷ್ಟ್ಯವನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ. (ನಿ. ೬-೮).
en: In the Maitra offering, if the morning homa has passed its time, then in the homa performed as its expiation this verse अभि यो महिना (*abhi yo mahinā*) is to be used as an anuvākyā mantra. This is set out in the Āśvalāyana-śrautasūtra by the sūtra अभि ये महिना दिवं प्रसमित्र मर्तो अस्तु प्रयस्वान् (*abhi ye mahinā divaṃ prasamitra marto astu prayasvān*) (Ā. 3-12).⟨NOTE:212⟩

In every verse of this sūkta there is praise of the Āditya in the form of Mitra. Especially in verses 6, 7 and 8 one important, all-pervading quality of Mitra is set out. In the verse before this, the 6th, he is described as मित्रस्य चर्षणीधृतः (*mitrasya carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ*). In the special topics on that verse it was explained that the word carṣaṇi does not mean merely human beings on earth but is a word of wide scope, indicating gods, humans and all. In the verse after this, the 8th, it is likewise described that पंच जनाः येमिरे (*paṃca janāḥ yemire*), the five peoples serve him.

अभि बभूव (*abhi babhūva*)—When the root bhū is joined with the prefix abhi it commonly means "defeat, overrun". In the present verse it means that by his lordship he has brought the whole atmosphere under his control and stands overrunning all heaven and earth. But in
अभी षू णः सखीनामविता जरित्कृणां । शतं भवास्कृतिभिः ॥ (*abhī ṣū ṇaḥ sakhīnāmavitā jaritkṛṇāṃ | śataṃ bhavāskṛtibhiḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-31-3)

the sense is, "O Indra, be (abhi bhavāsi) turned toward the singers". Elsewhere the sense is "subdue and defeat", but in this verse a coming of the nature of favour is prayed for. Even in the present verse it would not be wrong to say that Mitra stands pervading the whole atmosphere in the form of favour.

सप्रथाः (*saprathāḥ*)—प्रथः प्रसिद्धिः कीर्तिः । तत्सहितः (*prathaḥ prasiddhiḥ kīrtiḥ | tatsahitaḥ*). Pratha means fame; sapratha means one endowed with fame. The original sense of the word pratha is "to spread widely". Because a person's quality spreads widely everywhere, he becomes renowned everywhere; the sense is fame. The Nirukta-author also explains it so: after showing that सप्रथाः सर्वतः पृथुः (*saprathāḥ sarvataḥ pṛthuḥ*) means "spread out widely all round", he cites the verse त्वमग्ने सप्रथा असि .... .... (*tvamagne saprathā asi .... ....*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-13-4) and thereby shows the special sense of this word (Ni. 6-8).
notes: ಯೇ in the Special Topics sūtra, ಯೋ in the bhāṣya; ಪ್ರಸಮಿತ್ರ printed run together

ref: मि॒त्राय॒ पञ्च॑ येमिरे॒ जना॑ अ॒भिष्टि॑शवसे।
स दे॒वान्विश्वा॑न्बिभर्ति

kn: ಸಃ । ದೇವಾನ್ । ವಿಶ್ವಾನ್ । ಬಿ ಭ ರ್ತಿ ॥ ೮ ॥
ಪಂಚ ಜನಾ ನಿಷಾದಪಂಚಮಾಶ್ಚತ್ವಾರೋ ವರ್ಣಾ ಅಭಿಷ್ಟಿಶವಸೇ ಶತ್ರೂಣಾಮಭಿಗಂತೃಬಲಯುಕ್ತಾಯ ಮಿತ್ರಾಯ ಯೇಮಿರೇ । ಹವೀಂಷ್ಯುದ್ಯಚ್ಛಂತಿ । ಸ ತಾದೃಶೋ ಮಿತ್ರೋ ವಿಶ್ವಾನ್
ಸರ್ವಾನ್ದೇವಾನ್ಬಿಭರ್ತಿ । ಸ್ವಸ್ವರೂಪತಯಾ ಧಾರಯತಿ ॥ ಅಭಿಷ್ಟಿಶವಸೇ । ಇಷೇರ್ಮಂತ್ರೇ ವೃಷೇತ್ಯಾದಿನಾ ಕ್ತಿನ್ । ತಾದೌ ಚ ನಿತೀತ್ಯಭೇರಂತೋದಾತ್ತತ್ವಂ । ಶಕಂಧ್ವಾದಿತ್ವಾತ್ಪರರೂಪತ್ವಂ । ಬಹುವ್ರೀಹ

en: The five peoples (pañca janāḥ), that is the four varṇas with the Niṣāda as the fifth, offer (yemire) their oblations to Mitra, who has the strength that goes against enemies (abhiṣṭiśavase). The Gist continues in the next block.

Such a Mitra bears all the gods, holding them in his own form. On अभिष्टिशवसे (*abhiṣṭiśavase*) the remainder of the block gives derivation and accent only (the affix ktin, the accent on the final of abhi, the pararūpa and the accent of the bahuvrīhi compound).

kn: ಸಃ—ಅಂತಹ ಮಿತ್ರನು । ವಿಶ್ವಾನ್—ಸಮಸ್ತವಾದ । ದೇವಾನ್—ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನೂ । ಬಿಭರ್ತಿ—ತನ್ನ ಸ್ವರೂಪ
en: - पंचजनाः (*paṃcajanāḥ*)—the people, consisting of the five classes beginning with the Niṣādas, also
- अभिष्टिशवसे (*abhiṣṭiśavase*)—who has the power to destroy enemies

kn: ನಿಷಾದಾದಿ ಪಂಚವರ್ಣಾತ್ಮಕರಾದ ಜನರೂ ಸಹ ಶತ್ರುನಾಶಕವಾದ ಶಕ್ತಿಯುಳ್ಳ ಮಿತ್ರನನ್ನುದ್ದೇಶಿಸಿ
ಹವಿಸ್ಸನ್ನರ್ಪಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಅಂತಹ ಮಿತ್ರನು ಸಮಸ್ತರಾದ ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನೂ ತನ್ನ ಸ್ವರೂಪದಿಂದಲೇ ಧರಿಸಿದ್ದಾನೆ.
en: The people, consisting of the five classes beginning with the Niṣādas, also offer oblation to Mitra, who has the power to destroy enemies. Such a Mitra bears all the gods in his own form.

kn: The five classes of men have repaired to the victorious Mitra, for he supports all the gods.
en: The five classes of men have repaired to the victorious Mitra, for he supports all the gods.

kn: ಪ್ರಯುಕ್ತವಾಗಿದೆ. ಶವಃಶಬ್ದಕ್ಕೆ ಬಲವೆಂದರ್ಥ. ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಶತ್ರುಗಳನ್ನು ನಾಶಮಾಡಿ ಸ್ತೋತೃವನ್ನು ರಕ್ಷಿಸಬಲ್ಲ
ಶಕ್ತಿಯೆಂದು ತಾತ್ಪರ್ಯ. ಅಭಿಷ್ಟಿಮನ್ನಾಸತ್ಯಾ ವರೂಥಂ (ಋ. ಸಂ. ೧-೧೧೬-೧೧) ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಸಂದರ್ಭಗಳಲ್ಲಿ
ಪಂಚ ಜನಾಃ-ಗಂಧರ್ವಾ ಅಪ್ಸರಸೋ ದೇವಾ ಅಸುರಾ ರಕ್ಷಾಂಸಿ ಪಂಚಜನಾಃ । ನಿಷಾದಪಂಚಮಾಶ್ಚಾತ್ವಾರೋ ವರ್ಣಾ ವಾ । ಗಂಧರ್ವರೂ, ಅಪ್ಸರಸ್ಸುಗಳೂ- ದೇವತೆಗಳೂ, ಅಸುರರೂ ಮತ್ತು ರಾಕ್ಷಸರೂ
ಸೇರಿ ಐದು ಗುಂಪುಗಳು ಅಥವಾ ಐದನೆಯದಾದ ನಿಷಾದರ ಎಂದರೆ ಬೇಡರ ಗುಂಪಿನೊಂದಿಗೆ ಸೇರಿದ ನಾಲ್ಕು
ವರ್ಣದ ಜನರು ಎಂದು ಸಾಯಣರ ವಿವರಣೆಯಿದೆ. ಈ ವರ್ಗೀಕರಣದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಭೇದಗಳಿವೆ. ನಿರುಕ್ತಕಾರರು
ತಮ್ಮ ಮತವೇನೆಂದು ಹೇಳದೇ ಇತರರ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ಉದಹರಿಸಿರುವರು.
ಪಂಚಜನಾ ( ಮಮ ಹೋತ್ರಂ ಜುಷಧ್ವಂ ) ಗಂಧರ್ವಾಃ ಪಿತರೋ ದೇವಾ ಅಸುರಾ
ರಕ್ಷಾಂಸೀತ್ಯೇಕೇ । ಚತ್ವಾರೋ ವರ್ಣಾ ನಿಷಾದಃ ಪಂಚಮ ಇತ್ಯೌಪಮನ್ಯವಃ ।
ಗಂಧರ್ವರು, ಪಿತೃಗಳು, ದೇವತೆಗಳು, ಅಸುರರು, ರಾಕ್ಷಸರು ಎಂದು ಐದುವಿಧವಾದ ಜನರೆಂದು ಕೆಲವರೂ
ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಾದಿ ನಾಲ್ಕು ವರ್ಣದವರೊಂದಿಗೆ ನಿಷಾದರೆಂಬ ಐದನೆಯ ಗುಂಪೂ ಸೇರಿ ಪಂಚಜನರೆಂದು ಉಪಮನ್ಯುವೇ
ಮುಂತಾದವರೂ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಪಡುವರೆಂದು ಇತರರ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ಹೇಳಿರುವರು.
ಹಿಂದೆ ದೇವತೆಗಳೆಲ್ಲರೂ ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ಕುರಿತು ತಮಗಾಗಿ ಯಜ್ಞದಲ್ಲಿ ಅರ್ಪಿತವಾದ ಹವಿಸ್ಸನ್ನು ಸ್ವೀಕರಿಸಿ
ಎಲ್ಲರಿಗೂ ಹಂಚಬೇಕೆಂದು ಪ್ರಾರ್ಥಿಸಿದಾಗ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಒಪ್ಪಿಕೊಂಡು,
ತದದ್ಯ ವಾಚಃ ಪ್ರಥಮಂ ಮಸೀಯ ಯೇನಾಸುರಾ ಅಭಿ ದೇವಾ ಅಸಾಮ ।
ಊರ್ಜಾದ ಉತ ಯಜ್ಜಿಯಾಸಃ ಪಂಚ ಜನಾ ಮಮ ಹೋತ್ರಂ ಜುಷಧ್ವಂ ।
ಪಂಚಜನರೂ ಈ ಹವಿಸ್ಸನ್ನು ಭೋಗಿಸಲಿ ಎಂದು ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಕೊಟ್ಟಿರುವ ಈ ವಾಕ್ಯವನ್ನು ಬೃಹದ್ದೇವತಾ
ಕಾರರು ಉದಹರಿಸಿ ಪಂಚಜನರು ಯಾರು ಎಂದು ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಭೇದಗಳನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸಿ ಚರ್ಚಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ.
ತತ್ಕರಿಷ್ಯೇ ಜುಷಂತಾಂ ತು ಹೋತ್ರಂ ಪಂಚಜನಾ ಮಮ ॥
ಎಂಬ ಶ್ಲೋಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ದೇವತೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಕೊಟ್ಟ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ತಿಳಿಸಿ ಅನಂತರ ಪಂಚಜನಶಬ್ದವನ್ನು
ಎಂದರೆ, ಶಾಲೆಯ ಪ್ರವೇಶಭಾಗದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೂ, ಪ್ರಣೀತವಾದ ಆಹವನೀಯಾಗ್ನಿಯೂ ಯಜಮಾನನ ಪುತ್ರ
ಭೂತನಾದ ಗಾರ್ಹಪತ್ಯಾಗ್ನಿಯೂ, ದಕ್ಷಿಣೋತ್ತರಾಗ್ನಿಗಳೂ ಸೇರಿ ಈ ಐದು ವಿಧವಾದ ಅಗ್ನಿಗಳೂ ಐದು ಬಗೆಯ

ಇತರರ ಮತಗಳನ್ನು ಹೇಳಿದೆಯೇ ಹೊರತು ಯಾಸ್ಕರ ಮತವನ್ನು ನಿಷ್ಕರ್ಷವಾಗಿ ತಿಳಿಸಿಲ್ಲ. ಪ್ರಾಯಃ ಅದನ್ನೇ
ಹೋತ್ರಾದಿ ನಾಲ್ಕು ಋತ್ವಿಕ್ಕುಗಳೂ, ಯಜಮಾನನೂ ಸೇರಿ ಐದು ಜನರ ಗುಂಪೆಂದು ಶಾಕಪೂಣಿಯವರ ಮತ.
ಚಕ್ಷುಃ ಶ್ರೋತಂ ಮನೋ ವಾಕ್ ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಶ್ಚೇತ್ಯಾತ್ಮವಾದಿನಃ ।
ಚಕ್ಷುಸ್ಸು, ಶೋತ್ರ, ಮನಸ್ಸು, ವಾಕ್ಕು ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರಾಣ ಈ ಐದೂ ಪಂಚಜನರೆಂದು ಆಧ್ಯಾತ್ಮಿಕವಾದಿಗಳ ಮತ.

ವಿವರಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಭೇದಗಳು ಉದಹರಿಸಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಿವೆ. ಕೆಲವು ಕಡೆ ಜನಾಃ ಎಂಬ ಶಬ್ದಕ್ಕೆ ಬದಲಾಗಿ
ಕ್ಷಿತಯಃ ಎಂಬ ಶಬ್ದವು ಮನುಷ್ಯಾಃ ನರಾಃ ಮೊದಲಾದ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೈದು ಮನುಷ್ಯ ವಾಚಕನಾಮಗಳ
ಮಧ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಪಠಿತವಾಗಿದೆ. (ನಿ. ೩-೭) ಪಂಚ ಕ್ಷಿತೀನಾಂ ಎಂದರೆ ಪಂಚ ಜನಾನಾಂ ಎಂದರ್ಥವು

ಷ್ಯಾಣಾಂ ಪಂಚಾನಾಂ ಕ್ಷಿತೀನಾಂ ನಿವಸತಾಂ ಗಂಧರ್ವಾಃ ಪಿತರೋ ದೇವಾ ಅಸುರಾ ರಕ್ಷಾಂಸೀತಿ
ಪಂಚತ್ವಂ ಎಂದೂ ಅರ್ಥವಿವರಣೆಮಾಡಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಸಾಯಣರ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯದಂತೆ ಕ್ಷಿತೀನಾಂ ಎಂದರೆ ಭೂಮಿ

ಜನರೆಂದು ಅರ್ಥವಾಗುವುದು. ನಿಷಾದರೆಂದರೆ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಾದಿ ನಾಲ್ಕು ವರ್ಣಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸೇರದಿರುವ ಮತ್ತು
ಮೃಗಗಳ ಬೇಟೆಯಿಂದಲೇ ಜೀವಿಸುವ ಜನರೆಂದರ್ಥವು. ಈ ದೇಶದ ಪೂರ್ವನಿವಾಸಿಗಳಾದ ಗೊಂಡರು,
ಕೋಲರು, ಭಿಲ್ಲರು ಮೊದಲಾದವರು ಈ ಜಾತಿಗೆ ಸೇರಿದವರು. ಇವರು ಮಧ್ಯಪ್ರಾಂತ ಮೊದಲಾದ ಕೆಲವು
ಸ್ಥಳಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತ್ರ ಈಗಲೂ ಬಹು ಅಲ್ಪಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ವಾಸಿಸುತ್ತಿರುವರು. ಪಂಚ ಜನಾಃ ಮತ್ತು ಪಂಚ ಕೃಷ್ಟೀಃ
ಎಂಬ ಶಬ್ದಗಳು ಋಗ್ವೇದದಲ್ಲಿ ಅನೇಕ ಕಡೆ ಇವೆ.

ಸಾಯಣರು ಅನುಮೋದಿಸಿರುವರು). ನಿಷಾದರೆಂದರೆ ಪ್ರಾಣಿಗಳನ್ನು ಕೊಲ್ಲುವವರು ಅಥವಾ ಇವರಲ್ಲಿ ಪಾಪವು

ಮುಖ್ಯವಾದ ಪಂಗಡಗಳು (tribes) ಇದ್ದಿರಬಹುದು. ಕವಿಯು ಈ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯವನ್ನೇ ಇಟ್ಟುಕೊಂಡು
ಪಂಚ ಜನಾಃ ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಿರಬಹುದು. ಹೇಗಾದರೂ ಈ ವಿಚಾರದಲ್ಲಿ ನಿರುಕ್ತಕಾರರಾದ ಯಾಸ್ಕರ
en: अभिष्टिशवसे (*abhiṣṭiśavase*)—The word abhiṣṭi is commonly used in the sense of help in the form of protection. The word śavaḥ means strength. Here the sense is the power that can destroy enemies and protect the singer. The special senses of this word are explained in passages such as अभिष्टिमन्नासत्या वरूथं (*abhiṣṭimannāsatyā varūthaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-11).

पंच जनाः (*paṃca janāḥ*)—गंधर्वा अप्सरसो देवा असुरा रक्षांसि पंचजनाः । निषादपंचमाश्चात्वारो वर्णा वा । (*gaṃdharvā apsaraso devā asurā rakṣāṃsi paṃcajanāḥ | niṣādapaṃcamāścātvāro varṇā vā |*). Sāyaṇa's explanation is: five groups, namely Gandharvas, Apsarases, gods, Asuras and Rākṣasas; or the people of the four varṇas together with the fifth group of Niṣādas, that is hunters. There are differences of opinion in this classification. The Nirukta-author, without saying what his own view is, only cites the opinions of others:
गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा रक्षांसीत्येके (*gaṃdharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā rakṣāṃsītyeke*) । चत्वारो वर्णा निषादः पंचम इत्यौपमन्यवः (*catvāro varṇā niṣādaḥ paṃcama ityaupamanyavaḥ*) (Ni. 3-8).

He states only the opinions of others: some hold that the five kinds of people are Gandharvas, Pitṛs, gods, Asuras and Rākṣasas; Aupamanyu and others hold that the five peoples are the four varṇas beginning with Brāhmaṇas together with a fifth group, the Niṣādas.
Once, when all the gods prayed to Agni to accept the oblation offered for them in the sacrifice and to distribute it to all, Agni agreed and said:

तदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीय येनासुरा अभि देवा असाम । ऊर्जाद उत यज्जियासः पंच जना मम होत्रं जुषध्वं । (*tadadya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīya yenāsurā abhi devā asāma | ūrjāda uta yajjiyāsaḥ paṃca janā mama hotraṃ juṣadhvaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-53-4)
"May the five peoples enjoy this oblation": the authors of the Bṛhaddevatā cite this sentence, which gives the answer, show the differences of opinion on who the five peoples are, and discuss them.
प्रत्युवाचाथ तानग्निर्विश्वेदेवा यदूच मां । तत्करिष्ये जुषंतां तु होत्रं पंचजना मम ॥ (*pratyuvācātha tānagnirviśvedevā yadūca māṃ | tatkariṣye juṣaṃtāṃ tu hotraṃ paṃcajanā mama ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-66)
In this verse the answer Agni gave to the gods is stated, and afterwards the word pañcajana is explained.
शालामुख्यः प्रणीतश्च पुत्रो गृहपतेश्च यः । उत्तरो दक्षिणश्चाग्निरेते पंचजनाः स्मृताः ॥ (*śālāmukhyaḥ praṇītaśca putro gṛhapateśca yaḥ | uttaro dakṣiṇaścāgnirete paṃcajanāḥ smṛtāḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-67)

That is, the fire at the entrance of the hall, the consecrated Āhavanīya fire, the Gārhapatya fire which is as the son of the sacrificer, and the southern and northern fires, these five kinds of fires are traditionally called five classes. This is one view. Moreover:
मनुष्याः पितरो देवा गंधर्वोरगराक्षसाः । गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा यक्षराक्षसाः ॥ (*manuṣyāḥ pitaro devā gaṃdharvoragarākṣasāḥ | gaṃdharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā yakṣarākṣasāḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-68)
By the first view, one group is made of human beings and others together with serpents and Rākṣasas; in the second, Yakṣas and Rākṣasas form one group.
यास्कौपमन्यवावेतानाहतुः पंच वै जनान् । निषादपंचमान्वर्णा मन्यते शाकटायनः ॥ (*yāskaupamanyavāvetānāhatuḥ paṃca vai janān | niṣādapaṃcamānvarṇā manyate śākaṭāyanaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-69)

In this sentence the authors of the Bṛhaddevatā say that Yāska's view is the first. But in the Nirukta the views of others are stated and Yāska's own view is not stated definitively. Perhaps he too accepted that one.
The Brihaddevatā says: "Śākapūṇi, however, holds that the *pañca janāḥ* are the priests and the sacrificer." (Bṛ. De. 7-20)
The opinion of Śākapūṇi is that the four priests beginning with the Hotṛ, together with the sacrificer, make up a group of five persons.

The Brihaddevatā continues: "Eye, ear, mind, speech and breath are the five persons, according to the teachers of the self (ātmavādins). Gandharvas and Apsarases, gods, men and fathers, and also serpents, are heard of in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa."

The eye, ear, mind, speech and breath: these five are the five persons according to the teachers of the self. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa explains them as the Gandharvas and the rest. (Ai. Brā. 3-31-5) The explanation of the Brihaddevatā also cites these differences of opinion: that such five kinds of beings, too, may enjoy the oblation was Agni's answer to the gods. In some places the word *kṣitayaḥ* is used in place of *janāḥ*.

The word *kṣitayaḥ* is read among the twenty-five names for man, *manuṣyāḥ*, *narāḥ* and the rest. (Ni. 3-7) *Pañca kṣitīnām* means *pañca janānām*. The commentator (Yāska's) explains it as *niṣādapañcamānām*; Skandasvāmin as "of the human classes, of these: Gandharvas, fathers, gods"; and Veṅkaṭamādhava explains it as "the fivefold character of the five dwelling human races: Gandharvas, fathers, gods, Asuras and Rākṣasas." According to Sāyaṇa, *kṣitīnām* means the people of five classes fit to dwell on earth: Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, Śūdra and Niṣāda. Niṣādas are people who do not belong to the four varṇas beginning with the Brāhmaṇa, and who live by hunting animals. The Gonds, Kolas, Bhillas and others, former inhabitants of this country, belong to this class. They still live, in very small numbers, only in a few places such as the Central Provinces. The words *pañca janāḥ* and *pañca kṛṣṭīḥ* occur in many places in the Ṛgveda.

In sum, some say the five kinds of people are Gandharvas, fathers, gods, Asuras and Rākṣasas. The view of Upamanyu and others is that the five kinds are the people of the four varṇas beginning with the Brāhmaṇa, together with the hunter class called Niṣāda (Sāyaṇa has endorsed this). The Nairuktas say that Niṣādas are those who kill animals, or that they are so called because sin is full in them. It may also be that there were five main tribes at that time, and the poet may have said *pañca janāḥ* with this in mind. At all events it is clear that there was a difference of opinion on this matter even in the time of Yāska, the author of the Nirukta.
