गायत्रीद्वारेण चोच्यते ब्रह्म सर्वविशेषरहितस्य “ नेति नेति ” इत्यादि विशेषप्रतिषेधगम्यस्य दुर्बोधत्वात् । सत्त्वनेकेषु छंदस्सु गायत्रा एव ब्रह्मज्ञानतयोपादानं प्राधान्यात् । सोमाहरणादितरच्छंदोक्षरा- हरणेनेतरच्छंदोव्याप्त्या च सर्वसवनव्यापकत्वाच्च यज्ञे प्राधान्यं गायत्र्याः । गायत्रीसारत्वाच्च ब्राह्मणस्य मातरमिव । हित्वा गुरुतरां गायत्रीं ततोऽन्यद्गुरुतरं न प्रतिपद्यते यथोक्तं ब्रह्मापीति तस्यामत्यंतगौरवस्य प्रसिद्धत्वात् । अतो गायत्रीमुखेनैव ब्रहोच्यते ॥ (*gāyatrīdvāreṇa cocyate brahma sarvaviśeṣarahitasya “ neti neti ” ityādi viśeṣapratiṣedhagamyasya durbodhatvāt | sattvanekeṣu chaṃdassu gāyatrā eva brahmajñānatayopādānaṃ prādhānyāt | somāharaṇāditaracchaṃdokṣarā- haraṇenetaracchaṃdovyāptyā ca sarvasavanavyāpakatvācca yajñe prādhānyaṃ gāyatryāḥ | gāyatrīsāratvācca brāhmaṇasya mātaramiva | hitvā gurutarāṃ gāyatrīṃ tato 'nyadgurutaraṃ na pratipadyate yathoktaṃ brahmāpīti tasyāmatyaṃtagauravasya prasiddhatvāt | ato gāyatrīmukhenaiva brahocyate ‖*)

Supreme Brahman is beyond perception by the eye and the like. He is not an object visible to the eye, nor can he be seen by the mind's vision, nor is he any object in the world of ordinary dealings. The Supreme Self can be described only in the negative form, in this way. Though there are many other metres, realisation of the Supreme Self is possible only with the help of the Gāyatrī. That the Gāyatrī has this power as a means is shown by the prominent part it plays in the sacrificial act. Because sacrifices and other rites help divine knowledge, and because the Gāyatrī's help is indispensable in carrying out such sacrifices, the Gāyatrī is also the most important means to the knowledge of Brahman. This prominence is understood from three points:
(1) First, because the Gāyatrī brought to the gods the Soma that is central to the sacrifice;
(2) second, because it has drawn into itself the syllables of the other metres and pervades them all;
(3) third, because it pervades all three pressings (savana), the Gāyatrī has primacy in the sacrificial act.

Śaṅkarācārya makes clear that, because it is like a mother to Brāhmaṇas and the rest, and because the knowledge of the nature of Brahman also rests on the Gāyatrī, the Gāyatrī is the chief means for the direct realisation of the nature of the light of Brahman. What is the scriptural basis for each of these three points that Śaṅkarācārya states, and how is this primacy of the Gāyatrī described in the Śruti passages? This now has to be examined.
**(10) Three points showing the primacy of the Gāyatrī.**
**1. The episode of the bringing of Soma. The effort of the Śyena bird.**

First: सोमाहरणात् (*somāharaṇāt*), "because it brought the Soma that is central to the sacrifice". Thus the special power of the Gāyatrī is indicated. This episode of the bringing of Soma is described in all the most important places in the Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas. First of all,

it is told as a story in the Ṛk Saṃhitā itself. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26 and 4-27, when Indra describes his own valour, he tells how that valour grew through drinking Soma, and how the Gāyatrī brought that Soma.

[Whether this description is the speech of the seer Vāmadeva or of Indra, and whether the deity of these sūktas is Indra or the Supreme Self, are also matters to note. That discussion is unnecessary here.

प्र सु ष विभ्यो मरुतो विरस्तु प्र श्येनः श्येनेभ्य अशुपत्वा । अचक्रया यत्स्वधया सुपर्णो हव्यं भरन्मनवे देवजुष्टं ॥ (*pra su ṣa vibhyo maruto virastu pra śyenaḥ śyenebhya aśupatvā | acakrayā yatsvadhayā suparṇo havyaṃ bharanmanave devajuṣṭaṃ ‖*)

O Maruts, may this Suparṇa, who brought this Soma desired by the gods to Manu in a chariot without a wheel, swiftly, be greater in vigour than the other Śyena birds, and may he receive greater honour.

भरद्यदि विरतो वेविजानः पथोरुणा मनोजना असर्जि । तॊयं ययौ मधुना सोम्येगोत श्रवो विविदे श्येनो अत्र ॥ (*bharadyadi virato vevijānaḥ pathoruṇā manojanā asarji | tòyaṃ yayau madhunā somyegota śravo vivide śyeno atra ‖*)

This Śyena bird rebuked the guardians of the Soma, carried off the Soma, and glided down through the sky at the speed of thought and helped; therefore honour on earth came to the whole company of Śyena birds.

ऋजीषी श्येनो ददमानो अंशुं परावतः शकुनो मंद्रं मदं । सोमं भरद्दादृहाणो देवानान्दिवो अमुष्मादुत्तरादादाय ॥ (*ṛjīṣī śyeno dadamāno aṃśuṃ parāvataḥ śakuno maṃdraṃ madaṃ | somaṃ bharaddādṛhāṇo devānāndivo amuṣmāduttarādādāya ‖*)
This bird, flying straight through the sky at the speed of thought and followed by the gods, brought the Soma and with it increased resolve and faith. By bringing the Soma it did good to the world.

आदाय श्येनो आभरत्सोमं सहस्रं सना आयुतं च साकं । अत्रा पुरंधिरजहादरातीर्मदे सोमस्य मूरा अमूरः ॥ (*ādāya śyeno ābharatsomaṃ sahasraṃ sanā āyutaṃ ca sākaṃ | atrā puraṃdhirajahādarātīrmade somasya mūrā amūraḥ ‖*)
The Śyena bird brought the Soma from the heavenly world and helped in carrying out thousands of sacrifices. Indra, satisfied by drinking this Soma, grew in valour and crushed all his enemies.

अव यच्छेनो अस्वनीदथ द्योर्वि यद्यदि वात ऊहुः पुरंधिं । सृजद्यदस्मा अव ह क्षिपज्ज्यां कृशानुरस्ता मनसा भुरण्यन् ॥ (*ava yaccheno asvanīdatha dyorvi yadyadi vāta ūhuḥ puraṃdhiṃ | sṛjadyadasmā ava ha kṣipajjyāṃ kṛśānurastā manasā bhuraṇyan ‖*)

After bringing the Soma, as the Śyena was coming down from the sky expressing its joy, Kṛśānu, one of the Soma-guardians and an archer, also came down at the speed of thought, chased it, and shot an arrow at it from his bow.

यजिष्य ईमिंद्रावतो न भुज्युं श्येनो जभार बृहतो अधि ष्ठोः । अंतः पतत्पतत्र्यस्य पर्णमध यामनि प्रसितस्य तद्वेः ॥ (*yajiṣya īmiṃdrāvato na bhujyuṃ śyeno jabhāra bṛhato adhi ṣṭhoḥ | aṃtaḥ patatpatatryasya parṇamadha yāmani prasitasya tadveḥ ‖*)
As this Śyena was coming down from the sky that lies under Indra's lordship, it was struck by Kṛśānu's arrow, and in its struggle it lost a feather from its body and was wounded.

While the story is of this kind, finding what principle lies here costs effort. Even so, introducing the seer of this sūkta, Nāmadeva ⟨NOTE:259⟩, the Aitareya Āraṇyaka explains this same occasion from the standpoint of principle. There, quoting the Ṛk of the Ṛk Saṃhitā

गर्भे नु सन्नन्वेषामवेदमहं देवानां जनिमानि विश्वा । शतं मा पुर आयसीररक्षन्नध श्येनो जवसा निरदीयं ॥ (*garbhe nu sannanveṣāmavedamahaṃ devānāṃ janimāni viśvā | śataṃ mā pura āyasīrarakṣannadha śyeno javasā niradīyaṃ ‖*)

it says गर्भ एव एतच्छयानो वामदेव एवमुवाच (*garbha eva etacchayāno vāmadeva evamuvāca*) (Ai. Ā. 2-5). It says that Vāmadeva, while still lying in the womb, knew this principle and spoke it. The meaning of the above mantra is that the origins and natures of all the gods were revealed to Vāmadeva while he was in the womb, and that, although there was a bondage made of hundreds of iron bars, he slipped out of it like a Śyena bird and flew towards the earth. The purport of this passage is not easy. Śaṅkarācārya, Ānandatīrtha and Sāyaṇa, when they explain this occasion, take the purport to be that Vāmadeva entered hundreds of bodies as bonds, finally became a knower, was freed from them and attained liberation. But if the context of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka is examined, स एवं विद्वान् आस्माच्छरीरभेदादूर्ध्व उत्क्रम्यामुष्मिन् स्वर्गे लोके सर्वान्नामानाप्तामृतः समभवत्समभवत् । (*sa evaṃ vidvān āsmāccharīrabhedādūrdhva utkramyāmuṣmin svarge loke sarvānnāmānāptāmṛtaḥ samabhavatsamabhavat |*) (Ai. Ā. 2-5): it says that Vāmadeva, who knew this principle while in the womb, gave up the earthly body and attained liberation. It is therefore understood that the words of Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-27-1 apply to Vāmadeva himself ⟨NOTE:260⟩. Moreover, on the basis of the statement that in mantras such as 1-32-14 and 10-99-8 Indra is described as like the Śyena bird, some scholars hold that the mantra beginning "Garbhe nu …." (printed with abridgement dots)
refers to Indra himself. But that is wrong. Some others have said that it is the speech of Soma (Ludwig).
**2. The Gāyatrī in the form of a bird is the Śyena.**
श्येनभावं समास्थाय गर्भाद्योगेन निस्सृतः । ऋषिगर्भे शयानःसन् ब्रूते गर्भे नु सन्निति ॥ (*śyenabhāvaṃ samāsthāya garbhādyogena nissṛtaḥ | ṛṣigarbhe śayānaḥsan brūte garbhe nu sanniti ‖*)

that Vāmadeva himself, freed from the womb by the greatness of his yoga, utters this sentence. None of the English critics such as Ludwig has examined the reason and the basis for the Śyena being described in the form of the Gāyatrī. In describing this same occasion, the Śyena is called by the word Suparṇa and also by the word Gāyatrī. In some places, when explaining the word Śyena, Sāyaṇa explains it as शैनः शंसनीयगतिमान्पक्षि पक्ष्याकारा गायत्री (*śainaḥ śaṃsanīyagatimānpakṣi pakṣyākārā gāyatrī*). Since different words, Śyena, Suparṇa and Gāyatrī, are used in these contexts, a precise meaning cannot be stated here without knowing the narrative. So, after knowing this story as told in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, one can examine what the principle is in the matter of the Gāyatrī bringing the Soma.
**3. The incidental story of Kadrū and Suparṇī. The sons of Suparṇī are the metres.**
In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā this story is described as follows:

कद्रूश्च वै सुपर्णी चात्मरूपयोरस्पर्देताग्ं सा कद्रूस्सुपर्णीमजयताब्रवीत्तृतीयस्यामितो दिवि सोमस्तमाहर तेनात्मानं निष्क्रीणीष्टेतीयं वै कद्रूरसौ सुपर्णी छंदागांसि सौपर्णेयास्साब्रवीदस्मै वै पितरा पुत्रान् बिभृतस्तृतीयस्यामितो दिवि सोमस्तमाहर तेना - त्मानं निष्क्रीणीष्टेति मा कद्रूरवोचदिति जगत्युदपतच्चतुर्दशाक्षरा सती साप्राप्य न्यवर्तत तस्यै द्वे (*kadrūśca vai suparṇī cātmarūpayoraspardetāgṃ sā kadrūssuparṇīmajayatābravīttṛtīyasyāmito divi somastamāhara tenātmānaṃ niṣkrīṇīṣṭetīyaṃ vai kadrūrasau suparṇī chaṃdāgāṃsi sauparṇeyāssābravīdasmai vai pitarā putrān bibhṛtastṛtīyasyāmito divi somastamāhara tenā - tmānaṃ niṣkrīṇīṣṭeti mā kadrūravocaditi jagatyudapataccaturdaśākṣarā satī sāprāpya nyavartata tasyai dve*)

अक्षरे अमीयेताग्ं सा दक्षिणाभिश्च तपसा चागच्छत्तस्मात्रिष्टुभो लोके माध्यंदिने सवने दक्षिणा नीयंत एतत्खलु वाव तप इत्याहुर्यस्स्वं ददातीति गायत्र्युदपतच्चतुरक्षरा सत्यजया ज्योतिषा तमस्या अजाभ्यरुंध तदजाया अजत्वग्ं सा सोमं चाहरच्चत्कारि चाक्षराणि साष्टाक्षरा समपद्यत ब्रह्मवादिनो वदंति कस्मात्सत्याद्गायत्री कनिष्ठा छंदसाग्ं सती यज्ञमुखं परीयायेति यदेवादसोममाहरत्तस्माद्यज्ञमुखं परैत्तस्मात्तेजस्विनीतमा पद्भां द्वे सवने समग्रह्ञान्मुखेनैकं यन्नुखेन समगृह्णात्तदधयत्तस्माद्वे सवने शुक्रवशी प्रातस्सवनं च माध्यंदिनं च तस्मात्तृतीयसवन ऋजीषमभिषुण्वंति धीतमिव हि मन्यंते । (*akṣare amīyetāgṃ sā dakṣiṇābhiśca tapasā cāgacchattasmātriṣṭubho loke mādhyaṃdine savane dakṣiṇā nīyaṃta etatkhalu vāva tapa ityāhuryassvaṃ dadātīti gāyatryudapataccaturakṣarā satyajayā jyotiṣā tamasyā ajābhyaruṃdha tadajāyā ajatvagṃ sā somaṃ cāharaccatkāri cākṣarāṇi sāṣṭākṣarā samapadyata brahmavādino vadaṃti kasmātsatyādgāyatrī kaniṣṭhā chaṃdasāgṃ satī yajñamukhaṃ parīyāyeti yadevādasomamāharattasmādyajñamukhaṃ paraittasmāttejasvinītamā padbhāṃ dve savane samagrahñānmukhenaikaṃ yannukhena samagṛhṇāttadadhayattasmādve savane śukravaśī prātassavanaṃ ca mādhyaṃdinaṃ ca tasmāttṛtīyasavana ṛjīṣamabhiṣuṇvaṃti dhītamiva hi manyaṃte |*)

Kadrū and Suparṇī, the two of them, came to compete as to which of them was superior in her form. Kadrū won, defeated Suparṇī and kept her in her power. Then she gave the defeated Suparṇī this assurance: "In the third part of heaven there is Soma. Bring it, and you can obtain your release." Kadrū is this earth; Suparṇī is the sky. The metres are the offspring of Suparṇī. Kadrū told Suparṇī: "With the help of the children who are nourished for the service of their mother, bring me the Soma and obtain your freedom." In the same way Suparṇī too told her children of this occasion. Then the Jagatī, of fourteen syllables, flew up to the sky. But it could not get the Soma and turned back. It lost two syllables of the fourteen, and came back with the sacrificial animals. For this very reason the Jagatī metre is rich in the wealth of animals, and a man rich in animals is fit to be consecrated. Then the Triṣṭubh metre, of thirteen syllables, flew up to the sky. It too lost two syllables and did not obtain the Soma. But when it came back, it returned with the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) useful for the sacrifice and with the materials of austerity. Therefore in worldly practice the dakṣiṇā is offered at the midday pressing. One who gives away his wealth as a gift, that is called the act of austerity. Next the Gāyatrī, of four syllables, set out towards the sky together with an Aja (goat) in the form of light. That Aja made the Soma available to the Gāyatrī. Then, as the Gāyatrī came back taking the Soma, since it brought back with it the four syllables that the Triṣṭubh and the Jagatī had left behind there, these four syllables joined the four that it had before, and in all it became eight-syllabled. Thus, although it is the smallest of all the metres, because it brought the Soma, which is so important for the sacrifice, it holds a very prominent place in the sacrificial work; this is the view of the Brahmavādins. For that very reason it is the most brilliant of all the metres. That (the Gāyatrī in the form of a bird) with both feet

…it brought two savanas, the Prātaḥ and the Mādhyandina, and one from the mouth. The savana brought from the mouth it drank. For this reason the morning savana and the midday savana are accompanied by pure (white) Soma, while the third savana is accompanied by ṛjīṣa (the pressed-out residue). This is the order stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa this account is somewhat different. It is told in two passages. First:

सोमो वै राजा गंधर्वेष्वासीत्तं देवाश्च ऋषयश्चाभ्यध्यायन्कथमयमस्मान्सोमो राजागच्छेदिति सा वागब्रवीत् स्त्रीकामा वै गंधर्वा मयैव स्त्रीया भूतया पणध्वमिति नेति देवा अब्रुवन्नथं वयं त्वदृते स्यामेति साब्रवीत्क्रीणीतैव यर्हि वाव वो मयार्थो भविता तर्ह्येव वोऽहं पुनरागंतास्मीति तथेति तया महानग्न्या भूतया सोमं राजानमक्रीणन्. (*somo vai rājā gaṃdharveṣvāsīttaṃ devāśca ṛṣayaścābhyadhyāyankathamayamasmānsomo rājāgacchediti sā vāgabravīt strīkāmā vai gaṃdharvā mayaiva strīyā bhūtayā paṇadhvamiti neti devā abruvannathaṃ vayaṃ tvadṛte syāmeti sābravītkrīṇītaiva yarhi vāva vo mayārtho bhavitā tarhyeva vo 'haṃ punarāgaṃtāsmīti tatheti tayā mahānagnyā bhūtayā somaṃ rājānamakrīṇan.*) (Ai. Brā. 5-2)

While King Soma was living among the Gandharvas, the gods and the ṛṣis, wishing to obtain him, fell to meditating on him. While they were pondering the way to obtain him, the goddess Vāk came before them and said: "The Gandharvas are fond of women. Send me; I shall bring Soma and hand him over to you." The gods said: "We cannot be without you. That will not do." Then Vāk said: "For the present send me and obtain Soma. Afterwards, as soon as you wish for me, I shall come to you." After she had given this assurance, they obtained Soma with her help. So it is said. The same occasion is told elsewhere in this manner.
**4. The efforts of the metres to fetch Soma, and their defeat.**

सोमो वै राजामुष्मिलोक आसीत्तं देवाश्च ऋषयश्चाभ्यध्यायन्कथमयमस्मान्सोमो राजागच्छेदिति तेऽब्रुवंशद्वासि यूयं न इमं सोमं राजानमाहरतेति तथेति ते सुपर्णा भूत्वोदपतंस्ते यत्सुपर्णा भूत्वोदपतंस्तदेतत् सौपर्णमित्याख्यानविद आचक्षते । छंदांसि नै तत्सोमं राजानमच्छाचरंस्तानि ह तर्हि चतुरक्षराणि चतुरक्षराण्येव छंदांस्यासन् सा जगती चतुरक्षरा प्रथमोदपतत्सा पतित्वार्धमध्वनो गत्वाश्राम्यता परास्य त्रीण्यक्षराण्येकाक्षरा भूत्वा दीक्षां च तपश्च हरंती पुनरभ्यवापतत्तस्मात्तस्य वित्ता दीक्षा वित्तं तपो यस्य पशवः संति जागता हि पशवो जगती हि तानादरदथ त्रिष्टुबुदपतता (*somo vai rājāmuṣmiloka āsīttaṃ devāśca ṛṣayaścābhyadhyāyankathamayamasmānsomo rājāgacchediti te 'bruvaṃśadvāsi yūyaṃ na imaṃ somaṃ rājānamāharateti tatheti te suparṇā bhūtvodapataṃste yatsuparṇā bhūtvodapataṃstadetat sauparṇamityākhyānavida ācakṣate | chaṃdāṃsi nai tatsomaṃ rājānamacchācaraṃstāni ha tarhi caturakṣarāṇi caturakṣarāṇyeva chaṃdāṃsyāsan sā jagatī caturakṣarā prathamodapatatsā patitvārdhamadhvano gatvāśrāmyatā parāsya trīṇyakṣarāṇyekākṣarā bhūtvā dīkṣāṃ ca tapaśca haraṃtī punarabhyavāpatattasmāttasya vittā dīkṣā vittaṃ tapo yasya paśavaḥ saṃti jāgatā hi paśavo jagatī hi tānādaradatha triṣṭubudapatatā*) …

…पतित्वा भूयोऽर्धादध्वनो गत्वाश्राम्यता परास्यैकमक्षरं त्रैक्षरा भूत्वा दक्षिणा हरंती पुनरभ्यवापतत्तस्मान्माध्यंदिने दक्षिणा नीयंते त्रिष्टुभो लोके त्रिष्टुब्बि ता आहरत् । (*patitvā bhūyo 'rdhādadhvano gatvāśrāmyatā parāsyaikamakṣaraṃ traikṣarā bhūtvā dakṣiṇā haraṃtī punarabhyavāpatattasmānmādhyaṃdine dakṣiṇā nīyaṃte triṣṭubho loke triṣṭubbi tā āharat |*) (Ai. Brā. 13-25)
(The same closing line stands printed twice.)

The gods thought for a long time how the Soma that was in the atmosphere could be obtained; then they approached the metres and begged: "Bring us the Soma of the atmosphere." Giving the assurance "So be it," they took the form of birds and flew up into the atmosphere. Because they were transformed into the form of suparṇas (birds) and flew to fetch Soma, this episode became famous as the Suparṇa legend. When those metres in bird form flew toward Soma, each of them consisted of only four syllables. The four-syllabled Jagatī, flying first into the atmosphere, tired out in the middle of the way. Leaving three of her syllables there, she returned with only the remaining one syllable. But on coming back she brought the dīkṣā (consecration) and tapas (austerity). Because Jagatī is closely related to wealth in cattle, one who has wealth in cattle obtains faith and the power of austerity. Then Triṣṭubh also, having passed the middle of the way, grew tired after going only a little further. Leaving only one of her syllables there, she returned with the other three. On coming back she brought the dakṣiṇā, the requisite of the sacrifice. Therefore, at the time of the Mādhyandina savana, the dakṣiṇā has preference.

ते देवा अब्रुवन्गायत्रीं त्वं न इमं सोमं राजानमाहरेति सा तथे त्यब्रवीत्तां वै मा सर्वेण स्वस्त्ययनेनानुमंत्रयध्वमिति तथेति सोदपतत्तां देवाः सर्वेण स्वस्त्ययनेनान्वमंत्रयुत प्रेति चेति चेत्येतद्वै सर्वं स्वस्त्ययनं यत्प्रीति चेति चेति तद्योऽस्य प्रियः स्यात्तमेतेनानुमंत्रयेत प्रेति चेति तद्योऽस्य प्रियः स्यात्तमेतेनानुमंत्रयेत प्रेति चेति चेति स्वस्तेव गच्छति स्वस्ति पुनरागच्छति सा पतित्वा सोमपालान् भीषयित्वा पद्भ्यां च मुखेन च सोमं राजानं समगृभ्नाड्यानि चेतरे छंदसी अक्षराण्यजहितां तानि चोपसमगृभ्णात्तस्या अनु विसृज्य कृशानुः सोमपालः सव्यस्य पदो नखमच्चिदत्तच्छल्यकोऽभवत्तस्मात्सनखमिव यद्वशमस्रवत्सा वशाभवत्तस्मात्सा हविरिवाध यः शल्यो यदनीकमासीत्स सर्पो निर्दंश्यभवत्सहसस्सजो यानि पर्णानि ते मंथावला यानि स्नावानि ते गंडूपदा यत्तेजनं सोऽंधाहिः सो सा तथेषुरभवत् । (*te devā abruvangāyatrīṃ tvaṃ na imaṃ somaṃ rājānamāhareti sā tathe tyabravīttāṃ vai mā sarveṇa svastyayanenānumaṃtrayadhvamiti tatheti sodapatattāṃ devāḥ sarveṇa svastyayanenānvamaṃtrayuta preti ceti cetyetadvai sarvaṃ svastyayanaṃ yatprīti ceti ceti tadyo 'sya priyaḥ syāttametenānumaṃtrayeta preti ceti tadyo 'sya priyaḥ syāttametenānumaṃtrayeta preti ceti ceti svasteva gacchati svasti punarāgacchati sā patitvā somapālān bhīṣayitvā padbhyāṃ ca mukhena ca somaṃ rājānaṃ samagṛbhnāḍyāni cetare chaṃdasī akṣarāṇyajahitāṃ tāni copasamagṛbhṇāttasyā anu visṛjya kṛśānuḥ somapālaḥ savyasya pado nakhamaccidattacchalyako 'bhavattasmātsanakhamiva yadvaśamasravatsā vaśābhavattasmātsā havirivādha yaḥ śalyo yadanīkamāsītsa sarpo nirdaṃśyabhavatsahasassajo yāni parṇāni te maṃthāvalā yāni snāvāni te gaṃḍūpadā yattejanaṃ so 'ṃdhāhiḥ so sā tatheṣurabhavat |*) (Ai. Brā. 13-26)

Then the gods approached Gāyatrī and prayed: "Bring us King Soma." Gāyatrī agreed, saying "So be it," and said that the gods should follow her reciting a svastyayana (auspicious) mantra. The gods gladly accepted this and set out reciting the svastyayana mantra "pra" and "ā". Because by reciting this mantra the journey is accomplished without obstacle and the purpose is achieved, the gods recited it. Gāyatrī reached the region where Soma was without obstacle, took up Soma with her feet and her mouth, and also took the four syllables (3+1) that Triṣṭubh and Jagatī had left behind, and returned. But Kṛśānu, the guardian of Soma, cut off the nail of her left foot. It was transformed into a porcupine and became a śalya (quill). The blood that flowed from it became a barren cow, and the bone-frame became a serpent; but it did not come to spit poison and bite. In the same way the feather became the bat, and the sinew the earth-worm; thus the form of the arrow became such.
**6. The primacy of Gāyatrī in the times of the savanas.**

सा यद्दक्षिणेन पदा समगृभ्यात्तत्पातःसवनमभवत्तद्गायत्री स्वमायतनमकुरुत तस्मात्तत्समृद्धतमं मन्यंते सर्वॆषां सवनानामग्रियो मुख्यो भवति श्रेष्ठतामश्नुते य एवं वेदाथ यत्सव्येन पदा समगृभ्यात्तन्माध्यंदिनं सवनमभवत्तद्विस्स्रंसत तद्विस्स्रस्तं नान्वाप्पोत्तूर्वं सवनं ते देवाः प्राजिज्ञासंत तस्मिंस्किष्टुभं छंदसामदधुरिंद्रं देवतानां तेन तत्समावद्वीर्यमभवत्तूर्वेण सवनेनोभाभ्यां सवनाभ्यां समावद्वीर्याभ्यां समावज्जामाभ्यां राध्नोति य एवं वेदाथ यन्नुखेन समगृभ्यात्तृतीयसवनमभवत्तस्य पतंती रसमधयत्तद्धीतरसं नान्वाप्पोत्तूर्वे सवने ते देवाः प्राजिज्ञासंत तत्त्वशुष्पपश्यंस्तद्यदाशिरमवनयन्त्याज्येन पशुना चरंति तेन तत्समावद्वीर्यमभवत्तूर्वाभ्यां सवनाभ्यां सर्वैः सवनैः समावद्वीर्यैः समानाज्यामिभी राध्नोति य एवं वेद । (*sā yaddakṣiṇena padā samagṛbhyāttatpātaḥsavanamabhavattadgāyatrī svamāyatanamakuruta tasmāttatsamṛddhatamaṃ manyaṃte sarvèṣāṃ savanānāmagriyo mukhyo bhavati śreṣṭhatāmaśnute ya evaṃ vedātha yatsavyena padā samagṛbhyāttanmādhyaṃdinaṃ savanamabhavattadvissraṃsata tadvissrastaṃ nānvāppottūrvaṃ savanaṃ te devāḥ prājijñāsaṃta tasmiṃskiṣṭubhaṃ chaṃdasāmadadhuriṃdraṃ devatānāṃ tena tatsamāvadvīryamabhavattūrveṇa savanenobhābhyāṃ savanābhyāṃ samāvadvīryābhyāṃ samāvajjāmābhyāṃ rādhnoti ya evaṃ vedātha yannukhena samagṛbhyāttṛtīyasavanamabhavattasya pataṃtī rasamadhayattaddhītarasaṃ nānvāppottūrve savane te devāḥ prājijñāsaṃta tattvaśuṣpapaśyaṃstadyadāśiramavanayantyājyena paśunā caraṃti tena tatsamāvadvīryamabhavattūrvābhyāṃ savanābhyāṃ sarvaiḥ savanaiḥ samāvadvīryaiḥ samānājyāmibhī rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda |*) (Ai. Brā. 13-22)

The portion of Soma that Gāyatrī seized with her right foot became the Prātaḥsavana. This morning savana became Gāyatrī's own dwelling. Therefore the morning savana is regarded as the most prosperous of the savanas. One who knows this truth becomes foremost and chief among sacrificers. The portion of Soma that Gāyatrī seized with her left foot became the Mādhyandina savana. Because it slipped away, it did not obtain the excellence of the morning savana. The gods tried to remedy this deficiency, and placed in it Triṣṭubh among the metres and Indra among the deities…

…Thereafter it too obtained the vigour of the morning savana. The man who knows the equal strength and wealth of these two savanas prospers. The portion of Soma seized with the mouth became the third savana. While she was flying, the Śyena, in the form of Gāyatrī, drank it. Therefore it did not obtain the equality of strength of the first two savanas. The gods recognised that this deficiency must be remedied. They then looked for it among the animals, and then worshipped it with the āśira and the offering of ājya. Thereafter it too obtained the strength of the first two savanas. One who knows this truth prospers.
**7. The section on the division of the syllables of the metres.**

ते वा इमे इतरे छंदसी गायत्रीमभ्यवदेतां वित्तं नावक्षराण्यनुपर्यागुरिति नेत्यब्रवीद्गायत्री यथा वित्तमेव न इति ते देवेषु प्रश्नमैतां ते देवा अब्रुवन्यथावित्तमेव व इति तस्माद्याप्येतर्हि वित्तां व्याहुरथा वित्तमेव न इति ततो वा अष्टाक्षरा गायत्र्यभवत्र्यक्षरा त्रिष्टुबेकाक्षरा जगती साष्टाक्षरा गायत्री प्रातःसवनमुदयच्छन्नाशक्कोत्रिष्टुप् त्रक्षरा माध्यंदिनं समनमुद्यंतुं तां गायत्र्यब्रवीदायान्यपि मेऽत्रास्त्विति सा तथेत्यब्रवीत् त्रिष्टुप् तां वै मैत्रैरष्टाभिरक्षरैरुपसंधेहीति तथेति .... सा द्वादशाक्षरा भूत्वा तृतीयसवनमुदयच्छत्ततो वा अष्टाक्षरा गायत्र्यभवदेकादशाक्षरा त्रिष्टुब् द्वादशाक्षरा जगती सर्वॆश्चंदोभिः समावद्वीर्यैः समावज्ञामिभी राध्योति य एवं वेद ॥ (*te vā ime itare chaṃdasī gāyatrīmabhyavadetāṃ vittaṃ nāvakṣarāṇyanuparyāguriti netyabravīdgāyatrī yathā vittameva na iti te deveṣu praśnamaitāṃ te devā abruvanyathāvittameva va iti tasmādyāpyetarhi vittāṃ vyāhurathā vittameva na iti tato vā aṣṭākṣarā gāyatryabhavatryakṣarā triṣṭubekākṣarā jagatī sāṣṭākṣarā gāyatrī prātaḥsavanamudayacchannāśakkotriṣṭup trakṣarā mādhyaṃdinaṃ samanamudyaṃtuṃ tāṃ gāyatryabravīdāyānyapi me 'trāstviti sā tathetyabravīt triṣṭup tāṃ vai maitrairaṣṭābhirakṣarairupasaṃdhehīti tatheti .... sā dvādaśākṣarā bhūtvā tṛtīyasavanamudayacchattato vā aṣṭākṣarā gāyatryabhavadekādaśākṣarā triṣṭub dvādaśākṣarā jagatī sarvèścaṃdobhiḥ samāvadvīryaiḥ samāvajñāmibhī rādhyoti ya evaṃ veda ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 13-28)

After Gāyatrī had returned with the three syllables of Triṣṭubh and the one syllable of Jagatī, those two approached her and begged: "The syllables, our wealth, have come along with you. Give them back." Gāyatrī replied: "No, they are not yours; since I brought them, they have become mine." Then the two approached the gods and told their complaint. The gods took Gāyatrī's side: "Since you brought them, those four syllables have become yours. Just as in worldly dealings it is the custom that whatever property we have obtained becomes ours, so you have the right to take them as your own." Then Gāyatrī became eight-syllabled, Triṣṭubh three-syllabled, and Jagatī one-syllabled. Then Gāyatrī with her eight syllables became able to take part in the morning savana.

But Triṣṭubh, with her three syllables, could not take part in the Mādhyandina savana. Then Gāyatrī said: "I too shall take part in the Mādhyandina savana; let me too have a share of the sacrifice there." Triṣṭubh said: "So be it; join me with your eight syllables." Together, as eleven-syllabled, she became helpful to the Mādhyandina savana. Jagatī, being one-syllabled, was unable to carry out the third savana. Then Gāyatrī again asked that she join her and that she too have a share in the third savana. Jagatī agreed, "So be it," and Gāyatrī joined her at the time of the third savana. Then, as twelve-syllabled, she became helpful to the third savana. Then Gāyatrī became eight-syllabled, Triṣṭubh eleven-syllabled, and Jagatī twelve-syllabled. One who knows this truth obtains all wealth through the grace of these metres, which possess equal strength and splendour. Thus there is praise of Gāyatrī.
**1. The identity of Agni, Gāyatrī and Śyena; their place in the times of the savanas.**
In this way the story of the identity of this Gāyatrī with the Śyena is told in many places. Likewise in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa:

स वै खलु बर्हिः प्रथमं यजति । तद्वै कनिष्ठछंदः सद्गायत्री प्रथमा छंदसां युज्यते (*sa vai khalu barhiḥ prathamaṃ yajati | tadvai kaniṣṭhachaṃdaḥ sadgāyatrī prathamā chaṃdasāṃ yujyate*) (Śa. Brā 1-8-2-10)

Although she is the lowest of all the metres, Gāyatrī by her own greatness carried off Soma from the atmosphere. This was possible only through her own inner power. By this power she transformed herself into the Śyena and accomplished that task. For that reason the gods also showed her the first honour and revered her.

श्येनाय त्वा सोमभृते विष्णवेत्वति । तद्दायत्रीमन्वाभजति सा यद्दायत्री श्येन्नो भूत्वा दिवः सोममाभरत् ॥ (*śyenāya tvā somabhṛte viṣṇavetvati | taddāyatrīmanvābhajati sā yaddāyatrī śyenno bhūtvā divaḥ somamābharat ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 3-4-1-12)

Because Gāyatrī, in the form of the Śyena, carried off Soma from the atmosphere, the offering is addressed to the Śyena, the Soma-bearer, who has the nature of Viṣṇu; thus hospitality is offered to Gāyatrī. And so on.
Since this is said in many places of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa — 3-9-4-10; 4-3-2-7; 1-7-1-1; 11-7-2 8 and others — one point must be noted.⟨NOTE:261⟩

श्येनाय त्वा सोमभृत इति । तद्गायत्रै मिमितेऽग्नये त्वा रायस्पोषद इत्यग्निर्वै गायत्री तद्गायत्रै मिमिते स यद्गायत्री श्येनो भूत्वा । (*śyenāya tvā somabhṛta iti | tadgāyatrai mimite 'gnaye tvā rāyaspoṣada ityagnirvai gāyatrī tadgāyatrai mimite sa yadgāyatrī śyeno bhūtvā |*) …. (Śa. Brā 3-9-4-10)

Thus identity is stated among Gāyatrī, Śyena and Agni. This unity of Agni and Gāyatrī, in which Gāyatrī, being of the nature of Agni, fetched Soma in the form of the Śyena, is supported also by the passages of the Ṛk Saṃhitā:

अग्नेर्गायत्र्यभवत् सयुग्योष्ठिहया सविता सं बभूव । अनुष्टुभा सोम उक्थैर्महस्वान् बृहस्पतेर्बृहती वाचमावत् ॥ (*agnergāyatryabhavat sayugyoṣṭhihayā savitā saṃ babhūva | anuṣṭubhā soma ukthairmahasvān bṛhaspaterbṛhatī vācamāvat ‖*) (18-130-4)⟨NOTE:262⟩

Here it is stated that Gāyatrī, closely related to Agni, became Agni's helper. The same is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā: निरमिमीत तमग्निर्देवतान्नसृज्यत गायत्रि छंदः (*niramimīta tamagnirdevatānnasṛjyata gāyatri chaṃdaḥ*) (7-1-1-4). Not mere close relation only: there are abundant authorities such as गायत्रि वा अग्निः (*gāyatri vā agniḥ*); गायत्रोऽग्निः (*gāyatro 'gniḥ*); अग्निर्वै गायत्रि (*agnirvai gāyatri*); गायत्रमग्नेश्छंदः (*gāyatramagneśchaṃdaḥ*) (Śa. Brā. 6-1-3-19; Tai. Brā. 1-1-5-3; Tai. Saṃ. 2 2-5-5 and others)⟨NOTE:263⟩. In all these identity is stated. Moreover, Agni and Gāyatrī are both deities connected with the morning savana. Stating this, the Nirukta says:

तिस्र एव देवताः इत्युक्तं पुरस्तात् तासां भक्तिसाहचर्यं व्याख्यानस्यामः । अथैतान्यग्निभक्तान्ययं लोकः प्रातःसवनं वसंतो गायत्री । (*tisra eva devatāḥ ityuktaṃ purastāt tāsāṃ bhaktisāhacaryaṃ vyākhyānasyāmaḥ | athaitānyagnibhaktānyayaṃ lokaḥ prātaḥsavanaṃ vasaṃto gāyatrī |*) (Ni. 7-8)

Earlier, when speaking of the deities, it was stated that three deities are the chief ones and all the others are their special manifestations. Among them, as to Agni's association and who share in the sacrifice: this earth, the morning savana, spring, Gāyatrī and so on; thus the unity of Agni, Gāyatrī and the morning savana is stated. The Maitrī Upaniṣad too states the same matter:
अग्निर्गायत्रं त्रिवृद्रथंतरं वसंतः प्राणो नक्षत्राणि वसवः । (*agnirgāyatraṃ trivṛdrathaṃtaraṃ vasaṃtaḥ prāṇo nakṣatrāṇi vasavaḥ |*) (Mai. U. 7-1)
अग्ने जुषस्व नो हविः पुरोळाशं जातवेदः । प्रातःसावे धियावसो ॥ (*agne juṣasva no haviḥ puroḷāśaṃ jātavedaḥ | prātaḥsāve dhiyāvaso ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-28-1)

The Agni-hymn (आग्नेयं हि प्रातः सवनं (*āgneyaṃ hi prātaḥ savanaṃ*) Śa. Brā. 3-4-9-12) and भूरग्निर्ज्योतिरग्निरिति (*bhūragnirjyotiragniriti*) and what follows (Ai. Brā. 2-32): in this way the direct connection between the morning pressing and Agni is well known from the Śruti. Further: वसवस्तर्हग्निः। तस्मिन् यस्य तथाविधे जुह्वति।वसुष्टेवास्याग्निहोत्रग्ं हुतं भवति । (*vasavastarhagniḥ| tasmin yasya tathāvidhe juhvati|vasuṣṭevāsyāgnihotragṃ hutaṃ bhavati |*) (Tai. Brā. 2-1-10-1). Having thus stated the identity of Agni and the Vasus, it praises the matter by saying that an oblation offered in Agni is as if offered to the Vasus. For this very reason the deity who takes part in the morning pressing along with the Gāyatrī is indicated in some places as Agni and in others as the Vasus.

चतुर्विंशत्यक्षरा गायत्री गायत्रं प्रातःसवनं तदस्य वसवोऽन्वायत्ताः प्राणा एव वसव एते हीदं सर्वं वासयंति । ( (*caturviṃśatyakṣarā gāyatrī gāyatraṃ prātaḥsavanaṃ tadasya vasavo 'nvāyattāḥ prāṇā eva vasava ete hīdaṃ sarvaṃ vāsayaṃti | (*) (Bhā. 81, 3-6-1) ⟨NOTE:264⟩

The morning pressing is offered together with the Gāyatrī mantra (metre) of twenty-four syllables; the Vasus are those entitled to this share of the sacrifice. In the context of stating in this way the direct connection of Agni and the Gāyatrī, what is relevant for us is to examine whether these three, Agni, Śyena and Gāyatrī, all indicate one identity, or are different principles.
नवं नु स्तोममग्नये दिवः श्वेनाय जीजनं । वस्वः कुविद्वनाति नः ॥ (*navaṃ nu stomamagnaye divaḥ śvenāya jījanaṃ | vasvaḥ kuvidvanāti naḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-15-4)

Here Agni is designated as the Śyena of the heaven-world. The same sentence is cited in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa (Tai. Brā. 2-4-8-1). The words दिवः शैनः (*divaḥ śainaḥ*) are used in the Ṛk-Saṃhitā, besides the mantra cited above, in two Ṛks, 7-56-3 and 10-92-6; but in those passages the word Śyena tells the nature of the Marut deities. If, however, Agni is regarded as belonging to lightning, then this word Śyena can apply to Agni also; this conclusion can be drawn on the strength of sentences such as वैश्वानरो यदि वा वैद्युतोऽसि (*vaiśvānaro yadi vā vaidyuto 'si*) (Tai. Brā. 3-10-5). In the Ṛk-Saṃhitā too support for this conclusion is found: गर्भे मातुः ऒतुष्टिता विदिद्युतानो अक्षरे (*garbhe mātuḥ òtuṣṭitā vididyutāno akṣare*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16 35) ⟨NOTE:265⟩. The Gāyatrī, which has Agni as her food or accompaniment, is likewise described with the epithet विदिद्युदती (*vididyudatī*) (Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa 12-1-) ⟨NOTE:266⟩. The commentator, explaining this Brāhmaṇa sentence, says: गायत्री च अग्निना सरोत्पत्तेस्तेजोरूपत्वात् दीप्यमाना भवति । अतः .... .... गायत्री एवोपस्थाते ॥ (*gāyatrī ca agninā sarotpattestejorūpatvāt dīpyamānā bhavati | ataḥ .... .... gāyatrī evopasthāte ‖*)

Since the Gāyatrī too was born together with Agni, the epithet विदिद्युदती (*vididyudatī*) that applies to Agni applies to the Gāyatrī as well. As in the sentence तेजो गायत्री (*tejo gāyatrī*) (Tai. Brā. 3-8-4), just as Agni is of the form of brilliance, the Gāyatrī too has the form of brilliance. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-3-8 and 10-95-10 also the word दविद्योत् (*davidyot*) is connected with the word विद्युत् (*vidyut*)

In the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, in the context of the Divaḥ-Śyena offering (3-12-1, 2), the mantra तुभ्यं ता अंगिरस्तम (*tubhyaṃ tā aṃgirastama*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-43-18) clearly points to Agni; and in the same context the mantra अश्याम तं काममग्ने (*aśyāma taṃ kāmamagne*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-5-7) also is addressed to Agni. Therefore there is no doubt that the epithet दिवःशैन (*divaḥśaina*) is a description of Agni. Further, is there a context in which the word सुपर्ण (*suparṇa*) too, just as it indicates the Śyena, indicates Agni? If so, what its meaning is must also be examined. Although this word Suparṇa is merely a synonym of "bird", in many places it has a hidden meaning. For example:
सुपर्णं विप्राः कवयो वचोभिरेकं संतं बहुधा कल्पयंति । (*suparṇaṃ viprāḥ kavayo vacobhirekaṃ saṃtaṃ bahudhā kalpayaṃti |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-114 5)

Here, according to Sāyaṇa, it is an epithet of the Supreme Self; he explains सुपर्णं सुपतनं एकं संतं परमात्मानं (*suparṇaṃ supatanaṃ ekaṃ saṃtaṃ paramātmānaṃ*). This meaning of the principle will have to be examined later. In the present context, where the word Suparṇa is used with reference to the Āditya or Agni, it is explained as "rays":
यत्रा सुपर्णा अमृतस्य भागमनिमेषं विदथाभिस्स्वरंति । (*yatrā suparṇā amṛtasya bhāgamanimeṣaṃ vidathābhissvaraṃti |*) (1-164-21)
यस्मिन्वृक्षे मध्वदः सुपर्णा निविशंते सुवते चाधिविश्वे ॥ (*yasminvṛkṣe madhvadaḥ suparṇā niviśaṃte suvate cādhiviśve ‖*) (1-164.22)

In such places, when the material meaning is given, they are called the rays of the Āditya. The word Suparṇa is also used as a synonym for Agni or the Āditya: दिव्यं सुपर्णं वायसं बृहंतमपां गर्भं दर्शतनोषधीनां । (*divyaṃ suparṇaṃ vāyasaṃ bṛhaṃtamapāṃ garbhaṃ darśatanoṣadhīnāṃ |*) (1-164-52); this description indicates Agni who dwells in the middle region. In the places दिवः श्येनः (*divaḥ śyenaḥ*) and दिव्यं सुपर्णं (*divyaṃ suparṇaṃ*) the identity of Agni and the Āditya is what is stated. Thus it is understood that Śyena, Suparṇa, Agni and Gāyatrī are all synonyms of one principle; but the technical meaning has to be explained according to each context.
9. Soma is the brilliance of the Āditya; the Gāyatrī is the chief means for knowing this.

In the present context, if the word Śyena is taken to mean Agni of the middle region or the Āditya, then the word Soma comes to mean the seed (retas) of that Āditya. That is, for the Supreme Brahman who is in the form of the Āditya also, Soma is present in the form of seed. This Soma is the seed that produces the creation of all beings.

अथ यत्किंचेदमार्द्रं तद्रेतसोऽसृजत तदु सोम एतवद्वा इदं सर्वमन्नं चैवान्नादश्च सोम एवान्नमग्निरन्नादः । (*atha yatkiṃcedamārdraṃ tadretaso 'sṛjata tadu soma etavadvā idaṃ sarvamannaṃ caivānnādaśca soma evānnamagnirannādaḥ |*) (Bṛ. U. 1-4-6)

The one Supreme Brahman created from his seed all the moist things in the world. That seed is Soma. This Soma, offered in Agni, becomes with it mutually food and eater. Explaining this very matter, the Maitrī Upaniṣad says:
रविमध्ये स्थितः सोमः सोममध्ये हुताशनः । (*ravimadhye sthitaḥ somaḥ somamadhye hutāśanaḥ |*) (Mai. U. 6-38) ⟨NOTE:267⟩
It states that Soma stands in the middle of the orb of the Āditya, and Agni in the middle of Soma. The relation between the Āditya and Soma is stated in many places of the Ṛk-Saṃhitā. For example:
महत्तत्सोमो महिषश्च कारापां यद्दर्भोऽवृणीत देवान् । (*mahattatsomo mahiṣaśca kārāpāṃ yaddarbho 'vṛṇīta devān |*)
आदधादिंद्रे पवमान ओजोऽजनयत्सूर्ये ज्योतिरिंदुः ॥ (*ādadhādiṃdre pavamāna ojo 'janayatsūrye jyotiriṃduḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-97-41)
Soma, the embryo of the waters that are in the Āditya, brought satisfaction to the gods; being in the form of virile power, it created in the Āditya the light of the universe. And:
त्वं समुद्रो आसि विश्ववित्कवे तवेमाः पंच प्रदिशो विधर्मणि । (*tvaṃ samudro āsi viśvavitkave tavemāḥ paṃca pradiśo vidharmaṇi |*)
त्वं द्यां च पृथिवीं चाति जभ्रिषे तव ज्योतींषि पवमान सूर्यः ॥ (*tvaṃ dyāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ cāti jabhriṣe tava jyotīṃṣi pavamāna sūryaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-86-29)

Here it is stated that Soma is the ocean of the middle region, the support of all light, and that the Āditya shines by Soma's power. Explaining what principle Soma reflects here, the scholar Eggeling has said as follows:

"The poet of 9-86-29 while saying ' Thou art the heavenly ocean (Samudra), thine are the lights (ज्योतींषि (*jyotīṃṣi*)) O Pavamana, thine the Sun ' seems to conceive Soma, as the bright ether, the azure ' Sea of light ' generally ". [Sacred Books of the East. Vol. XXVI. p. XV.]
Thus, on the basis of Śruti sentences, they hold that Soma is the luminous essence of the Āditya. The purport is that the nature of such brilliance is obtainable only with the help of the Gāyatrī.

Secondly, what is the place of the Gāyatrī in the story cited from the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa: सोमो वै राजा गंधर्वेष्वासीत्.... ....तया महानग्न्या भूतया सोमं राजानमक्रीणन् (*somo vai rājā gaṃdharveṣvāsīt.... ....tayā mahānagnyā bhūtayā somaṃ rājānamakrīṇan*) (Ai. Brā. 1-27)? There is no reason for the doubt that here the bringing of Soma was done by a woman in the form of Speech, and that the Gāyatrī has no connection with Soma. Here the word Gandharva must be taken to mean the Āditya, the word Soma the brilliance of the Āditya, and the word Vāk the Gāyatrī in the form of speech. If it is asked what is the authority for this, the Śruti sentences themselves are the authority.
10. The Gandharva who guarded the Soma, the brilliance of the Āditya, is Hiraṇyagarbha.
गंधर्व इत्था पदमस्य रक्षति पाति देवानां जनिमान्यद्भुतः । (*gaṃdharva itthā padamasya rakṣati pāti devānāṃ janimānyadbhutaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-83-4)

गंधर्वः उदकानां धारकः आदित्यः सोमस्य द्युसंबंधिस्थानं रक्षति । (*gaṃdharvaḥ udakānāṃ dhārakaḥ ādityaḥ somasya dyusaṃbaṃdhisthānaṃ rakṣati |*) The Āditya, the bearer of the waters, guards the dwelling-place of Soma. There is a praise of the Āditya saying that this Soma protects the gods. This same Gandharva is also designated as Hiraṇyagarbha. On the sentence पतंगो वाचं मनसा बिभर्ति तां गंधर्वोऽवदद्गर्भे अंतः (*pataṃgo vācaṃ manasā bibharti tāṃ gaṃdharvo 'vadadgarbhe aṃtaḥ*) (10-177-2) Sāyaṇa says: गर्भॆ हिरण्मये ब्रह्मांडेऽंतर्वर्तमानः गंधर्वः हिरण्यगर्भः तां वाचमवदत् । (*garbhè hiraṇmaye brahmāṃḍe 'ṃtarvartamānaḥ gaṃdharvaḥ hiraṇyagarbhaḥ tāṃ vācamavadat |*)

The Gandharva, of the form of Hiraṇyagarbha, who is within the Brahmāṇḍa, first uttered the Speech lodged in himself; afterwards the gods, seers of the end (of things), placed that Speech in the place of truth. Thus the relation between the Supreme Self, of the nature of the Āditya, and Speech is described. The story of the bringing of Soma told in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa tells of the relation between this Supreme Person, who is within the Āditya, and the principle of Speech, and afterwards how Soma, the brilliance of the Āditya, became the protector of the gods.
दिवि वै सोम आसीत् ।....गंधर्वो विश्वावसुः पर्यमुष्णात् ।....सोमो वै भ्राट् । (*divi vai soma āsīt |....gaṃdharvo viśvāvasuḥ paryamuṣṇāt |....somo vai bhrāṭ |*) (Śa. Brā. 3-2-4-4)

By these sentences the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa tells the story cited earlier from the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. Here too it tells the manner in which the Gāyatrī, in the form of speech, carried off the Soma; the manner in which this Soma, in the form of brilliance, was contained within the Gandharva in the form of the Āditya; and that afterwards this brilliance is obtained by the man who worships the goddess Speech. By sentences such as सोमो वै भ्राट् (*somo vai bhrāṭ*) Soma is described as brilliance itself. The meaning is that the brilliance of the nature of Soma, from the Gandharva in the form of the Āditya, becomes obtainable through the Gāyatrī, which is of the nature of speech, and by means of this Gāyatrī, to the man who performs the worship. Thus, with Śruti sentences as proofs, for the words Suparṇa, Soma, Gandharva,
Vāk and so on, the purport stated is not improper; this can be shown by citing it together with Sāyaṇa's commentary, and the explanation above can also be shown to be consistent.
चतुष्कपर्दा युवतिः सुपेशा धृतप्रतीका वयुनानि वस्ते । (*catuṣkapardā yuvatiḥ supeśā dhṛtapratīkā vayunāni vaste |*)
तस्यां सुपर्णा वृषणा नि षेदतुर्यत्र देवा दधिरे भागधेयं ॥ (*tasyāṃ suparṇā vṛṣaṇā ni ṣedaturyatra devā dadhire bhāgadheyaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-114-3)

Here, and in the following mantras of this same sūkta, Sāyaṇa gives two kinds of purport: one an explanation that tells a material principle, the other one that explains a spiritual principle. In this cited mantra the meaning is that the Suparṇas are established in Speech. The woman who has four braids (kaparda), namely noun, verb, preposition and particle, who is of ever-youthful form, of the nature of the shining Upaniṣad and the like, adorns herself with garments in the form of knowledge. In such a beautiful woman the individual self and the Supreme Self are established. The meaning is that the principle of light, described as of the nature of Suparṇa and Gandharva, can be realised only through the woman in the form of Speech. Sāyaṇa holds that this is what is described by योषित्कामा वै गंधर्वाः (*yoṣitkāmā vai gaṃdharvāḥ*) and the like (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa commentary 3-2-4-5).
सुपर्णं विप्राः कवयो वचोभिरेकं संतं बहुधा कल्पयंति । (*suparṇaṃ viprāḥ kavayo vacobhirekaṃ saṃtaṃ bahudhā kalpayaṃti |*)
छंदांसि च दधतो अध्वरेषु ग्रहान्त्सोमस्य मिमते द्वादश ॥ (*chaṃdāṃsi ca dadhato adhvareṣu grahāntsomasya mimate dvādaśa ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-114-2)

In Ṛks of this kind also the above view is what is explained. Stating the relation among the Supreme Self in the form of Suparṇa, the metres such as Gāyatrī, and Soma as the means of worship, the purport is that the nature of the Supreme Self can be known with the help of metres such as Gāyatrī and by the means in the form of Soma. In all such contexts there is a praise of the Gāyatrī, which possesses a special power either as the direct means of knowledge or as a supporter of the rite that is a means of knowledge.

It was stated earlier that the Ācārya says in the Śaṅkara-bhāṣya that the Gāyatrī is the most important means for realising the Supreme Brahman, and that the greatness of the Gāyatrī is known from three points. Of these, the first, namely the manner of the bringing of Soma and its purpose, and the purport of the statement that the Gāyatrī carried off Soma, has been stated along with proofs from Śruti sentences. Of the points stated by Śaṅkarācārya, the second must now be examined.
The distinctiveness of the Gāyatrī among the metres.

इतश्चंदोक्षराहरणेन.... अनेकेषु छंदस्सु गायत्रा एव ब्रह्मज्ञानद्वारतयोपादानं प्राधान्यं । (*itaścaṃdokṣarāharaṇena.... anekeṣu chaṃdassu gāyatrā eva brahmajñānadvāratayopādānaṃ prādhānyaṃ |*) ⟨NOTE:268⟩
The praise that the Gāyatrī is pre-eminent because it pervades all the other metres and has unified everything in itself is well known in the Śruti sentences themselves.

तद्वै कनिष्ठं छंदः सद्गायत्री प्रथमा छंदसां युज्यते तदु तद्विर्येणैव यच्छ्येनो भूत्वा दिवः सोममाभरत् । (*tadvai kaniṣṭhaṃ chaṃdaḥ sadgāyatrī prathamā chaṃdasāṃ yujyate tadu tadviryeṇaiva yacchyeno bhūtvā divaḥ somamābharat |*) (Śa. Brā. 1-6-2-10)

Although it is the smallest in form among all metres, the Gāyatrī holds the foremost place among all metres. The explanation that by its own power it was transformed into the form of the Śyena and brought the Soma has been given above. Moreover, it has been stated earlier, citing sentences of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, that it added its own eight syllables to the Triṣṭubh, which remained with three syllables, and made it of eleven syllables; and that the Jagatī, which remained with one syllable, joined with the Triṣṭubh united with the Gāyatrī and was made to become of twelve syllables (Ai. Brā. 13-28).
गायत्री कनिष्ठा छंदसागं सती यज्ञमुखं परीयाय । (*gāyatrī kaniṣṭhā chaṃdasāgaṃ satī yajñamukhaṃ parīyāya |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-6-3)
अधातः शिरः । तद्दायत्रीषु भवत्यग्रं वै छंदसां गायत्र्यग्रमंगानां शिरः । (*adhātaḥ śiraḥ | taddāyatrīṣu bhavatyagraṃ vai chaṃdasāṃ gāyatryagramaṃgānāṃ śiraḥ |*) (Ai. Ā. 1-4-1)

It is stated that just as the head is the chief of all the limbs of the body, so the Gāyatrī is the chief of all metres, and that afterwards the remaining metres were constructed on its basis. For this very reason गायत्री छंदसां माता (*gāyatrī chaṃdasāṃ mātā*) (Tai. U. 4-15-1) ⟨NOTE:269⟩: the Gāyatrī is praised as the mother of all metres. All the other metres are formed on the basis of this metre. In the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ai. Ā. 10-4-1) ⟨NOTE:270⟩ there is the explanation, for the Aitareya Āraṇyaka sentence छंदसां माता (*chaṃdasāṃ mātā*), that the other metres are constructed on its basis: इतरेषां छंदसामस्यॆव चतुश्चतुरक्षराधिक्येन तत्तच्छंदोभिः प्रतिमिवीते ॥ (*itareṣāṃ chaṃdasāmasyèva catuścaturakṣarādhikyena tattacchaṃdobhiḥ pratimivīte ‖*) How this is so: if the Gāyatrī metre has twenty-four syllables—

The purport is that, taking the Gāyatrī as the base, the Uṣṇik and the rest are formed by adding four syllables each time. Moreover, Agni is the chief of all sacrifices, and the Gāyatrī metre is a synonym of Agni, so it is the head of all (the metres).
. गायत्रं पुरस्ताद्गायति । अग्निर्वैगायत्रमग्निमेवास्यैतच्छिरः करोत्यथो शिरः ॥ ( (*. gāyatraṃ purastādgāyati | agnirvaigāyatramagnimevāsyaitacchiraḥ karotyatho śiraḥ ‖ (*) (Śa. Brā. 9-1-2-35)

शिरो वै यज्ञ स्यातिथ्यं सवाक्षरा वै गायत्री अष्टौ तानि यान्यन्वाह प्रणवो नवमः पूर्वार्धो वै यज्ञस्य गायत्री ॥ (*śiro vai yajña syātithyaṃ savākṣarā vai gāyatrī aṣṭau tāni yānyanvāha praṇavo navamaḥ pūrvārdho vai yajñasya gāyatrī ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 3-4-1-15)
The Gāyatrī consists of nine syllables. The praṇava is one; the other eight belong to the Gāyatrī that is its root form. The Gāyatrī is the chief of the whole sacrifice. Why? Because:
यो गायत्रीं हरिणीं ।.... यजमानग्ग् स्वर्गं लोकमभिवहंतीं । (*yo gāyatrīṃ hariṇīṃ |.... yajamānagg svargaṃ lokamabhivahaṃtīṃ |*) (Śa. Brā. 11-4-1-8)
Such a meritorious Gāyatrī is praised as carrying the sacrificer to heaven. Such is the power of the Gāyatrī.

Śaṅkarācārya has shown a third point to prove that the Gāyatrī plays the most important part in the sacrifice: सर्वसवनव्यापकत्वाच्छ यज्ञस्य प्राधान्यं गायत्र्याः (*sarvasavanavyāpakatvāccha yajñasya prādhānyaṃ gāyatryāḥ*). In these three rites too, the Prātaḥsavana, the Mādhyandinasavana and the Tṛtīyasavana, the help of the Gāyatrī is absolutely necessary for performing the prescribed work; this is known from Brāhmaṇa and other passages.

गायत्री वै प्रातःसवनं वहति । त्रिष्टुप्माध्यंदिनग्ंसवनं जगतीतृतीयसवनं तद्वा अनेकाकिन्येव त्रिष्टुप्माध्यंदिनग्ंसवनं वहति गायत्रा च बृहत्या चानेकाकिनी जगतीतृतीयसवनं गायत्रोष्ठिहककुभ्यामनुष्टुभा । गायत्रैवैकाकिनी प्रातःसवनं वहति । (*gāyatrī vai prātaḥsavanaṃ vahati | triṣṭupmādhyaṃdinagṃsavanaṃ jagatītṛtīyasavanaṃ tadvā anekākinyeva triṣṭupmādhyaṃdinagṃsavanaṃ vahati gāyatrā ca bṛhatyā cānekākinī jagatītṛtīyasavanaṃ gāyatroṣṭhihakakubhyāmanuṣṭubhā | gāyatraivaikākinī prātaḥsavanaṃ vahati |*) (Śa. Brā. 4-2-4-10)

The Gāyatrī carries the Prātaḥsavana, the Triṣṭup the Mādhyandinasavana, and the Jagatī the Tṛtīyasavana. But the Triṣṭup cannot carry the Mādhyandinasavana without the help of the Gāyatrī. Only when the Gāyatrī, joined with the Bṛhatī,

helps the Triṣṭup can it do so. In the same way the Jagatī too cannot carry the Tṛtīyasavana without the help of the Gāyatrī; it can do so only with the help of the Gāyatrī joined with the Kakubh and the Uṣṇik. But the Gāyatrī alone can carry the Prātaḥsavana without seeking the help of any other metre. Because the Gāyatrī pervades all the savanas, it has primacy in the sacrifice.

The question may be asked: although the Triṣṭup has eleven syllables, the Jagatī twelve and the Gāyatrī only eight, why does the Gāyatrī have this greatness? The answer: it was only through the power of the Gāyatrī that the Triṣṭup and the Jagatī came to have more syllables. This was shown above by citing passages of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. That the pervasion of all the savanas also came to the Gāyatrī through that distinction is shown in the Śatapatha too, as follows. Since the account differs somewhat in order, these passages are also cited.

चतुरक्षराणि ह वा आग्रे छंदाग्स्यासुः । ततो जगती सोममच्छापतत्सा श्रीण्यक्षराणि हित्वाजगाम ततस्त्रिष्टुप्सोममच्छापतत्सैकमक्षरग्ं हित्वाजगाम ततो गायत्री सोममच्छापतत्सैतानि चाक्षराणि हरदित्यागच्छत्सोमं च ततोऽष्टाक्षरा गायत्र्यभवत्तस्मादाहुरष्टाक्षरा गायत्री । (श. ब्रा. ४-३-२-७) पूर्वदल्लि छंदस्सुगळिगॆल्ला नाल्कु अक्षरगळु मात्रविद्दवु. सोमाहरणक्कागि जगतियु हारिदाग बळलि मूरु अक्षरगळन्नु दारियल्लि बिट्टु ऒंदक्षरदॊंदिगॆ मात्र हिंतिरुगितु. नंतर त्रिष्टुप्पु हारि ऒंदक्षरवन्नु बिट्टु हिंतुरिगितु. गायत्रियु स्वशक्तियिंद सोमवन्नु तरुवुदर जॊतॆगॆ अल्लि बिट्टु बंदिद्द नाल्कक्षरगळन्नू हिंदक्कॆ तंदितु. आदुदरिंद गायत्रियु अष्टाक्षरात्मक वागि अष्टाक्षरा गायत्री (*caturakṣarāṇi ha vā āgre chaṃdāgsyāsuḥ | tato jagatī somamacchāpatatsā śrīṇyakṣarāṇi hitvājagāma tatastriṣṭupsomamacchāpatatsaikamakṣaragṃ hitvājagāma tato gāyatrī somamacchāpatatsaitāni cākṣarāṇi haradityāgacchatsomaṃ ca tato 'ṣṭākṣarā gāyatryabhavattasmādāhuraṣṭākṣarā gāyatrī | (śa. brā. 4-3-2-7) pūrvadalli chaṃdassugaḷigèllā nālku akṣaragaḷu mātraviddavu. somāharaṇakkāgi jagatiyu hāridāga baḷali mūru akṣaragaḷannu dāriyalli biṭṭu òṃdakṣaradòṃdigè mātra hiṃtirugitu. naṃtara triṣṭuppu hāri òṃdakṣaravannu biṭṭu hiṃturigitu. gāyatriyu svaśaktiyiṃda somavannu taruvudara jòtègè alli biṭṭu baṃdidda nālkakṣaragaḷannū hiṃdakkè taṃditu. ādudariṃda gāyatriyu aṣṭākṣarātmaka vāgi aṣṭākṣarā gāyatrī*) (Śa. Brā. 4-3-2-7)

In the beginning all the metres had only four syllables. When the Jagatī flew to fetch the Soma, it grew tired, left three syllables on the way, and returned with only one. Then the Triṣṭup flew, left one syllable, and returned. The Gāyatrī, by its own power, brought the Soma and also brought back the four syllables left behind there. Therefore the Gāyatrī, being of eight syllables, became famous as "the eight-syllabled Gāyatrī".

तया प्रातःसवनमतन्वत । तस्माद्गायत्रं प्रातःसवनमतन्वत ताग्ंह त्रिष्टुबुवाचोप त्वाहमायानि त्रिभिरक्षरैरुप मा ह्वयस्व मा मा यज्ञादंतर्गा इति तथेति तामुपाह्वयत तत एकादशाक्षरा त्रिष्टुबभवत्तस्मादाहुस्त्रैष्णुभं माध्यंदिनग्ं सवनमिति ॥ (*tayā prātaḥsavanamatanvata | tasmādgāyatraṃ prātaḥsavanamatanvata tāgṃha triṣṭubuvācopa tvāhamāyāni tribhirakṣarairupa mā hvayasva mā mā yajñādaṃtargā iti tatheti tāmupāhvayata tata ekādaśākṣarā triṣṭubabhavattasmādāhustraiṣṇubhaṃ mādhyaṃdinagṃ savanamiti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 4-3-2-8)

They performed the Prātaḥsavana with the Gāyatrī of such distinction. Therefore the Prātaḥsavana belongs to the Gāyatrī. With the help of the same Gāyatrī they began to perform the Mādhyandinasavana also. Then the Triṣṭup came and begged the Gāyatrī: "I too shall take part with the three syllables left to me; do not leave me without a share in the sacrifice." The Gāyatrī agreed and gave it room too. Therefore the Triṣṭup metre, united with the Gāyatrī, came to have eleven syllables.

तय्यैव तृतीयसवनमतन्वत । ताग्ं ह जगत्युवाचोप त्वाहमायान्येकेनाक्षरेणोप मा ह्वयस्व मा मा यज्ञादंतर्गा इति तथेति तामुपाह्वयत ततो द्वादशाक्षरा जगत्यभवत्तस्मादाहुर्जागतं तृतीयसवनमिति । (*tayyaiva tṛtīyasavanamatanvata | tāgṃ ha jagatyuvācopa tvāhamāyānyekenākṣareṇopa mā hvayasva mā mā yajñādaṃtargā iti tatheti tāmupāhvayata tato dvādaśākṣarā jagatyabhavattasmādāhurjāgataṃ tṛtīyasavanamiti |*) (Śa. Brā. 4-3-2-9)

With the same Gāyatrī they began to perform the Tṛtīyasavana also. Then the Jagatī approached the Gāyatrī and said: "Do not leave me without a share in the sacrifice. I too shall join you with my one remaining syllable." The Gāyatrī agreed. The Jagatī, joined with the eight syllables of the Gāyatrī and again with those three syllables with which the Gāyatrī had joined the Triṣṭup, came to have twelve syllables. Therefore the Tṛtīyasavana is famed as belonging to the Jagatī.

तदाहुः । गायत्राणि वै सर्वाणि सवनानि गायत्रि ह्येवैतदुपस्पजमानैदिति तस्मात्सग्ंसिद्धं प्रातःसवने प्रतिगृह्णीयात् सग्ंसिद्धा हि गायत्रागच्छत् ॥ (*tadāhuḥ | gāyatrāṇi vai sarvāṇi savanāni gāyatri hyevaitadupaspajamānaiditi tasmātsagṃsiddhaṃ prātaḥsavane pratigṛhṇīyāt sagṃsiddhā hi gāyatrāgacchat ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 4-3-2-10)

Because of this pervasion of all the savanas, all the savanas belong to the Gāyatrī. The sacrificers know that only the Gāyatrī kept growing. Since the Gāyatrī, unlike the other metres, suffered no deficiency and was not incomplete, it is praised, and the mantra signifying its victory must be recited in full. If one such mantra is taken as an example and examined, it becomes clear that it contains both the pre-eminence of the Gāyatrī metre and a prayer addressed to the deity Savitṛ, who is designated a Gandharva.

असौ वा आदित्यो देवः सविता.... ....दिव्यो गंधर्वः केतपूः केतं नः पुनात्वित्यसौ वा आदित्यो दिव्यो गंधर्वः । इमं नो देव सवितर्यज्ञं प्रणयेति । असौ वा आदित्यो देवः सविता यदु वा एष यज्जियं कर्म प्रणयति तदनार्तग्ग् स्वस्तु दृचमश्नुते देवाव्यमिति यो देवानवदित्येतत्सखविदग्ग् सत्राजितं धनजितग्ग् स्वर्जितमिति य एतत्सर्वं विंदादित्ये तदृचेत्यृचा स्तॊमगां समर्धय गायत्रेण रथंतरं बृहद्दायत्रवर्तनीति सामानि स्वाहेति..... ॥ तान्येतान्यष्ट् सावित्राणि । अष्टाक्षरा गायत्री गायत्रोऽग्निर्यावानग्निर्यावत्यस्य मात्रा ॥ (*asau vā ādityo devaḥ savitā.... ....divyo gaṃdharvaḥ ketapūḥ ketaṃ naḥ punātvityasau vā ādityo divyo gaṃdharvaḥ | imaṃ no deva savitaryajñaṃ praṇayeti | asau vā ādityo devaḥ savitā yadu vā eṣa yajjiyaṃ karma praṇayati tadanārtagg svastu dṛcamaśnute devāvyamiti yo devānavadityetatsakhavidagg satrājitaṃ dhanajitagg svarjitamiti ya etatsarvaṃ viṃdāditye tadṛcetyṛcā stòmagāṃ samardhaya gāyatreṇa rathaṃtaraṃ bṛhaddāyatravartanīti sāmāni svāheti..... ‖ tānyetānyaṣṭ sāvitrāṇi | aṣṭākṣarā gāyatrī gāyatro 'gniryāvānagniryāvatyasya mātrā ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 6-3-1-19, 21)

The Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā sentence (11-7), "O god Savitṛ, urge on our sacrifice quickly, so that it is accomplished without obstacle," is to be recited. The god Savitṛ is Āditya. All the sacrificial share belongs to him. The prayer is: "May Savitṛ, the purifier of the mind and the Gandharva of the atmosphere, who is Āditya, cause the sacrifice to be accomplished completely." If the Rathantara sāman is joined with the Gāyatrī metre and the Bṛhat sāman with the Gāyatrī measure, and an efficacious mantra is composed and recited, it always secures prosperity and heaven. The mantras recited in prayer to Savitṛ are eight in number; since the Gāyatrī consists of eight syllables, the number of these mantras is also eight. Since Agni, the chief of the whole sacrifice, is Gāyatra, Agni's glory is the glory of the Gāyatrī; thus the primacy of the Gāyatrī at the time of sacrifice is declared.
11. How can the Gāyatrī, chief in ritual action, be the means to the knowledge of Brahman? Objection and reply.

To make known the primacy of the Gāyatrī, Śaṅkarācārya said that it plays the chief part by three points, the Gāyatrī being the supreme means of knowing the Supreme Brahman, who is beyond ordinary perception. But here another doubt arises. The scriptural descriptions may be true that the Gāyatrī is the support of all the metres that form part of the sacrifice, and that all other metres grew by resting on it. But there is room for the question: merely because it is chief in the sacrifice, which is predominantly ritual action, how can the Gāyatrī also be a means to knowledge of Brahman? Yet the Śrutis themselves declare that the Gāyatrī is of the nature of Brahman, and that knowledge of Brahman is not possible by any means other than Brahman. All the metres useful to the sacrifice, which reflects the principle of Brahman, are indispensable to it; so what is this greatness of the Gāyatrī alone? The answer is that all the other metres cause only impermanent wealth, whereas the Gāyatrī alone can bestow wealth that is eternal and of the nature of Brahman. The greatness of the Gāyatrī is described in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa thus: एतद्द वै यजमानस्माध्यात्मानमिति.... (*etadda vai yajamānasmādhyātmānamiti....*). And as to which metre should be resorted to at the time of reciting the Praüga-śastra:

गायत्रं प्रउगं कुर्यादित्याहुस्तेजो वै ब्रह्मवर्चसं गायत्री तेजस्वी ब्रह्मवर्चसी भवतीति । औष्ठिहं प्रउगं कुर्यादित्याहुरायुर्वा उष्णिगायुष्मान्भवतीति । आनुष्टुभं प्रउगं कुर्यादित्याहुः क्षत्रं ना अनुष्टुप्क्षत्रस्याप्ता इति । बार्हतं प्रउगं कुर्यादित्याहुः श्रीर्वै बृहती श्री- मान्यवतीति । पाङ्कं प्रउगं कुर्यादित्याहुरन्नं वै पंक्तिरन्नवान्भवतीति । त्रैष्टुभं प्रउगं कुर्याद्वीर्यं वै त्रिष्टुब्बीर्यवान्भवतीति । जागतं प्रउगं कुर्यादित्याहुर्जागता वै पशवः पशुमान्भवतीति । तदु गायत्रमेव कुर्यादब्रह्म वै गायत्री ब्रह्मैतदहर्ब्रह्मणैव तद्ब्रह्म प्रतिपद्यते ॥ (*gāyatraṃ praugaṃ kuryādityāhustejo vai brahmavarcasaṃ gāyatrī tejasvī brahmavarcasī bhavatīti | auṣṭhihaṃ praugaṃ kuryādityāhurāyurvā uṣṇigāyuṣmānbhavatīti | ānuṣṭubhaṃ praugaṃ kuryādityāhuḥ kṣatraṃ nā anuṣṭupkṣatrasyāptā iti | bārhataṃ praugaṃ kuryādityāhuḥ śrīrvai bṛhatī śrī- mānyavatīti | pāṅkaṃ praugaṃ kuryādityāhurannaṃ vai paṃktirannavānbhavatīti | traiṣṭubhaṃ praugaṃ kuryādvīryaṃ vai triṣṭubbīryavānbhavatīti | jāgataṃ praugaṃ kuryādityāhurjāgatā vai paśavaḥ paśumānbhavatīti | tadu gāyatrameva kuryādabrahma vai gāyatrī brahmaitadaharbrahmaṇaiva tadbrahma pratipadyate ‖*) (Ai. Ā. 1-1-3)

If the Praüga-śastra is in the Gāyatrī metre, which is full of splendour and endowed with brahmavarcas, then the man who performs the sacrifice reciting it also becomes splendid and endowed with brahmavarcas; this is the view of some. Another view is that if the Praüga-śastra made of the Uṣṇik, which is life-giving, is recited, the sacrificer obtains long life. Some say that if it is made of the Anuṣṭup, which is full of vigour, the sacrificer becomes vigorous. Others say that by reciting the Praüga made of the Bṛhatī, which is wealth, the sacrificer becomes endowed with wealth. One tradition says that if it is made of the Paṅkti, which is food, and is recited, the sacrificer becomes possessed of the wealth of food. Another tradition says that the Triṣṭup, which is strength, makes it give strength. Still others hold that if the śastra made of the Jagatī, which is wealth in cattle, is recited, the sacrificer obtains wealth in cattle. But wealth in food and the like is all impermanent riches. It is beyond dispute that the eternal wealth of the knowledge of Brahman is obtained only by reciting the Praüga made of the Gāyatrī, which is of the nature of Brahman. Therefore the conclusion is that the Gāyatrī itself is the direct means to the knowledge of Brahman, and no other metre can be.

तदु माधुच्छंदसं (*tadu mādhucchaṃdasaṃ*). It is said that this Praüga made of the Gāyatrī should be made of Madhucchandas. But what is Madhucchandas here? What is the reason for this name? What is the close connection between the Gāyatrī and Madhucchandas? This will be explained later. As stated in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka, it is recited again in many Śruti passages that the Gāyatrī is of the nature of Brahman and that this is the means to knowledge of Brahman.
12. Since the sacrifice, which consists of ritual action, is itself of the nature of Brahman, the above objection has no room.

Even with these Śruti proofs, another question arises here. If knowledge alone were chief here, and one fixed one's aim on knowledge of Brahman through meditation, samādhi and austerity, then one could say that the Gāyatrī is the chief means to knowledge of Brahman. But the primacy of the Gāyatrī is

only in the sacrifice. The sacrifice is predominantly ritual action. So there is also room for the doubt how the Gāyatrī, which is chief in a sacrifice that is predominantly ritual, can directly lead to knowledge. To obtain the answer to this question and to know the chief part of the Gāyatrī in the search for knowledge, one must examine such matters as: what is the true nature of the sacrifice? What is the aim of the sacrifice? Is there opposition between the principle of Brahman and the principle of the sacrifice? The Saṃhitā and Brāhmaṇa passages that set forth the principle of the sacrifice do not describe the sacrifice merely as a rite yielding worldly fruit. In many places they declare the identity of the sacrifice with Prajāpati, the cause of creation, preservation and dissolution.
संवत्सरो यज्ञः प्रजापति स यावानेव यज्ञो यावत्यस्य मात्रा तावंतमेवैतत्परिगृह्णाति ॥ (*saṃvatsaro yajñaḥ prajāpati sa yāvāneva yajño yāvatyasya mātrā tāvaṃtamevaitatparigṛhṇāti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 1-2-5-12)

In passages such as this, the identity of Prajāpati with the year, which is of the nature of time, and with the sacrifice in the form of the year, is stated. The construction of such a sacrifice is as follows: तं छंदोभिरभितः परिगृह्य (*taṃ chaṃdobhirabhitaḥ parigṛhya*), that is, one should enclose the sacrificial altar with the metres and establish the fire. In the construction of the sacrifice the metres are the most important of all the materials. This sacrificial altar too is not different from the metres.

तानि वा एतानि सप्तविग्ंशतिर्नक्षत्राणि । छंदाग्ंसि ह त्वेवैषोऽग्निश्चितः । तानि वा एतानि सप्तच्छंदाग्ंसि । (*tāni vā etāni saptavigṃśatirnakṣatrāṇi | chaṃdāgṃsi ha tvevaiṣo 'gniścitaḥ | tāni vā etāni saptacchaṃdāgṃsi |*)
अयं नाव लोक एषोऽग्निश्चितः (*ayaṃ nāva loka eṣo 'gniścitaḥ*)

अंतरिक्षग्ंह त्वैवैषोऽग्निश्चितः । .... .... .... द्यौर्हत्वेवेषोऽग्निश्चितः । .... . .... .... .... आदित्यो ह त्वैवैषोऽग्निश्चितः । (*aṃtarikṣagṃha tvaivaiṣo 'gniścitaḥ | .... .... .... dyaurhatveveṣo 'gniścitaḥ | .... . .... .... .... ādityo ha tvaivaiṣo 'gniścitaḥ |*)

This sacrificial altar is the terrestrial world, this is the atmosphere, this is the heavenly world, this is Āditya. Three hundred and sixty directions and intermediate directions surround Āditya. The three hundred and sixty Yajuṣmatī bricks are the three hundred and sixty rays of Āditya. The Sūdadohas are the special principles lying between the rays of Āditya and the directions; these are the seven metres.

सर्वाणि ह त्त्वेव भूतानि । सर्वे देवा एषोऽग्निश्चित आपो वै सर्वे देवाः सर्वाणि भूतानि ता हैता आप एवैषोऽग्निश्चितस्तस्य नाव्या एव परिश्रितः .... .... आत्मायमेव स योऽयं हिरण्मयःपुरुषः । (*sarvāṇi ha ttveva bhūtāni | sarve devā eṣo 'gniścita āpo vai sarve devāḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni tā haitā āpa evaiṣo 'gniścitastasya nāvyā eva pariśritaḥ .... .... ātmāyameva sa yo 'yaṃ hiraṇmayaḥpuruṣaḥ |*) (Śa. Brā. 10-5-4-1 to 15)

Just as around Āditya the boats in the form of the three hundred and sixty rays surround him, so around this altar the gods, men and others in the form of the Yajuṣmatīs surround it. The body of this altar is Āditya
…the Golden Person who dwells within the sun. How attractive and how weighty is the nature of this Golden Person! It is said:

तस्यैते प्रतिष्ठे । रुक्ष्मश्च पुष्करसर्णं चापश्चादित्यमंडलं .... .... ताविंद्राग्नी द्वे स्वयमातृण्णे इयं चांतरिक्षं च .... .... विश्वज्योतिष एता देवता अग्निर्वायुरादित्य एता ह्येव देवताः .... .... आत्मा स एषः सर्वासामपां मध्यॆ स एष सर्वैः कामैः संपन्नः .... .... ॥ (*tasyaite pratiṣṭhe | rukṣmaśca puṣkarasarṇaṃ cāpaścādityamaṃḍalaṃ .... .... tāviṃdrāgnī dve svayamātṛṇṇe iyaṃ cāṃtarikṣaṃ ca .... .... viśvajyotiṣa etā devatā agnirvāyurāditya etā hyeva devatāḥ .... .... ātmā sa eṣaḥ sarvāsāmapāṃ madhyè sa eṣa sarvaiḥ kāmaiḥ saṃpannaḥ .... .... ‖*)

The golden vessel and the lotus leaf are the two feet of this Golden Person who dwells within the sun. The two ladles on the sacrificial altar are his arms. These are Candra and Agni.⟨NOTE:272⟩. The bricks in the form of the Viśvajyotis are all the deities. Their number is three, and these three reflect Agni, Vāyu and Āditya. The body of this altar is the end of everything. This Golden Person, who has the form of the altar and dwells within the sun, has obtained all desires, and therefore is free from desire and perfectly content.

Thus this principle of sacrifice teaches the unity of the universe, and that the ground of this unity is the principle called Parabrahman. What the Upaniṣads and the like call Parabrahman, the Saṃhitās and Brāhmaṇas call Prajāpati; and they speak of the identity of sacrifice and Prajāpati. The creation of the universe is the fruit of Prajāpati's sacrificial austerity. Prajāpati, the cause of the world, existing before creation and without a second, had to offer himself as the oblation if he was to perform the sacrifice that is the means of creation. By such statements as य आत्मदा बलदा (*ya ātmadā baladā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-121-2) it is described how Prajāpati carried out creation, whose command all the gods and others obey, and whose shadows are death and immortality. The supreme purpose of the sacrifice is thus declared: that we too should worship that Prajāpati, the cause of the universe, by performing sacrificial rites.

The faith to be placed in the principle of sacrifice is not blind faith. This faith must have the power to grasp the spiritual principle. It shows the relation between the sacrifice, the navel of the world, and the principle of Brahman. The sacrificer whose faith rests on spiritual knowledge recognises the identity between himself and the sacrifice. He knows that all the worldly activity of Parabrahman in the form of Prajāpati is contained in this principle of sacrifice, and that he too takes a share in that wheel of the universe. For this realisation meditation and the vision of the inner eye are absolutely necessary:
पश्यन् मन्ये मनसा चक्षसा तान् य इमं यज्ञमयजंत पूर्वे ॥ (*paśyan manye manasā cakṣasā tān ya imaṃ yajñamayajaṃta pūrve ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-130-6)

"With the help of the inner eye in the form of meditation I know and praise the gods and seers who knew the principle of sacrifice, the root of this worldly activity." Thus the necessity of meditation is shown.

This purpose of sacrifice is declared in the sūkta addressed to the deity Savitṛ, in which one prays: whose Bhargas we desire to know, whose nature as the great light we wish to know, "grant us the meditative intellect" — धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् (*dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt*).

युंजते मन उत युंजते धियो विप्रा विप्रस्य बृहतो विपश्चितः । वि होत्रा दधे वयुनाविदेक इन्मही देवस्य सवितुः परिष्टुतिः ॥ (*yuṃjate mana uta yuṃjate dhiyo viprā viprasya bṛhato vipaścitaḥ | vi hotrā dadhe vayunāvideka inmahī devasya savituḥ pariṣṭutiḥ ‖*) (Ma. Saṃ. 5-81-1)⟨NOTE:273⟩

This shows the necessity of meditation: the learned priests engaged in sacrificial work concentrate their minds and worship Savitṛ by meditation in the form of yoga. Knowing the divine nature of Savitṛ through this meditation is thus the supreme purpose of the sacrifice. In the present mantra तत्सवितुः (*tatsavituḥ*) the importance of the prayer "grant the dhī" is explained, and this matter will be explained again when the right meaning of the word dhī is examined.

Just as the principle of sacrifice is described as the thread of the universe by such statements as यो यज्ञो विश्वतस्तंतुभिस्तत एकशतं (*yo yajño viśvatastaṃtubhistata ekaśataṃ*), so too the Gāyatrī holds a primary place in carrying out sacrifice. By गायत्री वा इदं सर्वं भूतं यदिदं किंच (*gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ yadidaṃ kiṃca*), that all beings, moving and unmoving, are of the nature of Gāyatrī, the universal pervasion of Gāyatrī and its having merged the whole world into itself is shown.
**13. Discussion whether Gāyatrī is merely a means to the knowledge of Brahman or the attainable object in the form of knowledge.**

Now, the distinctive character of Gāyatrī as a metre is described in अथातः शिरः । तद्गायत्रीषु भवत्यग्रं वै छंदसां गायत्री । (*athātaḥ śiraḥ | tadgāyatrīṣu bhavatyagraṃ vai chaṃdasāṃ gāyatrī |*) (Ai. Ā. 1-4-1) and so on. For carrying out sacrifices and the like, too, Gāyatrī in the form of a metre holds a most useful primacy. A metre can only be a means for the search after the principle; it cannot itself be the object sought. The doubt therefore arises whether Gāyatrī, which has the form of a metre, can be of the nature of the principle that reflects and teaches the Parabrahman principle, and whether that is possible.

Such a doubt is anticipated in the Brahma-sūtra as well; an answer is given to it and the conclusion is upheld that Gāyatrī is the Parabrahman principle itself and not something different. Since that discussion also establishes the principle by taking Vedic sentences as authority, it may be examined here too.

अपि यदुक्तं पूर्वस्मिन्नपि वाक्ये न ब्रह्म अभिहितमस्ति । गायत्री वा इदं सर्वं भूतं यदिदं किंच, इति गायत्राख्यस्य छंदसोऽभिहित्वात् इति तत् परिहर्तव्यं । कथं पुनः छंदोऽभिधानात् न ब्रह्म अभिहितं इति शक्यते वक्तुं । यावता तावानस्य महिमा इत्येतस्यां ऋचि चतुष्पाद् ब्रह्म दर्शित्वं । नैतदस्ति । गायत्री वा इदं सर्वं इति गायत्रीं उपक्रम्य तामेव भूतपृथिवीशरीरहृदयवाक्प्रभेदैर्वाख्याय । सैषा चतुःप्पदा षड्विधा गायत्री तदेतदृचाभ्यनूक्तं तावानस्य महिमा इति तस्यामेव व्याख्यातरूपायां गायत्रां उदाहृतो मंत्रः कथं अकस्मात् ब्रह्म चतुष्पात् अभिदध्यात् । योऽपि यद्वैतद्ब्रह्मा इति ब्रह्मशब्दः सोऽपि छंदसः प्रकृतत्वात् छंदोविषय एव .... .... तस्मात् छंदोऽभिधानात् न ब्रह्मणः प्रकृतत्वं ॥ (*api yaduktaṃ pūrvasminnapi vākye na brahma abhihitamasti | gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ yadidaṃ kiṃca, iti gāyatrākhyasya chaṃdaso 'bhihitvāt iti tat parihartavyaṃ | kathaṃ punaḥ chaṃdo 'bhidhānāt na brahma abhihitaṃ iti śakyate vaktuṃ | yāvatā tāvānasya mahimā ityetasyāṃ ṛci catuṣpād brahma darśitvaṃ | naitadasti | gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvaṃ iti gāyatrīṃ upakramya tāmeva bhūtapṛthivīśarīrahṛdayavākprabhedairvākhyāya | saiṣā catuḥppadā ṣaḍvidhā gāyatrī tadetadṛcābhyanūktaṃ tāvānasya mahimā iti tasyāmeva vyākhyātarūpāyāṃ gāyatrāṃ udāhṛto maṃtraḥ kathaṃ akasmāt brahma catuṣpāt abhidadhyāt | yo 'pi yadvaitadbrahmā iti brahmaśabdaḥ so 'pi chaṃdasaḥ prakṛtatvāt chaṃdoviṣaya eva .... .... tasmāt chaṃdo 'bhidhānāt na brahmaṇaḥ prakṛtatvaṃ ‖*) (Brahma-sūtra, Śā. Bhā. 1-1-25)⟨NOTE:274⟩

Everything in the world, all beings movable and immovable, is Gāyatrī (Chā. U. 3-12-1); the objector's view is that in describing the nature of Gāyatrī this speaks only of the Gāyatrī in the form of a metre and not of a principle pointing to Parabrahman. To refute this, the siddhāntin points out that in the same Chāndogya Upaniṣad the mantra एतावानस्य महिमा (*etāvānasya mahimā*) ("such is its greatness, so boundless") (Chā. U. 3-12-6) declares the nature of Brahman with four feet. Therefore the word Gāyatrī here means the Parabrahman thing, not merely Gāyatrī as a metre. Against this the objector devises another meaning and explains that sentence thus: having begun with गायत्रि वा इदं सर्वं भूतं (*gāyatri vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ*), the text divides that same Gāyatrī into intermediate divisions — beings, earth, body, heart, speech, breath — saying that it has four feet and is of six kinds; and this is what the Ṛk-mantra describes as एतावानस्य महिमा (*etāvānasya mahimā*). How can such a description of a metre point to Brahman with four feet? Since the metre alone is the topic in hand, the matter of the metre is what is spoken; there is no mention of Parabrahman. So the objector defends his view. The siddhāntin's answer runs as follows:

नैष दोषः । तथा चेतोऽर्पणनिगदात् । तथा गायत्राख्यच्छंदोद्वारेण तदनुगते ब्रह्मणि चेतसः अर्पणं चित्तसमाधानं अनेन ब्राह्मणवाक्येन निगद्यते । गायत्रि वा इदं सर्वं इति । न हि अक्षरसंनिवेशमात्राया गायत्राः सर्वात्मकत्वं संभवति । तस्मात् यत् गायत्राख्यविकारे अनुगतं जगत्कारणं ब्रह्म तदिह सर्वं इत्युच्यते ... .... तस्मात् अस्ति छंदोऽभिधानेऽपि पूर्वस्मिन् वाक्ये चतुष्पात् ब्रह्म निर्दिष्टं । तदेव ज्योतिर्वाक्येऽपि परामृश्यते उपासनानंतरविधानाय ॥ (*naiṣa doṣaḥ | tathā ceto 'rpaṇanigadāt | tathā gāyatrākhyacchaṃdodvāreṇa tadanugate brahmaṇi cetasaḥ arpaṇaṃ cittasamādhānaṃ anena brāhmaṇavākyena nigadyate | gāyatri vā idaṃ sarvaṃ iti | na hi akṣarasaṃniveśamātrāyā gāyatrāḥ sarvātmakatvaṃ saṃbhavati | tasmāt yat gāyatrākhyavikāre anugataṃ jagatkāraṇaṃ brahma tadiha sarvaṃ ityucyate ... .... tasmāt asti chaṃdo 'bhidhāne 'pi pūrvasmin vākye catuṣpāt brahma nirdiṣṭaṃ | tadeva jyotirvākye 'pi parāmṛśyate upāsanānaṃtaravidhānāya ‖*) (Śa. Bhā. Bra. Sū. 1-1.-5)⟨NOTE:275⟩

The objector's view is not consistent. For in the present context it is said that one should place the mind on the supreme thing and meditate; so, through the metre called Gāyatrī, the mind is to be placed on the Brahman that pervades it, and this is said by the mantra sentence गायत्रि वा इदं सर्वं (*gāyatri vā idaṃ sarvaṃ*).⟨NOTE:276⟩. To say that Gāyatrī, which is merely an arrangement of syllables and has the form of a metre, is of the nature of everything would be inconsistent. Therefore it can be said decisively that the thing indicated is Parabrahman itself, existing in the form of the effect called Gāyatrī and being the cause of the whole world. That the cause is not different from the effect is said in the sūtra तदनन्यत्वमारंभणशब्दादिभ्यः (*tadananyatvamāraṃbhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ*) (2-1-14).
In other Śrutis too it is said that the Parabrahman principle, the cause, should be worshipped through the effect⟨NOTE:277⟩. (Ai. Ā. 3-2-3)

सर्वेषु भूतेष्वेतमेव ब्रह्मेत्याचक्षते ! स एष संवत्सरसमानश्च क्षुर्मयः शोत्रमयश्चंदोमयो मनोमयो वाङ्मय आत्मा स य एवमेतं .... .... .... शंसति ॥ (*sarveṣu bhūteṣvetameva brahmetyācakṣate ! sa eṣa saṃvatsarasamānaśca kṣurmayaḥ śotramayaścaṃdomayo manomayo vāṅmaya ātmā sa ya evametaṃ .... .... .... śaṃsati ‖*) (Ai. Ā. 3-2-3)⟨NOTE:278⟩

The cause-thing that has transformed itself into many forms as effects — eye, ear, metre and so on — is Parabrahman. These Śruti sentences teach the above meaning: that this very Parabrahman thing is to be worshipped in forms such as the metre.

Therefore, although in some places the word Gāyatrī clearly gives the meaning "metre", there is no doubt that the Upaniṣad sentence गायत्री वा इदग्ं सर्वं (*gāyatrī vā idagṃ sarvaṃ*) points to the Parabrahman thing itself. Even though it is counted as a metre, just as Parabrahman, who is supernatural, beyond ordinary worldly perception and the cause, reveals himself through worldly effect-things, so the Gāyatrī principle is described as the Parabrahman principle: सैषा चतुष्पदा गायत्री (*saiṣā catuṣpadā gāyatrī*) (Chā. U. 3-12-5)

Of these four feet, the first three reflect the world in the form of the effect, and the fourth (turīya) foot reflects the Brahman principle in the form of the cause. Even when the word Gāyatrī is taken to mean a metre, its purport must be stated as a metre that possesses both these forms. The first three feet are graspable by worldly understanding; the fourth foot is to be realised through yoga and meditation.
**14. The spiritual character of metre, and the primacy of Gāyatrī in the search for knowledge.**

देवा वै मृत्योर्भिभ्यतस्त्रयीं विद्यां प्राविशंस्ते छंदोभिराच्छादयन्यदेभिराच्छादयन्स्छंदसां छंदस्त्वं । (*devā vai mṛtyorbhibhyatastrayīṃ vidyāṃ prāviśaṃste chaṃdobhirācchādayanyadebhirācchādayanschaṃdasāṃ chaṃdastvaṃ |*) (Bhā. U. 1-4-2)⟨NOTE:279⟩

This sentence states the general characteristic of metre. When the gods, afraid of death, entered the threefold knowledge (trayī), the threefold knowledge concealed them with the metres. The word chandas is derived from the root chad, meaning "cover, conceal". Because they covered them from death, they are called chandas; thus its characteristic is stated. (The root is also used in the sense "to gladden".)

However, even though the metres concealed the gods from the face of death, death discovered that these gods were hidden in the trayī; thus a shortcoming in the power of the metres is also shown. The purport is that in such contexts the metre is worldly and belongs to the world of effects. Although such a metre gives joy, that joy is limited. In speaking of the Gāyatrī metre too, both these forms are described and Gāyatrī is praised. The Upaniṣads praise Gāyatrī by saying that its first three feet reflect the lower principle and the fourth foot reflects the higher principle.

भूमिरंतरिक्षं द्यौरित्यष्टावक्षराणि । अष्टाक्षरं ह वा एकं गायत्रै पदं । एतदु हैवास्या एतदेवं पदं वेद । (*bhūmiraṃtarikṣaṃ dyaurityaṣṭāvakṣarāṇi | aṣṭākṣaraṃ ha vā ekaṃ gāyatrai padaṃ | etadu haivāsyā etadevaṃ padaṃ veda |*) (Bṛ. U. 5-14-1)

Earth, atmosphere, heaven: these eight syllables are the first foot of Gāyatrī. Thus these three worlds together become one foot of Gāyatrī. One who knows this principle obtains the wealth of these three worlds.

यजो यजूग्ंषि, सामानि इत्यष्टावक्षराणि । अष्टाक्षरं ह ना एकं गायत्रै पदं । एतदु हैवास्या एतत् । स यावतीयं त्रयी विद्या तावद्ध जयति योऽस्या एतदेवं पदं वेद । (*yajo yajūgṃṣi, sāmāni ityaṣṭāvakṣarāṇi | aṣṭākṣaraṃ ha nā ekaṃ gāyatrai padaṃ | etadu haivāsyā etat | sa yāvatīyaṃ trayī vidyā tāvaddha jayati yo 'syā etadevaṃ padaṃ veda |*) (Bṛ. U. 5-14-2)

Ṛcs, Yajus formulas, Sāmans: these eight syllables are the second foot of Gāyatrī. One who knows this principle obtains all the wealth of knowledge to be gained from the trayī, the treasury of knowledge.

प्राणोऽपानो व्यान इत्याष्टावक्षराणि । अष्टाक्षरं ह वा एकं गायत्रैशि पदं । एतदु हैवास्या एतत् । स यावदिदं प्राणि तावद्ध जयति योऽस्या एतदेवं पदं वेद । (*prāṇo 'pāno vyāna ityāṣṭāvakṣarāṇi | aṣṭākṣaraṃ ha vā ekaṃ gāyatraiśi padaṃ | etadu haivāsyā etat | sa yāvadidaṃ prāṇi tāvaddha jayati yo 'syā etadevaṃ padaṃ veda |*) (Bṛ. U. 5-4-3)⟨NOTE:280⟩

The three principles prāṇa, apāna and vyāna are the third foot of Gāyatrī, which consists of eight syllables. One who knows this principle obtains all the wealth of power of the whole class of living beings. The sun, shining with his own radiance and visible to the whole world, is the fourth foot of Gāyatrī. Although he has a nature beyond worldly perception, the sun takes a form open to perception and appears to all; hence the epithet दर्शतं (*darśataṃ*) here. Because he shines in the excellent atmosphere, surpassing all the worlds full of darkness, there is the epithet परोरजाः (*parorajāḥ*). One who knows the nature of this fourth foot becomes radiant and endowed with Brahmanic splendour.

सैषा गायत्र्येतस्मिंस्तुरीये दर्शते पदे परोरजसि प्रतिष्ठिता । तद्वै तत्सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितं । चक्षुर्वै सत्यं । चक्षुर्हि वै सत्यं .... .... तस्मादाहुर्बलं सत्यादोगीय इति । एवं वैषा गायत्र्यध्यात्मं प्रतिष्ठिता । सा हैषा गयांस्तत्रे । प्राणा वै गयाः तत्पाणांस्तत्रे तद्यद्धयांस्तत्रे तस्माद्दायत्री नाम । स यामेवामुं सावित्रिमन्वाह । एवैष सा । स यस्मा अन्वाह तस्य प्राणास्त्रायंते ॥ (*saiṣā gāyatryetasmiṃsturīye darśate pade parorajasi pratiṣṭhitā | tadvai tatsatye pratiṣṭhitaṃ | cakṣurvai satyaṃ | cakṣurhi vai satyaṃ .... .... tasmādāhurbalaṃ satyādogīya iti | evaṃ vaiṣā gāyatryadhyātmaṃ pratiṣṭhitā | sā haiṣā gayāṃstatre | prāṇā vai gayāḥ tatpāṇāṃstatre tadyaddhayāṃstatre tasmāddāyatrī nāma | sa yāmevāmuṃ sāvitrimanvāha | evaiṣa sā | sa yasmā anvāha tasya prāṇāstrāyaṃte ‖*)
