ಗಳಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಪ್ರಶಂಸಿತವಾಗಿ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಾದಿ ಸಕಲ ಶ್ರುತಿಗಳೂ ಒಂದಲ್ಲ ಒಂದು ಕಡೆ ಈ ಮಹರ್ಷಿಯ ಕೃತಿಯನ್ನುದ್ಧ
en: That this Ṛk गृणाना जमदग्निना (*gṛṇānā jamadagninā*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra of the Maitrāvaruṇa graha is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, होता यक्षन्मित्रावरुणा गृणाना जमदग्निना (*hotā yakṣanmitrāvaruṇā gṛṇānā jamadagninā*) (Ā. 5-5). And that, at the *adhyāyopākaraṇa*, the Ṛk गृणाना जमदग्निना (*gṛṇānā jamadagninā*) is to be recited as a homa mantra at the end of the maṇḍala is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra गृणाना जमदग्निना (*gṛṇānā jamadagninā*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-5-6).

एतन्नामकेन महर्षिणा स्तूयमानौ । यद्वा । जमदग्निना प्रज्वलिताग्निना विश्वामित्रेण स्तूयमानौ । (*etannāmakena maharṣiṇā stūyamānau | yadvā | jamadagninā prajvalitāgninā viśvāmitreṇa stūyamānau |*) One meaning is: Mitra and Varuṇa praised by the great seer named Jamadagni. Or, if the word *jamadagni* is taken as "kindled fire", it means Viśvāmitra, who kindled the fire for the sacrifice; the other meaning is then Mitra and Varuṇa praised by such a Viśvāmitra. Thus Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of explanation. To say that the seer is named Jamadagni is the proper course.

The great seer Jamadagni was an intimate friend of Viśvāmitra. In the Ṛgveda, these hymns are famed as composed by Jamadagni: 3-62-16 to 18; 8-101; 9-62; 9-65; 9-67-16 to 18; 10-110; 10-137-6; 10-167. He is the son of Bhṛgu, and so is known as Jamadagni Bhārgava. In many places he states his own praise openly with the words गृणानो जमदग्निना (*gṛṇāno jamadagninā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-62-24; 9-65-25, etc.).

In प्रसूतो भक्षमकरं चरावपि स्तोमं चेमं प्रथमः सूरिरुन्मृजे । सुते सातेन यद्यागमं नां प्रति विश्वामित्रजमदग्नी दमे ॥ (*prasūto bhakṣamakaraṃ carāvapi stomaṃ cemaṃ prathamaḥ sūrirunmṛje | sute sātena yadyāgamaṃ nāṃ prati viśvāmitrajamadagnī dame ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-167-4), Indra addresses Viśvāmitra and Jamadagni together and shows his favour. This companionship is described in many places. That the two were able to contend with Vasiṣṭha is also well known in the Saṃhitās and other works.

विश्वामित्रजमदग्नी वसिष्ठेनास्पर्धेताग्ं स एतज्जव दग्निर्विहव्यमपश्यत्तेन वै स वसिष्ठस्येंद्रियं वीर्यमवृंक्त ॥ (*viśvāmitrajamadagnī vasiṣṭhenāspardhetāgṃ sa etajjava dagnirvihavyamapaśyattena vai sa vasiṣṭhasyeṃdriyaṃ vīryamavṛṃkta ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-1-7-3). While Viśvāmitra and Jamadagni were both contending with Vasiṣṭha, Jamadagni received the vision of the Vihavya hymn, which begins with the mantra ममाग्ने वर्चो विहवेष्टस्तु वयं तैंधानास्तन्वं पुषेम (*mamāgne varco vihaveṣṭastu vayaṃ taiṃdhānāstanvaṃ puṣema*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-128). With its help he took all of Vasiṣṭha's power for himself; this is told in story form in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. In the Bṛhaddevatā another historical occasion of the same kind is stated thus:

सुदासश्च महायज्ञे शक्तिना गाथिसूनवे । निगृहीतं बलाच्चेतः सोऽवसीदद्विचेतनः । तस्मै ब्राह्मीं तु सौरीं वा नाम्ना वाचं ससर्परीं । सूर्यक्षयादिहाहृत्य वदुस्ते जमदग यः । कुशिकानां ततः सा नागमुतिं तामपाहनत् ॥ (*sudāsaśca mahāyajñe śaktinā gāthisūnave | nigṛhītaṃ balāccetaḥ so 'vasīdadvicetanaḥ | tasmai brāhmīṃ tu saurīṃ vā nāmnā vācaṃ sasarparīṃ | sūryakṣayādihāhṛtya vaduste jamadaga yaḥ | kuśikānāṃ tataḥ sā nāgamutiṃ tāmapāhanat ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 4-112 to 114).

At the great sacrifice of Sudās, the son of Gādhi (Viśvāmitra), struck by Śakti, the son of Vasiṣṭha, fainted and fell to the ground bereft of consciousness. Then Jamadagni provided the help of the speech named Sasarparī, the daughter of the Sun (or of Brahmā). That goddess of speech removed the faint of the son of Kuśika and made consciousness return to him. This occasion is indicated in the Ṛgveda in Ṛks such as

ससर्परीरमतिं बाधमाना बृहन्दि माय जमदग्नि दत्ता । आ सूरस्य दुहिता ततान श्रवो देवेष्वमृतमजुर्यं ॥ ( (*sasarparīramatiṃ bādhamānā bṛhandi māya jamadagni dattā | ā sūrasya duhitā tatāna śravo deveṣvamṛtamajuryaṃ ‖ (*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3 53-5). ⟨NOTE:334⟩
Its special meaning was explained earlier.

Even when relating such stories, the word *jamadagni* is sometimes explained also from the spiritual point of view. In such contexts it is said that Jamadagni was a son of Prajāpati and that, looking at the truth of the world with his divine vision, he made a knowledge-like light for the world. For example:

प्रजापतिर्विराजमपश्यत्तया भूतं च भव्यं चासृजत तामृषिभ्यस्तिरोदधात्तां जमदग्निस्तपदापश्यत्तया वै स पृश्नीन्मानसृजत । (*prajāpatirvirājamapaśyattayā bhūtaṃ ca bhavyaṃ cāsṛjata tāmṛṣibhyastirodadhāttāṃ jamadagnistapadāpaśyattayā vai sa pṛśnīnmānasṛjata |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-3-5-2).

Prajāpati received the vision of the Virāj; with its help he created what has been and what is to be. But he made both of them lie outside the range of the seers' perception. Then Jamadagni, by the greatness of his austerity, obtained the vision of them and created from them many kinds of objects of desire; so his power of divine vision is described. In the same way the Upaniṣads tell us that Jamadagni is a part that mirrors the spiritual truth:

इमावेव गोतमभारद्वाजौ, अयमेव गोतमः, अयं भारद्वाजः । इमावेव विश्वामित्रजमदग्नी, अयमेव विश्वामित्रः, अयं जमदग्निः । (*imāveva gotamabhāradvājau, ayameva gotamaḥ, ayaṃ bhāradvājaḥ | imāveva viśvāmitrajamadagnī, ayameva viśvāmitraḥ, ayaṃ jamadagniḥ |*) (Bṛ. U. 2-2-4).

This is stated in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka when the truth of the body is explained. Of these, Gotama and Bharadvāja expound the principle of the ear; Viśvāmitra and Jamadagni expound the principle of the eye. Viśvāmitra is said to be the right eye and Jamadagni the left eye. But here the meaning is not merely the physical eye; it is to be understood as the eye of knowledge. How? In the sentence प्रजापतिर्वै जमदग्निः, सोऽश्वमेधः । (*prajāpatirvai jamadagniḥ, so 'śvamedhaḥ |*) (Śa. Brā. 13-2-2-14), Jamadagni is designated as Prajāpati himself, and the special quality of such a Jamadagni is this:

जमदग्नि र्यषिरिति । चक्षुर्वै जमदग्नि र्यषिर्यदेनेन जगत्पश्यत्यथो मनुते तस्माच्चक्षुर्जमदग्नि र्यषिः प्रजापतिगृहीतया त्वयेति प्रजापतिसृष्टया त्वयेत्येतच्चक्षुर्गृह्णामि ॥ (*jamadagni ryaṣiriti | cakṣurvai jamadagni ryaṣiryadenena jagatpaśyatyatho manute tasmāccakṣurjamadagni ryaṣiḥ prajāpatigṛhītayā tvayeti prajāpatisṛṣṭayā tvayetyetaccakṣurgṛhṇāmi ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 8-1-2-3).

The great seer Jamadagni himself is the eye. He is the divine eye by whose help the whole world gains the power of sight and the power of consciousness. "O Jamadagni, created by Prajāpati, by your divine favour may the power of sight come to all my progeny": thus Jamadagni is prayed to for the divine knowledge by which the spiritual truth is known. The Taittirīya Āraṇyaka states the same import:

यदक्षरं भूतकृतं । विश्वेदेवा उपासते । महर्षिमस्य गोप्तारं । जमदग्निमकुर्वत । जमदग्निराप्यायते । छंदोभिश्च तुरुत्तरैः । राजस्थोमस्य तृप्ता सः ॥ (*yadakṣaraṃ bhūtakṛtaṃ | viśvedevā upāsate | maharṣimasya goptāraṃ | jamadagnimakurvata | jamadagnirāpyāyate | chaṃdobhiśca turuttaraiḥ | rājasthomasya tṛptā saḥ ‖*) (Trai. Ā. 1-9-7). ⟨NOTE:335⟩
By these sentences it is shown that Jamadagni is of the nature of the imperishable (*akṣara*) Supreme Self.
वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः । (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ |*)

इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वरवैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तकश्रीवीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये तृतीयाष्टके तृतीये मंडले पंचमोऽनुवाकः (*iti śrīmadrājādhirājaparameśvaravaidikamārgapravartakaśrīvīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye tṛtīyāṣṭake tṛtīye maṃḍale paṃcamo 'nuvākaḥ*)
Here the third Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā (in the third Aṣṭaka), accompanied by the Bhāṣya of Śrī Sāyaṇa and by a Kannada translation, is concluded.
यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ (*yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yadbhavet | tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stu te ‖*)
A brief account of the seer Vāmadeva.

This sūkta was seen by the seer Vāmadeva. We shall describe the seer Vāmadeva briefly at the beginning of this Maṇḍala. This Vāmadeva is the son of the seer Gotama. Of the sūktas of this fourth Maṇḍala, sūktas 1–7 (206 Ṛks in all); in the 18th sūkta, verses 2–3½ and 8–13 (8½ Ṛks in all); sūktas 19–41 (299 Ṛks in all); and 45–58 (107 Ṛks in all)—all these together make a total of 560½ Ṛks, and he is the seer of them.

The Śruti passages praise Vāmadeva in many ways as a great seer who had attained knowledge of Brahman. The Bṛhadāraṇyaka and the other Upaniṣads, the author of the Brahma-sūtras and others, when they examine the nature of the knowledge of Brahman and its means, praise the example of Vāmadeva himself. Such a divine knower is renowned as the seer of the fourth Maṇḍala of the Ṛk Saṃhitā. It is also stated that he is a part of Brahman who shines in the outer space in the form of the Sun and in the heart-space of man in the form of the vital breath. Although all the seers of the Ṛk Saṃhitā are described as particular manifestations of Brahman, the praise concerning Vāmadeva is extraordinary. That this great seer is a manifest person of Brahman in the form of the vital breath is described in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka as follows.
एष इमं लोकमभ्यार्चत्पुरुषरूपेण य एष तपति (*eṣa imaṃ lokamabhyārcatpuruṣarūpeṇa ya eṣa tapati*)

The Supreme Brahman who shines in the form of the Sun pervaded the earth in the form of a person. Then all the gods too wished, "May he be dear to us all." Because he whom all the gods wished to be dear to them became known as Vāmadeva, even though he was born from the form of a person, he was not covered by the ignorance natural to a person.

By the three mantras beginning अहं मनुरभवं (*ahaṃ manurabhavaṃ*), Vāmadeva, dwelling in the womb, having attained knowledge of the truth, declared his experience of being everything, showing it in the forms of Manu and the rest. By three mantras of the meaning "I became Manu, the Prajāpati" and so on, Vāmadeva describes how, while still in the womb, he attained omniscience and the experience of himself in the forms of Manu and others.

गर्भे नु सन्नन्वेषामवेदमहं देवानां जनिमानि विश्वा । शतं मा पुर आयसीररक्षन्नध श्येनो जवसा निरदीयं ॥ (*garbhe nu sannanveṣāmavedamahaṃ devānāṃ janimāni viśvā | śataṃ mā pura āyasīrarakṣannadha śyeno javasā niradīyaṃ ‖*)

"While still in the womb I knew the manner of origin of all the gods. Hundreds of iron bars bound me. But freed from them, I flew out swiftly like a falcon (śyena)." Quoting this Saṃhitā passage, which he himself spoke, in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka,

गर्भ एवैतच्छयानो वामदेव एवमुवाच । स एवं विद्वानस्माच्छरीरभेदादूर्ध्व उत्क्रम्यामुष्मिन्वर्गे लोके सर्वान्कामानाप्त्वामृतः समभवत्समभवत् ॥ (*garbha evaitacchayāno vāmadeva evamuvāca | sa evaṃ vidvānasmāccharīrabhedādūrdhva utkramyāmuṣminvarge loke sarvānkāmānāptvāmṛtaḥ samabhavatsamabhavat ‖*)

it is praised thus: Vāmadeva recited this sentence while still in the womb; having known this truth, he broke through the body in the womb, became free, enjoyed all the delights of heaven and became immortal. In अध शैनो जवसा निरदीयं (*adha śaino javasā niradīyaṃ*), for शैनः (*śainaḥ*) Sāyaṇa has stated शैनवत् (*śainavat*), "like the falcon", the word being a mark of comparison. Others say that, since there is here no word that indicates comparison, identity of Vāmadeva with the falcon is stated. If identity is stated in this way, one must examine what the word शैन (*śaina*) means. Moreover, that such a divine knower is said to have suffered the misery of poverty and, as a result, to have done a blameworthy deed is also a cause of doubt.

अवर्त्या शुन आंत्राणि पेचे न देवेषु विविदे मर्डितारं । अपश्यं जायाममहीयमानामधा मे श्येनो मध्वा जभार ॥ (*avartyā śuna āṃtrāṇi pece na deveṣu vivide marḍitāraṃ | apaśyaṃ jāyāmamahīyamānāmadhā me śyeno madhvā jabhāra ‖*)

"Without means of livelihood I cooked the entrails of a dog. No god who would make me happy appeared to me. I saw my wife too in a wretched state. Then Indra, swift like a falcon, brought me honey." So runs the description. In such circumstances it is a labour to know what the real meaning is. Speaking of himself,
महो रुजामि बंधुता वचोभिस्तन्ना पितुर्गोतमादन्वियाय । (*maho rujāmi baṃdhutā vacobhistannā piturgotamādanviyāya |*)

"O Agni, praising you with the speech of praise received from my father Gotama, I shall be able, by your grace, to destroy all enemies." In saying this he has declared himself the son of Gotama. This seer composed most excellent sūktas addressed to deities such as Agni and Indra. Stating this very thing, the Bṛhaddevatā says:
सोग्निं तु पंचदशभिरिंद्रं षोडशभिः परैः । यषिस्वामिति तुष्टाव सूक्तैरेति तु गौतमः ॥ (*sogniṃ tu paṃcadaśabhiriṃdraṃ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ paraiḥ | yaṣisvāmiti tuṣṭāva sūktaireti tu gautamaḥ ‖*)

Vāmadeva, son of Gotama, praised Agni with the fifteen sūktas beginning with the mantra त्वां ह्यग्ने सदमित् (*tvāṃ hyagne sadamit*), and Indra with the sixteen sūktas beginning with the mantra आ सत्यो यातु (*ā satyo yātu*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-16-32). Thus the sūktas are divided according to the order of the deities. And in the mantras beginning स भ्रातरं (*sa bhrātaraṃ*) the circumstances that give room for doubt are also described. That a fight took place between Vāmadeva and Indra, and that although Indra was defeated Vāmadeva praised Indra, is also a strange circumstance from the worldly point of view. This story is described as follows.

अंजसा न जनिष्येऽहं ब्रुवाणं गर्भमेव तु । अन्वशाददितिः पुत्रं इंद्रमात्महितैषिणी । स जातमात्रो युद्धाय ऋषिमेवाजुहाव तु ॥ (*aṃjasā na janiṣye 'haṃ bruvāṇaṃ garbhameva tu | anvaśādaditiḥ putraṃ iṃdramātmahitaiṣiṇī | sa jātamātro yuddhāya ṛṣimevājuhāva tu ‖*)

As soon as the son in the womb said, "I shall not be born in the natural way," Aditi, intent on her own protection, rebuked her son Indra. That same Indra, as soon as he was born, confronted the seer Vāmadeva as if to fight him.
योधयन्नामदेवस्तं कृत्वात्मनि बलं तथा । दिनानि दश रात्रीश्च विजिग्ये चैनमोजसा ॥ (*yodhayannāmadevastaṃ kṛtvātmani balaṃ tathā | dināni daśa rātrīśca vijigye cainamojasā ‖*)
Fighting with Indra, who had resolved to do him harm, he made him struggle for ten days, night and day. In the end, by his superior strength, he defeated him completely.
स तं क इममित्य स्यां विक्रीणन्नृषिसंसदि । स्वयं तेनाभितुष्टाव नकिरिंद्रेति गौतमः ॥ (*sa taṃ ka imamitya syāṃ vikrīṇannṛṣisaṃsadi | svayaṃ tenābhituṣṭāva nakiriṃdreti gautamaḥ ‖*)

Then Vāmadeva, by the Ṛk क इमं (*ka imaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-24-10), presenting Indra who had come under his control, became in the assembly of seers a seller of Indra, and even at the time of the sale he fixes the terms. (Sāyaṇācārya has described the circumstances of this same occasion, in the form of verses composed by earlier teachers, in the introduction to mantra 4-24-10.) And by the mantras beginning न किरिंद्र त्वदुत्तरः (*na kiriṃdra tvaduttaraḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-30-1) he praised Indra.

किमादुतासीति चास्यां मन्युमर्धे पराणुदत् । अथास्य रूपवीर्याणि धैर्यकार्याणि तान्वृषिः ॥ विविधानि च कर्माणि शशंसादितये तथा । अह मित्यात्मसंस्तावस्त्रचे स्तुतिरिवास्य हि ॥ प्र सु ष विभो नवभिर्यग्निः श्येनस्य संस्तवः । पराभिस्तृति पंचर्चे सोमेनेंद्रः स्तुतः सह ॥ (*kimādutāsīti cāsyāṃ manyumardhe parāṇudat | athāsya rūpavīryāṇi dhairyakāryāṇi tānvṛṣiḥ ‖ vividhāni ca karmāṇi śaśaṃsāditaye tathā | aha mityātmasaṃstāvastrace stutirivāsya hi ‖ pra su ṣa vibho navabhiryagniḥ śyenasya saṃstavaḥ | parābhistṛti paṃcarce someneṃdraḥ stutaḥ saha ‖*)

By the mantra किमादुतासि (*kimādutāsi*) (4-20-7) he praised Indra and appeased his anger. Then he praised and extolled Indra's heroic deeds, his firmness and his daring. By the mantras beginning अहं मनुः (*ahaṃ manuḥ*) (4-26-1) he also praised his own greatness and declared it before Aditi. In these praises he seems to have declared identity between himself and Indra. In the mantras beginning प्र सु ष विभ्यः (*pra su ṣa vibhyaḥ*) (4-26-4-7) there is praise of the falcon (Śyena). After that there is again praise of Indra together with Soma. Thus Vāmadeva's skill of composition is praised. In the same way his skill of composition is praised in other places also.

संपातौ भवतो निष्केवल्यमरुत्वतीययोर्निविद्वाने वामदेवो वा इमाल्लोकानपश्यत्तान्संपातैः समपतद्यत्संपातैः समपतत्तत्संपातानां संपा- तत्वं तद्यत्संपातौ प्रथमेऽहनि शंसति स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्टेऽ संपत्तेऽ संगत्यै ॥ (*saṃpātau bhavato niṣkevalyamarutvatīyayornividvāne vāmadevo vā imāllokānapaśyattānsaṃpātaiḥ samapatadyatsaṃpātaiḥ samapatattatsaṃpātānāṃ saṃpā- tatvaṃ tadyatsaṃpātau prathame 'hani śaṃsati svargasya lokasya samaṣṭe ' saṃpatte ' saṃgatyai ‖*)

In the Niṣkevalya-śastra and also in the Marutvatīya-śastra, the mantras to be offered are in the form of saṃpātas (they follow upon one another). आ यात्विंद्रोऽवस (*ā yātviṃdro 'vasa*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-21-1) is the sūkta, in the form of a nivid-dhāna, to be offered in the Marutvatīya-śastra. The one that begins with the mantra आ न इंद्रो दूरात् (*ā na iṃdro dūrāt*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-20-1) is the sūkta

to be offered in the Niṣkevalya-śastra in the form of a nivid-dhāna. Both of these bear the name saṃpāta. Formerly the seer Vāmadeva, having surveyed all the worlds beginning with Bhūr and wishing to visit them all, was thinking about the means of reaching them, and finally composed these saṃpāta-sūktas; by their power he flew to all of them in the manner of a bird's flight and reached them. Since it is established that, by their greatness, all who recite them will likewise go and reach the worlds beginning with Bhūr, the name saṃpāta became famous for them. The man who, on the first day of the Niṣkevalya and Marutvatīya śastras, recites these saṃpāta-sūktas with faith obtains all prosperity and attains union with heaven. Thus the power of Vāmadeva's composition is praised. A circumstance in which the seer Viśvāmitra could not bear the greatness of the power of these mantras is also stated as follows:

तान्ना एतान्संपातान्विश्वामित्रः प्रथममपश्यत्तान्विश्वामित्रेण दृष्टान्वामदेपोऽसृजतैवा त्वामिंद्र वज्रिन्नत्र .... .... .... तत्संपातानां संपातत्वं ॥ (*tānnā etānsaṃpātānviśvāmitraḥ prathamamapaśyattānviśvāmitreṇa dṛṣṭānvāmadepo 'sṛjataivā tvāmiṃdra vajrinnatra .... .... .... tatsaṃpātānāṃ saṃpātatvaṃ ‖*)

The great seer Viśvāmitra, by the grace of God, saw the saṃpāta-sūktas at the very time of creation, and also knew in his mind the power of these mantras among the Vedas. Vāmadeva studied these sūktas seen by Viśvāmitra and published them in the world in his own name. एवा त्वामिंद्र वज्रिन् (*evā tvāmiṃdra vajrin*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-19-1), यन्न इंद्रो जुजुषे (*yanna iṃdro jujuṣe*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-22-1), कथा महामवृधत्कस्य होतुः (*kathā mahāmavṛdhatkasya hotuḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-23-1) are those seen by Viśvāmitra and created by Vāmadeva. Knowing this, Viśvāmitra, wishing to make his own name famous, composed in return for these the saṃpāta-mantras beginning सद्यो ह जातो वृषभः (*sadyo ha jāto vṛṣabhaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-48-1); this circumstance too is described. Circumstances of this kind also praise Vāmadeva's skill of composition.

The Upaniṣads and other texts praise his divine knowledge, saying that Vāmadeva was a great divine knower, and that everyone who wishes to be freed from the sorrow of saṃsāra and to attain the eternal union with Brahman must know what the nature of the great seer Vāmadeva's knowledge was. In the Aitareya Upaniṣad:
तदुक्तमृषिणा—गर्भे नु सन्नन्वेषां .... .... .... इति । गर्भ ए वैतच्छयानो वामदेव एवमुवाच ॥ (*taduktamṛṣiṇā—garbhe nu sannanveṣāṃ .... .... .... iti | garbha e vaitacchayāno vāmadeva evamuvāca ‖*)

The text continues the account of Vāmadeva's divine knowledge. In all three states that bind a man, beginning with birth, a man falls into the ocean of saṃsāra and wanders in it. The Vāmadeva Ṛṣi has declared that such a man is freed from the bondage of saṃsāra the moment he knows the nature of the Self. While still in his mother's womb, he says, "I have come to know all the births of the deities, of Vāk, Agni and the rest. The limbs of the body were bonds to me, like iron bars. As a hawk breaks the net and flies off with the speed of the wind, so I too, the moment I was without bonds, flew out with the strength gained from knowledge of the Self." Vāmadeva spoke this utterance while still in the womb.

स एवं विद्वानस्माच्छरीरभेदादूर्ध्व उत्क्रम्यामुष्मिन् स्वर्गे लोके सर्वान् कामानाप्त्वामृतः समभवत्समभवत् ॥ (*sa evaṃ vidvānasmāccharīrabhedādūrdhva utkramyāmuṣmin svarge loke sarvān kāmānāptvāmṛtaḥ samabhavatsamabhavat ‖*) (I. U. 2-6) ⟨NOTE:339⟩

The moment Vāmadeva had knowledge of the Self, the body was split. That is, the chain of bodies, imagined through ignorance, hard like things of iron and an extremely firm bondage, joined to hundreds of series of misfortunes such as birth and death, all the fetters in the form of nescience were destroyed as soon as he tasted the nectar of knowledge of the Supreme Self. Then, having the nature of the Supreme Self and having attained the state of being the Self of all, he became immortal.

ब्रह्मविद्यासाधनकृतसर्वात्मभावफलावाप्तिं नामदेवाद्याचार्यपरंपरया श्रुत्या अवद्योत्यमानां ब्रह्मवित्परिषदि अत्यंतप्रसिद्धां उपलभमाना मुमुक्षवः अधुनातनाः ब्रह्मजिज्ञासवः अनित्यात् साध्यसाधनलक्षणात् संसारात् आजीवभावाद्व्याविवृत्सवो विचारयंतोऽन्योन्यं पृच्छंति ।.... यदेतद्हृदयं मनश्चैतत् ॥ (*brahmavidyāsādhanakṛtasarvātmabhāvaphalāvāptiṃ nāmadevādyācāryaparaṃparayā śrutyā avadyotyamānāṃ brahmavitpariṣadi atyaṃtaprasiddhāṃ upalabhamānā mumukṣavaḥ adhunātanāḥ brahmajijñāsavaḥ anityāt sādhyasādhanalakṣaṇāt saṃsārāt ājīvabhāvādvyāvivṛtsavo vicārayaṃto 'nyonyaṃ pṛcchaṃti |.... yadetadhṛdayaṃ manaścaitat ‖*) (Ai. U. Śa. Bhā. 3-1) ⟨NOTE:340⟩

That the fruit called the state of being the Self of all is obtained by the means that is the knowledge of Brahman has been made clear by the tradition of teachers beginning with Vāmadeva and by the Śruti passages composed by them. Those who wish to be freed from impermanent saṃsāra, and those who desire to know Brahman, are questioning one another on this matter: "Who is the Self? How is it to be worshipped?" and so on. The divine knowledge of Vāmadeva is praised because even for such questions the utterances of seers like Vāmadeva are the authority. The meaning is that when the divine knowledge "I am Brahman" arises, as Vāmadeva knew it, people are freed from saṃsāra just as Vāmadeva was.

ब्रह्म वा इदमग्र आसीत्तदात्मानमेवावेत् । अहं ब्रह्मास्मीति । तस्मात्तत्सर्वमभवत्तद्यो यो देवानां प्रत्यबुध्यत स एव तदभवत्तथर्षिणां तथा मनुष्याणां तद्भैतत्पश्यन्नृषिर्वामदेवः प्रतिपेदेऽहं मनुरभवं सूर्यश्चेति । तदिदमप्येतर्हि य एवं वेदाहं ब्रह्मास्मीति स इदं सर्वं भवति॥ (*brahma vā idamagra āsīttadātmānamevāvet | ahaṃ brahmāsmīti | tasmāttatsarvamabhavattadyo yo devānāṃ pratyabudhyata sa eva tadabhavattatharṣiṇāṃ tathā manuṣyāṇāṃ tadbhaitatpaśyannṛṣirvāmadevaḥ pratipede 'haṃ manurabhavaṃ sūryaśceti | tadidamapyetarhi ya evaṃ vedāhaṃ brahmāsmīti sa idaṃ sarvaṃ bhavati‖*) (Bṛ. U. 1-4-10)

At first, before creation, only Brahman existed. It gained the knowledge of the Self, "I am Brahman." Therefore it attained the state of being the Self of all and became all-pervading. Among the deities too, whoever gained this knowledge attained this same state. The seers and men too gained perfection by this means in the form of knowledge. Vāmadeva also, having gained this same knowledge of Brahman, declared his state of being the Self of all: "I was Manu, I was Sūrya." Thus the nature of the knowledge of Brahman is taught: all who gain the knowledge "I am Brahman" attain perfection in the form of being the Self of all.
Vāmadeva's utterance "I was Manu" is quoted in the Vedānta Sūtra, and there it has given occasion for a statement of meaning in the inquiry into the nature of the knowledge of Brahman.
शास्त्रदृष्टि तपदेशो नामदेववत् (*śāstradṛṣṭi tapadeśo nāmadevavat*) (Bra. Sū. 1-1-31)

In the passage of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad अनेन जीवेनात्मनानुप्रविश्य नामरूपे व्याकरवाणीति (*anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇīti*) (Chā. U. 6-3-2), "entering all places in the form of the living self, he becomes modified by the respective names and forms." The relation of identity between Brahman and the deity that holds there is understood in the same way from Vāmadeva's utterances such as "I was Manu." But here it has also given room to the debate between dualism and non-dualism, whether the individual nature of the living self is one with the principle of Brahman or distinct from it. This question is not now in hand. The main point is that the divine knowledge of Vāmadeva is praised in all the Śruti passages, and all the Śrutis, the Brāhmaṇas and the rest, somewhere or other quote and discuss the utterance of this great seer.

ತ್ವಾಂ ಹ್ಯಗ್ನೇ ವಿಂಶತಿರಷ್ಟೃತಿಜಗತೀಧೃತಯ ಆದ್ಯಾ ಉಪಾದ್ಯಾಶ್ಚತಸ್ರೋ ವಾರುಣ್ಯಶ್ಚ ನಾ ಎಂದು

ಅತಿಜಗತೀಛಂದಸ್ಕವು ; ಎಪ್ಪತ್ತೆರಡು ಅಕ್ಷರಗಳುಳ್ಳ ಮೂರನೆಯ ಋಕ್ಕು ಧೃತಿ ಎಂಬ ಛಂದಸ್ಸಿನದು ; ನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ
ಋಕ್ಕಿನಿಂದ ಸೂಕ್ತದ ಕೊನೆಯವರೆಗಿನ ಹದಿನೇಳು ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳೂ ತ್ರಿಷ್ಟುಪ್ ಛಂದಸ್ಕವು. ಮಂಡಲಾದಿಷ್ಟಾಗ್ನೇಯಂ—ಮಂಡಲದ ಪ್ರಾರಂಭದ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ಅಗ್ನಿ ದೇವತಾಕವಾಗಿರುವುದು ಎಂಬ ಪರಿಭಾಷೆಗನುಸಾರವಾಗಿ
ಈ ಮೊದಲನೆಯ ಪೂರ್ತಾ ಸೂಕ್ತಕ್ಕೆ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ದೇವತೆಯು ; ಎರಡನೆಯ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಿಂದ ನಾಲ್ಕು ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳಿಗೆ
(೨-೫ ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳಿಗೆ) ಅಗ್ನಿ ಅಥವಾ ವರುಣನು ದೇವತೆಯು. ಸೂಕ್ತವಿನಿಯೋಗವು ಲೈಂಗಿಕವು. ಈ ಸೂಕ್ತದ
ಮೊದಲನೆಯ ಋಕ್ಕನ್ನು ಅಧ್ಯಾಯೋತ್ಸರ್ಜನ ಉಪಾಕರ್ಮಹೋಮಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಮಂಡಲಹೋಮಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ವಿನಿಯೋಗಿ
en: वामदेव्ये चतुर्थे मंडले पंचानुवाकाः । तत्र प्रथमेऽनुवाके दश
सूक्तानि । तेषु त्वां ह्यग्ने सदमिदिति विंशत्यृचं प्रथमं सूक्तं । अत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । त्वां ह्यग्ने विंशतिरष्ट्यतिजगतीधृतय आद्या उपाद्याश्चतस्रो
वारुण्यश्च वेति । मंडलद्रष्टा वामदेवऋषिः । प्रथमा चतुःषष्ट्यक्षराष्टिर्द्वितीया
सप्तदश त्रिष्टुभः । कृत्सस्य सूक्तस्य मंडलादिष्टाग्नेयमिति परिभाषयाग्निर्देवता
द्वितीयाद्याश्चतस्रो वरुणदेवत्या वा ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥ आद्याध्यायो
अनुवादवु—वामदेवऋषिदृष्टवाद ई नाल्कनॆय मंडलदल्लि ऐदु अनुवाकगळिरुववु
अवुगळल्लि मॊदलनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि हत्तु सूक्तगळिरुववु. आ हत्तु सूक्तगळल्लि त्वां ह्यग्ने
सदमित् ऎंब ई सूक्तवु मॊदलनॆयदु. इदरल्लि इप्पत्तु ऋक्कुगळिरुववु. अनुक्रमणिकॆयल्लि—
त्वां ह्यग्ने विंशतिरष्टृतिजगतीधृतय आद्या उपाद्याश्चतस्रो वारुण्यश्च ना ऎंदु
हेळिरुवुदु. ई सूक्तक्कॆ मंडलद्रष्टृवाद वामदेवने ऋषियु ; ई सूक्तदल्लि अरवत्तुनाल्कु
अक्षरगळुळ्ळ मॊदलनॆय ऋक्कु अष्टि ऎंब छंदस्सिनदु ; ऐवत्तॆरडु अक्षरगळुळ्ळ ऎरडनॆय ऋक्कु
अतिजगतीछंदस्कवु ; ऎप्पत्तॆरडु अक्षरगळुळ्ळ मूरनॆय ऋक्कु धृति ऎंब छंदस्सिनदु ; नाल्कनॆय
ऋक्किनिंद सूक्तद कॊनॆयवरॆगिन हदिनेळु ऋक्कुगळू त्रिष्टुप् छंदस्कवु. मंडलादिष्टाग्नेयं—मंडलद प्रारंभद सूक्तवु अग्नि देवताकवागिरुवुदु ऎंब परिभाषॆगनुसारवागि
ई मॊदलनॆय पूर्ता सूक्तक्कॆ अग्नियु देवतॆयु ; ऎरडनॆय ऋक्किनिंद नाल्कु ऋक्कुगळिगॆ
(२-५ ऋक्कुगळिगॆ) अग्नि अथवा वरुणनु देवतॆयु. सूक्तविनियोगवु लैंगिकवु. ई सूक्तद
मॊदलनॆय ऋक्कन्नु अध्यायोत्सर्जन उपाकर्महोमगळल्लि मंडलहोमक्कागि विनियोगि

In the fourth maṇḍala, called Vāmadevya, there are five anuvākas. In the first anuvāka there are ten sūktas. Among them the first is the sūkta of twenty ṛks beginning त्वां ह्यग्ने सदमित् (*tvāṃ hyagne sadamit*). He cites the Anukramaṇikā: the twenty ṛks beginning त्वां ह्यग्ने (*tvāṃ hyagne*) are in the metres aṣṭi, atijagatī and dhṛti, and the Vāruṇī ṛks are mentioned there. ⟨NOTE:341⟩. The seer is Vāmadeva, the seer of the maṇḍala. The first ṛk has sixty-four syllables and is aṣṭi; the second has fifty-two syllables and is atijagatī; the third has seventy-two syllables and is dhṛti. By the rule of unspecified cases, the seventeen from the fourth are triṣṭubh. The deity of the whole sūkta is Agni, by the rule that the first sūkta of a maṇḍala is Āgneya; or else the second and the following four ṛks have Varuṇa as deity. The use of the sūkta is that stated in the Liṅga (laiṅgika). The first ṛk is employed in the Maṇḍala-ādi homa in connection with the Adhyāya-upākaraṇa. ⟨NOTE:342⟩

Anuvāda (Kannada, within the same block): In this fourth maṇḍala, seen by the Vāmadeva Ṛṣi, there are five anuvākas. In the first anuvāka there are ten sūktas. Of these ten, this sūkta beginning त्वां ह्यग्ने सदमित् (*tvāṃ hyagne sadamit*) is the first. It has twenty ṛks. In the Anukramaṇikā it is stated: त्वां ह्यग्ने विंशतिरष्टृतिजगतीधृतय आद्या उपाद्याश्चतस्रो वारुण्यश्च ना (*tvāṃ hyagne viṃśatiraṣṭṛtijagatīdhṛtaya ādyā upādyāścatasro vāruṇyaśca nā*). The seer of this sūkta is Vāmadeva, the seer of the maṇḍala. In this sūkta the first ṛk, of sixty-four syllables, is in the metre called aṣṭi; the second, of fifty-two syllables, is in atijagatī; the third, of seventy-two syllables, is in the metre called dhṛti; and the seventeen ṛks from the fourth to the end of the sūkta are in triṣṭubh. According to the rule मंडलादिष्टाग्नेयं (*maṃḍalādiṣṭāgneyaṃ*), that the opening sūkta of a maṇḍala has Agni as deity, Agni is the deity of this whole first sūkta; for the four ṛks from the second (ṛks 2-5) the deity is Agni or Varuṇa. The use of the sūkta is that stated in the Liṅga. It is the custom to employ the first ṛk of this sūkta for the Maṇḍala-homa in the Adhyāyotsarjana and Upākarma homas.

kn: ತ್ವಾಂ ಹ್ಯಗ್ನೇ ಸದಮಿತ್ಸಮನ್ಯವೋ ದೇವಾಸೋ ದೇವಮರತಿಂ ನೈರಿರ
ref: त्वां ह्य॑ग्ने॒ सद॒मित्स॑म॒न्यवो॑ दे॒वासो॑ दे॒वम॑र॒तिं न्ये॑रि॒र इति॒ क्रत्वा॑ न्येरि॒रे।
अम॑र्त्यं यजत॒ मर्त्ये॒ष्वा दे॒वमादे॑वं जनत॒ प्रचे॑तसं॒ विश्व॒मादे॑वं जनत॒ प्रचे॑तसम्

kn: ತ್ವಾಂ । ಹಿ । ಅಗ್ನೇ । ಸದಂ । ಇತ್ । ಸಮನ್ಯವಃ । ದೇವಾಸಃ । ದೇವಂ । ಅರತಿಂ । ನಿಏರಿರೇ ।
ಅಮರ್ತ್ಯಂ । ಯಜತ । ಮರ್ತ್ಯೇಷು । ಆ । ದೇವಂ । ಆದೇವಂ । ಜನತ । ಪ್ರಚೇತಸಂ । ವಿಶ್ವಂ ।
ನಾಮದೇವಃ ಸ್ತೌತಿ । ಹೇ ಅಗ್ನೇ ಸಮನ್ಯವಃ । ಮನ್ಯುಃ ಸ್ಪರ್ಧಾ । ತಯಾ ಸಹ ವರ್ತಮಾನಾಃ । ಸ್ವಸಮಾನೈಃ ಸ್ಪರ್ಧಾಮಾನಾ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ । ದೇವಾಸೋ ದೇವನಶೀಲಾ ಇಂದ್ರಾದಯೋ
ದೇವಾ ದೇವಂ ದ್ಯೋತಮಾನಮರತಿಂ ಶೀಘ್ರಂ ಗಂತಾರಂ ತ್ವಾಂ ಸದಮಿತ್ಸದೈವ ನೈರಿರೇ ಹಿ। ಸ್ಪರ್ಧಾನಿಮಿತ್ತೇ ಯುದ್ಧೇ ಪ್ರೇರಯಂತಿ ಖುಲು । ಇತಿಶಬ್ದೋ ಹೇತ್ವರ್ಥಃ । ಯಸ್ಮಾದ್ದೇವಾಸ್ತಾಂ
ಯುದ್ದಾರ್ಥಂ ನಿತರಾಂ ಪ್ರೇರಯಂತಿ ತಸ್ಮಾದ್ಯಜಮಾನಾಃ ಕ್ರತ್ವಾ ಸ್ತುತಿಲಕ್ಷೇನ ಕರ್ಮಣಾ ನೈರಿರೇ ।
ಯಜ್ಞಕರ್ಮಣಿ ದೇವಾನ್ಹವಿಃ ಪ್ರಾಪಯಿತುಂ ದೇವಾನಾಹ್ವಾತುಂ ಚ ತ್ವಾಂ ನಿತರಾಂ ಪ್ರೇರಯಂತಿ
ಖಲು । ಯಜತ ಯಜನೀಯ ಹೇ ಅಗ್ನೇ ಅಮರ್ತ್ಯಂ ಮರಣಧರ್ಮರಹಿತಮಾ ಸರ್ವತೋ ದೇವಂ
ದ್ಯೋತಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಚೇತಸಂ । ಪ್ರಕೃಷ್ಟಂ ಕರ್ಮವಿಷಯಂ ಚೇತೋ ಜ್ಞಾನಂ ಯಸ್ಯ ತಾದೃಶಂ ತ್ವಾಂ
ಮರ್ತ್ಯೇಷು ಯಾಗಂ ಕುರ್ವಾಣೇಷು ಮನುಷ್ಯೆಷ್ವಾದೇವನಾಗಂತಾರಂ ಜನತ । ದೇವಾ ಹವಿಃಶ್ರಪಣಾರ್ಥಮಜನಯನ್ । ತಥಾ ಪ್ರಚೇತಸಂ ಕರ್ಮಾಭಿಜ್ಞಮಾದೇವಂ ತತ್ತದ್ಯಜ್ಞೆಷ್ಟಾಗಂತಾರಂ ತ್ವಾಂ
ವಿಶ್ವಂ ಜನತ । ಯುಗಪನ್ನಾನಾದೇಶವರ್ತಿಷು ಯಜ್ಞೇಷು ಯೌಗಪದ್ಯೇನ ಹವಿರಾನಯನಾರ್ಥಂ
ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಂ ದೇವಾ ಅಕುರ್ವನ್ ॥ ನೈರಿರೇ । ಈರ ಗತೌ । ಲಿಟ ಮಂತ್ರತ್ವಾದಾನ್ನು ಭವತಿ । ಸಹೇತಿ
ಯೋಗವಿಭಾಗಾತ್ಸಮಾಸಃ । ಹಿಯೋಗಾದನಿಘಾತಃ । ಕ್ರತ್ವಾ । ಜಸಾದಿಷು ಛಂದಸಿ ವಾವಚನಮಿತಿ

en: Vāmadeva praises. O Agni, the gods are समन्यवः (*samanyavaḥ*): manyu is rivalry, so "existing together with it", that is, rivalling their own equals. The gods, the Indras and others who are of shining nature, ever (सदमित् (*sadamit*), "always") urge you, who are shining and swift-going (अरतिं (*aratiṃ*)), into battle that arises from rivalry. The word इति (*iti*) has the sense of cause: because the gods urge you strongly for battle, therefore the sacrificers also urge you strongly, by क्रत्वा (*kratvā*), the act of praise, in the sacrificial rite, to convey the oblation to the gods and to call the gods. O adorable Agni, you who are immortal, free from the nature of death, shining on every side, प्रचेतसं (*pracetasaṃ*), one whose mind or knowledge concerning rites is excellent: the gods generated you as one who comes to men who perform sacrifice (मर्त्येषु (*martyeṣu*)), आदेवं (*ādevaṃ*), to cook the oblation. Likewise, knowing the rites and coming to this and that sacrifice, the gods made you विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*), pervading, so as to bring the oblation at one and the same time to sacrifices taking place in different regions.

kn: ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ । ನೈರಿರೇ ಹಿ—(ಯುದ್ಧಕ್ಕಾಗಿ) ಪ್ರೇರಿಸುತ್ತಾರಲ್ಲವೇ ? (ಅದೇ ಕಾರಣದಿಂದ ಯಜ್ಞಕರ್ತರೂ
ಸಹ) । ಕ್ರತ್ವಾ—ಸ್ತುತಿರೂಪವಾದ ಕರ್ಮದಿಂದ । ನೈರಿರೇ—(ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಕರೆಯುವುದಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ನಿನ್ನನ್ನು)
ದೇವಂ—ಪ್ರಕಾಶಮಾನನೂ । ಪ್ರಚೇತಸಂ—ಪ್ರಕೃಷ್ಟವಾದ ಜ್ಞಾನವುಳ್ಳವನೂ ಆದ ನಿನ್ನನ್ನು । ಮರ್ತ್ಯೇಷು—
ಯಾಗಮಾಡತಕ್ಕ ಮಾನವರಲ್ಲಿ । ಆದೇವಂ—ಸರ್ವದಾ ಆಗಮಿಸುವವನೆಂದು । ಜನತ—(ದೇವತೆಗಳು) ತಿಳಿ
ದಿದ್ದಾರೆ । ಪ್ರಚೇತಸಂ- - ಕರ್ಮವಿಷಯಕವಾದ ಜ್ಞಾನವುಳ್ಳವನೂ । ಆದೇವಂ—ಆಯಾ ಯಜ್ಞಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಬರುವ
ವನೂ ಆದ ನಿನ್ನನ್ನು । ವಿಶ್ವಂ ಜನತ—ವಿಶ್ವವ್ಯಾಪಿಯಾಗಿ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಯಾಗಗಳಲ್ಲೂ ಭಾಗವಹಿಸುವಂತೆ ಮಾಡಿದರು.
en: - नैरिरे हि (*nairire hi*)—urge (to battle), do they not? (for that very reason the sacrificers also)
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—by the act in the form of praise
- नैरिरे (*nairire*)—urge (you, in order to call the gods)
- आदेवं (*ādevaṃ*)—one who comes for each sacrifice, you
- विश्वं जनत (*viśvaṃ janata*)—made you pervade the world and take part in all sacrifices

kn: ಎಲೈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ, ಪರಸ್ಪರ ಸ್ಪರ್ಧಿಸತಕ್ಕ ದೇವತೆಗಳು ಪ್ರಕಾಶಮಾನನೂ ಶೀಘ್ರಸಂಚಾರಿಯೂ ಆದ
ನಿನ್ನನ್ನು ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ ಯುದ್ಧಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಪ್ರೇರಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ ಅದೇ ಕಾರಣದಿಂದ ಯಜ್ಞಕರ್ತರೂ ಸಹ ಸ್ತುತಿರೂಪ
ವಾದ ಕರ್ಮದಿಂದ ದೇವತೆಗಳ ಆಹ್ವಾನಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ನಿನ್ನನ್ನು ಪ್ರೇರಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಯಜ್ಞಾರ್ಹನಾದ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ, ಮರಣ
ರಹಿತನೂ ಸರ್ವತ್ರ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಮಾನನೂ ಪ್ರಕೃಷ್ಟವಾದ ಜ್ಞಾನವುಳ್ಳವನೂ ಆದ ನಿನ್ನನ್ನು ಯಾಗಮಾಡತಕ್ಕ ಮಾನವ
ರಲ್ಲಿರುವವನೆಂದು ದೇವತೆಗಳು ತಿಳಿದಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಕರ್ಮವಿಷಯಕವಾದ ಜ್ಞಾನವುಳ್ಳವನೂ ಆಯಾ ಯಜ್ಞಕ್ಕಾಗಿ
ಆಗಮಿಸುವವನೂ ಆದ ನಿನ್ನನ್ನು ಆ ದೇವತೆಗಳು ವಿಶ್ವವ್ಯಾಪಿಯಾಗಿ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಯಾಗಗಳಲ್ಲೂ ಭಾಗವಹಿಸುವಂತೆ
en: O Agni, the gods, rivalling one another, always urge you, who are shining and swift-moving, to battle. For that same reason the sacrificers too, by the act in the form of praise, urge you for the calling of the gods. O Agni, worthy of sacrifice, the gods have known you, deathless, shining everywhere and possessed of excellent knowledge, as dwelling among men who perform sacrifice. You, who have knowledge concerning rites and who come for each sacrifice, those gods made all-pervading, so as to take part in all sacrifices.

kn: Since the emuolus gods ever excite you, Agni, who is a deity swift
of motion, (to contest), therefore do (your worshippers) urge you by their
devotions (to bring the deities to their sacrifices) : adorable Agni, they (the
deities), have generated you, immortal, divine, all-wise, as the present
divinity among men : they have generated you as the all-wise deity.
en: Since the emuolus gods ever excite you, Agni, who is a deity swift of motion, (to contest), therefore do (your worshippers) urge you by their devotions (to bring the deities to their sacrifices) : adorable Agni, they (the deities), have generated you, immortal, divine, all-wise, as the present divinity among men : they have generated you as the all-wise deity. ⟨NOTE:343⟩
notes: emuolus printed; probably "emulous"

kn: ಈ ಸೂಕ್ತದ ಮೊದಲನೆಯ ಋಕ್ಕು ಅಷ್ಟಿ ಎಂಬ ಛಂದಸ್ಸಿನದು. ಎರಡನೆಯ ಋಕ್ಕು ಅತಿಜಗತೀ
ಮತ್ತು ಮೂರನೆಯ ಋಕ್ಕು ಧೃತಿ ಎಂಬ ಛಂದಸ್ಸಿನದು. ಈ ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳಲ್ಲಿರುವ ವೈಶಿಷ್ಟ್ಯವೇನೆಂದರೆ—ಋಕ್ಕಿನ
ಪೂರ್ವಾರ್ಧದ ಮತ್ತು ಉತ್ತರಾರ್ಧದ (ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಮೂರು ಅರ್ಧಗಳಿದ್ದ ಪಕ್ಷದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೊನೆಯ ಅರ್ಧದ) ಕೊನೆಯ
ಒಂದೆರಡು ಶಬ್ದಗಳು ಎರಡಾವರ್ತಿ ಪಠಿತವಾಗಿರುವವು, ಎಂದರೆ ಒಂದೇಕಡೆ ಎರಡಾವರ್ತಿ ಪಠಿತವಾಗಿರುವುದಿಲ್ಲ
ಇವುಗಳ ಮಧ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದೆರಡು ಶಬ್ದಗಳಿರುವವು. ಹೇಗೆಂದರೆ ನೈರಿರ ಇತಿ ಕ್ರತ್ವಾ ನೈರಿರೇ ಎಂಬಲ್ಲಿ ನೈರಿರೇ
ಎಂಬ ಶಬ್ದವು ಎರಡಾವರ್ತಿ ಪಠಿತವಾಗಿರುವುದು. ಈ ಶಬ್ದಗಳ ಮಧ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಇತಿ ಕ್ರತ್ವಾ ಎಂಬ ಪದಗಳಿರುವವು.
ಇದರಂತೆ ಪ್ರಚೇತಸಂ ವಿಶ್ವಮಾದೇವಂ ಜನತ ಪ್ರಚೇತಸಂ ಎಂಬಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಹೀಗೆಯೇ ಇರುವುದು. ಈ ರೀತಿ
ಇರುವ ಪ್ರಾಸವು ಪಠಿಸುವಾಗ ಶುಕ್ರಾವ್ಯವಾಗಿರಲೆಂಬ ಉದ್ದೇಶದಿಂದ ಉಪಯೋಗಿಸಲ್ಪಡುವುದು. ಆದರೆ ಭಾಷ್ಯ
ಕಾರರು ಎರಡಾವರ್ತಿ ಪಠಿತವಾಗಿರತಕ್ಕ ಶಬ್ದಗಳಿಗೆ ಕೆಲವು ಸಂದರ್ಭಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕವಾದ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ವಿವರಿಸಿರು
ವರು. ಈ ವಿಧವಾದ ಛಂದಸ್ಸು ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರಾಸವು ದಿವೋದಾಸನ ಪುತ್ರನಾದ ಪರುಚ್ಛೇಪನೆಂಬ ಋಷಿದೃಷ್ಟವಾದ
ಸೂಕ್ತಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಎಂದರೆ ಪ್ರಥಮ ಮಂಡಲದ ೧೨೭-೧೩೯ ನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ವಿಶೇಷವಾಗಿ ಕಂಡು ಬರುವುದು
ಸಮನ್ಯವಃ—ಮನ್ಯುಃ ಸ್ಪರ್ಧಾ । ತಯಾ ಸಹ ವರ್ತಮಾನಾಃ । ಸ್ವಸಮಾನೈಃ ಸ್ಪರ್ಧಮಾನಾ
ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ । ಮನ್ಯುಶಬ್ದಕ್ಕೆ, ಕ್ರೋಧ, ಕೋಪ ಎಂಬರ್ಥವಿದ್ದರೂ ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾಷ್ಯಕಾರರು ಸ್ಪರ್ಧೆ (ಹೋರಾಟ)
ಎಂದು ಅರ್ಥಮಾಡಿ ತಮ್ಮ ತಮ್ಮಲ್ಲಿ ಪರಸ್ಪರವಾಗಿ ಸ್ಪರ್ಧಿಸತಕ್ಕವರು ಎಂದು ಅರ್ಥವಿವರಣೆ ಮಾಡಿರುವರು.
ಈ ಶಬ್ದವು ದೇವಾಸಃ ಎಂಬ ಪದಕ್ಕೆ ವಿಶೇಷಣವಾಗಿರುವುದು.
ಅರತಿಂ—ಶೀಘ್ರಂ ಗಂತಾರಂ । ಯ ಗತೌ ಎಂಬ ಧಾತುವಿನಿಂದ ನಿಷ್ಪನ್ನವಾದ ಈ ಶಬ್ದಕ್ಕೆ ವೇಗವಾದ
ಇತಿ—ಇತಿ ಎಂಬ ಶಬ್ದವು ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಹೇತ್ವರ್ಥದಲ್ಲಿ (ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಎಂಬ ಅರ್ಥದಲ್ಲಿ) ಉಪಯೋಗಿಸಲ್ಪಟ್ಟರು
ಪ್ರ ಚೇತಸಂ- ಪ್ರಕೃಷ್ಟಂ ಕರ್ಮವಿಷಯಂ ಚೇತೋ ಜ್ಞಾನಂ ಯಸ್ಯ । ಕರ್ಮಾಭಿಜ್ಞಂ ।
ವಿಶ್ವಂ ಜನತ—ದೇಶದ ನಾನಾಭಾಗಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅನೇಕ ಯಜಮಾನರು ಏಕಕಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಯಜ್ಞ ಮಾಡಿದರೂ
ಅವುಗಳಲ್ಲೆಲ್ಲಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ತನ್ನ ಅನೇಕ ರೂಪಗಳಿಂದ ಏಕಕಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಯಜ್ಞಕರ್ಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾಗವಹಿಸಿ ಅದನ್ನು
ಯಶಸ್ವಿಯಾಗಿ ನೆರವೇರಿಸುವ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯವು ಅಗ್ನಿಗೆ ಇರುವುದು. ಇಂತಹ ವಿಶ್ವವ್ಯಾಪಕವಾದ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯವು ಅಗ್ನಿಗೆ
ದೇವತೆಗಳಿಂದ ಉಂಟಾಯಿತು ಎಂದು ಈ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ವಾಮದೇವಋಷಿಯು ವಿವರಿಸಿದ್ದಾನೆ.
en: The first ṛk of this sūkta is in the metre called aṣṭi. The second ṛk is in atijagatī and the third in the metre called dhṛti. The peculiarity of these ṛks is that one or two words at the end of the first half and of the second half of the ṛk (of the last half, where a ṛk has three halves) are recited twice. That is, they are not recited twice in one place; one or two words stand between them. For example, in नैरिर इति क्रत्वा नैरिरे (*nairira iti kratvā nairire*) the word नैरिरे (*nairire*) is recited twice, and between these words stand the words इति क्रत्वा (*iti kratvā*). It is the same in प्रचेतसं विश्वमादेवं जनत प्रचेतसं (*pracetasaṃ viśvamādevaṃ janata pracetasaṃ*). Such rhyme is used with the purpose that it be pleasant to the ear when recited. The Bhāṣyakāra, however, in some places explains a separate meaning for the words recited twice. This kind of metre and rhyme is found especially in the sūktas seen by the seer Paruchchhepa, son of Divodāsa, that is, in sūktas 127-139 of the first maṇḍala.

समन्यवः—मन्युः स्पर्धा । तया सह वर्तमानाः । स्वसमानैः स्पर्धमाना इत्यर्थः । (*samanyavaḥ—manyuḥ spardhā | tayā saha vartamānāḥ | svasamānaiḥ spardhamānā ityarthaḥ |*) Although the word manyu has the meanings of anger and wrath, here the Bhāṣyakāra explains it as spardhā (contest) and gives the meaning "those who rival one another among themselves." This word is an adjective of the word देवासः (*devāsaḥ*).
अरतिं—शीघ्रं गंतारं । (*aratiṃ—śīghraṃ gaṃtāraṃ |*) For this word, formed from the root य गतौ (*ya gatau*), the meaning "one who has swift movement" is given.
इति (*iti*)—The word इति (*iti*) is used here in the sense of cause (the sense "therefore").

kn: ಸ ಭ್ರಾತರಂ ವರುಣಮಗ್ನ ಆ ವವೃತ್ಸ್ವದೇವಾಂ ಅಚ್ಛಾಸುಮತೀ ಯಜ್ಞವನಸಂ ಜ್ಯೇಷ್ಠಂ ಯಜ್ಞವನಸಂ ।
ref: स भ्रात॑रं॒ वरु॑णमग्न॒ आ व॑वृत्स्व दे॒वाँ अच्छा॑ सुम॒ती य॒ज्ञव॑नसं॒ ज्येष्ठं॑ य॒ज्ञव॑नसम्।
ऋ॒तावा॑नमादि॒त्यं च॑र्षणी॒धृतं॒ राजा॑नं चर्षणी॒धृत॑म्

kn: ಸಃ । ಭ್ರಾತರಂ । ವರುಣಂ । ಅಗ್ನೇ । ಆ । ವವೃತ್ಸ್ವ । ದೇವಾನ್ । ಅಚ್ಛ । ಸುಮತೀ । ಯಜ್ಞವನಸಂ । ಜ್ಯೇಷ್ಠಂ । ಯಜ್ಞವನಸಂ ॥
ಹೇ ಅಗ್ನೇ ಸ ತಾದೃಶಸ್ತ್ವಂ ಭ್ರಾತರಮೇಕಸ್ಥಾನವಾಸೇನ ಭ್ರಾತರಂ ವರುಣಂ । ವೃಣೋತ್ಯುದಕಮಿತಿ ವರುಣಃ । ತಂ ದೇವಂ ಯಜ್ಞವನಸಂ ಯಜ್ಞೈರ್ವನನೀಯೈರ್ಹವಿರ್ಭಿಃ ಸಂಭಜನೀಯಂ

ಯಜ್ಞವನಸಂ ಚ ಯಜ್ಞಸ್ಯ ಸಂಭಕ್ತಾರಂ ಜ್ಯೇಷ್ಠಮತಿಶಯೇನ ಪ್ರಶಸ್ಯಮೃತಾವಾನಮಪಾಂ ಸ್ವಾಮಿತಯೋದಕವಂತಂ ಸತ್ಯವಂತಂ ನಾ ಆದಿತ್ಯಮದಿತೇಃ ಪುತ್ರಂ ಚರ್ಷಣೀಧೃತಂ ಮನುಷ್ಯಾಣಾಮುದಕಪ್ರದಾನೇನ ಧಾರಕಂ ಸುಮತೀ ಶೋಭನಬುದ್ಧ್ಯಾ ಹೇತುನಾ ಚರ್ಷಣೀಧೃತಂ ಚರ್ಷಣಿಭಿರ್ವಿದ್ವದ್ಭಿರ್ಧೃತಂ ರಾಜಾನಂ ರಾಜಂತಂ ಏತಾದೃಶಂ ವರುಣಂ ದೇವಂ ದೇವಾನ್ ದೇವನಶೀಲಾನ್ ಸ್ತೋತ್ಥನಚ್ಛಾಭ್ಯಾ ವವೃತ್ಸ್ವ । ಆವರ್ತಯ । ಅಭಿಮುಖೀಕುರು ॥ ವವೃತ್ಸ್ವ । ವೃತು ವರ್ತನೇ । ಲೋಟ
ಬಹುಲಂ ಛಂದಸೀತಿ ವಿಕರಣಸ್ಯ ಶ್ಲುಃ । ನಿಘಾತಃ । ಸುಮತೀ । ಮಂತ್ರೇ ವೃಷೇತ್ಯಾದಿನಾ ಕ್ತಿನ್ನುದಾತ್ತಃ । ಸುಪಾಂ ಸುಲುಗಿತಿ ತೃತೀಯಾಯಾಃ ಪೂರ್ವಸವರ್ಣದೀರ್ಘಃ । ಏಕಾದೇಶಸ್ವರಃ । ಜ್ಯೇಷ್ಠಂ ।
ಪ್ರಶಸ್ಯಸ್ಯೆಷ್ಟನಿ ಜ್ಯ ಚೇತಿ ಜ್ಯಾದೇಶಃ । ನಿತ್ವಾದಾದ್ಯುದಾತ್ತಃ । ಏಕಾದೇಶಸ್ವರಃ । ಯಜ್ಞವನಸಂ ।
ವನ ಷಣ ಸಂಭಕ್ತೌ । ಕರ್ಮಕರ್ತರಿ ಚಾಸುನ್ಪ್ರತ್ಯಯಃ । ಗತಿಕಾರಕಯೋರಪಿ ಪೂರ್ವಪದಪ್ರಕೃತಿಸ್ವರತ್ವಂ ಚೇತಿ ಪೂರ್ವಪದಸ್ವರಃ ॥

en: O Agni, being such, turn towards us the gods' Varuṇa, a brother by dwelling in one place. Varuṇa is so called because he covers (vṛṇoti) the water. He is the god to be shared in by sacrifices, that is, by oblations that are to be enjoyed; a sharer in the sacrifice; the eldest, most praiseworthy; ṛtāvan, possessing water as lord of the waters, and truthful; Āditya, son of Aditi; supporter of men (carṣaṇi) by giving them water; sumatī, "with good intelligence", as the reason; supported by the carṣaṇis, the learned; a king, shining. Turn such a Varuṇa towards the gods, the shining ones, by praise and by our wish. Vavṛtsva is from vṛtu in the sense of turning, in the imperative.
Grammar of the words of the verse (the Grammar section carries it).

kn: ಅಗ್ನೇ—ಎಲೈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ । ಸಃ—ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧವಾದ ನೀನು । ಭ್ರಾತರಂ—ನಿನಗೆ ಭ್ರಾತೃರೂಪನೂ । ಯಜ್ಞ
ಧ್ಯಾನರೂಪದಲ್ಲಿ ಧೃತನಾಗಿರುವವನೂ । ರಾಜಾನಂ—ವಿಶ್ವಕ್ಕೆ ಪ್ರಭುವಾದವನೂ ಆದ । ವರುಣಂ—ವರುಣ
ದೇವನನ್ನು । ದೇವಾನ್—ಸ್ತೋತೃಗಳಿಗೆ । ಅಚ್ಛ—ಅಭಿಮುಖವಾಗಿ । ಆ ವವೃತ್ಸ್—ಕರೆದುಕೊಂಡು ಬಾ.
en: - भ्रातरं (*bhrātaraṃ*)—one who is a brother to you
- यज्ञवनसं (*yajñavanasaṃ*)—one who takes a share in the sacrifice
- चर्षणीधृतं (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaṃ*)—one held in meditation in the minds of men

kn: ಎಲೈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ, ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧನಾದ ನೀನು ನಿನಗೆ ಭ್ರಾತೃರೂಪನೂ ಹವಿಸ್ಸುಗಳಿಂದ ಪೂಜಿಸಲ್ಪಡುವವನೂ
ಯಜ್ಞದಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾಗವನ್ನು ವಹಿಸುವವನೂ ಪ್ರಶಸ್ಯನೂ ಸತ್ಯಾತ್ಮನೂ ಅದಿತಿಪುತ್ರನೂ ಮಾನವರಧಾರಕನೂ, ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠ
ವಾದ ಬುದ್ಧಿಯಿಂದ ಮಾನವರ ಮನಸ್ಸಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನರೂಪದಲ್ಲಿ ಧೃತನಾಗಿರುವವನೂ, ವಿಶ್ವಕ್ಕೆ ಪ್ರಭುವಾದವನೂ ಆದ
en: O Agni, you, the well-known, bring Varuṇa, who is a brother to you, worshipped with oblations, a sharer in the sacrifice, praiseworthy, truthful, son of Aditi, supporter of men, held with excellent intelligence in meditation in the minds of men, and lord of the universe, to face the worshippers.

kn: Bring to the presence of the worshippers, Agni, your brother Varuna, as a participator of the sacrifice, with a willing mind, the elder participator of the sacrifice ; the ruler of the water, the Aditya, the supporter of men, the sovereign venerated by mankind.
en: Bring to the presence of the worshippers, Agni, your brother Varuna, as a participator of the sacrifice, with a willing mind, the elder participator of the sacrifice ; the ruler of the water, the Aditya, the supporter of men, the sovereign venerated by mankind.

kn: ಈ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಆದಿತಿಪುತ್ರನಾದ ವರುಣದೇವನನ್ನು ಯಜ್ಞಕ್ಕೆ ಕರತರಬೇಕೆಂದು ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ಪ್ರಾರ್ಥಿಸ
ಭ್ರಾತರಂ—ವರುಣನು ಅಗ್ನಿಗೆ ಹೇಗೆ ಸಹೋದರನು ಎಂದರೆ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೂ, ಇಂದ್ರಾದಿದೇವತೆಗಳೂ,
ವರುಣನೂ ಸಹೋದರರೆಂದು ಹೇಳುವುದು ಯುಕ್ತವಾಗಿದೆ. ಈ ವಿಷಯವು—
ಅಷ್ಟೌ ಪುತ್ರಾಸೋ ಅದಿಶೇಃ । ಯೇ ಜಾತಾಸ್ತನ್ವಃಪರಿ । ದೇವಾ ಉಪಪ್ರೈತ್ಸಸ್ತಭಿಃ । ಪರಾಮಾರ್ತಾಂಡಮಾಸ್ಯತ್ । ಸಪ್ತಭಿಃ ಪುತ್ರೈರದಿತಿಃ। ಉಪಪ್ರೈತ್ಸೂರ್ವ್ಯಂ ಯುಗಂ । ಪ್ರಜಾಯೈ
ವರುಣಶ್ಚ । ಧಾತಾ ಚಾರ್ಯಮಾ ಚ । ಅಗಂಶಶ್ಚ ಭಗಶ್ಚ । ಇಂದ್ರಶ್ಚ ವಿವಸ್ವಾಗ್
ಅದಿತಿದೇವಿಗೆ—ಮಿತ್ರ, ವರುಣ, ಧಾತಾ, ಅರ್ಯಮಾ, ಅಂಶ, ಭಗ, ಇಂದ್ರ, ವಿವಸ್ವಾನಾ ಎಂದು ಎಂಟು ಮಂದಿ
ಪುತ್ರರೆಂದು ಹೇಳಿದೆ. ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ಸ್ವರ್ಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಆದಿತ್ಯ ಅಥವಾ ಸೂರ್ಯರೂಪದಿಂದ ಇರುವನು ಎಂದು ಅನೇಕ
ಕಡೆ ಹೇಳಿರುವುದು. ಆದಿತ್ಯನು ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ಮೂರು ರೂಪಗಳಲ್ಲೊಂದು ಎಂಬ ವಿಷಯವು ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧವಾಗಿರುವುದು.
ಆದುದರಿಂದ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ಮತ್ತು ವರುಣನು ಸಹೋದರರು ಎಂಬ ವಿಷಯವನ್ನು ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಭ್ರಾತರಂ ಎಂಬ ಶಬ್ದದಿಂದ
en: In this Ṛk Agni is asked to bring Varuṇa, son of Aditi, to the sacrifice.
Bhrātaram: how is Varuṇa a brother to Agni? It is proper to say that Agni, Indra and the other gods, and Varuṇa are brothers. This matter is stated in:

अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदिशेः । ये जातास्तन्वःपरि । देवा उपप्रैत्सस्तभिः । परामार्तांडमास्यत् । सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिः। उपप्रैत्सूर्व्यं युगं । प्रजायै मृत्यनेतत् । परामार्तांडमा भरदिति । ताननुक्रमिष्यामः । मित्रश्च वरुणश्च । धाता चार्यमा च । अगंशश्च भगश्च । इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग् श्चेत्येते ॥ (*aṣṭau putrāso adiśeḥ | ye jātāstanvaḥpari | devā upapraitsastabhiḥ | parāmārtāṃḍamāsyat | saptabhiḥ putrairaditiḥ| upapraitsūrvyaṃ yugaṃ | prajāyai mṛtyanetat | parāmārtāṃḍamā bharaditi | tānanukramiṣyāmaḥ | mitraśca varuṇaśca | dhātā cāryamā ca | agaṃśaśca bhagaśca | iṃdraśca vivasvāg ścetyete ‖*) (Kṛ. Ā. 1-13-2)

Aditi is said to have eight sons: Mitra, Varuṇa, Dhātā, Aryamā, Aṃśa, Bhaga, Indra and Vivasvān. In many places it is said that Agni is in heaven as Āditya or the sun, and it is well known that Āditya is one of Agni's three forms. Therefore the fact that Agni and Varuṇa are brothers is indicated here by the word bhrātaram.

Pracetasam: one whose cognition (cetas, jñāna) concerning ritual action is excellent; that is, one who knows rites well. The meaning is: one who has proper understanding in sacrificial performances and the like.

Viśvaṃ janata: although many sacrificers in various parts of the country perform sacrifices at the same time, Agni, in his many forms, takes part in the sacrificial act in all of them at once and has the power to bring it to successful completion. In this Ṛk the seer Vāmadeva explains that this all-pervading power came to Agni from the gods.

kn: ಸಖೇ ಸಖಾಯಮಭ್ಯಾ ನವೃತ್ಸ್ವಾಶುಂ ನ ಚಕ್ರಂ ರಥ್ಯೇವ ರಂಹ್ಯಾಸ್ಮಭ್ಯಂ
ಆಗ್ನೇ ಮೃಳೀಕಂ ವರುಣೇ ಸಚಾ ವಿದೋ ಮರುತ್ಸು ವಿಶ್ವಭಾನುಷು ।
ತೋಕಾಯ ತುಜೇ ಶುಶುಚಾನ ಶಂ ಕೃಧ್ಯಸ್ಮಭ್ಯಂ ದಸ್ಮ ಶಂ ಕೃಧಿ ॥ ೩ ॥
ref: सखे॒ सखा॑यम॒भ्या व॑वृत्स्वा॒शुं न च॒क्रं रथ्ये॑व॒ रंह्या॒स्मभ्यं॑ दस्म॒ रंह्या॑।
अग्ने॑ मृळी॒कं वरु॑णे॒ सचा॑ विदो म॒रुत्सु॑ वि॒श्वभा॑नुषु।
तो॒काय॑ तु॒जे शु॑शुचान॒ शं कृ॑ध्य॒स्मभ्यं॑ दस्म॒ शं कृ॑धि

kn: ಸಖೇ । ಸಖಾಯಂ । ಅಭಿ । ಆ । ವವೃತ್ಸ್ವ । ಆಶುಂ । ನ । ಚಕ್ರಂ । ರಥ್ಯಾ ಇವ । ರಂಹ್ಯಾ ।
ಅಗ್ನೇ । ಮೃಳೀಕಂ । ವರುಣೇ । ಸಚಾ । ವಿದಃ । ಮರುತ್ಸು । ವಿಶ್ವಭಾನುಷು ।
ತೋಕಾಯ । ತುಜೇ । ಶುಶುಚಾನ । ಶಮ್ । ಕೃಧಿ । ಅಸ್ಮಭ್ಯಂ । ದಸ್ಮ । ಶಂ । ಕೃಧಿ ॥ ೩ ॥
ಪ್ರವರ್ಜ್ಯೇಽಭಿಷ್ಟವ ಉತ್ತರಸ್ಮಿನ್ಪಟಲೇ ಸಖೇ ಸಖಾಯಮಿತ್ಯೇಷಾ । ಸೂತ್ರಿತಂ ಚ । ಸಖೇ
ಸಖಾಯಮಭ್ಯಾ ವವೃತ್ಸೋದ್ವರ್ಷ ಊ ಷು ಣ ಊತಯೇ । ಆ. ೪-೭ । ಇತಿ ॥
ಸಖೇ ಸಖಿಭೂತ ದಸ್ಮ ದರ್ಶನೀಯ ಹೇ ಅಗ್ನೇ ತ್ವಂ ತವ ಸಖಾಯಂ ವರುಣಮಸ್ಮಭ್ಯಮಸ್ಮದರ್ಥಮಾ ವವೃತ್ಸ್ವ । ಅಭಿಮುಖೀಕುರು । ತತ್ರ ದೃಷ್ಟಾಂತಃ । ರಂಹ್ಯಾ ರಂಹಣೇ ಗಮನೇ

ಸಾಧುಭೂತೌ ರಥ್ಯೇವ ರಥೇ ಯೋಜಿತಾವಶ್ವಾ ಯಥಾಶುಂ ಶೀಘ್ರಗಂತೃ ಚಕ್ರಂ ಲಕ್ಷ್ಯದೇಶಂ ಪ್ರತ್ಯಭಿಮುಖೀಕುರುತಸ್ತದ್ವತ್ । ಹೇ ಅಗ್ನೇ ಸಚಾ ತವ ಸಹಾಯೇ ವರುಣೇ ಮೃಳೀಕಂ ಸುಖಕರಂ ಹವಿರ್ವಿದಃ । ಲಬ್ಧವಾನಸಿ । ತಥಾ ವಿಶ್ವಭಾನುಷು ಸರ್ವತೋ ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತತೇಜಸ್ಕೇಷು ಮರುತ್ತು ಸುಖಕರಂ
ದೀಪ್ಯಮಾನ ಹೇ ಅಗ್ನೇ ತೋಕಾಯ । ತುಜ್ಯತೇ ಪೀಡ್ಯತೇಽನೇನ ಮಾತಾ ಗರ್ಭವಾಸೇನೇತಿ ತೋಕಂ
ಪುತ್ರಃ । ತಸ್ಮೈ ತುಜೇ । ಗಚ್ಛತ್ಯನೇನಾನ್ಯಂ ಪಿತೇತಿ ತುಕ್ ಪೌತ್ರಃ । ತಸ್ಮೈ ಶಂ ಸುಖಂ ಕೃಧಿ ।
ಕುರು । ದಸ್ಮ ದರ್ಶನೀಯ ಹೇ ಅಗ್ನೇ ಅಸಭ್ಯಂ ಶಂ ಕೃಧಿ । ಸುಖಂ ಕುರು ॥ ರಥ್ಯೇವ । ರಥಸ್ಯೆಮಾವಿತ್ಯರ್ಥೇ ರಥಾದ್ಯದಿತಿ ಯತ್ । ಸುಪಾಂ ಸುಲುಗಿತಿ ಸುಪೋ ಡಾದೇಶಃ । ರಂಹ್ಯಾ । ರಂಹಶಬ್ದಾತ್ತತ್ರ

en: In the Pravargya, in the later paṭala of the Abhiṣṭava, the verse *sakhe sakhāyam* is used. It is also stated in the sūtra: सखे सखायमभ्या ववृत्सोद्वर्ष ऊ षु ण ऊतये (*sakhe sakhāyamabhyā vavṛtsodvarṣa ū ṣu ṇa ūtaye*) (Ā. 4-7).

O Agni, friend, beautiful one, turn your friend Varuṇa towards us, for our sake. The example: as two good-going horses yoked to a chariot bring the swift wheel (chariot) facing the goal. O Agni, with Varuṇa, your companion, you have obtained the pleasing oblation; likewise with the Maruts, whose splendour pervades everywhere, you have obtained it. The sense: you have offered in the rites of Agni-Varuṇa and Agni-Māruta. O shining Agni, to toka, the son (so called because the mother is troubled (tujyate) by him in dwelling in the womb), to tuj, that is tuk, the grandson (by whom the father goes elsewhere), make happiness. O beautiful Agni, make happiness for us. Remaining grammatical notes omitted.

kn: ಸಖೇ—ಸಖಿಭೂತನಾದವನೂ । ದಸ್ಮ—ದರ್ಶನೀಯನೂ ಆದ ಎಲೈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ । ರಂಹ್ಯಾ—ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠವಾದ
ಪ್ರದೇಶಕ್ಕೆ ಒಯ್ಯುವಂತೆ) । ಸಖಾಯಂ—ನಮ್ಮ ಸಖಿಭೂತನಾದ ವರುಣನನ್ನು । ಅಸ್ಮಭ್ಯಂ—ನಮ್ಮ ಪ್ರಯೋಜನ
ಕ್ಕಾಗಿ । ಆ ವವೃತ್ಸ್ಯ—ಕರೆದುಕೊಂಡು ಬಾ । ಅಗ್ನೇ—ಎಲೈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ । ವರುಣೇ ಸಚಾ—ವರುಣನೊಡನೆ ।
ಎಲೈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ । ತೋಕಾಯ—ನಮ್ಮ ಪುತ್ರರಿಗೂ । ತುಜೇ—ಪೌತ್ರರಿಗೂ । ಶಂ—ಸುಖವನ್ನು । ಕೃಧಿ-ಉಂಟು
ಮಾಡು । ದಸ್ಮ—ಆಕರ್ಷಕವಾದ ರೂಪವುಳ್ಳ ಎಲೈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ । ಅಸ್ಮಭ್ಯಂ—ನಮಗೆ । ಶಂ—ಸುಖವನ್ನು ।
en: - सखे (*sakhe*)—O one who is a friend
- चक्रं न (*cakraṃ na*)—as they carry the chariot (to a fixed place)
- मरुत्तु (*maruttu*)—with the Maruts (also you have obtained)

kn: ಸಖಿಭೂತನೂ, ದರ್ಶನೀಯನೂ ಆದ ಎಲೈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ, ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠವಾದ ಸಂಚಾರವುಳ್ಳ ಅಶ್ವಗಳು ಶ್ರೀಘ್ರಗಾಮಿ
ಯಾದ ರಥವನ್ನು ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟವಾದ ಪ್ರದೇಶಕ್ಕೆ ಒಯ್ಯುವಂತೆ ನಮ್ಮ ಸಖಿಭೂತನಾದ ವರುಣನನ್ನು ನಮ್ಮ ಪ್ರಯೋ
ಜನಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಶೀಘ್ರವಾಗಿ ಕರೆದುಕೊಂಡು ಬಾ. ಎಲೈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ, ನೀನು ವರುಣನೊಡನೆಯೂ, ಸರ್ವತ್ರವ್ಯಾಪ್ತ
ವಾದ ತೇಜಸ್ಸುಳ್ಳ ಮರುತ್ತುಗಳೊಡನೆಯೂ ಸುಖಕರವಾದ ಹವಿಸ್ಸುಗಳನ್ನು ಹೊಂದಿದ್ದೀಯೆ. ಪ್ರಕಾಶಮಾನನಾದ
ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ, ನಮ್ಮ ಪುತ್ರರಿಗೂ, ಪೌತ್ರರಿಗೂ, ನಮಗೂ ಸುಖವನ್ನುಂಟುಮಾಡು.
en: O Agni, friend and beautiful one, as horses of excellent movement carry the swift chariot to a fixed place, bring quickly our friend Varuṇa for our purpose. O Agni, you have obtained pleasing oblations with Varuṇa and with the Maruts of all-pervading splendour. O shining Agni, make happiness for our sons, our grandsons and ourselves.

kn: Friendly and beautiful (Agni), bring your friend (Varuna) to our presence, as two strong horses conyey the swift chariot along the road to Vol. 17 [43]
its goal : you receive, Agni, the gratifying (oblation) together with Varuna ,
and with the all-illumining Maruts : grant, brilliant Agni, happiness to
our sons and grandsons ; grant, beautiful Agni, happiness to ourselves.
en: Friendly and beautiful (Agni), bring your friend (Varuna) to our presence, as two strong horses conyey the swift chariot along the road to

its goal : you receive, Agni, the gratifying (oblation) together with Varuna , and with the all-illumining Maruts : grant, brilliant Agni, happiness to our sons and grandsons ; grant, beautiful Agni, happiness to ourselves.

kn: ಭಾಷ್ಯಕಾರರು ಈ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿರುವ ತೋಕಾಯ, ತುಜೇ ಎಂಬ ಶಬ್ದಗಳಿಗೆ ಅವಯವಾರ್ಥವನ್ನು ವಿವರಿಸಿ
ತೋಕಾಯ—ತುಜ್ಯತೇ ಪೀಡ್ಯತೇಽನೇನ ಮಾತಾ ಗರ್ಭವಾಸೇನೇತಿ ತೋಕಂ ಪುತ್ರಃ ತಸ್ಮೈ ।
ತುಜಧಾತುವಿಗೆ ಹಿಂಸೆಮಾಡು ಎಂದರ್ಥವಿರುವುದು. ಈ ಧಾತುವಿನಿಂದ ನಿಷ್ಪನ್ನವಾದ ತೋಕಶಬ್ದಕ್ಕೆ—ಪುತ್ರನು
ತಾಯಿಯ ಗರ್ಭವಾಸದಲ್ಲಿದ್ದಾಗಲೂ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರಸವಕಾಲದಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ತಾಯಿಗೆ ಹಿಂಸೆಯನ್ನುಂಟುಮಾಡುವವನಾದ್ದ
ತುಜೇ—ಗಚ್ಛತ್ಯನೇನಾನೃಣ್ಯಂ ಪಿತೇತಿ ತುಕ್ ಪೌತ್ರಃ । ತಸ್ಮೈ । ತುಕ್ ಎಂದರೆ ಪೌತ್ರನು,
ಮೊಮ್ಮಗನು. ಇವನಿಂದ ಎಂದರೆ ಇವನ ಜನನದಿಂದ (ತಂದೆ) ಎನಿಸಿದವನು ತನ್ನ ಋಣವನ್ನು ತೀರಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳು
ವನು, ಎಂದರೆ ಅನೃಣ (ಋಣವಿಲ್ಲದವನು) ನಾಗುವನು. ತೈ. ಸಂಹಿತೆಯಲ್ಲಿ—ಜಾಯಮಾನೋ ವೈ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಸ್ತ್ರಿಭಿರ್ಯಣವಾ ಜಾಯತೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಋಷಿಭ್ಯೋ ಯಜ್ಞೇನ ದೇವೇಭ್ಯಃ ಪ್ರಜಯಾ ಪಿತೃಭ್ಯ
ಏಷ ವಾ ಅನೃಣೋ ಯಃ ಪುತ್ರೀ ಯಜ್ವಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚಾರಿವಾಸೀ ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಿರುವುದು. ಎಂದರೆ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣನಾದ
ವನು ಹುಟ್ಟುವಾಗಲೇ ಮೂರು ವಿಧವಾದ ಋಣಗಳಿಂದ ಸಹಿತನಾಗಿ ಹುಟ್ಟುವನು. ಋಷಿಋಣ, ದೇವಋಣ,
ಪಿತೃಋಣಗಳೇ ಆ ಋಣಗಳು. ಅವುಗಳನ್ನು ತೀರಿಸುವ ಬಗೆ ಹೇಗೆಂದರೆ—ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯನಿಯಮದಿಂದ ಗುರುಕುಲ
ವಾಸಮಾಡುತ್ತಾ ವೇದಾಧ್ಯಯನ ಮಾಡಿದರೆ ಋಷಿಋಣವು ತೀರುವುದು. ಗೃಹಸ್ಥವಾಗಿ ಯಜ್ಞಯಾಗಾದಿಗಳನ್ನು
ಮಾಡುತ್ತಾ ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಸಂತೋಷಪಡಿಸಿದರೆ ದೇವಋಣವು ತೀರುವುದು. ವಿವಾಹಾನಂತರ ತನ್ನ ಧರ್ಮಪತ್ನಿ
ಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಜೋತ್ಪಾದನೆ ಮಾಡಿದರೆ ಪಿತೃಋಣವು ತೀರುವುದು. ಆದುದರಿಂದ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣನಾದವನು ಈ ಮೂರು
ಋಣಗಳನ್ನು ಮೇಲೆ ಹೇಳಿದ ರೀತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ತೀರಿಸಿದರೆ ಅವನು ಅನೃಣನೆನಿಸುವನು. ಪುತ್ರಪೌತ್ರಾದಿ ಸಂತತಿಯಿಂದ
ಮೇಲೆ ಹೇಳಿದ ಋಣಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದು ತೀರುವುದು. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದಲೇ ಪುತ್ರ ಮತ್ತು ಪೌತ್ರನು ತನ್ನ ತಂದೆಯನ್ನು
ಅನೃಣ-ಋಣರಹಿತನನ್ನಾಗಿ ಮಾಡುವನು ಎಂದು ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾಷ್ಯಕಾರರು ವಿವರಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ.
en: The commentator has explained the component meaning of the words toka and tuj in this Ṛk:

Tokāya: तुज्यते पीड्यतेऽनेन माता गर्भवासेनेति तोकं पुत्रः तस्मै । (*tujyate pīḍyate 'nena mātā garbhavāseneti tokaṃ putraḥ tasmai |*) The root tuj means "to harm". Of the word toka derived from it, the meaning is that since a son harms the mother both while in the womb and at the time of birth, the son is called toka.

Tuje: गच्छत्यनेनानृण्यं पितेति तुक् पौत्रः । तस्मै । (*gacchatyanenānṛṇyaṃ piteti tuk pautraḥ | tasmai |*) Tuk means the grandson. Through him, that is, through his birth, the father clears his debt, that is, becomes anṛṇa (free of debt). In the Tai. Saṃhitā it is said: जायमानो वै ब्राह्मणस्त्रिभिर्यणवा जायते ब्रह्मचर्येण ऋषिभ्यो यज्ञेन देवेभ्यः प्रजया पितृभ्य एष वा अनृणो यः पुत्री यज्वा ब्रह्मचारिवासी (*jāyamāno vai brāhmaṇastribhiryaṇavā jāyate brahmacaryeṇa ṛṣibhyo yajñena devebhyaḥ prajayā pitṛbhya eṣa vā anṛṇo yaḥ putrī yajvā brahmacārivāsī*) ⟨NOTE:344⟩. That is, a Brāhmaṇa is born with three kinds of debts: the debt to the seers, to the gods and to the fathers. They are repaid thus: by living in the teacher's house under the rule of brahmacarya and studying the Veda, the debt to the seers is repaid. By performing sacrifices as a householder and pleasing the gods, the debt to the gods is repaid. By begetting offspring in his lawful wife after marriage, the debt to the fathers is repaid. Therefore a Brāhmaṇa who repays these three debts in the manner stated is called anṛṇa. By offspring such as sons and grandsons, one of the debts mentioned is repaid. Hence the commentator explains here that son and grandson make their father anṛṇa, free of debt.
notes: ಯಣವಾ, ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚಾರಿವಾಸೀ printed; text seems garbled, no reference given

kn: ತ್ವಂ ನೋ ಅಗ್ನೇ ವರುಣಸ್ಯ ವಿದ್ವಾನ್ದೇವಸ್ಯ ಹೇಳೋs ವಯಾಸಿಸೀಷ್ಠಾಃ ।
ಯಜಿಷ್ಟೋ ವಹ್ನಿತಮಃ ಶೋಶುಚಾನೋ ವಿಶ್ವಾದ್ವೇಷಾಂಸಿ ಪ್ರ ಮುಮುಗ್ಧ್ಯಸ್ಮತ್ ॥ ೪ ॥
ref: त्वं नो॑ अग्ने॒ वरु॑णस्य वि॒द्वान्दे॒वस्य॒ हेळोऽव॑ यासिसीष्ठाः।
यजि॑ष्ठो॒ वह्नि॑तम॒ः शोशु॑चानो॒ विश्वा॒ द्वेषां॑सि॒ प्र मु॑मुग्ध्य॒स्मत्

kn: ತ್ವಂ । ನಃ । ಅಗ್ನೇ । ವರುಣಸ್ಯ । ವಿದ್ವಾನ್ । ದೇವಸ್ಯ । ಹೇಳಃ । ಅವ । ಯಾಸಿಸೀಷ್ಠಾಃ ।
ಯಜಿಷ್ಠಃ । ವಹ್ನಿತಮಃ । ಶೋಶುಚಾನಃ । ವಿಶ್ವಾ । ದ್ವೇಷಾಂಸಿ । ಪ್ರ । ಮುಮುಗ್ನಿ । ಅಸ್ಮತ್ ॥ ೪ ॥
ತ್ವಂ ನೋ ಅಗ್ನ ಇತ್ಯೇತದಾರಭ್ಯೇದಂ ಸೂಕ್ತಮುತ್ತರಾಣಿ ಸೂಕ್ತಾನಿ ಚ ಪ್ರಾತರನುವಾಕ
ಆಗ್ನೇಯೇ ಕ್ರತ್ ತ್ರೈಷ್ಟುಭೇ ಛಂದಸ್ಯಾಶ್ವಿನಶಸ್ತ್ರೇ ಚ ವಿನಿಯುಕ್ತಾನಿ । ಸೂತ್ರಿತಂ ಚ । ತ್ವಂ ನೋ
ಅಗ್ನೇ ವರುಣಸ್ಯ ವಿದ್ವಾನಿತ್ಯೇತತ್ಪೃಥ್ವೀನಿ ಚತ್ವಾರಿ । ಆ. ೪-೧೩ । ಇತಿ ॥ ಅವಭೃಥೇಷ್ಟಾಂ ಸ್ವಿಷ್ಟಕೃದರ್ಥೇಽಗ್ನಿವರುಣೌ ಯಷ್ಟವ್ಯಾ । ತತ್ರ ತ್ವಂ ನೋ ಅಗ್ನ ಇತಿ ದ್ವೇ ಯಾಜ್ಯಾನುವಾಕ್ಯೇ । ಸೂತ್ರಿತಂ
ಚ । ಅಗ್ನೀವರುಣೌ ಸ್ವಿಷ್ಟಕೃದರ್ಥೇ ತ್ವಂ ನೋ ಅಗ್ನೇ ವರುಣಸ್ಯ ವಿದ್ವಾನಿತಿ ದ್ವೇ । ಆ. ೬-೧೩ । ಇತಿ ॥
ಅಸ್ನಾತೋ ಯದ್ಯಗ್ನಿಹೋತ್ರಂ ಜುಹುಯಾತ್ತದಾಗ್ನಿ ವಾರುಣೀಷ್ಟಿಃ । ತಸ್ಯಾಮೇತೇ ಏವ ಯಾಜ್ಯಾನುವಾಕ್ಯೇ । ತದಾಹುರ್ಯ ಆಹಿತಾಗ್ನಿರಿತ್ಯುಪಕ್ರಮ್ಯಾನ್ನಾತಂ । ತಸ್ಯ ಯಾಜ್ಯಾನುವಾಕ್ಯೇ ತ್ವಂ ನೋ
ಅಗ್ನೇ ವರುಣಸ್ಯ ವಿದ್ವಾನ್ತ್ಸ ತ್ವಂ ನೋ ಅಗ್ನೇಽವಮೋ ಭವೋತೀ । ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ. ೭-೯ । ಇತಿ ॥
ಹೇ ಅಗ್ನೇ ವಿದ್ವಾನ್ ಸರ್ವಪುರುಷಾರ್ಥಸಾಧನೋಪಾಯಜ್ಞಸ್ತ್ವಂ ದೇವಸ್ಯ ದ್ಯೋತಮಾನಸ್ಯ
ವರುಣಸ್ಯ ಹೇಳಃ ಕ್ರೋಧಾನ್ ನೋಽಸ್ಮತ್ಸಂಬಧಿನೋ ವರುಣಕರ್ತೃಕಾನ್ಪಾಶಗ್ರಹಣಾನವ ಯಾಸಿಸೀಷ್ಠಾಃ । ಅಪನಯ । ಕಿಂಚ ಯಜಿಷ್ಟೋ ಯಷ್ಟೃತಮೋ ವಹ್ನಿತಮೋ ಹವಿಷಾಮತಿಶಯೇನ
ವೋಢಾ ಶೋಶುಚಾನೋಽತಿಶಯೇನ ದೀಪ್ಯಮಾನಸ್ತ್ವಂ ವಿಶ್ವಾ ಸರ್ವಾಣಿ ದ್ವೇಷಾಂಸಿ ಪಾಪಾನಿ
ದ್ವೇಷ್ಟಣಿ ರಜಾಂಸಿ ವಾ ಅಸ್ಮದಸ್ಮತ್ತಃ ಪ್ರ ಮುಮುಗ್ಧಿ । ಪ್ರಕರ್ಷೇಣ ಮೋಚಯ ॥ ಹೇಳಃ ।
ಹೇಡೃ ಅನಾದರೇ । ಕ್ವಿಪ್ । ಶಸಿ ರೂಪಂ । ಶಸಃ ಸುಸ್ತ್ಯಾದನುದಾತ್ತತ್ವೇ ಧಾತುಸ್ವರಃ । ಯಾಸಿಸೀಷ್ಠಾಃ । ಯಸೇರ್ಣ್ಯಂತಾದಾಶೀರ್ಲಿಜ್ । ಥಾಸಿ ಸೀಯುಡಾಗಮಃ । ಛಂದಸ್ಯುಭಯಥೇತಿ ಲಿಜಃ
ಮುಂಚತೇರ್ಲೋಟಿ ರೂಪಂ । ಬಹುಲಂ ಛಂದಸೀತಿ ಶಪಃ ಶ್ಲುಃ ॥

en: Beginning with त्वं नो अग्ने (*tvaṃ no agne*), this sūkta and the following sūktas are applied in the Prātaranuvāka, in the Āgneya kratu, in the Triṣṭubh section and in the Āśvina-śastra. It is stated in the sūtra: त्वं नो अग्ने वरुणस्य विद्वानित्येतत्पृथ्वीनि चत्वारि (*tvaṃ no agne varuṇasya vidvānityetatpṛthvīni catvāri*) (Ā. 4-13). In the avabhṛtheṣṭi, Agni and Varuṇa are to be sacrificed to for the Sviṣṭakṛt; there the two verses beginning त्वं नो अग्ने (*tvaṃ no agne*) are the yājyā and anuvākyā. The sūtra: अग्नीवरुणौ स्विष्टकृदर्थे त्वं नो अग्ने वरुणस्य विद्वानिति द्वे (*agnīvaruṇau sviṣṭakṛdarthe tvaṃ no agne varuṇasya vidvāniti dve*) (Ā. 6-13). If one unbathed offers the agnihotra, there is the Āgni-Vāruṇī iṣṭi; these same two are its yājyā and anuvākyā; so the Brāhmaṇa says, beginning "he who has set up the fire … unbathed": its yājyā and anuvākyā are त्वं नो अग्ने वरुणस्य विद्वान् (*tvaṃ no agne varuṇasya vidvān*) and स त्वं नो अग्नेऽवमो भवोती (*sa tvaṃ no agne 'vamo bhavotī*) (Ai. Brā. 7-9).

Meaning: O Agni, knowing the means of accomplishing all human aims, remove from us the wrath of the shining Varuṇa, the seizures by the noose caused by Varuṇa. Further, you, most worshipful, the best carrier of oblations, most brightly shining, release us utterly from all hatreds, that is, sins, the haters, or faults. Remaining notes concern grammar.

kn: ವರುಣಸ್ಯ—ವರುಣನ । ಹೇಳೆಃ—ಕ್ರೋಧವನ್ನು । ನಃ—ನಮ್ಮಿಂದ । ಅವ ಯಾಸಿಸೀಷ್ಠಾಃ—ತಪ್ಪಿಸಿ ದೂರ
ಮಾಡು । ಯಜಿಷ್ಠಃ—ಪೂಜ್ಯತಮನೂ । ವಹ್ನಿ ತಮಃ—ಹವಿಸ್ಸುಗಳನ್ನು ಅತಿಶಯವಾಗಿ ವಹಿಸುವವನೂ ॥
en: - वह्नि तमः (*vahni tamaḥ*)—greatest bearer of oblations
- द्वेषांसि (*dveṣāṃsi*)—sins in the form of enemies

kn: ಎಲೈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ, ಸರ್ವಜ್ಞನಾದ ನೀನು ದೇವತಾತ್ಮನಾದ ವರುಣನ ಕ್ರೋಧವನ್ನು ನಮ್ಮಿಂದ ತಪ್ಪಿಸಿ
ದೂರಮಾಡು. ಪೂಜ್ಯತಮನೂ, ಹವಿಸ್ಸಿನ ವಾಹಕನೂ, ಪ್ರಕಾಶಮಾನನೂ ಆದ ನೀನು ಸಮಸ್ತವಾದ ಪಾಪ
en: O Agni, you who are all-knowing, turn away from us the wrath of Varuṇa, who is the divine being. You who are most worthy of worship, the bearer of the oblation, and resplendent, release us from all sins and destroy them.

kn: May you, Agni, who are wise, avert from us the wrath of the divine Varuna : you are the most frequent sacrificer, the most diligent bearer (of oblations), the most resplendent, liberate us from all animosities.
en: May you, Agni, who are wise, avert from us the wrath of the divine Varuna : you are the most frequent sacrificer, the most diligent bearer (of oblations), the most resplendent, liberate us from all animosities.

kn: ಸ ತ್ವಂ ನೋ ಅಗ್ನೇಽವಮೋ ಭವೋತೀ ನೇದಿಷ್ಠೋ ಅಸ್ಯಾ ಉಷಸೋ
ಅವ ಯಕ್ಷ್ವ ನೋ ವರುಣಂ ರರಾಣೋ ವೀಹಿ ಮೃಳೀಕಂ ಸುಹವೋ
ref: स त्वं नो॑ अग्नेऽव॒मो भ॑वो॒ती नेदि॑ष्ठो अ॒स्या उ॒षसो॒ व्यु॑ष्टौ।
अव॑ यक्ष्व नो॒ वरु॑णं॒ ररा॑णो वी॒हि मृ॑ळी॒कं सु॒हवो॑ न एधि

kn: ಸಃ । ತ್ವಂ । ನಃ । ಅಗ್ನೇ । ಅವಮಃ । ಭವ । ಊತೀ । ನೇದಿಷ್ಠಃ । ಅಸ್ಯಾಃ । ಉಷಸಃ । ವಿಉಷ್ಟೌ ।
ಅವ । ಯಕ್ಷ್ವ । ನಃ । ವರುಣಂ । ರರಾಣಃ । ವೀಹಿ । ಮೃಳೀಕಂ । ಸುಹವಃ । ನಃ । ವಿಧಿ ॥ ೫ ॥
ಹೇ ಅಗ್ನೇ ಸ ತಾದೃಶಸ್ತ್ವಮೂತೀ ಊತ್ಯಾ ರಕ್ಷಣೇನ ನೋಽಸ್ಮಾಕಮವಮೋಽರ್ವಾಚೀನಃ

ಪ್ರತ್ಯಾಸನ್ನಃ ಸನ್ ಅಸ್ಯಾ ಉಷಸೋ ವ್ಯುಷ್ಟೌ ವ್ಯುಚ್ಛನೇ ಪ್ರಾತಃಕಾಲೇಽಗ್ನಿಹೋತ್ರಾದಿಕರ್ಮಸಿದ್ಧ್ಯರ್ಥಂ ನೇದಿಷ್ಟೋ ಭವ । ಅತಿಶಯೇನಾಸ್ಮದಂತಿಕಸ್ಥೋ ಭವ । ಯದ್ವಾ । ಊತ್ಯಾ ಗಮನೇನಾಸ್ಮಾಕಮವಮೋ ರಕ್ಷಕೋ ಭವ । ಕಿಂಚ ನೋಽಸ್ಮಾಕು ವರುಣಂ ವರುಣಕೃತಂ ಜಲೋದರಾದಿರೋಗಂ
ಆವಾರಕಂ ಪಾಪಂ ವಾ ಅವ ಯಕ್ಷ್ವ । ಅವಯಜ । ವಿನಾಶಯೇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ । ರರಾಣೋಽಸ್ಮದತ್ತೇ
ಸುಖಕರಮಿದಂ ಹವಿರ್ವೀಹಿ । ಭಕ್ಷಯ । ಕಿಂಚ ನೋಽಸ್ಮಾಕಂ ಸುಹವಃ ಶೋಭನಾಹ್ವಾನೋಪೇತ
ಐಧಿ । ಭವ ॥ ನೇದಿಷ್ಟಃ । ಅಂತಿಕಶಬ್ದಾ ದಿಷ್ಠನ್ಯಂತಿಕವಾಢಯೋರ್ನೆದಸಾಧಾವಿತಿ ನೇದ ಇತ್ಯಾದೇಶಃ।

ನಿತ್ತ್ವಾದಾದ್ಯುದಾತ್ತಃ । ರರಾಣಃ । ರಮತೇಃ ಕಾನಚಿ ಮಕಾರಲೋಪಶ್ಚಾಂದಸಃ । ಯದ್ವಾ । ರಾತೇರ್ಯಜ್ ಲುಕಿ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಯೇನ ಕಾನಚ್ । ಅಭ್ಯಸ್ತಾನಾಮಾದಿಃ । ಏಧಿ । ಅಸ್ತೇರ್ಲೋಟಿ ಧ್ವಸೋರೇದ್ಧಾವಭ್ಯಾಸಲೋಪಶ್ಚೇತಿ ಐ ಇತ್ಯಾದೇಶಃ । ತಸ್ಯಾಸಿದ್ಧತ್ವಾದ್ದು ಝಲ್ಭೋ ಹೇರ್ಧಿಃ । ನಿಘಾತಃ ॥

en: "O Agni, you, such as you are, by ऊत्या (*ūtyā*) (protection) become अवमः (*avamaḥ*) for us, that is, near and close at hand; at the dawning (व्युष्टौ (*vyuṣṭau*), the breaking) of this dawn, in the morning, for the accomplishment of rites such as the Agnihotra, be नेदिष्ठः (*nediṣṭhaḥ*), that is, be exceedingly close to us." Or else: "by coming (गमनेन (*gamanena*)) be our protector." Further: "वरुणं (*varuṇaṃ*) — the disease caused by Varuṇa, such as dropsy, or the sin that covers us — अव यक्ष्व (*ava yakṣva*), that is, अवयज (*avayaja*), destroy it." रराणः (*rarāṇaḥ*) means delighting in the oblation given by us. Or else: "you who bestow on the sacrificers the fruit they most desire, मृळीकं (*mṛḷīkaṃ*) …" (the sentence continues on the next page).

"… this pleasing (*sukhakaraṃ*) oblation, वीहि (*vīhi*), that is, eat. Further, be सुहवः (*suhavaḥ*), one who has a good invocation, for us: ऐधि (*aidhi*), that is, be." The rest of the block gives the grammar of नेदिष्टः (*nediṣṭaḥ*), रराणः (*rarāṇaḥ*) and एधि (*edhi*), which is given in the Grammar section.

kn: ಅಗ್ನೇ—ಎಲೈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ । ಸಃ ತ್ವಂ—ಅಂತಹ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧನಾದ ನೀನು । ನಃ—ನಮಗೆ । ಊತೀ—ನಿನ್ನ
ರಕ್ಷಣೆಯೊಡನೆ । ಅವಮಃ—ಪಕ್ಕದಲ್ಲಿದ್ದು । ಅಸ್ಯಾಃ ಉಷಸಃ—ಈ ಉಷಸ್ಸಿನ । ವ್ಯುಷ್ಟೌ—ಆವಿರ್ಭಾವದ
ಕಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ । ನೇದಿಷ್ಟಃ ಭವ—ನಮಗೆ ಸಾನ್ನಿಧ್ಯವನ್ನು ಕೊಡು । ನಃ—ನಮ್ಮಿಂದ । ವರುಣಂ—ವರುಣಕೃತವಾದ
ರೋಗಗಳನ್ನು । ಅವ ಯಕ್ಷ್ವಾ—ನಾಶಪಡಿಸು । ರರಾಣಃ—ಹವಿಸ್ಸುಗಳನ್ನು ಭೋಗಿಸುತ್ತಾ । ಮೃಳೀಕಂ—
ಸುಖಕರವಾದ ಈ ಹವಿಸ್ಸನ್ನು । ವೀಹಿ—ಭಕ್ಷಿಸು । ನಃ—ನಮಗೋಸ್ಕರ । ಸುಹವಃ—ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠವಾದ ಆಹ್ವಾನ
en: - व्युष्टौ (*vyuṣṭau*)—at the time of its manifestation
- नेदिष्टः भव (*nediṣṭaḥ bhava*)—grant us your presence

kn: ಎಲೈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ, ಅಂತಹ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧನಾದ ನೀನು, ನಿನ್ನ ರಕ್ಷಣೆಯೊಡನೆ ನಮ್ಮ ಪಕ್ಕದಲ್ಲಿದ್ದು ಈ ಉಷಸ್ಸಿನ
ಆವಿರ್ಭಾವದ ಕಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ನಮಗೆ ಸಾನ್ನಿಧ್ಯವನ್ನು ಕೊಡು. ವರುಣಕೃತವಾದ ರೋಗಗಳನ್ನು ನಮ್ಮಿಂದ ನಾಶಪಡಿಸು.
ಸುಖಕರವಾದ ಈ ಹವಿಸ್ಸನ್ನು ಭಕ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತಾ ರಮಿಸು. ನಮಗಾಗಿ ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠವಾದ ಆಹ್ವಾನವುಳ್ಳವನಾಗಿರು.
en: O Agni, you, so famed, be by our side with your protection and grant us your presence at the time of this dawn's manifestation. Destroy the diseases caused by Varuṇa, away from us. Delight in eating this pleasing oblation. Be one who has an excellent invocation for us.

kn: Agni, our preserver, be most nigh to us with your protection at the breaking of this dawn : deprecate V₄runa for us, and, propitiated (by our praise). feed upon the grateful (oblation), and be to us of auspicious invoca- tion.
en: Agni, our preserver, be most nigh to us with your protection at the breaking of this dawn : deprecate Varuna for us, and, propitiated (by our praise). feed upon the grateful (oblation), and be to us of auspicious invocation.

kn: ಅವರಕಂ ಪಾಪಂ ವಾ ವಿನಾಶಯೇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ । ಇಲ್ಲಿ ವರುಣಸಂಬಧವಾದ ಎಂದರೆ ವರುಣದೇವನ ಕೋಪದಿಂದ
ಉಂಟಾಗಬಹುದಾದ ಜಲೋದರ ಮುಂತಾದ ಮಹಾರೋಗಗಳನ್ನೂ ಅಥವಾ ನಮ್ಮನ್ನು ಆವರಿಸುವ ನಾನಾವಿಧ
ಪಾಪಗಳನ್ನೂ ನಾಶಮಾಡು ಎಂದು ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ಪ್ರಾರ್ಥಿಸಲಾಗಿದೆ. ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಜಲೋದರ (Dropsy) ಎಂದರೆ
ಶರೀರದಲ್ಲಿ ನೀರುತುಂಬಿಕೊಂಡು ಊದಿಕೊಳ್ಳುವ ಒಂದುವಿಧವಾದ ಮಹಾರೋಗವು. ಇದು ಜಲಕ್ಕೆ ಸಂಬಂಧ
ಪಟ್ಟಿರುವುದರಿಂದಲೂ ವರುಣನು ಜಾಲಾಧಿಪತಿಯೆಂದು ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧನಾಗಿರುವುದರಿಂದಲೂ ಈ ವಿಧವಾದರೋಗವು
ವರುಣನ ಆಗ್ರಹದಿಂದ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತವಾಗುವುದೆಂದು ನಂಬಿಕೆ. ಅಥವಾ ನೀರಿನ ಭಯ ಎಂದರೆ ನೀರಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಮುಳುಗಿ
ಸಾಯುವುದು ಸಹ ವರುಣನಿಂದಲೇ ಉಂಟಾಗಬಹುದು. ಇಂತಹ ಭಯಗಳನ್ನು ನಿವಾರಣೆಮಾಡಿ ಪಾಪಗಳನ್ನು
en: नः वरुणं अवयुक्ष—अस्माकं वरुणाकृतं जलोदरादिरोगान् अवरकं पापं वा विनाशयेत्यर्थः । (*naḥ varuṇaṃ avayukṣa—asmākaṃ varuṇākṛtaṃ jalodarādirogān avarakaṃ pāpaṃ vā vināśayetyarthaḥ |*) Here "connected with Varuṇa" means: destroy the great diseases such as dropsy that may arise from the anger of the god Varuṇa, or the many kinds of sin that envelop us; thus Agni is prayed to. Here jalodara (dropsy) is a kind of great disease in which the body fills with water and swells. Because it is connected with water, and because Varuṇa is famed as lord of the waters, it is believed that this kind of disease comes through Varuṇa's pressure. Or again, the fear of water, that is, death by drowning, may likewise come from Varuṇa (continued on the next page).
Such fears are to be removed and the sins destroyed: so the prayer is made.

kn: ಅಸ್ಯ ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠಾ ಸುಭಗಸ್ಯ ಸಂದೃಗ್ದೇವಸ್ಯ ಚಿತ್ರತಮಾ ಮರ್ತ್ಯೇಷು ।
ಶುಚಿ ಘೃತಂ ನ ತಪ್ತಮಘ್ನ್ಯಾಯಾಃ ಸ್ಪಾರ್ಹಾ ದೇವಸ್ಯ ಮಂಹನೇವ
ref: अ॒स्य श्रेष्ठा॑ सु॒भग॑स्य सं॒दृग्दे॒वस्य॑ चि॒त्रत॑मा॒ मर्त्ये॑षु।
शुचि॑ घृ॒तं न त॒प्तमघ्न्या॑याः स्पा॒र्हा दे॒वस्य॑ मं॒हने॑व धे॒नोः

kn: ಅಸ್ಯ । ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠಾ । ಸುಭಗಸ್ಯ । ಸಂದೃಕ್ । ದೇವಸ್ಯ । ಚಿತ್ರತಮಾ । ಮರ್ತ್ಯೇಷು ।
ಶುಚಿ । ಧೃತಂ । ನೃ । ತಪ್ತಂ । ಅಘ್ನ್ಯಾಯಾಃ । ಸ್ಪಾರ್ಹಾ । ದೇವಸ್ಯ । ಮಂಹನಾಇವ । ಧೇನೋಃ ॥
ಸುಭಗಸ್ಯ ಸುಧನಸ್ಯ ಸುಷ್ಟು ಭಜನೀಯಸ್ಯಾಗ್ನೇರ್ದೇವಸ್ಯ ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠಾತಿಶಯೇನ ಪ್ರಶಸ್ಯಾ
ಸಂದೃಕ್ ಸಂದೃಷ್ಟಿರ್ಮರ್ತ್ಯೇಷು ಚಿತ್ರತಮಾತಿಶಯೇನ ಚಾಯನೀಯಾ ಪೂಜನಿಯಾ ಭವತಿ । ಸ್ಮಾರ್ಹಾ
ಸರ್ವೈಃ ಸ್ಪೃಹಣೀಯಾ ಭವತಿ । ತತ್ರ ದೃಷ್ಟಾಂತಃ । ಯಥಾ ದೇವಸ್ಯ ಕ್ಷೀರಂ ಕಾಮಯಮಾನಸ್ಯ
ಪುರುಷಸ್ಯಾಘ್ನ್ಯಾಯಾ ಗೋಃ ಶುಚಿ ತೇಜೋಯುಕ್ತಂ ಘೃತಂ ಕ್ಷರಣಯುಕ್ತಂ ಸಪ್ತಂ ಕ್ಷೀರಂ
ಸ್ಪೃಹಣೀಯಂ ಭವತಿ । ತತ್ರೈವ ದೃಷ್ಟಾಂತಾಂತರಂ । ಯಥಾ ಗಾಂ ಭಿಕ್ಷಮಾಣಸ್ಯ ಮರ್ತ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಧೇನೋರ್ದೋಗ್ಧಾ ರ್ಯ ಗೋರ್ಮಂಹನೇವ । ಮಂಹತಿರ್ದಾನಕರ್ಮಾ । ದಾನಂ ಯಥಾ ಪ್ರಿಯಕರಂ ಭವತಿ
ತದ್ವತ್ ॥ ಸುಭಗಸ್ಯ । ಆದ್ಯುದಾತ್ತಂ ದ್ವ್ಯಚ್ಛಂದಸೀತ್ಯುತ್ತರಪದಾದ್ಯುದಾತ್ತತ್ವಂ । ಸ್ಮಾರ್ಹಾ । ಕರ್ಷಾತ್ವತೋ ಘಞತೋಂತ ಉದಾತ್ತಃ । ದೇವಸ್ಯ । ದೀವ್ಯತೀತಿ ದೇವಃ । ದೀವ್ಯತೇಃ ಕಾಂತ್ಯರ್ಥಸ್ಯ

en: Of the god Agni, सुभगस्य (*subhagasya*) — of good wealth, one who is to be well resorted to — the संदृक् (*saṃdṛk*) (sight, glance) is श्रेष्ठा (*śreṣṭhā*), exceedingly praiseworthy; among mortals it is चित्रतमा (*citratamā*), most to be honoured and worshipped, and it is स्पार्हा (*spārhā*), to be desired by all. An illustration follows. As, for a man who desires milk, the शुचि (*śuci*) (bright, full of splendour) घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*), the heated (सप्तं (*saptaṃ*)) milk of the अघ्न्या (*aghnyā*) cow that flows forth, is desirable; ⟨NOTE:345⟩ so too the sight is desired. There is a second illustration: as, for a mortal begging for a cow, the मंहना (*maṃhanā*) of a milch cow — मंहति (*maṃhati*) is a root meaning giving — ⟨NOTE:346⟩ that is, as a gift is pleasing, so is it. The rest gives accent and derivation of सुभगस्य (*subhagasya*), स्मार्हा (*smārhā*) and देवस्य (*devasya*) (Grammar section).
notes: ಸಪ್ತಂ printed; read as ತಪ್ತಂ "heated" (cf. verse ತಪ್ತಂ)
ಧೇನೋರ್ದೋಗ್ಧಾ ರ್ಯ ಗೋರ್ಮಂಹನೇವ garbled in print; sense taken as the gift of a milch cow

kn: ವಾದುದೂ । ಧೃತಂ—ಸುಸಂಸ್ಕೃತವಾದುದೂ ಆದ । ತಪ್ತಂ ನ—ಕ್ಷೀರವು ಹೇಗೆ ಹಿತಕರವಾದುದೋ (ಮತ್ತು) ।
ಧೇನೋಃ—ಧೇನುವಿನ । ಮಂಹನೇವ—ದಾನವು ಯಾವ ರೀತಿ ಹಿತಕರವಾಗಿರುವುದೋ ಹಾಗೆ । ಸುಭಗಸ್ಯ—
ವದಪೂಜ್ಯನಾನೂ । ಅಸ್ಯ ದೇವಸ್ಯ—ದೇವತಾತ್ಮನೂ ಆದ ಅಗ್ನಿಯ । ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠಾ—ಪ್ರಶಸ್ಯವಾದ । ಸಂದೃಕ್—
en: - देवस्य (*devasya*)—for a man who desires milk
- तप्तं न (*taptaṃ na*)—as the milk is beneficial (and)
- अस्य देवस्य (*asya devasya*)—of this Agni, the divine being
notes: ವದಪೂಜ್ಯನಾನೂ printed; garbled, read as ಪೂಜ್ಯನಾದವನೂ "worshipful"

kn: ಕ್ಷೀರವನ್ನಪೇಕ್ಷಿಸುವ ಪುರುಷನಿಗೆ ಗೋವಿನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಮಾನವಾದುದೂ, ಸುಸಂಸ್ಕೃತವಾದುದೂ ಆದ
ಕ್ಷೀರವು ಹೇಗೆ ಹಿತಕರವಾದುದೋ ಮತ್ತು ಧೇನುವಿನ ದಾನವು ಯಾವ ರೀತಿ ಹಿತಕರವಾದುದೋ ಹಾಗೆ ಪೂಜ್ಯ
ನಾದವನೂ, ದೇವತಾತ್ಮನೂ ಆದ ಅಗ್ನಿಯ ಪ್ರಶಸ್ಯವಾದ ದರ್ಶನವು ಮಾನವರಲ್ಲಿ ಪೂಜನೀಯವೂ, ಆದ್ಯತವೂ
en: As, for a man who desires milk, the bright and well prepared milk of the cow is beneficial, and as the gift of a milch cow is beneficial, so the praiseworthy sight of Agni, who is worshipful and the divine being, is worthy of worship among men and respected. ⟨NOTE:348⟩
notes: ಆದ್ಯತವೂ printed; read as ಆದೃತವೂ "respected" (as in Pratipadārtha)

kn: The glance of this auspicious deity, directed towards men, is most
excellent, most wonderful, acceptable (to all), as the pure warm butter
(from the milk) of the cow (is acceptable) to the deity ; as the gift of a
en: The glance of this auspicious deity, directed towards men, is most excellent, most wonderful, acceptable (to all), as the pure warm butter (from the milk) of the cow (is acceptable) to the deity ; as the gift of a milch-cow (is to a man).

kn: ದೇವಸ್ಯ ಅಸ್ಯ ಅಗ್ನೇಃ ತಾ ಪರಮಾ ಸತ್ಯಾ ತ್ರಿಃ ಜನಿಮಾನಿ ಸ್ಪಾರ್ಹಾ ಸಂತಿ—ದೇವತಾತ್ಮನಾದ
ಅಥವಾ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಮಾನನಾದ ಈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧವೂ ಸತ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕವೂ ಆದ ಮೂರು ಜನ್ಮಗಳು ಅಥವಾ ಉತ್ಪತ್ತಿ
ಸ್ವರೂಪಗಳು ಅತ್ಯಂತ ಆಕರ್ಷಣೀಯಗಳಾಗಿವೆ ಎಂದು ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಹೇಳಿದೆ. ಭಾಷ್ಯಕಾರರು--
ತ್ರೀಣಿ ಜಾನಾ ಪರಿ ಭೂಷಂತ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಸಮುದ್ರ ಏಕಂ ದಿವ್ಯೇಕಮಪ್ಪು ।
ದಿವಸ್ಪರಿ ಪ್ರಥಮಂ ಜಜ್ಞೇ ಅಗ್ನಿರಸ್ಮದ್ವಿತೀಯಂ ಪರಿ ಜಾವೇದಾಃ ।
ಎಂಬ ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳನ್ನು ದಾಹರಿಸಿ ಅಗ್ನಿಯ ಮೂರುವಿಧವಾದ ಸ್ವರೂಪಗಳನ್ನು ವಿವರಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಎಂದರೆ ಅಗ್ನಿಗೆ
ಮೂರು ರೂಪಗಳಿವೆ. ಸಮುದ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ಬಾಡಬಾನಲರೂಪದಿಂದಲೂ ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷದಲ್ಲಿ ವೈದ್ಯುತಾಗ್ನಿರೂಪದಿಂದಲೂ
(ಮಿಂಚಿನರೂಪ) ಸ್ವರ್ಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಆದಿತ್ಯರೂಪದಿಂದಲೂ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ಇರುವನೆಂದು ಈ ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಹೇಳಿದೆ. ಇದಲ್ಲದೆ
ಅಗ್ನಿಗೆ ಪವಮಾನ, ವನಸ್ಪತಿ, ಶುಚಿ ಎಂಬ ಮೂರು ವಿಧರೂಪಗಳು, ಪವಮಾನ, ಶುಚಿ, ಪಾವಕ ಎಂದೂ
ಅಥವಾ ಅಗ್ನಿ, ವೈಶ್ವಾನರ, ಜಾತವೇದಾಃ ಎಂದೂ ಮೂರು ವಿಧಗಳಾದರೂಪಗಳಿರುವುವೆಂದು ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಿಯಾಗಿದೆ.
ಈ ವಿಷಯದಲ್ಲಿ ವಿಸ್ತಾರವಾದ ವಿವರಣೆಯನ್ನು ಋ. ಸಂ. ಭಾಗ. ೮. ಪುಟ. 17-19ರಲ್ಲಿ ನೋಡಿ.
en: देवस्य अस्य अग्नेः ता परमा सत्या त्रिः जनिमानि स्पार्हा संति (*devasya asya agneḥ tā paramā satyā triḥ janimāni spārhā saṃti*) — It is said here that the three famed and true births, or forms of origin, of this Agni, the divine or resplendent one, are most attractive. The commentator cites the Ṛks
त्रीणि जाना परि भूषंत्यस्य समुद्र एकं दिव्येकमप्पु । (*trīṇi jānā pari bhūṣaṃtyasya samudra ekaṃ divyekamappu |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-95-3)

दिवस्परि प्रथमं जज्ञे अग्निरस्मद्वितीयं परि जावेदाः । (ऋ. सं. १०-४५-१) ऎंब ऋक्कुगळन्नु दाहरिसि अग्निय मूरुविधवाद स्वरूपगळन्नु विवरिसिद्दारॆ. ऎंदरॆ अग्निगॆ मूरु रूपगळिवॆ. समुद्रदल्लि बाडबानलरूपदिंदलू अंतरिक्षदल्लि वैद्युताग्निरूपदिंदलू (मिंचिनरूप) स्वर्गदल्लि आदित्यरूपदिंदलू अग्नियु इरुवनॆंदु ई ऋक्कुगळल्लियू हेळिदॆ. इदल्लदॆ अग्निगॆ पवमान, वनस्पति, शुचि ऎंब मूरु विधरूपगळु, पवमान, शुचि, पावक ऎंदू अथवा अग्नि, वैश्वानर, जातवेदाः (*divaspari prathamaṃ jajñe agnirasmadvitīyaṃ pari jāvedāḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 10-45-1) èṃba ṛkkugaḷannu dāharisi agniya mūruvidhavāda svarūpagaḷannu vivarisiddārè. èṃdarè agnigè mūru rūpagaḷivè. samudradalli bāḍabānalarūpadiṃdalū aṃtarikṣadalli vaidyutāgnirūpadiṃdalū (miṃcinarūpa) svargadalli ādityarūpadiṃdalū agniyu iruvanèṃdu ī ṛkkugaḷalliyū heḷidè. idalladè agnigè pavamāna, vanaspati, śuci èṃba mūru vidharūpagaḷu, pavamāna, śuci, pāvaka èṃdū athavā agni, vaiśvānara, jātavedāḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-45-1)

and explains the threefold forms of Agni. That is, Agni has three forms: these Ṛks too say that Agni exists in the sea as the submarine fire, in the atmosphere as lightning fire (the form of lightning), and in heaven as the sun. Besides this, it is well known that Agni has three forms called Pavamāna, Vanaspati and Śuci; or three forms called Pavamāna, Śuci and Pāvaka; or Agni, Vaiśvānara and Jātavedas. For a detailed explanation of this subject see Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 8, pp. 17-19.

kn: ತ್ರಿರಸ್ಯ ತಾ ಪರಮಾ ಸಂತಿ ಸತ್ಯಾ ಸ್ವಾಹರ್ಣ ದೇವಸ್ಯ ಜನಿಮಾನ್ಯಗ್ನೇಃ ।
ಅನಂತೇ ಅಂತಃ ಪರಿವೀತ ಆಗಾಚ್ಛುಚಿಃ ಶುಕ್ರೋ ಅಯೋರೋ ರೋರುಚಾನಃ ॥ ೭ ॥
ref: त्रिर॑स्य॒ ता प॑र॒मा स॑न्ति स॒त्या स्पा॒र्हा दे॒वस्य॒ जनि॑मान्य॒ग्नेः।
अ॒न॒न्ते अ॒न्तः परि॑वीत॒ आगा॒च्छुचि॑ः शु॒क्रो अ॒र्यो रोरु॑चानः

kn: ತ್ರಿಃ । ಅಸ್ಯ । ತಾ । ಪರಮಾ । ಸಂತಿ । ಸತ್ಯಾ । ಸ್ವಾರ್ಹಾ । ದೇವಸ್ಯ । ಜನಿಮಾನಿ । ಅಗ್ನೇಃ ।
ಅನಂತೇ । ಅಂತರಿತಿ । ಪರಿಽವೀತಃ । ಆ । ಅಗಾತ್ । ಶುಚಿಃ । ಶುಕ್ರಃ । ಅರ್ಯಃ । ರೋರುಚಾನಃ ॥೭॥
ಅಗ್ನೇರಗ್ನ್ಯಭಿಮಾನಿನೋಽಸ್ಯ ದೇವಸ್ಯ ತ್ರಿಸ್ತ್ರೀಣ್ಯಗ್ನಿವಾಯುಸೂರ್ಯಾತ್ಮನಾ ತ್ರೀಣಿ ತಾ ತಾನಿ
ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಾನಿ ಪರಮೋತ್ತಮಾನಿ ಸತ್ಯಾ ಯಥಾರ್ಥಭೂತಾನಿ ಜನಿಮಾನಿ ಜನ್ಮಾನಿ ಸ್ವಾಹರ್ಣಾ ಸರ್ವೈಃ ಸ್ಪೃಹಣೀಯಾನಿ ಸಂತಿ । ಯದ್ವಾ । ಅಗ್ನೇರೇವ ತ್ರೀಣಿ ಜನ್ಮಾನಿ ದಿವಸ್ಪರಿ ಪ್ರಥಮಂ ಜಜ್ಞೇ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ । ಋಗ್ವೇ.
೧೦-೪೫-೧ । ಇತಿ ತ್ರೀಣಿ ಜಾನಾ ಪರಿ ಭೂಷಂತ್ಯಸ್ಯ । ಋಗ್ವೇ. ೧-೯೫-೩ । ಇತ್ಯೇವಮಾದಿಷು ಮಂತ್ರೇಷು
ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಾನಿ । ಅನಂತೇಽಪರ್ಯಂತೇ ನಭಸ್ಯಂತರ್ಮಧ್ಯೆ ಸ್ವತೇಜಸಾ ಪರಿವೀತಃ ಪರಿವೇಷ್ಟಿತಃ ಶುಚಿಃ
ಸರ್ವಸ್ಯ ಶೋಧಕಃ ಶುಕ್ರೋ ದೀಪ್ತಿಯುಕ್ತೋಽತ ಏವ ರೋರುಚಾನೋ ಭೃಶಂ ದೀಪ್ಯಮಾನೋಽರ್ಯಃ
ಸ್ವಾಮಿಾ ತಾದೃಶೋ ದೇವ ಆಗಾತ್ । ಅಸ್ಮದೀಯಂ ಯಜ್ಞಂ ಪ್ರತ್ಯಾಗಚ್ಛತು ॥ ಸತ್ಯಾ । ಶೇಶ್ಬಂದಸಿ

ಬಹುಲಮಿತಿ ಶೇರ್ಲುಕ್ । ಪರಿವೀತಃ । ವ್ಯೇಞ್ ಸಂವರಣೇ । ಕರ್ಮಣಿ ಕ್ತಃ । ಯಜಾದಿತ್ವಾತ್ಸಂಪ್ರಸಾರಣಂ । ಗತಿರನಂತರ ಇತಿ ಗತೇಃ ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಸ್ವರತ್ವಂ । ಅರ್ಯಃ । ಋ ಗತೌ । ಅರ್ಯಃ ಸ್ವಾಮಿವೈಶ್ಯಯೋರಿತಿ ಯತ್ಪತ್ಯಯಾಂತೋ ನಿಪಾತಿತಃ । ಸ್ವಾಮಿನ್ಯಂತೋದಾತ್ತತ್ವಂ ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಮಿತ್ಯಂತೋದಾತ್ತತ್ವಂ ॥

en: Of this divine Agni, who presides over fire, the three — as fire, wind and sun — the famed, supreme, true (that is, real) births (जनिमानि (*janimāni*), जन्मानि (*janmāni*)) are desirable to all. Or else: Agni's own three births are famed in mantras such as दिवस्परि प्रथमं जज्ञे अग्निः (*divaspari prathamaṃ jajñe agniḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-45-1) and त्रीणि जाना परि भूषंत्यस्य (*trīṇi jānā pari bhūṣaṃtyasya*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-95-3). In the endless sky, in the middle, enveloped (परिवीतः (*parivītaḥ*)) by his own radiance, शुचिः (*śuciḥ*) (the purifier of all), शुक्रः (*śukraḥ*) (full of brightness), and therefore रोरुचानः (*rorucānaḥ*) (shining intensely), the अर्यः (*aryaḥ*) (lord), such a god, आगात् (*āgāt*): may he come to our sacrifice. The rest gives the grammar of सत्या (*satyā*), परिवीतः (*parivītaḥ*) and अर्यः (*aryaḥ*) (Grammar section).

kn: ದೇವಸ್ಯ—ದೇವತಾತ್ಮನಾದ । ಅಸ್ಯ ಅಗ್ನೇಃ—ಈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯ । ತಾ—ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧವಾದವೂ । ಪರಮಾ—
ಉತ್ತಮವಾದವೂ । ಸತ್ಯಾ—ಸತ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕವಾದವೂ ಆದ । ತ್ರಿಃ ಜನಿಮಾನಿ—ಮೂರು ಉತ್ಪತ್ತಿಸ್ವರೂಪಗಳೂ ಸಹ।
ಸ್ಪಾರ್ಹಾ ಸಂತಿ— ಅತ್ಯಂತ ಆಕರ್ಷಣೀಯಗಳಾಗಿವೆ । ಅನಂತೇ—ಅಂತರಹಿತವಾದ ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷದ । ಅಂತಃ—
en: - त्रिः जनिमानि (*triḥ janimāni*)—the three forms of origin also
- आगात् (*āgāt*)—may he come graciously to our sacrifice

kn: ದೇವತಾತ್ಮನಾದ ಈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧವಾದವೂ ಉತ್ತಮವಾದವೂ ಸತ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕವಾದವೂ ಆದ (ಅಗ್ನಿ,
ವಾಯು, ಸೂರಾತ್ಮಕಗಳಾದ) ಮೂರು ಉತ್ಪತ್ತಿಸ್ವರೂಪಗಳೂ ಸಹ ಅತ್ಯಂತ ಆಕರ್ಷಣೀಯಗಳಾಗಿವೆ. ಅಗಾಧ
ವಾದ ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷದ ಮಧ್ಯಭಾಗದಲ್ಲಿ ತನ್ನ ತೇಜಸ್ಸಿನಿಂದ ಆವೃತನಾಗಿಯೂ, ಶುದ್ಧಿಕಾರಕನಾಗಿಯೂ, ಕಾಂತಿಯುತ
ನಾಗಿಯೂ, ಅತ್ಯಂತ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಕನಾಗಿಯೂ, ಸ್ವಾಮಿಯೂ ಆದ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ನಮ್ಮ ಯಜ್ಞಕ್ಕೆ ದಯಮಾಡಲಿ.
en: The famed, supreme and true three forms of origin (as fire, wind and sun) of this Agni, the divine being, are also most attractive. In the middle of the unfathomable
atmosphere, enveloped by his own radiance, the purifier, endowed with brightness, shining intensely, the lord, Agni — may he come graciously to our sacrifice.

kn: These are the supreme, true, and desirable births of this divine Agni, invested (with radiance) in the unbounded (firmament): pure, bright, radiant lord (of all), may he come (to our) sacrifice.
en: These are the supreme, true, and desirable births of this divine Agni, invested (with radiance) in the unbounded (firmament): pure, bright, radiant lord (of all), may he come (to our) sacrifice.

kn: ಸ ದೂತೋ ವಿಶ್ವೇದಭಿ ವಷ್ಟಿ ಸದ್ಮಾ ಹೋತಾ ಹಿರಣ್ಯರಥೋ ರಂಸುಜಿಹ್ವಃ ।
ರೋಹಿತ್ಸ್ಯ ಅಶ್ವಃ ವಪುಷ್ಯೋ ವಿಭಾವಾ ಸದಾ ರಣ್ವಃ ಪಿತುಮತೀವ ಸಂಸತ್ ॥
ref: स दू॒तो विश्वेद॒भि व॑ष्टि॒ सद्मा॒ होता॒ हिर॑ण्यरथो॒ रंसु॑जिह्वः।
रो॒हिद॑श्वो वपु॒ष्यो॑ वि॒भावा॒ सदा॑ र॒ण्वः पि॑तु॒मती॑व सं॒सत्

kn: ಸಃ । ದೂತಃ । ವಿಶ್ವಾ । ಇತ್ । ಅಭಿ । ವಷ್ಟಿ । ಸದ್ಮ । ಹೋತಾ । ಹಿರಣ್ಯರಥಃ । ರಂಸುಜಿಹ್ವಃ ।
ರೋಹಿತ್ಸ್ಯ ಅಶ್ವಃ । ವಪುಷ್ಯಃ । ವಿಭಾವಾ । ಸದಾ । ರಣ್ವಃ । ಪಿತುಮತೀಇವ । ಸಂಸತ್ ॥ ೮ ॥
ದೇವಾನಾಂ ದೂತೋ ಹೋತಾ ದೇವಾನಾಮಾಹ್ವಾತಾ ಹಿರಣ್ಯರಥಃ ಸುವರ್ಣಮಯರಥೋಪೇತೋ ರಂಸುಜಿಹ್ವೊ ರಮಣೀಯಶೋಭನಜ್ವಾಲೋಪೇತಃ ಸ ತಾದೃಶೋಗ್ನಿರ್ವಿಶ್ವೇತ್ ಸರ್ವಾಣ್ವೇವ ಸದ್ಮ ದೇವಯಜನಸ್ಥಾನಾನ್ಯಭಿ ವಷ್ಟಿ । ಕಾಮಯತೇ । ಪುನಶ್ಚ ಕೀದೃಶಃ । ರೋಹಿದಶ್ವಃ ।
ರೋಹಿತವರ್ಣಾ ಅಶ್ವಾ ಯಸ್ಯ ಸ ತಥೋಕ್ತಃ । ವಪುಷ್ಯೋ ವಪುಷಿ ರೂಪೇ ಸಾಧುರ್ವಿಭಾವಾ ಕಾಂತಿಯುಕ್ತೋಽತ ಏವ ಸದಾ ರಣೋ ರಮಣೀಯೋ ಭವತಿ । ತತ್ರ ದೃಷ್ಟಾಂತಃ । ಪಿತುಮತೀವ ಸಂಸತ್ ।
ಯಥಾನ್ನಾದಿವತ್ಸಮೃದ್ಧಂ ಗೃಹಂ ರಮಣೀಯಂ ತದ್ವತ್ ॥ ರಂಸುಜಿಹ್ವಃ । ರಮತೇರನ್ಯೇಭ್ಯೋಽಪಿ
ದೃಶ್ಯಂತ ಇತಿ ವಿಚ್ । ಬಹುವ್ರಿಹ ಪೂರ್ವಪದಸ್ವರಃ । ವಪುಷ್ಯಃ । ತತ್ರ ಸಾಧುರಿತಿ ಯತ್ । ತಿತ್ಸ್ವರಿತಃ।

en: Agni is the messenger of the gods, the होता (*hotā*) (the caller of the gods), हिरण्यरथः (*hiraṇyarathaḥ*) (possessed of a golden chariot), रंसुजिह्वः (*raṃsujihvaḥ*) (possessed of lovely, beautiful flames). Such an Agni विश्वेत् (*viśvet*), all the सद्म (*sadma*) (the places of the gods' sacrifice), अभि वष्टि (*abhi vaṣṭi*), desires. And of what kind is he further? रोहिदश्वः (*rohidaśvaḥ*): he whose horses are red. वपुष्यः (*vapuṣyaḥ*): excellent in form; विभावा (*vibhāvā*): full of radiance, and therefore he is always रण्वः (*raṇvaḥ*), delightful. The illustration: पितुमतीव संसत् (*pitumatīva saṃsat*) — as a house abundant in food and the like is delightful, so is he. The rest gives the grammar of रंसुजिह्वः (*raṃsujihvaḥ*), वपुष्यः (*vapuṣyaḥ*) and विभावा (*vibhāvā*) (Grammar section).

kn: ದೂತಃ- ದೇವದೂತನೂ । ಹೋತಾ-ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಕರೆಯುವವನೂ । ಹಿರಣ್ಯರಥಃ- ಸುವರ್ಣ
ಮಯವಾದ ರಥವುಳ್ಳವನೂ । ರಂಸುಜಿಹ್ವಃ- ರಮಣೀಯವಾಗ ಜ್ವಾಲಾಯುತನೂ । ಸಃ- ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧನೂ ಆದ
ಅಗ್ನಿಯೂ । ವಿಶ್ವೇತ್ ಸದ್ಮ—ಸಮಸ್ತವಾದ ಯಜ್ಞಗೃಹಗಳನ್ನೂ । ಅಭಿ ವಷ್ಟಿ—ಆಪೇಕ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ । ಸಂಸತ್—
ಅಶ್ವವುಳ್ಳವನೂ । ವಪುಷ್ಯಃ—ಆಕರ್ಷಕವಾದ ರೂಪವುಳ್ಳವನೂ । ವಿಭಾವಾ ಕಾಂತಿಯುತನೂ ಆದ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ।
en: - होता (*hotā*)—the one who calls the gods
- हिरण्यरथः (*hiraṇyarathaḥ*)—one who has a golden chariot

kn: ದೇವದೂತನೂ, ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಯಜ್ಞಕ್ಕೆ ಕರೆಯುವವನೂ, ಸುವರ್ಣಮಯವಾದ ರಥವುಳ್ಳವನೂ,
ರಮಣೀಯವಾದ ಜ್ವಾಲಾಯುತನೂ, ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧನೂ ಆದ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ಸಮಸ್ತವಾದ ಯಜ್ಞಗೃಹಗಳನ್ನೂ ಅಪೇಕ್ಷಿಸು
ತ್ತಾನೆ. ಅನ್ನಯುಕ್ತವಾಗಿರುವ ಗೃಹವು ತೃಪ್ತಿದಾಯಕವಾಗಿರುವಂತೆ, ಹೊಂಬಣ್ಣವುಳ್ಳ ಅಶ್ವವುಳ್ಳವನೂ, ಆಕರ್ಷಕ
ವಾದ ರೂಪವುಳ್ಳವನೂ, ಕಾಂತಿಯುತನೂ ಆದ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ ಪ್ರಿಯಕಾರಕನಾಗಿರುತ್ತಾನೆ.
en: Agni, the messenger of the gods, who calls the gods to the sacrifice, who has a golden chariot, whose flames are lovely, the renowned one, desires all the sacrificial houses. As a house supplied with food is pleasing, so Agni, whose horses are golden-hued, who has an attractive form, who is resplendent, is always one who gives pleasure.

kn: The messenger, the invoker (of the gods), riding in a golden chariot
with a tongue of flame, he frequents all the chambers (of sacrifice); drawn
by red horses, embodied, resplendent, always agreeable, as a dwelling well
en: The messenger, the invoker (of the gods), riding in a golden chariot with a tongue of flame, he frequents all the chambers (of sacrifice); drawn by red horses, embodied, resplendent, always agreeable, as a dwelling well supplied with food.

kn: ಸ ಚೇತಯನ್ಮನುಷೋ ಯಜ್ಞಬಂಧುಃ ಪ್ರ ತಂ ಮಹ್ಯಾ ರಶನಯಾ
ಸ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ಯಸ್ಯ ದುರ್ಯಾಸು ಸಾಧನ್ದೇವೋ ಮರ್ತಸ್ಯ ಸಧನಿತ್ವಮಾಪ ॥ ೯ ॥
ref: स चे॑तय॒न्मनु॑षो य॒ज्ञब॑न्धु॒ः प्र तं म॒ह्या र॑श॒नया॑ नयन्ति।
स क्षे॑त्यस्य॒ दुर्या॑सु॒ साध॑न्दे॒वो मर्त॑स्य सधनि॒त्वमा॑प

kn: ಸಃ । ಚೇತಯತ್ । ಮನುಷಃ । ಯಜ್ಞಬಂಧುಃ । ಪ್ರ । ತಮ್ । ಮಹ್ಯಾ । ರಶನಯಾ । ನಯಂತಿ ।
ಸಃ । ಕ್ಷೇತಿ । ಅಸ್ಯ । ದುರ್ಯಾಸು । ಸಾಧನ್ । ದೇವಃ । ಮರ್ತಸ್ಯ । ಸಧನಿತ್ವಂ । ಆಪ ॥ ೯ ॥
ಯಜ್ಞ ಬಂಧುಃ । ಯಜ್ಞೇಽಗ್ನಿಹೋತ್ರಾದೌ ಬಂಧನಂ ವಿನಿಯೋಚನಂ ಯಸ್ಯ ಸ ತಥೋಕ್ತಃ ।
ಕೋಽಗ್ನಿರ್ಮನುಷಃ ಕರ್ಮಣಿ ಪ್ರವೃತ್ತಾನ್ಮನುಷ್ಯಾನ್ ಚೇತಯತ್ । ಜಾನಾತಿ । ಮಹ್ಯಾ ಮಹತ್ಯಾ
ರಶನಯಾ ಸ್ತುತಿರೂಪಯಾ ರಜ್ಜ್ಞಾ ಯುಕ್ತಂ ತಂ ತಾದೃಶಮಗ್ನಿಂ ಪ್ರಣಯಂತಿ । ಉತ್ತರವೇದ್ಯಾದಿಷ್ಟಧ್ವರ್ಯ್ಯಾದಯಃ ಪ್ರಕ್ಷಿಪಂತಿ । ಮರ್ತಸ್ಯ ಮನುಷ್ಯಸ್ಯಾಸ್ಯ ಯಜಮಾನಸ್ಯ ದುರ್ಯಾಸು ಗೃಹೇಷು
ಸಾಧನ್ ಅಭೀಷ್ಟಾನಿ ಸಾಧಯನ್ ಸೋಽಗ್ನಿಃ ಕ್ಷೇತಿ । ವಸತಿ । ಸ ದೇವೋ ದ್ಯೋತಮಾನೋಽಗ್ನಿಃ
ಸಧನಿತ್ವಂ ಯಸ್ಯ ಗೃಹೇ ನಿವಸತಿ ತೇನ ಧನಿನಾ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯಮಾಪ । ಪ್ರಾಪ್ನೋತಿ । ಪ್ರಭೂತಂ ಧನಂ
ಯಜಮಾನಾಯ ದಾಪಯಿತ್ವಾ ತೇನ ಸಹಿತೋಽಭವದಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ॥ ಸಾಧನ್ । ರಾಧ ಸಾಧ ಸಂಸಿದ್ಧೌ ।

en: यज्ञ बंधुः (*yajña baṃdhuḥ*): one whose binding, that is, employment, is in the sacrifice, in the Agnihotra and the like. Agni "knows" (चेतयत् (*cetayat*)) the men engaged in rites. मह्या (*mahyā*) means "by the great" (cord)…

…रशनया (*raśanayā*): Agni, joined to such a cord, in the form of praise, is led forward; the Adhvaryu and others place him on the Uttaravedi and so on. In the houses (दुर्यासु (*duryāsu*)) of this mortal, the sacrificer, accomplishing his desires, Agni dwells. That shining god obtains सधनित्वं (*sadhanitvaṃ*), fellowship with the wealthy man in whose house he lives; the meaning is that he has a great wealth given to the sacrificer and becomes associated with it. Grammar of साधन् (*sādhan*) is given in the commentary.

kn: ರೂಪವಾದುದೂ ಆದ ರಜ್ಜುವಿನಿಂದ ಕೂಡಿದ । ತಂ—ಆ ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು । ಪ್ರ ನಯಂತಿ—ಅಧ್ವರ್ಯುಗಳು ಸ್ಥಾಪಿಸು
ತ್ತಾರೆ । ಮರ್ತಸ್ಯ—ಮಾನವನಾದ । ಅಸ್ಯ—ಈ ಯಜಮಾನನ । ದುರ್ಯಾಸು—ಗೃಹಗಳಲ್ಲಿ । ಸಾಧನ್—ಅವನ
en: - रशनया (*raśanayā*)—with a cord that is of the nature of praise

kn: ಯಜ್ಞಕ್ಕೆ ಬಂಧುಭೂತನಾದ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ಕರ್ಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರವೃತ್ತರಾದ ಮಾನವರ ಭಕ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ತಿಳಿದುಕೊಳ್ಳು
ತ್ತಾನೆ. ಮಹತ್ತಾದುದೂ ಸ್ತುತಿರೂಪವಾದುದೂ ಆದ ರಜ್ಜುವಿನಿಂದ ಕೂಡಿದ ಆ ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ಅಧ್ವರ್ಯುಗಳು
ಸ್ಥಾಪಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಮಾನವನಾದ ಈ ಯಜಮಾನನ ಗೃಹಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅವನ ಇಷ್ಟಾರ್ಥಗಳನ್ನು ಸಾಧಿಸಿಕೊಡುತ್ತಾ
ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ವಾಸಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಪ್ರಕಾಶಮಾನನಾದ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ಧನಿಕನಾದ ಯಜಮಾನನೊಂದಿಗೆ ಐಕ್ಯನಾಗಿ ಅವನ
en: Agni, the kinsman of the sacrifice, comes to know the devotion of men engaged in the rite. The Adhvaryus establish that Agni, joined to the great cord that is of the nature of praise. In the houses of this mortal sacrificer Agni dwells, accomplishing his desires. The shining Agni, united with the wealthy sacrificer, accomplishes his welfare.

kn: Associated with sacrifice, and knowing those men (who are engaged
in good works), they lead him with the strong cord (of praise): he the
divine Agni, fulfilling (all desires), abides in the dwelling of this mortal,
and obtains fellowship in his wealth.
en: Associated with sacrifice, and knowing those men (who are engaged in good works), they lead him with the strong cord (of praise): he the divine Agni, fulfilling (all desires), abides in the dwelling of this mortal, and obtains fellowship in his wealth.

kn: ಸ ತೂ ನೋ ಅಗ್ನಿರ್ನಯತು ಪ್ರಜಾನನ್ನಚ್ಛಾ ರತ್ನಂ ದೇವಭಕ್ತಂ ಯದಸ್ಯ।
ಧಿಯಾ ಯದ್ವಿಶ್ವೇ ಅಮೃತಾ ಅಕೃಣ್ವನ್ದೌ ಷ್ಟಿತಾ ಜನಿತಾ ಸತ್ಯಮುಕ್ಸನ್ ॥
ref: स तू नो॑ अ॒ग्निर्न॑यतु प्रजा॒नन्नच्छा॒ रत्नं॑ दे॒वभ॑क्तं॒ यद॑स्य।
धि॒या यद्विश्वे॑ अ॒मृता॒ अकृ॑ण्व॒न्द्यौष्पि॒ता ज॑नि॒ता स॒त्यमु॑क्षन्

kn: ಸಃ । ತು । ನಃ । ಅಗ್ನಿಃ । ನಯತು । ಪ್ರಜಾನನ್ । ಅಚ್ಛ । ರತ್ನಂ । ದೇವಭಕ್ತಂ । ಯತ್ । ಅಸ್ಯ ।
ಧಿಯಾ । ಯತ್ । ವಿಶ್ವೇ । ಅಮೃತಾಃ । ಅಕೃಣ್ವನ್ । ದ್ಯೌಃ । ಪಿತಾ । ಜನಿತಾ । ಸತ್ಯಂ । ಉಕ್ಷನ್ ॥೧೦॥
ಪ್ರಜಾನನ್ ಸರ್ವಂ ಜಾನಾನಃ ಸೋಗ್ನಿರ್ದೇವಭಕ್ತಂ ದೇವೈರ್ದೇವನಶೀಲೈಃ ಸ್ತೋತೃಭಿಃ ಸಂಭಜನೀಯಮಸ್ವಾಗ್ನೇಃ ಸಂಬಂಧಿ ಯದುತ್ತಮಂ ರತ್ನಂ ಧನಮಸ್ತಿ ತದ್ರತ್ನಮಚ್ಛಾಭಿಮುಖ್ಯೇನ ತು
ಕ್ಷಿಪ್ರಂ ನೋಽಸ್ಮಾನ್ನಯತು । ಪ್ರಾಪಯತು । ಅಮೃತಾ ಮರಣಧರ್ಮರಹಿತಾ ವಿಶ್ವೇ ಸರ್ವೆ ದೇವಾ
ಧಿಯಾ ಹವಿರ್ವಹನಲಕ್ಷಣೇನ ಕರ್ಮಣಾ ಹೇತುನಾ ಯದ್ಯಮಗ್ನಿಮಕೃಣ್ವನ್ ಹವಿಷಾಂ ಪ್ರಾಪಯಿತಾರಮಕುರ್ವನ್ । ಯಸ್ಯ ಚಾಗ್ನೇರ್ದೌಃ ಪಿತಾ ಪಾಲಯತ್ರೀ ಜನಿತಾ ಜನಯಿತ್ರಿ ಚ । ಅಗ್ನೇ ದಿವಃ
ಸೂನುರಸಿ ಪ್ರಚೇತಾಃ । ಋಗ್ವೇ. ೩-೨೫-೧ । ಇತಿ ಶ್ರವಣಾತ್ । ಯದ್ವಾ । ದ್ಯಾರ್ದೇವನಶೀಲ ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ
ಪಿತಾ ಜನಯಿತಾ ಚ ಆದಿತ್ಯಾದಗ್ನಿರಿತ್ಯಾಮ್ನಾನಾತ್ । ಸತ್ಯಂ ಯಥಾರ್ಥಭೂತಂ ತಮಗ್ನಿಮುಕ್ಸನ್ ।
ಘೃತಾದ್ಯಾಹುತಿಭಿರಧ್ವಯ್ದಾದಯಃ ಸಿಂಚಂತಿ ॥ ದೇವಭಕ್ತಂ । ಭಜ ಸೇವಾಯಾಂ । ಕರ್ಮಣಿ ಕ್ತಃ ।
ತೃತೀಯಾ ಕರ್ಮಣೀತಿ ಪೂರ್ವಪದಪ್ರಕೃತಿಸ್ವರಃ । ಉಕ್ಷನ್ । ಉಕ್ಷ ಸೇಚನೇ । ಲಜಿ ರೂಪಂ ।

en: Agni, who knows all, is asked to bring to us quickly, face to face, the best treasure, wealth, that belongs to him and is to be shared by the gods, the shining praisers. The immortal gods, all of them, by the rite of carrying oblations made him the conveyor of oblations; and heaven is his father, protector, and his mother, begetter, as is heard in अग्ने दिवः सूनुरसि प्रचेताः । (*agne divaḥ sūnurasi pracetāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-25-1). Or else: Dyu, the shining Āditya, is father and begetter, since tradition says Agni is from Āditya. सत्यं (*satyaṃ*) is the real Agni; the Adhvaryus and others sprinkle him with oblations such as ghee. Grammar of देवभक्तं (*devabhaktaṃ*) and उक्षन् (*ukṣan*) follows.

kn: ಪ್ರಜಾನನ್—ಸಕಲವನ್ನೂ ತಿಳಿದ । ಸಃ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ—ಅಗ್ನಿಯು । ದೇವಭಕ್ತಂ—ಸ್ತೋತೃಗಳಿಗೆ ಪೂಜ್ಯ
ವಾದುದೂ । ಅಸ್ಯ—ತತ್ಸಂಬಂದಿಯಾದುದೂ ಆದ । ಯತ್ ರತ್ನಂ—ಯಾವ ಧನವಿದೆಯೋ ಅದನ್ನು । ತು—
ಕ್ಷಿಪ್ರವಾಗಿ । ನಃ ಅಚ್ಛ—ನಮಗೆ ಅಭಿಮುಖವಾಗಿ । ನಯತು—ತಂದೊದಗಿಸಲಿ । ಅಮೃತಾಃ—ಮರಣರ್ಮ
ರಹಿತರಾದ । ವಿಶ್ವೇ—ಸಮಸ್ತದೇವತೆಗಳೂ । ಧಿಯಾ—(ತಮಗೆ ಹವಿಸ್ಸನ್ನು ವಹಿಸತಕ್ಕ) ಕರ್ಮನಿಮಿತ್ತವಾಗಿ ।
ಯತ್—ಯಾವ ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು । ಅಕೃಣ್ವನ್—ದೇವದೂತನನ್ನಾಗಿ ಮಾಡಿದರೋ ಮತ್ತು । ಯಸ್ಯ—ಯಾವ
ಸತ್ಯಂ—ಸತ್ಯಾತ್ಮನಾದ ಆ ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು । ಉಕ್ಷನ್—(ಅಧ್ವರ್ಯುಗಳು) ಧೃತಾದಿಗಳಿಂದ ಪ್ರೋಕ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ ।
en: - देवभक्तं (*devabhaktaṃ*)—worthy of worship by the praisers
- यत् रत्नं (*yat ratnaṃ*)—whatever wealth there is, that
- नः अच्छ (*naḥ accha*)—to us, face to face
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—by the rite of carrying oblations to them
- उक्षन् (*ukṣan*)—(the Adhvaryus) sprinkle with ghee and the like

kn: ಸ್ತೋತೃಗಳಿಗೆಲ್ಲಾ ಪೂಜ್ಯವಾಗಿರತಕ್ಕ ಧನಸಂಪತ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಸರ್ವಜ್ಞನಾದ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ಕ್ಷಿಪ್ರವಾಗಿ ನಮಗೆ
ತಂದೊದಗಿಸಲಿ. ಮರಣಧರ್ಮರಹಿತರಾದ ಸಮಸ್ತದೇವತೆಗಳೂ ಸಹ ತಮಗೆ ಹವಿಸ್ಸನ್ನು ವಹಿಸುವ ಕರ್ಮನಿಮಿತ್ತ
ವಾಗಿ ಯಾವ ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ತಮಗೆ ದೂತನನ್ನಾಗಿ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಂಡರೋ ಮತ್ತು ಯಾವ ಅಗ್ನಿಗೆ ದ್ಯುಲೋಕವು
ಜನಕವೂ ಪಾಲಕವೂ ಆಗಿದೆಯೋ ಅಂತಹ ಸತ್ಯಾತ್ಮನಾದ ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ಅಧ್ವರ್ಯುಗಳು ಧೃತಾದಿಗಳಿಂದ ಪ್ರೋಕ್ಷಿ
en: May Agni, the all-knowing, quickly bring us the wealth that is worthy of worship by all praisers. The Adhvaryus sprinkle with ghee and the like that Agni, true in nature, whom all the immortal gods, by the rite of carrying their oblations, made their messenger, and whose begetter and protector is heaven.

kn: May that wise Agni conduct us to that wealth which is desired by the
devout ; he whom all the immortals have created for (the performance of)
sacred rites ; of whom heaven is the parent and progenitor, and whom (the
en: May that wise Agni conduct us to that wealth which is desired by the devout; he whom all the immortals have created for (the performance of) sacred rites; of whom heaven is the parent and progenitor, and whom (the priests) verily sprinkle (with oblations).

kn: ಯಸ್ಯ ದ್ಯೌಃ ಪಿತಾ ಜನಿತಾ—ಅಗ್ನಿಗೆ ಸ್ವರ್ಗವು ತಂದೆಯೂ ಪಾಲಕನೂ ಆಗಿರುವನೆಂದು ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಹೇಳಿದೆಅಗ್ನೇ ದಿವಃ ಸೂನುರಸಿ ಪ್ರಚೇತಾಸ್ತನಾ ಪೃಥಿವ್ಯಾ ಉತ ವಿಶ್ವವೇದಾಃ ।
ಎಲೈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ, ನೀನು ಸಮಸ್ತವನ್ನೂ ತಿಳಿದ ಸರ್ವಜ್ಞನೆನಿಸಿದ್ದೀಯೆ. ನೀನು ಸ್ವರ್ಗದ (ಅಥವಾ ಸ್ವರ್ಗಾಭಿಮಾನಿ
ದೇವತೆಯ) ಮತ್ತು ಪೃಥಿವಿಯ ಪುತ್ರನಾಗಿದ್ದೀಯೆ ಎಂದು ವಿಶ್ವಾಮಿತ್ರಋಷಿಯು ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ಸ್ತೋತ್ರಮಾಡಿದ್ದಾನೆ.
ಇದಲ್ಲದೆ ದ್ಯಾವಾಪೃಥಿವಿಗಳು ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ ಮೊದಲಾದ ಇತರ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ದೇವತೆಗಳಿಗೂ ತಂದೆತಾಯಿಗಳೆಂದು ಅನೇಕ
en: यस्य द्यौः पिता जनिता (*yasya dyauḥ pitā janitā*)—Here it is said that heaven is father and protector of Agni: अग्ने दिवः सूनुरसि प्रचेतास्तना पृथिव्या उत विश्ववेदाः (*agne divaḥ sūnurasi pracetāstanā pṛthivyā uta viśvavedāḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-25-1).
