ಹಿಂದೆ ಹೇಳಿದ ಉದಾಹರಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ—ವೈಶ್ವಾನರೋ ಯತತೇ ಸೂರ್ಯೇಣ । ಎಂಬ ವಾಕ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿ
ಯು ಸೂರ್ಯನೊಡನೆ ಸೇರಿ ವಿಸ್ತ್ರತನಾಗುವನು ಎಂದರೆ ಎಲ್ಲವನ್ನೂ ವ್ಯಾಪಿಸುವನು ಎಂಬರ್ಥವನ್ನು ಮಂತ್ರದ್ರಷ್ಟೃ
ವಾದ ಋಷಿಯು ಹೇಳಿದ್ದಾನೆ. ಸೂರ್ಯನ ಸ್ಥಾನವು ವ್ಯತ್ಯಸ್ಥವಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲವಾದ್ದರಿಂದ ಸೂರ್ಯನು ತನ್ನ ಸ್ಥಾನ
ದಿಂದ ಮುಂದಕ್ಕೆ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಯೊಡನೆ ಹೋಗಿ ವ್ಯಾಪಿಸುವನು ಎಂಬುದು ಅಸಂಭವವು. ಒಂದು ವಸ್ತುವು
ಒಂದೇಕಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದು ಸ್ಥಾನದಲ್ಲಿರಬಹುದೇ ಹೊರತು ಅಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಇದ್ದು ಮುಂದಕ್ಕೂ ಹೋಗಲು ಸಾಧ್ಯವಿಲ್ಲ.
ಅದರ ಜೊತೆಗೆ ಬೇರೆ ವಸ್ತುವು ಸೇರಿದರೆ ಮಾತ್ರ ಬೇರೆ ಸ್ಥಳವನ್ನು ವ್ಯಾಪಿಸಬಲ್ಲುದು. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಸೂರ್ಯನೇ
ಬೇರೆ, ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಯೇ ಬೇರೆ. ಇಬ್ಬರೂ ಸೇರಿ ಎಲ್ಲವನ್ನೂ ವ್ಯಾಪಿಸಲು ಸಮರ್ಥರು. ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಪಾರ್ಥಿವಾಗ್ನಿ
ಯನ್ನು ಇಲ್ಲಿಯೇ (ಭೂಮಿಯಲ್ಲಿಯೇ) ಹೊತ್ತಿಸುವರು. ಆದಿತ್ಯನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶವು ದ್ಯುಲೋಕದಿಂದ ರಶ್ಮಿಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ
ಹೊರಟು ಭೂಮಿಯಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಪಾರ್ಥಿವಾಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ಸಂಧಿಸುವುದು. ಎಂದರೆ ಸೂರ್ಯನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶವೂ, ಅಗ್ನಿಯ
ಪ್ರಕಾಶವೂ ಒಂದಾಗಿ ಸೇರಿ ಆ ಪ್ರಕಾಶವು ರಶ್ಮಿಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಎಲ್ಲೆಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಹರಡುವುದು ಎಂಬ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯವನ್ನೇ
ಮಂತ್ರದ್ರಷ್ಟೃವಾದ ಋಷಿಯು ಮನಸ್ಸಿನಲ್ಲಿಟ್ಟುಕೊಂಡು ವೈಶ್ವಾನರೋ ಯತತೇ ಸೂರ್ಯೇಣ ಎಂಬ ವಾಕ್ಯ
ಅಥ ಯಾನ್ಯೇತಾನ್ಯೌತ್ತಮಿಕಾನಿ ಸೂಕ್ತಾನಿ ಭಾಗಾನಿ ನಾ ಸಾವಿತ್ರಾಣಿ ನಾ ಸೌರ್ಯಾಣಿ ವಾ
ಪೌಷ್ಣಾನಿ ವಾ ವೈಷ್ಣವಾನಿ ವಾ ವೈಶ್ವದೇನ್ಯಾನಿ ವಾ ತೇಷು ವೈಶ್ವಾನರೀಯಾಃ ಪ್ರವಾದಾ
ಅಭವಿಷ್ಯನ್ನಾದಿತ್ಯಕರ್ಮಣಾ ಜೈನಮಸ್ತೋಷ್ಯನ್ನಿತ್ಯುದೇಷೀತ್ಯಸ್ತಮೇಷೀತಿ ವಿಪರ್ಯೇಷೀತಿ ॥ ಆಗ್ನೇಯೇಷ್ಟೇವ ಹಿ ಸೂಕ್ತೇಷು ವೈಶ್ವಾನರೀಯಾಃ ಪ್ರವಾದಾ ಭವಂತಿ । ಅಗ್ನಿಕರ್ಮಾಣಾ ಚೈನಂ ಸ್ತೌತೀತಿ ವಹಸೀತಿ ಪಚಸೀತಿ ದಹಸೀತಿ ॥
ಒಂದುವೇಳೆ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರನೇ ಆದಿತ್ಯನಾಗಿದ್ದ ಪಕ್ಷದಲ್ಲಿ ಆದಿತ್ಯ ಅಥವಾ ಸವಿತೃಸಂಬಂಧವಾದ ಸೂಕ್ತಗಳಲ್ಲಿಯೂ
ಅಥವಾ ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಅಥವಾ ಸೂರ್ಯ, ಪೂಷಾ, ವಿಷ್ಣು, ವಿಶ್ವೇದೇವತೆಗಳು ಪ್ರತಿಪಾದಿತರಾಗಿರುವ ಸೂಕ್ತ
ಗಳಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಗೆ ಆದಿತ್ಯಪರವಾದ ಗುಣಗಳು, ವೈಶಿಷ್ಟ್ಯಗಳು ಎಂದರೆ (ಸೂರ್ಯನ ವಿಷಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಹೇಳು
ವಂತೆ) ನೀನು ಉದಯಿಸುತ್ತೀಯೆ, ಮುಳುಗುತ್ತೀಯೆ, ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಚರಿಸುತ್ತೀಯೆ ಎಂದು ಮೊದಲಾದ ಅರ್ಥ
ಬೋಧಕಗಳಾದ ವಾಕ್ಯಾದಿಗಳಿಂದ ಸ್ತುತಿಸಲ್ಪಡಬೇಕಾಗಿದ್ದಿತು. ಆದರೆ ಹಾಗಿಲ್ಲ. ಅಗ್ನಿಸಂಬಂಧವಾದ ಸೂಕ್ತ
ಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತ್ರ ಅಗ್ನಿಯ ಗುಣಗಳಾದ ಹವಿರ್ವಹನ, ಪಾಚನ, ದಹನ ಮೊದಲಾದ ಕ್ರಿಯೆಗಳನ್ನು ವರ್ಣಿಸುವ ವಾಕ್ಯ
ಗಳೇ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಗೂ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುವಂತೆ ಹೇಳಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಿದೆ. ಎಂದರೆ ಅಗ್ನಿಯ ಗುಣಗಳನ್ನೇ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಗೂ
ಅನ್ವಯಿಸಿ ವರ್ಣಿಸಿದೆ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಯು ಪಾರ್ಥಿವಾಗ್ನಿಯೇ ಹೊರತು ಆದಿತ್ಯನಲ್ಲ
ಈ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ವೃಷ್ಟಿಕರ್ಮಕ್ಕೆ ಪ್ರೇರಕನನ್ನಾಗಿ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುವ ಮಂತ್ರಗಳಿರುವವು. ಆದುದರಿಂದ ವೃಷ್ಟಿ
ಕರ್ಮಕ್ಕೆ ಆದಿತ್ಯನು ಪ್ರೇರಕನಾದುದರಿಂದ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಗೂ ಆದಿತ್ಯಗುಣಗಳಿದ್ದಂತಾಯಿ. ಆದುದರಿಂದ ವೈಶ್ವಾನ
ರಾಗ್ನಿಯೇ ಆದಿತ್ಯನು ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಬಹುದಲ್ಲವೇ ? ಎಂದರೆ, ಹಾಗಲ್ಲ. ಹಗಲುಗಳು ರಾತ್ರೆಕಳೆದನಂತರ ಮತ್ತೆ ಮತ್ತೆ
ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತವಾಗುವಂತೆ ಉದಕಗಳು ಭೂಮಿಯಿಂದ ಮೇಲಕ್ಕೂ (ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷಕ್ಕೂ) ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷದಿಂದ ಭೂಮಿಗೂ ಮತ್ತೆ
ಮತ್ತೆ ಬರುತ್ತಿರುವವು. ಆದುದರಿಂದ ಉದಕಗಳಿಗೂ, ಹಗಲುಗಳಿಗೂ ಸಮಾನಧರ್ಮವಿದ್ದಂತಾಯಿತು. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ
ಭೂಮಿಯನ್ನು ವೃಷ್ಟುದಕದಿಂದ ಪರ್ಜನ್ಯದೇವತೆಯು ತೃಪ್ತಿ ಪಡಿಸುವನು. ಸ್ವರ್ಗವನ್ನು ಅಗ್ನಿಗಳು ತೃಪ್ತಿಪಡಿಸು
ವವು. ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ಸ್ವರ್ಗವನ್ನು ತೃಪ್ತಿಪಡಿಸುವುದು ಹೇಗೆಂದರೆ—ಯಜ್ಞದಲ್ಲಿ ಯಜಮಾನರು ಅಗ್ನಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹೋಮ
ಮಾಡುವ ಹವಿರಾದಿಗಳು ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮರೂಪದಿಂದ ಎಂದರೆ ಧೂಮಾಕಾರದಿಂದ ದೇವಯೋಗ್ಯವಾದ ರೂಪವನ್ನು ಹೊಂದಿ
ದೇವತೆಗಳಿಗೆ ತೃಪ್ತಿಯನ್ನುಂಟುಮಾಡುವವು ದೇವತೆಗಳು ಪ್ರೀತರಾಗಿ ಭೂಲೋಕನಿವಾಸಿಗಳಿಗೆ ವೃಷ್ಟಿಯ
ಎಂಬ ವಾಕ್ಯಾನುಸಾರವಾಗಿ ಅಗ್ನಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅರ್ಪಿಸಿದ ಆಹುತಿಯು ಸ್ವರ್ಗದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಆದಿತ್ಯನನ್ನು ಸಂತೋಷಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ
ಎಂದಿರುವುದರಿಂದ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ಸ್ವರ್ಗ ಅಥವಾ ಆದಿತ್ಯನನ್ನು ತೃಪ್ತಿಪಡಿಸಿದಂತಾಯಿತು. ವೃಷ್ಟಿಯು ಭೂಲೋಕದಿಂದ
ಸ್ವರ್ಗಕ್ಕೂ, ಸ್ವರ್ಗದಿಂದ ಭೂಮಿಗೂ ಪರಸ್ಪರ ಸಹಾಯಮಾಡುವ ಸಾಧನವಾಯಿತು. ಈ ಕಾರಣಗಳಿಂದ ಅಗ್ನಿ
ಯನ್ನು ಅಥವಾ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ವೃಷ್ಟಿಕರ್ಮಕ್ಕೆ ಕಾರಣನೆಂದು ಸ್ತುತಿಸಿರುವುದೇ ಹೊರತು ವೈಶ್ವಾನರನೇ
ಆದಿತ್ಯನೆಂದು ಇದರಿಂದ ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟ ಪಡುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಈ ಋಕ್ಕಿನ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯವು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟವಾಗಿರುವುದರಿಂದ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ವಿವರಣೆಯ
ಕೃಷ್ಣಂ ನಿಯಾನಂ ಹರಯಃ ಸುಪರ್ಣಾ ಅಪೋ ವಸಾನಾ ದಿವಮುತ್ಪತಂತಿ ।
ಕೃಷ್ಣಂ ನಿರಯಣಂ ರಾತ್ರಿರಾದಿತ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಹರಯಃ ಸುಪರ್ಣಾ ಹರಣಾ ಆದಿತ್ಯರಶ್ಮಯಸ್ತೇ ಯದಾಮುತೋಽರ್ವಾಂಚಃ ಪರ್ಯಾವರ್ತಂತೇ ಸಹಸ್ಥಾನಾದುದಕಸ್ಯಾದಿತ್ಯಾದಥ ಧೃತೇನೋದಕೇನ ಪೃಥಿವೀ ವ್ಯುದ್ಯತೇ ಧೃತಮಿತ್ಯುದಕನಾಮ ಜಿಘರ್ತೆಃ ಸಿಂಚತಿಕರ್ಮಣಃ ॥
ಉದಕವನ್ನು ವಹಿಸಿರತಕ್ಕವೂ, ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠವಾದ ಸಂಚಾರವುಳ್ಳವೂ ಆದ ರಶ್ಮಿಗಳು ಕಪ್ಪುಬಣ್ಣವುಳ್ಳದ್ದೂ, ನಿಯತವಾದ
ಗತಿಯುಳ್ಳದ್ದು ಆದ ಮೇಘವನ್ನು (ಅಥವಾ ರಾತ್ರಿಯನ್ನು) ಉದಕದಿಂದ ಆಚ್ಛಾದಿತವಾಗುವಂತೆ ಮಾಡಿ ಎಂದರೆ
ಉದಕದಿಂದ ಕೂಡಿ ದ್ಯುಲೋಕಾಭಿಮುಖವಾಗಿ ಮೇಲಕ್ಕೆ ಪ್ರಸರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಪುನಃ ಅವು ಉದಕದ ಸ್ಥಾನವಾದ
ಆದಿತ್ಯನಿಂದ ಹಿಂತಿರುಗುತ್ತವೆ. ಒಡನೆಯೇ ಪೃಥ್ವಿಯು ಉದಕದಿಂದ ತೋಯಲ್ಪಡುತ್ತದೆ (ನೆನೆಸಲ್ಪಡುತ್ತದೆ).
ನಿರಯಣವೆಂದರೆ ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಚಾರಮಾರ್ಗವೆಂದು ಹೇಳಬಹುದು. ನಿರ್ಗಮನಮಾರ್ಗವೆಂದು ಈ ಶಬ್ದಕ್ಕೆ
ಸಾಧಾರಣವಾದ ಅರ್ಥವಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಆದಿತ್ಯನ ಸಂಚಾರಮಾರ್ಗಗಳೆರಡು. ಒಂದು ಕೃಷ್ಣವರ್ಣದ್ದು, ಇನ್ನೊಂದು
ಶುಕ್ಲವರ್ಣದ್ದು. ಕೃಷ್ಣವರ್ಗದ ಸಂಚಾರಮಾರ್ಗಕ್ಕೆ ರಾತ್ರಿಯೆಂದಾಗಲಿ, ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನವೆಂದಾಗಲಿ ಅರ್ಥಮಾಡ
ಬಹುದು. ಅಥವಾ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನ ಸಂಚಾರವನ್ನೇ ಆದಿತ್ಯನ ರಾತ್ರಿ ಸಂಚಾರವೆಂದು ಹೇಳಬಹುದು. ದುರ್ಗಾಚಾ
ರ್ಯರು ಮೇಲಿನ ನಿರುಕ್ತವಾಕ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ಈ ರೀತಿ ವ್ಯಾಖ್ಯಾನವನ್ನು ಬರೆದಿರುತ್ತಾರೆ—
ನಿಯಾನಂ ನಿರಯಣಂ ನಿರ್ಗತಿಃ (ನಿರ್ಯಾತಿ) ನಿರ್ಗಚ್ಛಂತ್ಯೇತದಿತಿ ನಿಯಾನಂ ವರ್ತ್ಮ ಪಂಥಾಃ।
ತಚ್ಚ ಪುನರೇತತ್ । ರಾತ್ರಿ ಆದಿತ್ಯಸ್ಯ । ದ್ವೇ ಹ್ಯಸ್ಯಾಯನೇ ಶುಕ್ಲಂ ಚೋತ್ತರಂ ಕೃಷ್ಣಂ ಚ
ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ । ಸಾ ಹಿ ದೈವೀರಾತ್ರಿರಭಿಪ್ರೇತಾ । ತತೋ ಬ್ರವೀತಿ ರಾತ್ರಿರಾದಿತ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಜ್ಯೋತಿಷಃ ।
ಸ ಏಷ ಭಗವಾನಾದಿತ್ಯೋ ಯದಾ ಜಗದನುಗ್ರಹಾಯ ಗರ್ಭಮುದಕಮಾತ್ಮನ್ಯಾಧಿತ್ಸುರುತ್ತ
ರಾಯಣಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯತೇ ತದೈತೇ ಹರಯಃ ರಸಹರಣಾಃ ಸುಪರ್ಣಾಸ್ತಸ್ಯ ರಶ್ಮಯಃ ಸರ್ವಸ್ಮಾದಸ್ಮಾಲ್ಲೋಕಾದಪೋವಸಾನಾಃ ಆತ್ಮನ್ಯಾಚ್ಛಾದಯಂತಃ ಆದದಾನಾಃ ದಿವಂ ದ್ಯೋತನವಂತಮೇತಮಾದಿತ್ಯಂ ಪ್ರತ್ಯುತ್ಪತಂತಿ ।
ಆದಿತ್ಯನ ಗತಿಯು ಎರಡು ವಿಧವಾಗಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಂದು ಉತ್ತರಾಯಣಕ್ಕೂ ಮತ್ತೊಂದು ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನಕ್ಕೂ ಸಂಬಂಧಿ
ಸಿದುದು. ಒಂದನ್ನು ಶುಕ್ಲವೆಂದೂ ಇನ್ನೊಂದನ್ನು ಕೃಷ್ಣವೆಂದೂ ಕರೆದಿದೆ. ಇಲ್ಲಿ ರಾತ್ರಿಯೆಂಬುದು ಕೃಷ್ಣಾಯನಕ್ಕೆ
ಪರ್ಯಾಯವಾದ ಪದವಾಗಿದೆ.—ಕೃಷ್ಣಂ ನಿಯಾನಂ ನಿಯಮನಂ ರಾತ್ರಿಃ । ದೇವಾನಾಂ ಹಿ ರಾತ್ರಿರ್ದಕ್ಷಿ
ಣಾಯನಂ । ತತ್ಪತಿ ತಸ್ಮಿನ್ವರ್ಷಾಕಾಲೇ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ । ದೇವತೆಗಳ ರಾತ್ರಿಕಾಲಕ್ಕೆ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನವೆಂದು ಹೆಸರು.
ಆದಿತ್ಯನು ಉತ್ತರಾಯಣದ ಗತಿಯನ್ನನುಸರಿಸುತ್ತಿದ್ದಾಗ ಅವನ ರಶ್ಮಿಗಳೆಲ್ಲವೂ ಪ್ರಪಂಚದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಸರಿಸಿ ಎಲ್ಲಾ
ಪ್ರದೇಶಗಳಿಂದಲೂ ಉದಕವನ್ನು ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸಿ ಈ ರಾತ್ರಿಕಾಲಕ್ಕೆ ಸರಿಯಾಗಿ ಪುನಃ ಆದಿತ್ಯನನ್ನು ಸೇರುವವು. ಇದೇ
ವರ್ಷಾಕಾಲವು. ಈ ಕಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ವೃಷ್ಟಿಯು ಬಹಳವಾಗಿ ಸುರಿಯುವುದು ಧೃತವೆಂದಶೆ ಉದಕಕ್ಕೆ ಹೆಸರು.
ಅಥಾಪಿ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಂ ಭವತ್ಯಗ್ನಿರ್ವಾ ಇತೋ ವೃಷ್ಟಿಂ ಸಮೀರಯತಿ ಧಾಮಚ್ಛದಿತಿ ಖಲು
ಭೂತ್ವಾ ವರ್ಷತಿ ಮರುತಃ ಸೃಷ್ಟಾಂ ವೃಷ್ಟಿಂ ನಯಂತಿ ।
ಯದಾ ಖಲು ವಾಸಾನಾದಿತ್ಯೋಗ್ನಿಂ ರಶ್ಮಿಭಿಃ ಪರ್ಯಾವರ್ತತೇಽಥ ವರ್ಷತೀತಿ ।
ಯಥೋ ಏತದ್ವೈಶ್ವಾನರೀಯೋ ದ್ವಾದಶಕಪಾಲೋ ಭವತೀತ್ಯನಿರ್ವಚನಂ ಕಪಾಲಾನಿ ಭವಂತ್ಯಸ್ತಿ ಹಿ ಸೌರ್ಯ ಏಕಕಪಾಲಃ ಪಂಚಕಪಾಲಶ್ಚ ।
ಯಥೋ ಏತದ್ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಂ ಭವತೀತಿ-ಬಹುಭಕ್ತಿವಾದೀನಿ ಹಿ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಾನಿ ಭವಂತಿ-ಪೃಥಿವೀ
ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರೋ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರೋ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣೋ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರ ಇತಿ ॥
ಇದಲ್ಲದೆ ಅನೇಕ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣವಾಕ್ಯಗಳೂ ಈ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ಸಮರ್ಥಿಸುವವು. ಹೇಗೆಂದರೆ ' ಅಗ್ನಿಯು ಈ ಲೋಕದಿಂದ
ಮಳೆಯನ್ನು ಸುರಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ' ಎಂಬ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣವಾಕ್ಯವಿದೆ—ಅಗ್ನೇವೈ ಧೂಮೋ ಜಾಯತೇ, ಧೂಮಾದಭ್ರಂ,
ಅಭ್ರಾತ್ ವೃಷ್ಟಿರಿತಿ ಹ ವಿಜ್ಞಾಯತೇ—ಅಗ್ನಿಯಿಂದ ಧೂಮವು (ಹೊಗೆಯು) ಉತ್ಪನ್ನವಾಗುವುದು. ಧೂಮ
ದಿಂದ ಮೇಘವೂ ಮೇಘದಿಂದ ವೃಷ್ಟಿಯೂ ಉಂಟಾಗುವುದು ಎಂದು ತಿಳಿಯಬೇಕು ಎಂದರ್ಥವು. ಅಥವಾ ಈ
ಆದಿತ್ಯನು ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ತನ್ನ ರಶ್ಮಿಗಳಿಂದ ಹಿಂತಿರುಗುವಂತೆ ಮಾಡಿದಾಗ ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತದೆ. ಅಥವಾ ರೋಹಪ್ರತ್ಯವ
ರೋಹಕ್ರಮದಿಂದ ಎಂದರೆ ಅಗ್ನಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅರ್ಪಿಸಿದ ಆಹುತಿಯು ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮರೂಪದಿಂದ ಧೂಮವಾಗಿ ಸ್ವರ್ಗದಲ್ಲಿರುವ
ದೇವತೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಸೇರಿ ಅವರು ತೃಪ್ತಿಗೊಂಡು ಅದರಿಂದ ವೃಷ್ಟಿಕರ್ಮವುಂಟಾಗುವುದು ಎಂದು ಹೇಳುವುದಕ್ಕೆ
ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣವಾಕ್ಯ ಹೊರತು ಮತ್ಯಾವ ಆಧಾರವೂ ಇಲ್ಲ. ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಗೆ ದ್ವಾದಶಕಪಾಲವೆಂದೂ ಸೂರ್ಯನಿಗೆ ಏಕ
(ಒಂದು) ಕಪಾಲ ಅಥವಾ ಐದು ಕಪಾಲಗಳ ಹವಿಸ್ಸೆಂದು ಹೇಳಿರುವುದು ಈ ವಿಷಯಕ್ಕೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಪಟ್ಟಿದ್ದಲ್ಲ. ಅದು
ಯಜ್ಞಾಂಗಗಳಾದ ಕಾರ್ಯಗಳಿಗೆ ಮಾತ್ರ ಸಂಬಂಧಪಟ್ಟಿರುವುದು. ಇನ್ನು ಕೆಲವು ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣವಾಕ್ಯಗಳಲ್ಲಿ—
ಪೃಥಿವೀ, ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ವಾಕ್ಯಗಳಲ್ಲಿ—ಪೃಥಿವಿಯು ವೈಶ್ವಾನರನು, ಸಂವತ್ಸರವೂ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರನು, ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮ
ಣನೂ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರನು, ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಿರುವುದು ಸರಿಯಷ್ಟೆ. ಈ ಸಂದರ್ಭದಲ್ಲಿ ಪೃಥಿವೀ ಮೊದಲಾದ ದೇವತೆಗಳೇ
ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಯೆಂದಲ್ಲ. ವೈಶ್ವಾನರನು ಪೃಥಿವೀ ಮೊದಲಾದ ದೇವತೆಗಳ ಗುಣಗಳನ್ನು ಹೊಂದಿರುವನೆಂದು ವೈಶ್ವಾ
ನರನ ಗುಣವರ್ಣನೆ ಮಾಡುವುದಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಹೇಳಿರುವ ಸ್ತುತಿವಾಕ್ಯಗಳು ಎಂದು ತಿಳಿಯಬೇಕು.
ಯಥೋ ಏತನ್ನಿವಿತ್ಸೌರ್ಯವೈಶ್ವಾನರೀ ಭವತೀತ್ಯಸ್ಯೈವ ಸಾ ಭವತಿ—ಯೋ ವಿಡ್ಭೋ
ಮಾನುಷೀಭ್ಯೋ ದೀದೇತ್-ಇತ್ಯೇಷ ಹಿ ವಿಡ್ಭೋ ಮಾನುಷೀಭ್ಯೋ ದೀಪ್ಯತೇ ।
ಜಮದಗ್ನಿಭಿರಾಹುತ ಇತಿ। ಜಮದಗ್ನಯಃ ಪ್ರಜಮಿತಾಗ್ನಯೋ ವಾ ಪ್ರಜ್ವಲಿತಾಗ್ನಯೋ ನಾ
ಸೂರ್ಯನನ್ನೂ, ವೈಶ್ವಾನರನನ್ನೂ ಸ್ತುತಿಸತಕ್ಕ ಒಂದು ನಿವಿತ್ಸೂಕ್ತವಿದೆ. ಈ ಸೂಕ್ತವನ್ನು ಆಗ್ನಿಮಾರುಶಸ್ತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ
ಅಗ್ನಿರ್ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ ಸೋಮಸ್ಯ ಮತ್ಸತ್ । ವಿಶ್ವೇಷಾಂ ದೇವಾನಾಂ ಸಮಿತ್ । ಅಜಸ್ರಂ ದೈವಂ
ಜ್ಯೋತಿಃ । ಯೋ ವಿಡ್ಭ್ಯೋ ಮಾನುಷೀಭ್ಯೋ ದೀದೇತ್ । ದ್ಯುಷು ಪೂರ್ವಾಸು ದಿದ್ಯುತಾನಃ । ಅಜರ ಉಷಸಾಮನೀಕೇ । ಆ ಯೋ ದ್ಯಾಂ ಭಾತ್ಯಾ ಪೃಥಿವೀಂ । ಔರ್ವಮುತ-
ರಿಕ್ಷಂ । ಜ್ಯೋತಿಷಾ ಯಜ್ಞಾಯ ಶರ್ಮ ಸಂಯತ್ । ಅಗ್ನಿರ್ವೈಶ್ವಾನರ ಇಹ ಶ್ರವದಿಹ
ಸೋಮಸ್ಯ ಮತ್ಸತ್ । ಪ್ರೇಮಾಂ ದೇವೋ ದೇವಹೂತಿಮವತು ದೇವ್ಯಾ ಧಿಯಾ । ಪ್ರೇದಂ
ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಪ್ರೇದಂ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಂ । ಪ್ರೇಮಂ ಸುನ್ವಂತಂ ಯಜಮಾನಮವತು । ಚಿತ್ರಶ್ಚಿತ್ತಾಭಿರೂತಿಭಿಃ।
ಎಂಬ ಈ ಸೂಕ್ತವೇ ಆಗ್ನಿಮಾರುತಶಸ್ತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ಉದ್ದೇಶಿಸಿ ಪಠಿಸಲ್ಪಡುವುದು. ಈ ಮಂತ್ರದ
ಮಧ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ—ಯೋ ವಿಡ್ಭೋ ಮಾನುಷೀಭ್ಯೋ ದೀದೇತ್—ಎಂಬ ವಾಕ್ಯವಿದೆ. ಇದಕ್ಕೆ-ಈ ದೇವನು
ಮಾನವರಾದ ಪ್ರಜೆಗಳ ಉಪಕಾರಾರ್ಥವಾಗಿ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಿಸುವವನು ಸೂರ್ಯನೇ ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಸೂರ್ಯನನ್ನೇ
ವೈಶ್ವಾನರ ಎಂಬ ಶಬ್ದದಿಂದ ಸಂಬೋಧಿಸಿದೆ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಸೂರ್ಯನಿಗೂ, ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಗೂ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವಿಲ್ಲ.
ಎಂದರೆ, ಹಾಗಲ್ಲ. ಈ ಮಂತ್ರವು ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನೇ ಉದ್ದೇಶಿಸಿ ಪಠಿತವಾಗಿದೆ. ಯಜ್ಞವೇದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪಾರ್ಥಿವಾಗ್ನಿಯೇ
ಯಜ್ಞ ಮಾಡುವ ಯಜಮಾನರು ಮೊದಲಾದ ಪ್ರಜೆಗಳ ಉಪಕಾರಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಿಸುತ್ತಿರುವನು ಎಂಬ ಅರ್ಥವೂ ಈ
ಮಂತ್ರಕ್ಕೆ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುವುದು. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಯು ಸೂರ್ಯನಲ್ಲ, ಪಾರ್ಥಿವಾಗ್ನಿಯೇ ಆಗಿರುವನು
ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಬೇಕು. ಇದಲ್ಲದೆ ದಶರಾತ್ರವೆಂಬ ಛಾಂದೋಮಿಕ ಯಜ್ಞದಲ್ಲಿ ಜಮದಗ್ನಿಭಿರಾಹುತಃ ಎಂಬ ಸೌರ್ಯ
ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಸೂಕ್ತವನ್ನು ಪಠಿಸುವರು. ಈ ಸೂಕ್ತವೂ ಸಹ ಸೂರ್ಯನಿಗೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಪಡುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಅಗ್ನಿಗೇ ಅನ್ವ
ಯಿಸುವುದು. ಏಕೆಂದರೆ, ಜಮದಗ್ನಿಶಬ್ದಕ್ಕೆ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ಹೊತ್ತಿಸಲ್ಪಟ್ಟು ಧಗಧಗನೆ ಉರಿಯುತ್ತಿರುವ ಅಗ್ನಿಯಿಂದ
ರ್ಥವು. ಯಜ್ಞಾದಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅಗ್ನಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹೋಮಮಾಡುವಾಗ ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ಸಮಿದಾಜ್ಯಾದಿದ್ರವ್ಯಗಳಿಂದ ಪ್ರಜ್ವಲಿತ
ನಾಗಿ ಮಾಡಿ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ಉರಿಯುತ್ತಿರುವ ಆ ಅಗ್ನಿಯಲ್ಲಿಯೇ ಹೋಮಾದಿಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾಡುವುದು ರೂಢಿಯು.
ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಇದು ಆದಿತ್ಯ (ಅಥವಾ ಸೂರ್ಯ) ನನ್ನು ನಿರ್ದೇಶಿಸದೆ ಪಾರ್ಥಿವಾಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನೇ ನಿರ್ದೇಶಿಸುವುದೆಂದಭಿ
ಯಥೋ ಏತದ್ಧವಿಷ್ವಾಂತೀಯಂ ಸೂಕ್ತಂ ಸೌರ್ಯವೈಶ್ವಾನರಂ ಭವತೀತ್ಯಸ್ಯೈವ ತದ್ಭವತಿ ।
ತಸ್ಯ ಭರ್ಮಣೇ ಭುವನಾಯ ದೇವಾ ಧರ್ಮಣೇ ಕಂ ಸ್ವಧಯಾ ಪಪ್ರಥಂತ ॥
ಭರಣಾಯ ಚ ಭಾವನಾಯ ಚ ಧಾರಣಾಯ ಚ ಚೈತೇಭ್ಯಃ ಸರ್ವೇಭ್ಯಃ ಕರ್ಮಭ
ಇದಲ್ಲದೆ ಹವಿಷ್ವಾಂತಮಜರಂ ಎಂಬ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ಸೌರ್ಯವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿ ದೇವತಾಕವು. ಈ ಸೂಕ್ತದಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ತುತಿಸ
ಲಾಗಿರುವ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರನೇ ಆದಿತ್ಯನು ಎಂದು ಹೇಳುವುದಾದರೆ, ಅದು ಸರಿಯಲ್ಲ. ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಹೇಳಿರುವ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಯೇ
ಪಾರ್ಥಿವಾಗ್ನಿಯು. ಇದರ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿದರೆ ಈ ವಿಷಯವು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟವಾಗುವುದು-ಜರಾರಹಿತವಾದುದೂ
ಎಂದರೆ ನಾಶರಹಿತವಾದುದೂ, ಆಹ್ಲಾದಕರವಾದುದೂ ಆದ ಹವಿಸ್ಸನ್ನು ಪಾನಮಾಡುವುದಕ್ಕೆ ಪೂರ್ವದಲ್ಲಿ ತನ್ನ
ಪ್ರಕಾಶದಿಂದ ಸ್ವರ್ಗವನ್ನು ಮುಟ್ಟುತ್ತಿರುವ ಮತ್ತು ಸೂರ್ಯನನ್ನು ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ತಿಳಿದಿರುವ ಈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಈ ಹವಿಸ್ಸು
ಹೋಮಮಾಡಲ್ಪಡುವುದು. ದೇವತೆಗಳು ಆ ಹವಿಸ್ಸಿನ ಭರಣ, ಧಾರಣ, ಭಾವನಾದಿಕರ್ಮಗಳಿಗಾಗಿ ಅದನ್ನು ಅನ್ನ
ದೊಡನೆ ಸೇರಿಸಿ ವೃದ್ಧಿ ಪಡಿಸುವರು ಎಂದು ಈ ಋಕ್ಕಿನ ಮುಖ್ಯಾಭಿಪ್ರಾಯವು. ಈ ಸೂಕ್ತದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಥವಾ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ
ಉಕ್ತವಾಗಿರುವ ಹವಿಸ್ಸನ್ನು ಪಾನಮಾಡುವುದಕ್ಕೆ ಪೂರ್ವಭಾವಿಯಾಗಿ ಅಗ್ನಿ ಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹೋಮಮಾಡುವರು. ಈ ಹವಿಸು
ನಾಶರಹಿತವಾಗಿಯೂ ಮನಸ್ಸಿಗೆ (ಪಾನಮಾಡಲು) ಆಹ್ಲಾದಕರವಾಗಿಯೂ ಇರುವುದು. ಇದನ್ನು ತನ್ನ ಜ್ವಾಲೆ
ಗಳಿಂದ ಆಕಾಶವನ್ನು (ಸ್ವರ್ಗ) ಮುಟ್ಟುತ್ತಿರುವ ಎಂದರೆ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ಪ್ರಜ್ವಲಿತವಾದ ಮತ್ತು ಸೂರ್ಯನ ವಿಷಯದಲ್ಲಿ
ಪ್ರಜ್ಞೆಯುಳ್ಳ ಯಜ್ಞಾಗ್ನಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹೋಮಮಾಡುವರು. ಈ ಹವಿಸ್ಸು ಧಾರಣ, ಪೋಷಣ, ಭರಣ, ಭಾವನಾ,
ಮೊದಲಾದ ಶಕ್ತಿಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯಗಳುಳ್ಳದ್ದನ್ನಾಗಿ ಮಾಡುವುದಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ದೇವತೆಗಳು ಇದರ ಜೊತೆಗೆ ಅನ್ನವನ್ನು ಸೇರಿಸಿ
ವೃದ್ಧಿಯಾಗುವಂತೆ ಮಾಡುವರು. ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಹವಿಸ್ಸನ್ನು ಹೋಮಮಾಡುವ ವಿಷಯವು ಉಕ್ತವಾಗಿರುವುದರಿಂದ
ಹೋಮವು ಅಗ್ನಿಗೇ ಎಂದರೆ ಪಾರ್ಥಿವಾಗ್ನಿಗೇ ಸಂಬಂಧಪಟ್ಟುದು, ಸೂರ್ಯನಿಗೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಪಟ್ಟುದಲ್ಲ. ಅಗ್ನಿ ಯಲ್ಲಿ
ಹೋಮಮಾಡುವರೇ ಹೊರತು ಸೂರ್ಯನಲ್ಲಲ್ಲ. ಆದುದರಿಂದ ಈಸೂಕ್ತದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರತಿಪಾದಿತನಾದ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರದೇವತೆಯು
ಅಪಾಮುಪಸ್ಥೇ ಮಹಿಷಾ ಅಗೃಭ್ಯತ ವಿಶೋ ರಾಜಾನಮುಪ ತಸ್ಥು ರ್ಋಗ್ಮೀಯಂ ।
ಆ ದೂತೋ ಅಗ್ನಿರಭರದ್ವಿವಸ್ವತೋ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಂ ಮಾತರಿಶ್ವಾ ಪರಾವತಃ ॥
ಅಪಾಮುಪಸ್ಥ ಉಪಸ್ಥಾನೇ ಮಹತ್ಯಂತರಿಕ್ಷಲೋಕ ಆಸೀನಾ ಮಹಾಂತ ಇತಿ ವಾಗೃಹ್ಣತ
ಮಾಧ್ಯಮಿಕಾ ದೇವಗಣಾ ವಿಶ ಇವ ರಾಜಾನಮುಪತಸ್ಥು ರ್ಯಗ್ನಿಯಮೃಗ್ಯಂತಮಿತಿ
ವಾರ್ಚನೀಯಮಿತಿ ನಾ ಪೂಜನೀಯಮಿತಿ ವಾಹರದ್ಯಂ ದೂತೋ ದೇವಾನಾಂ ವಿವಸ್ವತ
ಮಾತರಿಶ್ವಾ ವಾಯುರ್ಮಾ ತರ್ಯಂತರಿಕ್ಷೇ ಶ್ವಸಿತಿ ಮಾತರ್ಯಾಶ್ವನಿತೀತಿ ವಾ ॥
ಮತ್ತು ಈ ವಿಷಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ಋಕ್ಕಿನ ಉದಾಹರಣೆಯನ್ನು ಹೇಳಿರುವರು. ಉದಕಗಳ ಅಂಕಪ್ರದೇಶದ
ಸಮೀಪದಲ್ಲಿ ಎಂದರೆ ವಿಸ್ತಾರವಾದ ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷಲೋಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಇರುವ ಮಹಾಮಹಿಮರಾದ ಮಾಧ್ಯಮಿಕ (ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷಸ್ಥ)
ದೇವತೆಗಳು ಈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ಸ್ವಾಗತಿಸಿದರು. ಹೇಗೆಂದರೆ ಪ್ರಜೆಗಳು ತಮ್ಮ ರಾಜನನ್ನು ಯಾವರೀತಿ ಆದರಾತಿ
ಶಯಗಳಿಂದ ಬರಮಾಡಿಕೊಳ್ಳುವರೋ ಅದರಂತೆ ದೇವತೆಗಳು ಮಂತ್ರಪ್ರತಿಪಾದ್ಯನೂ, ಪೂಜ್ಯನೂ, ಗೌರವಾರ್ಹನೂ
ಆದ ಈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ಸ್ವಾಗತಿಸಿ ಸತ್ಕರಿಸಿದರು. ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷದಲ್ಲಿ ವಾಸಿಸುವ ಮಾತರಿಶ್ವನು(ವಾಯುವು)ಮೊದಲು ದೇವತೆ
ಗಳಿಂದ ಪ್ರೇರಿತನಾಗಿ ಬಹುದೂರಪ್ರದೇಶದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಆದಿತ್ಯನಿಂದ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ತಂದನು. ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾ
ಗ್ನಿಯು ಮೊದಲು ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷದಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತರಿಶ್ವನಿಗೇ ಗೋಚರಿಸಿದನು. ಆ ಮಾತರಿಶ್ವನು ಬಹುದೂರ ಪ್ರದೇಶದಲ್ಲಿರುವಲ್ಲಿದ್ದ
ಆದಿತ್ಯನ ಸಮೀಪದಿಂದ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿ ಯನ್ನು ತಂದನು. ಮಾತರಿಶ್ವನೆಂದರ ವಾಯುವು. ಈ ವಾಯುವು ಅಂತ
ರಿಕ್ಷದಲ್ಲಿ ವಾಸಮಾಡುವುದರಿಂದಾಗಲಿ, ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷದಲ್ಲಿ ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಸಂಚಾರಮಾಡುವುದರಿಂದಾಗಲಿ ವಾಯುವಿಗೆ
ಮಾತರಿಶ್ವಾ ಎಂಬ ಹೆಸರು ಬಂದಿರುವುದು. ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಗಮನಿಸಬೇಕಾದ ವಿಷಯವೇನೆಂದರೆ-ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷಸ್ಥ ದೇವತೆಗಳು
ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ಸೂರ್ಯನಿರುವ ಪ್ರದೇಶದಿಂದ ತಂದರು ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಿದೆ. ಸೂರ್ಯನನ್ನು ಒಂದು ಪ್ರದೇಶದಿಂದ
ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ಪ್ರದೇಶಕ್ಕೆ ತರಲು ಯಾರಿಂದಲೂ ಸಾಧ್ಯವಿಲ್ಲ. ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ತರಬಹುದು. ಆದುದರಿಂದ
ಇಲ್ಲಿ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರನೆಂದರೆ ಪಾರ್ಥಿವಾಗ್ನಿಯೇ ಉಕ್ತವಾಗಿರುವುದೆಂದು ತಿಳಿಯಬೇಕು. ಇದಲ್ಲದೆ ಅನೇಕ ಮಂತ್ರಗಳಲ್ಲಿ
ವಿಶ್ವಸ್ಮಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಂ ಭುವನಾಯ ದೇವಾ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಂ ಕೇತುಮಹ್ನಾಮಕೃಣ್ವನ್ ಎಂಬ ಮಂತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ದೇವತೆ
ಗಳು ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ಅಹಸ್ಸುಗಳಿಗೆ (ಹಗಲುಗಳಿಗೆ, ದಿನಗಳಿಗೆ) ಕರ್ತನನ್ನಾಗಿ ಮಾಡಿದರು ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಿದೆ.
ದಿನಗಳಿಗೆ ಕರ್ತನೆಂಬ ಗುಣವು ಸೂರ್ಯನಿಗೆ ಸಲ್ಲತಕ್ಕದ್ದಾದರೂ ಇಲ್ಲಿ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಗೆ ಈ ಗುಣವು ಉಕ್ತವಾಗಿದೆ.
ಏಕೆಂದರೆ ಈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು—ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ಸರ್ವಾದೇವತಾಃ (ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ. ೨-೧-೨), ಇಂದ್ರಂ ಮಿತ್ರಂ ವರುಣಮಗ್ನಿಮಾಹುಃ (೧-೧೬೪-೪೬). ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಮಂತ್ರಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಈ ಅಗ್ನಿಯೇ ಸರ್ವದೇವತಾತ್ಮಕನೆಂದು ಹೇಳಿರುವುದರಿಂದ
ಸೂರ್ಯನೇ ಮೊದಲಾದ ಇತರ ದೇವತೆಗಳ ಗುಣಗಳನ್ನು ಅಗ್ನಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಆರೋಪಿಸುವುದು ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯವಾಗಿದೆ. ಆದುದ
ಮೂರ್ಧಾ ಭುವೋ ಭವತಿ ನಕ್ತಮಗ್ನಿಸ್ತತಃ ಸೂರ್ಯೋ ಜಾಯತೇ ಪ್ರಾತರುದ್ಯನ್ ।
ಮೂರ್ಧಾ ಮೂರ್ತಮಸ್ಮಿನ್ದೀಯತೇ ಮೂರ್ಧಾಯಃ ಸರ್ವೇಷಾಂ ಭೂತಾನಾಂ ಭವತಿ ನಕ್ತಮಗ್ನಿಸ್ತತಃ ಸೂರ್ಯೋ ಜಾಯತೇ ಪ್ರಾತರುದ್ಯನ್ ಸ ಏವ ಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾಂ ತ್ವೇತಾಂ ಮನ್ಯಂತೇ
ಯಜ್ಞಿಯಾನಾಂ ದೇವಾನಾಂ ಯಜ್ಞಸಂಪಾದಿನಾಮಪೋ ಯತ್ಕರ್ಮ ಚರತಿ ಪ್ರಜಾನನ್
ಪಾರ್ಥಿವಾಗ್ನಿಯು ಅನೇಕ ಸನ್ನಿವೇಶಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸೂರ್ಯ ಮೊದಲಾದ ಇತರ ದೇವತಾ ವಿಶೇಷಗಳ ಗುಣವೈಶಿಷ್ಟ್ಯವನ್ನೊಳ
ಗೊಂಡಿರುವಂತೆ ಸ್ತುತಿಸಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಿರುವುದು. ಈ ವಿಷಯದಲ್ಲಿ ನಿರುಕ್ತಕಾರರು ಎರಡು ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳನ್ನು ಉದಾಹರಣೆಯಾಗಿ
ದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಶಾಖ, ಇದನ್ನು ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಯೆಂದು ಕರೆಯುವರು) ಜೀವಿಸುವುದು ಸಾಧ್ಯವಿಲ್ಲ. ಇಂತಹ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು

ದ್ದೇಶಿಸಿ) ಹವಿಸ್ಸು ಹೋಮ ಮಾಡಲ್ಪಡುವುದೋ ಆ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರನೇ ಈ ಪಾರ್ಥಿವಾಗ್ನಿಯು.
ಸೂರ್ಯೋ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ । ಅಗ್ನಿರ್ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ । ಎಂದು ಮೊದಲಾದ ವಾಕ್ಯಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಹೇಳಿರುವಂತೆ,
ಮಧ್ಯಮಸ್ಥಾನದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ವಿದ್ಯುದ್ರೂಪವಾದ ಜ್ಯೋತಿಯೂ ಸ್ವರ್ಗಸ್ಥಾನದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಆದಿತ್ಯರೂಪವಾದ ಜ್ಯೋತಿಯೂ
ಇವೆರಡು ಜ್ಯೋತಿಗಳೂ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರ ಎಂಬ ಒಂದೇ ಹೆಸರಿನಿಂದ ವ್ಯವಹರಿಸಲ್ಪಡುವವು. ಎಂದರೆ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರ ಶಬ್ದದಿಂದ
ವ್ಯವಹರಿಸಲ್ಪಡುವ ಪಾರ್ಥಿವಾಗ್ನಿಯು ಸ್ವರ್ಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಆದಿತ್ಯರೂಪದಿಂದಲೂ, ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷದಲ್ಲಿ ವೈದ್ಯುತರೂಪದಿಂದಲೂ,
ಪೃಥ್ವಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪಾರ್ಥಿವಾಗ್ನಿರೂಪದಿಂದಲೂ ಮೂರು ರೂಪಗಳಿಂದ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಿಸುತ್ತಿರುವನು ಎಂದು ಮುಖ್ಯಾ
ಚತುರ್ಥೇ ಮಂಡಲೇ ಪ್ರಥಮೇಽನುವಾಕೇ ದಶ ಸೂಕ್ತಾನಿ । ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಯೇತಿ ಪಂಚದಶರ್ಚಂ ಪಂಚಮಂ ಸೂಕ್ತಂ ನಾಮದೇವಸ್ಯಾರ್ಷಂ ತ್ರೈಷ್ಟುಭಂ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿ ದೇವತಾಕಂ । ಅತ್ರಾನುಕ್ರಮಣಿಕಾ । ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಯ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರೀಯಮಿತಿ ॥ ವಿನಿಯೋಗೋ ಲೈಂಗಿಕಃ ॥
ಅನುವಾದವು—ನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ ಮಂಡಲದ ಮೊದಲನೆಯ ಅನುವಾಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಹತ್ತು ಸೂಕ್ತಳಿಳಿರುವವು. ಅವು
ಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಯ ಎಂಬ ಈ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ಐದನೆಯದು. ಇದರಲ್ಲಿ ಹದಿನೈದು ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳಿರುವವು ಈ ಸೂಕ್ತಕ್ಕೆ
ವಾಮದೇವನು ಋಷಿಯು ; ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಗ್ನಿಯು ದೇವತೆಯು ; ತ್ರಿಷ್ಟುಪ್ ಛಂದಸ್ಸು ಅನುಕ್ರಮಣಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ—
ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಯ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಾಯಂ ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಿರುವುದು. ವಿನಿಯೋಗವು ಲೈಂಗಿಕವು.
en: Hymns of the Fourth Maṇḍala, 5–18. The fifth hymn.

In this hymn Vaiśvānara Agni is praised. Although we have earlier given extensive explanations about Vaiśvānara Agni many times, here we explain, as Yāska has stated them, the matters Yāska has set out at length in the Nirukta, and the differing opinions of other sages.

वैश्वानरः। इति त्रीणि पदानि । वैश्वानरः कस्माद्विश्वान्नरान्नयति । विश्व एनं नरा नयंतीति वा । अपि ना विश्वानर एव स्यात् प्रत्यृतः सर्वाणि भूतानि तस्य वैश्वानरः ॥ (*vaiśvānaraḥ| iti trīṇi padāni | vaiśvānaraḥ kasmādviśvānnarānnayati | viśva enaṃ narā nayaṃtīti vā | api nā viśvānara eva syāt pratyṛtaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni tasya vaiśvānaraḥ ‖*) (Ni. 7-21).

Now we shall explain the word वैश्वानर (*vaiśvānara*). This word वैश्वानर (*vaiśvānara*) denotes a deity possessing the meaning of the three words विश्वान् नरान् नयति (*viśvān narān nayati*). Why did Vaiśvānara get this name? This god विश्वान् नरान् नयति (*viśvān narān nayati*)—leads all people along the good path; that is, he is the one who sets all people on the good path; therefore this god is named Vaiśvānara.

Or: विश्व एनं नरा नयंतीति (*viśva enaṃ narā nayaṃtīti*)—all people carry this god in the sacrifices they perform to the northern altar. That is, when performing the rite called Agni-praṇayana in sacrifices, they take Agni, churned and produced at the place of its origin, according to rule to the northern altar and establish it there. Or, all people take Agni to their own houses and establish it in places such as the great kitchen for the work of cooking; therefore this Agni is called Vaiśvānara. Or Viśvānara himself is Vaiśvānara. This Viśvānara pervades the bodies of all creatures, dwells there in the form of the digestive fire and digests the food and the like that creatures eat. Therefore the Viśvānara in the bodies of all creatures is Vaiśvānara Agni. ⟨NOTE:396⟩

वैश्वानरस्य सुमतौ स्याम राजा हिकं भुवनानामभि श्रीः । इतो जातो विश्वमिदं विचष्टे वैश्वानरो यतते सूर्येण ॥ (*vaiśvānarasya sumatau syāma rājā hikaṃ bhuvanānāmabhi śrīḥ | ito jāto viśvamidaṃ vicaṣṭe vaiśvānaro yatate sūryeṇa ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-98-1).

This Ṛk praises Vaiśvānara Agni: may we become worthy of the favourable mind of Vaiśvānara Agni. For this Vaiśvānara Agni is a king, and a king is the support of all worlds. Born in this world, he looks upon the whole universe; together with the sun he pervades everything. This is the main purport of the Ṛk.
Who is Vaiśvānara Agni? Is he a deity of the middle region?

इतो जातः सर्वमिदनुभिविपश्यति वैश्वानरः संयतते सूर्येण राजा यः सर्वेषां भूतानामभिश्रयणीयस्तस्य वयं वैश्वानरस्य कल्याण्यां मत् स्यामेति । तत्को वैश्वानरः । मध्यम इत्याचार्याः ॥ (*ito jātaḥ sarvamidanubhivipaśyati vaiśvānaraḥ saṃyatate sūryeṇa rājā yaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāmabhiśrayaṇīyastasya vayaṃ vaiśvānarasya kalyāṇyāṃ mat syāmeti | tatko vaiśvānaraḥ | madhyama ityācāryāḥ ‖*) (Ni. 7-22).

This is the explanation of the Ṛk. This Vaiśvānara Agni, born in this very world, is able to see the whole universe; together with the sun he pervades the whole universe. May we become worthy of the best mind, that is, the favour, of such a Vaiśvānara Agni. He is the king and the support of all created beings.

But who is this Vaiśvānara? What is his nature? Some teachers say that Vaiśvānara is a deity dwelling in the middle region (the atmosphere), because their view is that this Vaiśvānara is the cause of rain. Therefore a Ṛk describing the part this Vaiśvānara plays in the rain-rite is cited here:

प्र नू महित्वं वृषभस्य वोचं यं पूरवो वृत्रहणं सचंते । वैश्वानरो दस्युमग्निर्जघन्वा अधूनोत्कृष्टा अन शंबरं भेत् ॥ (*pra nū mahitvaṃ vṛṣabhasya vocaṃ yaṃ pūravo vṛtrahaṇaṃ sacaṃte | vaiśvānaro dasyumagnirjaghanvā adhūnotkṛṣṭā ana śaṃbaraṃ bhet ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-59-6).

I shall describe in particular the greatness of this Vaiśvānara Agni, the giver of what is desired. Many people serve with devotion this Vaiśvānara Agni, the slayer of Vṛtra. This Vaiśvānara Agni destroyed Vṛtra the Dasyu. He split (killed) Śambara (the cloud) and made the waters stored in the clouds fall on the earth as rain. This is the main purport of the Ṛk.

प्रब्रवीमि तन्महित्वं माहाभाग्यं वृषभस्य वर्षितुरपां यं पूरवः पूरयि तव्या मनुष्या वृत्रहणं मेघहनं सचंते सेवंते वर्षकामाः । दस्युर्दस्यतेः क्षयार्थादुपदस्यंत्यस्मिन्न्रसा उपदासयति कर्माणि तमग्निर्वैश्वा नरो घ्नन्नवादूनोदपः काष्ठा अभिनच्छंबरं मेघं ॥ (*prabravīmi tanmahitvaṃ māhābhāgyaṃ vṛṣabhasya varṣiturapāṃ yaṃ pūravaḥ pūrayi tavyā manuṣyā vṛtrahaṇaṃ meghahanaṃ sacaṃte sevaṃte varṣakāmāḥ | dasyurdasyateḥ kṣayārthādupadasyaṃtyasminnrasā upadāsayati karmāṇi tamagnirvaiśvā naro ghnannavādūnodapaḥ kāṣṭhā abhinacchaṃbaraṃ meghaṃ ‖*) (Ni. 7-23).

So it stands. I shall describe in a special manner the great majesty (the surpassing power) of this Vaiśvānara Agni who pours down rain-water. People who desire what they wish for and who long for rain serve with reverence, with praises and the like, this Vaiśvānara Agni who destroys Vṛtra (the cloud). The word दस्यु (*dasyu*), formed from the root दस् (*das*) "to destroy", denotes a wicked one who prevents the water from falling on the earth and ruins it. Vaiśvānara Agni struck such a Dasyu, Śambara (the cloud; the word शंबर (*śaṃbara*) is read among the names of the cloud), scattered the waters collected in the cloud and made them fall on the earth as rain. This is the main purport.
The view of the earlier Yājñikas that Vaiśvānara is Āditya (objections and answers on this point)

अथासावादित्य इति पूर्वे याज्ञिकाः । एषां लोकानां रोहेण सवनानां रोह आम्मातो रोहात् प्रत्यवरोहश्चिकीर्षितस्तामनुकृतिं होताग्नि- मारुते शस्त्रे वैश्वानरीयेण सूक्तेन प्रतिपद्यते सोऽपि न स्तोत्रियमाद्रियेताग्नेयो हि भवति । तत आगच्छति मध्यस्थाना देवता रुद्रं च मरुतश्च ततोऽग्निमिहस्थानमत्रवै स्तोत्रियं शंसति. (*athāsāvāditya iti pūrve yājñikāḥ | eṣāṃ lokānāṃ roheṇa savanānāṃ roha āmmāto rohāt pratyavarohaścikīrṣitastāmanukṛtiṃ hotāgni- mārute śastre vaiśvānarīyeṇa sūktena pratipadyate so 'pi na stotriyamādriyetāgneyo hi bhavati | tata āgacchati madhyasthānā devatā rudraṃ ca marutaśca tato 'gnimihasthānamatravai stotriyaṃ śaṃsati.*) (Ni. 7-23).

Certain earlier teachers, skilled in the performance of sacrifices, say that this Āditya visible to our eyes is Vaiśvānara. They give the reason thus. In sacrificial rites such as the morning pressing there is an order of rohā and avaroha, that is, ascent and descent. In the worlds also it is so: the earth (the lower region), the atmosphere (the middle region), heaven (the celestial region). Likewise in the pressings there are three: the morning pressing, the midday pressing and the third pressing. In sacrifices the Hotṛ at the morning pressing invokes and praises the deities of the earth region, at the midday pressing the deities of the middle region, and at the third pressing the deities of the celestial region (heaven). This is the order of ascent. After the ascent comes the order of descent: first the deities of the celestial region, then those of the middle region, then those of the earth region are praised in order. This is the order of descent. In the order of descent they praise first Vaiśvānara Agni with the hymn वैश्वानराय पृथुपाजसे (*vaiśvānarāya pṛthupājase*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-1), then the middle-region deities Rudra and the Maruts with the hymn आते पितर्मरुतां (*āte pitarmarutāṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-23-1), then Agni, the deity of the earth region, with the hymn यज्ञायज्ञा वो अग्नये (*yajñāyajñā vo agnaye*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-48-1). Since in the order of descent the praise of Vaiśvānara Agni comes first, and since Āditya is a deity of the celestial region, this Vaiśvānara Agni is Āditya. This is their line of argument.
अथापि वैश्वानरीयो द्वादशकपालो भवत्येतस्य हि द्वादशविधं कर्म । (*athāpi vaiśvānarīyo dvādaśakapālo bhavatyetasya hi dvādaśavidhaṃ karma |*).

Moreover, to Vaiśvānara Agni an oblation of twelve potsherds is always offered; and for Āditya also, आदित्यं द्वादशकपालं (*ādityaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ*), the offering of twelve potsherds is prescribed. Just as for Āditya an offering in twelve parts, indicating the twelve months, is prescribed, so it is for Vaiśvānara Agni; therefore this Vaiśvānara Agni is Āditya.
अथापि ब्राह्मणं भवत्यसौ ना आदित्योऽग्निर्वैश्वानरः ॥ (*athāpi brāhmaṇaṃ bhavatyasau nā ādityo 'gnirvaiśvānaraḥ ‖*).
Moreover, there is also a Brāhmaṇa statement that this Āditya is Vaiśvānara Agni.
अथापि निवित् सौर्यवैश्वानरी भवत्या यो द्यां भात्या पृथिवीमित्येष हि द्यानापृथिव्यानाभासयति । (*athāpi nivit sauryavaiśvānarī bhavatyā yo dyāṃ bhātyā pṛthivīmityeṣa hi dyānāpṛthivyānābhāsayati |*)

A nivid mantra is a particular mantra that praises one deity, praising that deity's distinction in the midst of the śastra mantras; it is a separate mantra inserted and recited among the śastra mantras. Here, when the nivid mantras addressed to Āditya are recited, the Saurya-Vaiśvānarī mantra is recited; that is, that nivid mantra praises both the sun and Vaiśvānara Agni (sings the qualities of those deities). That mantra begins आ यो द्यां भात्या प्रथिवीं (*ā yo dyāṃ bhātyā prathivīṃ*) and means "who lights heaven and earth with his own light". The one who lights heaven and earth with his own light is Āditya; therefore Vaiśvānara Agni, as taught in this mantra, is Āditya too.

अथापि छांदोमिकं सूक्तं सौर्यवैश्वानरं भवति दिवि पृष्ठो अरोचत इत्येष हि दिवि पृष्ठो अरोचतेति । (*athāpi chāṃdomikaṃ sūktaṃ sauryavaiśvānaraṃ bhavati divi pṛṣṭho arocata ityeṣa hi divi pṛṣṭho arocateti |*).

And the Chāndomika hymn दिवि पृष्ठो अरोचत (*divi pṛṣṭho arocata*) (Vā. Saṃ. 33-92) has the sun-and-Vaiśvānara as its deity. In it it is said that he shines on the back (the lower part) of heaven. One who shines in heaven is Āditya. Since Vaiśvānara is praised in this very hymn, this Vaiśvānara Agni is Āditya.
अथापि हविष्वांतीयं सूक्तं सौर्यवैश्वानरं भवति (*athāpi haviṣvāṃtīyaṃ sūktaṃ sauryavaiśvānaraṃ bhavati*).

And the hymn हविष्वांतमजरं (*haviṣvāṃtamajaraṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-1), called Haviṣvantīya (the hymn recited at the time of drinking the oblation), has the sun and Vaiśvānara Agni as its deities; that is, this hymn is addressed to Saurya-Vaiśvānara Agni. In the Ṛk of this hymn
विश्वस्था अग्निं भुवनाय देवा वैश्वानरं केतुमह्नामकृण्वन् । (*viśvasthā agniṃ bhuvanāya devā vaiśvānaraṃ ketumahnāmakṛṇvan |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-2)

it is said that the gods appointed this Vaiśvānara Agni to produce the ahas (days, daytimes), in order to give light to the whole world. Since it is the sun who produces the days, and since this Vaiśvānara Agni too has the power to produce days, Vaiśvānara Agni and Āditya are one person; that is, this Vaiśvānara Agni is Āditya. All this is the view of the earlier teachers, the Yājñikas.
The view of Śākapūṇi that Vaiśvānara is the earthly Agni (not Āditya) (objections and answers on this point)

अयमेवाग्निर्वैश्वानर इति शाकपूणिः । विश्वानरावेते उत्तरे ज्योतिषी वैश्वानरोऽयं यत्ताभ्यां जायते । कथं नृयमेताभ्यां जायत इति यत्र वैद्युतः शरणमभिहंति यावदनुपात्तो भवति मध्यमधर्मैव तावद्भवत्युदकेंधनः शरीरोपशमन उपादीयमान एवायं संपद्यत उदकोपशमनः शरीरदीप्तिः ॥ (*ayamevāgnirvaiśvānara iti śākapūṇiḥ | viśvānarāvete uttare jyotiṣī vaiśvānaro 'yaṃ yattābhyāṃ jāyate | kathaṃ nṛyametābhyāṃ jāyata iti yatra vaidyutaḥ śaraṇamabhihaṃti yāvadanupātto bhavati madhyamadharmaiva tāvadbhavatyudakeṃdhanaḥ śarīropaśamana upādīyamāna evāyaṃ saṃpadyata udakopaśamanaḥ śarīradīptiḥ ‖*)

The view of the teacher called Śākapūṇi is that this earthly Agni is Vaiśvānara Agni. For the earthly Agni arises from two lights (viśvānara fires): the light of Āditya in the celestial region and the lightning light in the middle region. Therefore the fire born of the viśvānara fires is called Vaiśvānara Agni; that is, the earthly Agni is Vaiśvānara Agni. How the earthly Agni arises from the two lights, the light of Āditya and the light of lightning, they now explain. The light of Āditya, which undergoes no change in place or nature, is called the first quality. That is, this light of Āditya, staying where it is, draws up by its rays the waters of oceans and other reservoirs and turns those waters into clouds. This is the work of the first light. Next the lightning fire is called the second. The nature of this lightning fire is the "middle quality", that is, different. This lightning fire has the nature of moving in the midst of the waters (the clouds) and of striking and destroying trees, houses and the like on which people depend; that is, because this lightning fire is able to move in water, it cannot be quenched by water (as ordinary fire is quenched). And ordinary fire, kindled by trees, wood and the like, begins to blaze; but when the lightning fire touches trees and the like, it is quenched there itself, that is, its force ends right there; it does not grow from trees and the like. And this lightning fire cannot be held with the hands and the like. This is the nature of the lightning fire. But the nature of the earthly (ordinary) fire is quite the opposite: the earthly fire can be increased by wood and the like, quenched by water, and held with the hands. These are the natural qualities of the earthly fire.

An explanation is necessary on how the earthly Agni arises from the two lights, that of the celestial region and that of the middle region. Āditya, the light of the celestial region, attracts by his rays the waters of oceans and other reservoirs and turns them into clouds; when the lightning fire that appears in those clouds touches trees and the like, the earthly fire arises and burns. This is well known in the world. Therefore it is explained here that the earthly Agni arises from both lights, that of the celestial region and that of the middle region. Hence the earthly Agni, born of the two lights that are viśvānara fires, is called Vaiśvānara Agni.

अथादित्यादुदीचीप्रथमसमावृत्त आदित्ये कंसं वा मणिं वा परिमृज्य प्रतिस्वरे यत्र शुष्कगोमयमसंस्पर्शयन् धारयति यत् प्रदीप्यते सोऽयमेव संपद्यते । (*athādityādudīcīprathamasamāvṛtta āditye kaṃsaṃ vā maṇiṃ vā parimṛjya pratisvare yatra śuṣkagomayamasaṃsparśayan dhārayati yat pradīpyate so 'yameva saṃpadyate |*)

They give another example of the earthly fire arising from Āditya. When the sun has come in the atmosphere facing the northern direction, that is, at midday, when he is very hot, if one holds a well-shining copper plate or a mirror facing the sun and makes its rays converge (gather together) and fall on a powder of dry cow-dung placed on the ground, fire at once catches. This too is an example showing that the earthly fire arises from Āditya.

अथाप्याह—वैश्वानरो यतते सूर्येण—न च पुनरात्मनात्मा संयततेऽन्येन्नैवान्यः संयतत इति इममादधात्यमुतोऽमुष्य रश्मयः प्रादुर्भवंतीतोऽस्यार्चिषस्तयोर्भासोः संसंगं दृष्ट्वावमवक्ष्यत् । (*athāpyāha—vaiśvānaro yatate sūryeṇa—na ca punarātmanātmā saṃyatate 'nyennaivānyaḥ saṃyatata iti imamādadhātyamuto 'muṣya raśmayaḥ prādurbhavaṃtīto 'syārciṣastayorbhāsoḥ saṃsaṃgaṃ dṛṣṭvāvamavakṣyat |*)

In the example given before, in the sentence वैश्वानरो यतते सूर्येण (*vaiśvānaro yatate sūryeṇa*), the seer, the beholder of the mantra, has said that Vaiśvānara Agni, joined with the sun, spreads, that is, pervades everything. Since the sun's position does not change, it is impossible that the sun goes forward from his place with Vaiśvānara Agni and pervades. A thing can be in one place at one time, but it cannot be there and also go forward. Only if another thing joins it can it pervade another place. Therefore here the sun is one and Vaiśvānara Agni another; the two together are able to pervade everything. Here the earthly fire is kindled right here (on the earth). The light of Āditya, setting out from the celestial world by way of the rays, meets the earthly fire on the earth. That is, the light of the sun and the light of Agni join as one and that light spreads everywhere by the rays; it is with this thought in mind that the seer, the beholder of the mantra, spoke the sentence वैश्वानरो यतते सूर्येण (*vaiśvānaro yatate sūryeṇa*).

अथ यान्येतान्यौत्तमिकानि सूक्तानि भागानि ना सावित्राणि ना सौर्याणि वा पौष्णानि वा वैष्णवानि वा वैश्वदेन्यानि वा तेषु वैश्वानरीयाः प्रवादा अभविष्यन्नादित्यकर्मणा जैनमस्तोष्यन्नित्युदेषीत्यस्तमेषीति विपर्येषीति ॥ आ (*atha yānyetānyauttamikāni sūktāni bhāgāni nā sāvitrāṇi nā sauryāṇi vā pauṣṇāni vā vaiṣṇavāni vā vaiśvadenyāni vā teṣu vaiśvānarīyāḥ pravādā abhaviṣyannādityakarmaṇā jainamastoṣyannityudeṣītyastameṣīti viparyeṣīti ‖ ā*) आग्नेयेष्टेव हि सूक्तेषु वैश्वानरीयाः प्रवादा भवंति । अग्निकर्माणा चैनं स्तौतीति वहसीति पचसीति दहसीति ॥ (*āgneyeṣṭeva hi sūkteṣu vaiśvānarīyāḥ pravādā bhavaṃti | agnikarmāṇā cainaṃ stautīti vahasīti pacasīti dahasīti ‖*)

If Vaiselvānara were Āditya, then in the hymns or Ṛks relating to Āditya or Savitṛ, or in the hymns in which Sūrya, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu or the Viśve-devas are the subjects, the qualities and distinctions pertaining to Āditya would be attributed to Vaiśvānara Agni, that is (as is said of the sun) "you rise, you set, you travel in the atmosphere", and so on in the sense …

…they ought to have been praised by signifying sentences and the like. But it is not so. Only in the hymns that concern Agni are the sentences describing Agni's qualities and functions, such as carrying the oblation, cooking and burning, said in a way that applies also to Vaiśvānara-Agni. That is, Agni's own qualities are applied to Vaiśvānara-Agni and described. Therefore Vaiśvānara-Agni is the terrestrial fire and not Āditya.

Yāska says that this, too, holds in the case of the one who is praised through the rain-action (the rain-work). The water is common to both: it goes up and, by the days, comes down again (े । समानमेतदुदकमुच्चैत्यव चाहभिः । भूमिं पर्जन्या जिन्वंति दिवं जिन्वंत्यग्नयः ॥ (*e | samānametadudakamuccaityava cāhabhiḥ | bhūmiṃ parjanyā jinvaṃti divaṃ jinvaṃtyagnayaḥ ‖*)). He then cites the Ṛk: the Parjanyas quicken the earth, the fires quicken heaven. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-51)
Yāska says that this Ṛk is "nigada-explained" ⟨NOTE:398⟩. (Ni. 7-23)

There are mantras that praise this Vaiśvānara-Agni as the one who impels the rain-action. Since Āditya is the impeller of the rain-action, Vaiśvānara-Agni would also possess Āditya's qualities; so can one not say that Vaiśvānara-Agni is Āditya himself? No, it is not so. As the days come again and again after the night has passed, so the waters come again and again from the earth up to the atmosphere and from the atmosphere to the earth. So the waters and the days have a common property. Therefore the deity Parjanya satisfies the earth with rain-water, and the fires satisfy heaven. How Agni satisfies heaven: the oblations and the like that the sacrificers offer into Agni in the sacrifice take, in subtle form, that is in the form of smoke, a shape fit for the gods, and bring satisfaction to the gods; the gods, being pleased, bring satisfaction to the dwellers of the earth through rain. Moreover, according to the sentence अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते (*agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyagādityamupatiṣṭhate*), the oblation offered into Agni gladdens Āditya who is in heaven; so Agni satisfies heaven or Āditya. Rain became the means of mutual help from the earth to heaven and from heaven to the earth. For these reasons Agni, or Vaiśvānara-Agni, is praised as the cause of the rain-action; it does not follow clearly from this that Vaiśvānara is Āditya himself. Since the meaning of this Ṛk is clear, no further explanation is needed.
कृष्णं नियानं हरयः सुपर्णा अपो वसाना दिवमुत्पतंति ।

Sāyaṇa cites the Ṛk without a gloss of his own. It says: the bay, fair-winged ones, clothing themselves in the waters, fly up to heaven towards the dark course; they turned back from the seat of ṛta, and then the earth is wetted with ghṛta (water). (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-47)
कृष्णं निरयणं रात्रिरादित्यस्य हरयः सुपर्णा हरणा आदित्यरश्मयस्ते यदामुतोऽर्वांचः पर्यावर्तंते सहस्थानादुदकस्यादित्यादथ धृतेनोदकेन पृथिवी व्युद्यते धृतमित्युदकनाम जिघर्तॆः सिंचतिकर्मणः ॥

Yāska explains the verse. The dark course (niyāna, niraya) is the night of Āditya. The bay, fair-winged ones (hari, suparṇa) are the bearers, the rays of Āditya. When they turn back from there, from the common seat of the water, Āditya, then the earth is wetted with ghṛta, i.e. water. *dhṛtam* is a name of water, from the root जिघर्ति (*jigharti*), which has the sense of sprinkling. (Ni. 7-24)

The rays, which carry water and have an excellent motion, cover with water the dark cloud (or the night) of fixed course; that is, joined with water they spread upward towards heaven. Again they return from Āditya, the seat of the water. At once the earth is wetted (soaked) with water. Here niraya·ṇa may be said to mean a course of movement; the ordinary meaning of this word is a path of exit. Āditya has two courses of movement, one dark in colour and one bright. The dark course may be understood as the night or as the southern course (dakṣiṇāyana); or the movement of the southern course may itself be called Āditya's night-movement. Durgācārya wrote the following explanation of the above Nirukta sentence—
नियानं निरयणं निर्गतिः (निर्याति) निर्गच्छंत्येतदिति नियानं वर्त्म पंथाः।
तच्च पुनरेतत् । रात्रि आदित्यस्य । द्वे ह्यस्यायने शुक्लं चोत्तरं कृष्णं च
दक्षिणं । सा हि दैवीरात्रिरभिप्रेता । ततो ब्रवीति रात्रिरादित्यस्य ज्योतिषः ।
स एष भगवानादित्यो यदा जगदनुग्रहाय गर्भमुदकमात्मन्याधित्सुरुत्त
रायणं प्रतिपद्यते तदैते हरयः रसहरणाः सुपर्णास्तस्य रश्मयः सर्वस्मादस्माल्लोकादपोवसानाः आत्मन्याच्छादयंतः आददानाः दिवं द्योतनवंतमेतमादित्यं प्रत्युत्पतंति ।

Durga says: niyāna is going out; it is the way, the path. That is the night of Āditya. For he has two courses, the bright northern and the dark southern; the southern is the intended divine night; therefore the text says "the night of Āditya's light". When the venerable Āditya, wishing for the good of the world to place the embryo, water, in himself, enters the northern course, then these bay ones, the carriers of sap, the fair-winged, his rays, covering themselves with the waters from this whole world, taking them, fly up towards the shining Āditya. (Nirukta-vyākhyā 7-24)

Āditya's course is of two kinds: one belongs to the northern course and the other to the southern. One is called bright and the other dark. Here "night" is a synonym for the dark course. कृष्णं नियानं नियमनं रात्रिः । देवानां हि रात्रिर्दक्षिणायनं । (*kṛṣṇaṃ niyānaṃ niyamanaṃ rātriḥ | devānāṃ hi rātrirdakṣiṇāyanaṃ |*) "In that" means in that rainy season. The night-time of the gods is called the southern course. When Āditya follows the course of the northern course, all his rays spread through the world, gather water from every region, and join Āditya again at the right time of this night. This is the rainy season; in this season the rain pours down in plenty. धृत (*dhṛta*) is a name for water; the word ghṛta is formed from the root जिघर्ति (*jigharti*), "to sprinkle".
अथापि ब्राह्मणं भवत्यग्निर्वा इतो वृष्टिं समीरयति धामच्छदिति खलु
भूत्वा वर्षति मरुतः सृष्टां वृष्टिं नयंति ।
यदा खलु वासानादित्योग्निं रश्मिभिः पर्यावर्ततेऽथ वर्षतीति ।

There is also a Brāhmaṇa: Agni sends the rain from here; having become "dhāmacchad" he rains; the Maruts lead the released rain. When Āditya, clothing himself, turns Agni about with his rays, then it rains. ⟨NOTE:399⟩
यथो एतद्वैश्वानरीयो द्वादशकपालो भवतीत्यनिर्वचनं कपालानि भवंत्यस्ति हि सौर्य एककपालः पंचकपालश्च ।
यथो एतद्ब्राह्मणं भवतीति-बहुभक्तिवादीनि हि ब्राह्मणानि भवंति-पृथिवी
वैश्वानरः संवत्सरो वैश्वानरो ब्राह्मणो वैश्वानर इति ॥

Sāyaṇa (Yāska) adds that this also follows from the Āmnāya statement about ascent and descent ⟨NOTE:400⟩. The statement that the Vaiśvānarīya has twelve potsherds is no explanation; potsherds belong to the offering, and there is also a Saurya offering with one potsherd and one with five. And as to the Brāhmaṇa statement: Brāhmaṇas speak with many figurative ascriptions; "the earth is Vaiśvānara, the year is Vaiśvānara, the Brāhmaṇa is Vaiśvānara". (Ni. 7-24)

Besides this, many Brāhmaṇa sentences also support this meaning. For example, there is the Brāhmaṇa sentence "Agni sends the rain from this world": अग्नेवै धूमो जायते, धूमादभ्रं, अभ्रात् वृष्टिरिति ह विज्ञायते (*agnevai dhūmo jāyate, dhūmādabhraṃ, abhrāt vṛṣṭiriti ha vijñāyate*)—smoke arises from Agni; from the smoke the cloud and from the cloud the rain; so it is to be understood. Or, when this Āditya makes Agni turn back with his rays, rain comes. Or, by the order of ascent and descent, that is, the oblation offered into Agni reaches, as subtle smoke, the gods in heaven, they are satisfied, and from that the rain-action comes about: for saying this there is no other support than the Brāhmaṇa sentence. The statement that the offering for Vaiśvānara-Agni is of twelve potsherds and that for Sūrya of one potsherd or five is not connected with this matter; it belongs only to the acts that are parts of the sacrifice. In some other Brāhmaṇa sentences, पृथिवी वैश्वानरः (*pṛthivī vaiśvānaraḥ*) and so on, it is said that the earth is Vaiśvānara, the year is Vaiśvānara, the Brāhmaṇa is Vaiśvānara; that is right. But in this context it does not mean that the deities such as the earth are Vaiśvānara-Agni; these are praising sentences, spoken to describe Vaiśvānara's qualities, saying that Vaiśvānara has the qualities of deities such as the earth.
यथो एतन्निवित्सौर्यवैश्वानरी भवतीत्यस्यैव सा भवति—यो विड्भो
मानुषीभ्यो दीदेत्-इत्येष हि विड्भो मानुषीभ्यो दीप्यते ।
जमदग्निभिराहुत इति। जमदग्नयः प्रजमिताग्नयो वा प्रज्वलिताग्नयो ना

The Saurya-Vaiśvānarī nivid belongs to him (Agni): "he who shines for the human clans"; for he shines for the human clans. And the Chandomika hymn that is Saurya-Vaiśvānara, "invoked by the Jamadagnis", also belongs to him. The Jamadagnis are kindled fires, or blazing fires; by them he is invoked ⟨NOTE:401⟩. (Ni. 7-24)
There is a nivid-hymn that praises Sūrya and Vaiśvānara. This hymn is recited in the Āgnimāruta-śastra.
अग्निर्वैश्वानरः सोमस्य मत्सत् । विश्वेषां देवानां समित् । अजस्रं दैवं
ज्योतिः । यो विड्भ्यो मानुषीभ्यो दीदेत् । द्युषु पूर्वासु दिद्युतानः । अजर उषसामनीके । आ यो द्यां भात्या पृथिवीं । और्वमुत-

The text of the hymn begins: Agni Vaiśvānara, may he rejoice in the Soma; the sāmidhenī of all the gods; unceasing divine light; he who shines for the human clans; shining in the former days; ageless at the front of the dawns; who shines upon heaven and earth… (continued on the next page).
रिक्षं । ज्योतिषा यज्ञाय शर्म संयत् । अग्निर्वैश्वानर इह श्रवदिह
सोमस्य मत्सत् । प्रेमां देवो देवहूतिमवतु देव्या धिया । प्रेदं
ब्रह्म प्रेदं क्षत्रं । प्रेमं सुन्वंतं यजमानमवतु । चित्रश्चित्ताभिरूतिभिः।

The hymn continues: the wide atmosphere; with his light he gives shelter to the sacrifice; may Agni Vaiśvānara hear here and rejoice in the Soma; may the god favour this invocation of the gods with his divine thought; this prayer, this lordly power; may he favour the sacrificer who presses the Soma; wondrous with wondrous helps, may he come hearing the prayer with his aid.

This hymn is recited in the Āgnimāruta-śastra addressed to Vaiśvānara-Agni. In the middle of this mantra there is the sentence यो विड्भो मानुषीभ्यो दीदेत् (*yo viḍbho mānuṣībhyo dīdet*). Some may say: the one who shines for the benefit of human subjects is Sūrya, so here Sūrya himself is addressed by the word Vaiśvānara, and there is no difference between Sūrya and Vaiśvānara-Agni. Not so. This mantra is recited addressed to Agni. The meaning that the terrestrial fire on the sacrificial altar shines for the benefit of the sacrificers and other people also fits this mantra. Therefore it should be said that Vaiśvānara-Agni is not Sūrya but the terrestrial fire. Besides, in the Chandomika sacrifice called Daśarātra the Saurya-Vaiśvānara hymn जमदग्निभिराहुतः (*jamadagnibhirāhutaḥ*) is recited. This hymn also does not belong to Sūrya; it applies to Agni. For the word jamadagni means a fire well kindled and blazing. In sacrifices and the like, when offering into Agni, it is the custom to make Agni blaze with fuel, ghee and other substances and to make the offerings into that well-burning Agni itself. So the meaning is that this points to the terrestrial fire and not to Āditya (or Sūrya).
यथो एतद्धविष्वांतीयं सूक्तं सौर्यवैश्वानरं भवतीत्यस्यैव तद्भवति ।
तस्य भर्मणे भुवनाय देवा धर्मणे कं स्वधया पप्रथंत ॥

The hymn beginning हविष्वांतमजरं (*haviṣvāṃtamajaraṃ*) (Haviṣvāntīya), the Saurya-Vaiśvānara hymn, also belongs to him (Agni). The verse says: the oblation, ageless, knowing heaven (svarvid), touching heaven, offered, welcome in Agni; for the bearing, becoming and holding of the world the gods, with svadhā, spread it out. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-1)
भरणाय च भावनाय च धारणाय च चैतेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः कर्मभ

Yāska explains: the oblation that is ageless, सूर्यविदि (*sūryavidi*), touching heaven, offered into Agni and welcomed; for the bearing, becoming and holding, for all these acts, the gods increase this Agni with food. (Ni. 7-25)

Moreover, the hymn हविष्वांतमजरं (*haviṣvāṃtamajaraṃ*) has the Saurya-Vaiśvānara-Agni as deity. If it is said that the Vaiśvānara praised in this hymn is Āditya, that is not right. The Vaiśvānara-Agni spoken of there is the terrestrial fire. This becomes clear if the meaning is examined: this oblation, ageless, that is imperishable, and pleasing, is offered, before it is drunk, into this Agni who touches heaven with his light and knows the sun well.

The gods, for the bearing, holding, becoming and other acts of that oblation, join food with it and make it grow; this is the main sense of the Ṛk. Before drinking the oblation spoken of in this hymn or Ṛk, they offer it into Agni. This oblation is imperishable and pleasant to the mind (for drinking). They offer it into the sacrificial fire that touches the sky (heaven) with its flames, that is, that is well kindled and is aware of the sun. In order that this oblation may have the powers of holding, nourishing, bearing, becoming and so on, the gods add food to it and make it increase. Since the offering of the oblation is spoken of here, the offering belongs to Agni, that is to the terrestrial fire, not to Sūrya. They offer into Agni and not into Sūrya. Therefore the deity Vaiśvānara set forth in this hymn is not Āditya or Sūrya; it must be said that it is the terrestrial fire.
अपामुपस्थे महिषा अगृभ्यत विशो राजानमुप तस्थु र्ऋग्मीयं ।
आ दूतो अग्निरभरद्विवस्वतो वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वा परावतः ॥

He says further: in the lap of the waters the great ones were seized; the clans waited upon the king, the worthy of praise; the messenger Agni brought Vaiśvānara from afar, from Vivasvat; Mātariśvan. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-8-4)
अपामुपस्थ उपस्थाने महत्यंतरिक्षलोक आसीना महांत इति वागृह्णत
माध्यमिका देवगणा विश इव राजानमुपतस्थु र्यग्नियमृग्यंतमिति
वार्चनीयमिति ना पूजनीयमिति वाहरद्यं दूतो देवानां विवस्वत
मातरिश्वा वायुर्मा तर्यंतरिक्षे श्वसिति मातर्याश्वनितीति वा ॥

Yāska explains: "in the lap of the waters", in the great atmosphere world, seated, the great ones (mahānta), the divine hosts of the middle region, waited upon him as clans upon a king, upon the praiseworthy or the worshipful; the messenger of the gods, from Vivasvat, i.e. Āditya, the radiant, or from one sent, or from afar; Mātariśvan brought Vaiśvānara Agni ⟨NOTE:402⟩. Mātariśvan is the wind: he breathes in the mātar (the atmosphere), or मातर्याश्वनितीति वा (*mātaryāśvanitīti vā*). (Ni. 7-26)

And on this point another Ṛk is cited as an example. Near the lap of the waters, that is in the wide atmosphere world, the greatly glorious Mādhyamika (atmosphere-dwelling) gods welcomed this Agni. As subjects receive their king with great honour, so the gods welcomed and honoured this Agni, who is to be set forth by mantras, worshipful and venerable. Mātariśvan (the wind), who lives in the atmosphere, first impelled by the gods, brought Vaiśvānara-Agni from Āditya, who is in a very distant region. Vaiśvānara-Agni first became visible in the atmosphere to Mātariśvan himself. That Mātariśvan brought Vaiśvānara-Agni from near Āditya who was in the very distant region.

Mātariśvan means the wind. The wind gets the name Mātariśvan either because it lives in the atmosphere or because it moves swiftly in the atmosphere. What is to be noted here is that it is said that the gods of the atmosphere brought Agni from the region where Sūrya is. No one can bring Sūrya from one region to another; only Agni can be brought. So it must be understood that here Vaiśvānara means the terrestrial fire. Besides, in many mantras the qualities of Sūrya (Āditya) are said of Vaiśvānara-Agni: in the twelfth Ṛk of the Haviṣkānta hymn, in the mantra विश्वस्मा अग्निं भुवनाय देवा वैश्वानरं केतुमह्नामकृण्वन् (*viśvasmā agniṃ bhuvanāya devā vaiśvānaraṃ ketumahnāmakṛṇvan*), it is said that the gods made Vaiśvānara-Agni the maker of the days (ahas). Although the quality of being the maker of the days belongs properly to Sūrya, here this quality is said of Vaiśvānara-Agni. For this Agni is said to be of the nature of all the deities in mantras such as अग्निः सर्वादेवताः (*agniḥ sarvādevatāḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 2-1-2) and इंद्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमाहुः (*iṃdraṃ mitraṃ varuṇamagnimāhuḥ*) (1-164-46); so it is common to ascribe to Agni the qualities of Sūrya and other deities. Therefore Vaiśvānara-Agni is the terrestrial fire, not Āditya.
मूर्धा भुवो भवति नक्तमग्निस्ततः सूर्यो जायते प्रातरुद्यन् ।

Then with these two verses he praises him in all places from the foot. The verse says: the head of the world he becomes; at night he is Agni, then Sūrya is born rising at dawn; … (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-6) ⟨NOTE:403⟩
मूर्धा मूर्तमस्मिन्दीयते मूर्धायः सर्वेषां भूतानां भवति नक्तमग्निस्ततः सूर्यो जायते प्रातरुद्यन् स एव प्रज्ञां त्वेतां मन्यंते
यज्ञियानां देवानां यज्ञसंपादिनामपो यत्कर्म चरति प्रजानन्

Yāska explains: mūrdhā, that on which the head is placed; he becomes the head of all beings; at night Agni, then Sūrya is born rising at dawn; he himself … of the sacrificial gods who accomplish the sacrifice, the work he moves about knowing; hastening he moves through all places. (Ni. 7-27) ⟨NOTE:404⟩

The terrestrial fire is praised in many contexts as containing the distinguishing qualities of other special deities such as Sūrya. In this matter the author of the Nirukta has given two Ṛks as examples: for all living creatures Agni is absolutely necessary for life. Without Agni (the heat in the body, which is called Vaiśvānara-Agni) it is impossible to live. Such an Agni (the Agni in the form of Sūrya) shines at night as lord of the world that contains all creatures. In the morning the same Agni rises in the form of Sūrya. The gods can know the unique power and capacity of such an Agni, that is, how, being Sūrya by day and Agni by night, he carries out his duty.

Here Agni is said to be the lord of the night. To convey the meaning "lord", the word मूर्धा (*mūrdhā*) is used in this ṛk. This word comes to mean "lord" in the following way: among the various limbs of the body the head (mūrdhā, śiras) is the chief, as the saying सर्वस्य गात्रस्य शिरः प्रधानं (*sarvasya gātrasya śiraḥ pradhānaṃ*) shows. Therefore the use of the word mūrdhā here conveys the meaning "lord". The meaning is that Agni is the lord of all beings during the night. In the night, when there is no heat of the sun, Agni himself provides the beings with heat and light and discharges the sun's function. In the morning this same Agni rises as the sun and protects beings. The sages and others who perform sacrifice are able to know this power and capacity of the deities. The intention is that Agni has the power to move swiftly in all regions in order to do this work. That this ṛk says that Agni performs the sun's function is praise of Agni's uncommon quality; it does not mean that Agni is the Āditya. Or else it should be understood that this ṛk indicates that Agni possesses the powers and capacities of the other deities.
The following ṛk is for a fuller explanation of it.

स्तोमेन हि दिवि देवासो अग्निमजीजनञ्क्तिभी रोदसिप्रां । तनू अकृण्वन्त्रेधा भुवे कं स ओषधीः पचति विश्वरूपाः ॥ (*stomena hi divi devāso agnimajījanañktibhī rodasiprāṃ | tanū akṛṇvantredhā bhuve kaṃ sa oṣadhīḥ pacati viśvarūpāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-10)

स्तोमेन हि यं दिवि देवा अग्निमजनयञ्क्तिभिः कर्मभिद्यावापृथिव्योः पूरणं तमकुर्वंस्त्रेधाभावाय पृथिव्यामंतरिक्षे दिवीति शाकपूणिः यदस्य दिवि तृतीयं तदसावादित्य इति हि ब्राह्मणं तदंगीकृत्य स्तौति. (*stomena hi yaṃ divi devā agnimajanayañktibhiḥ karmabhidyāvāpṛthivyoḥ pūraṇaṃ tamakurvaṃstredhābhāvāya pṛthivyāmaṃtarikṣe divīti śākapūṇiḥ yadasya divi tṛtīyaṃ tadasāvāditya iti hi brāhmaṇaṃ tadaṃgīkṛtya stauti.*) (Ni. 7-28).

The gods, by praise, brought Agni into being in heaven. That Agni, by his powers and capacities, filled and illumined heaven and earth. Again, those gods made that Agni three-formed. That Agni ripens all the plants (the herbs), that is, makes them grow and prosper.

The Agni whom the gods brought into being and established in heaven by the stoma (praise) pervaded heaven and earth by his powers and capacities. That is, the teacher Śākapūṇi says that the gods produced Agni in order that he might dwell in the three places: earth, atmosphere and heaven. In this matter there is also a Brāhmaṇa sentence यदस्य दिवि तृतीयं (*yadasya divi tṛtīyaṃ*) …
… तदसावादित्यः (*tadasāvādityaḥ*): the third form of Agni which shines in heaven is that very Āditya who is visible to our eyes. Accepting this view, the seer praises Agni in the next ṛk.

यदेदेनमदधुर्यज्जियासो दिवि देवाः सूर्यमादितेयं । यदा चरिष्णू मिथुनावभूतामादित प्रापश्यन् भुवनानि विश्वा ॥ (*yadedenamadadhuryajjiyāso divi devāḥ sūryamāditeyaṃ | yadā cariṣṇū mithunāvabhūtāmādita prāpaśyan bhuvanāni viśvā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-11).

यदैनमदधुर्यज्जियाः सर्वे दिवि देवाः सूर्यमादितेयमदितेः पुत्रं यदा चरिष्णू मिथुनौ प्रादुरभूतां सर्वदा सहचारिणावुषाश्चादित्यश्च । म (*yadainamadadhuryajjiyāḥ sarve divi devāḥ sūryamāditeyamaditeḥ putraṃ yadā cariṣṇū mithunau prādurabhūtāṃ sarvadā sahacāriṇāvuṣāścādityaśca | ma*).

मिथुनौ कस्मान्मिनोतिः श्रयतिकर्मा, थु इति नामकरणस्थकारो वा नयतिः परो, वनिर्वा, समाश्रितावन्योन्यं नयतो, वनुतो वा, मनुष्यमिथुनावप्यैतस्मादेव, मेधंतावन्योन्यं वनुत इति वा. (*mithunau kasmānminotiḥ śrayatikarmā, thu iti nāmakaraṇasthakāro vā nayatiḥ paro, vanirvā, samāśritāvanyonyaṃ nayato, vanuto vā, manuṣyamithunāvapyaitasmādeva, medhaṃtāvanyonyaṃ vanuta iti vā.*).

Accepting the view that this Agni is the Āditya, the seer praises with this ṛk. When the gods, worthy of sacrifice, established in heaven the sun, the son of Aditi, and when this pair of deities (Uṣas and Āditya) were created and began to move together, then they saw all the beings of the world.

When the gods, worthy of sacrifice, that is, praised in sacrifices and the like, established the Āditya (the sun), the son of Aditi, in heaven, and when the two who are mithunabhūta, that is, always together (the two, Uṣas and Āditya) came into being, from then on these two deities, Uṣas and Āditya, move always together and became able to see all the beings in the world.

Here the derivation of the word mithuna is given. The word mithuna is formed from the root minoti, which has the sense of "resorting to". That is: the root mi in the word mithuna has the meaning "resort to"; thu, or the letter tha, is the affix; the last letter na is from the root nayati (नयतिः परः (*nayatiḥ paraḥ*)), and indicates the meaning "leads" or "carries" another. So the word mithuna means two that resort to each other mutually and remain together. समाश्रित् अन्योन्यं प्रति आत्मानं नयतः कालं वा समाश्रितौ भवतः परस्परं संभक्तौ (*samāśrit anyonyaṃ prati ātmānaṃ nayataḥ kālaṃ vā samāśritau bhavataḥ parasparaṃ saṃbhaktau*) ⟨NOTE:406⟩. That is, the word mithunau means two who resort to each other mutually, or, in respect of time, that after one time another comes
(night, day and so on) is the meaning it conveys. In the case of human beings too, the word mithuna means two persons who resort to each other, or who pass their time together in mutual affection.

यत्रा वदेते अवरः परश्च यज्ञन्योः कतरो नौ वि वेद । अ शेकुरित्सधमादं सखायो नक्षंत यज्ञं क इदं वि वोचत् ॥ (*yatrā vadete avaraḥ paraśca yajñanyoḥ kataro nau vi veda | a śekuritsadhamādaṃ sakhāyo nakṣaṃta yajñaṃ ka idaṃ vi vocat ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-17).

यत्र विवदेते दौन्यौ होतारावयं चाग्निरसौ च मध्यमः कतरो नौ यज्ञे भूयो वेदेत्याशक्नुवंति सत्सहमदनं समानख्याना ऋत्विजस्तेषां यज्ञं समश्नुवानानां को न इदं विपक्ष्यतीति ॥ (*yatra vivadete daunyau hotārāvayaṃ cāgnirasau ca madhyamaḥ kataro nau yajñe bhūyo vedetyāśaknuvaṃti satsahamadanaṃ samānakhyānā ṛtvijasteṣāṃ yajñaṃ samaśnuvānānāṃ ko na idaṃ vipakṣyatīti ‖*) (Ni. 7-30).

Taking this Vaiśvānara Agni to be the earthly Agni, the seer praises with this ṛk. Of the lower and the upper Agnis who know the matter of sacrifice, which knows more? Who is able to decide this question? The ṛtvijs and others who take equal shares in the sacrifice are able to decide it.

दैन्य होतारौ (*dainya hotārau*) means the hotṛs of divine nature: the Agni named Hotṛ who invites the gods to the sacrifice. Since the word hotārau is in the dual, the two deities are the earthly (the sacrificial Agni) established on earth, and the Vāyu or lightning-Agni in the middle region. Since both are only other forms of Agni, they are addressed with the dual word hotārau. अवरः परश्च (*avaraḥ paraśca*) means "the lower and the upper". "Lower" is to be understood as the earthly Agni in the place of earth, and परः (*paraḥ*) as the Agni (lightning) in the middle region. Which of these two has the greater knowledge? Among the ṛtvijs who, taking equal shares, that is, the chief roles, in sacrificial rites, know the matter of sacrifice well, which ṛtvij is able to decide this question?
The following ṛk is for a fuller explanation of it.

यावन्मात्रमुषसो न प्रतीकं सुपर्णो,३वसते मातरिश्वः । तावद्धधात्युप यज्ञमायान्ब्राह्मणो होतुरवरो निषीदन् ॥ (*yāvanmātramuṣaso na pratīkaṃ suparṇo,3vasate mātariśvaḥ | tāvaddhadhātyupa yajñamāyānbrāhmaṇo hoturavaro niṣīdan ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88)

यावन्मात्रमुषसः प्रत्यक्तं भवति प्रतिदर्शनमिति वास्तुपमानस्य संप्रत्यर्थे प्रयोग इहेव निधेहीति यथा सुपर्ण्यः सुपतना एता रात्रयो (*yāvanmātramuṣasaḥ pratyaktaṃ bhavati pratidarśanamiti vāstupamānasya saṃpratyarthe prayoga iheva nidhehīti yathā suparṇyaḥ supatanā etā rātrayo*)

वसते मातरिश्वन् ज्योतिर्वर्णस्य तावदुपदधाति यज्ञमागच्छन् ब्राह्मणो होतास्याग्नेर्होतुरवरो निषीदन् ॥ (*vasate mātariśvan jyotirvarṇasya tāvadupadadhāti yajñamāgacchan brāhmaṇo hotāsyāgnerhoturavaro niṣīdan ‖*) (Ni. 7-31)

Another ṛk is given as an example in this matter. In the previous ṛk Agni and Vāyu are praised; in this ṛk Agni alone is praised. Mātariśvan (Vāyu) asked a man: can the brāhmaṇa, the human hotṛ taking part in the sacrifice, hold, that is, know, the knowledge of Agni, the hotṛ of the gods (the understanding in the performance of sacrifice)? The man replied to this as follows. O Mātariśvan, for as long as (for how long) the birds of fine wings hold the dawn, for so long the brāhmaṇa, the human hotṛ, seated on the sacrificial altar near the sacrificial fire, in a place lower than Agni, holds it (that is, by Agni's grace knows it to a small extent).

The word न (*na*) in this ṛk does not have the sense of comparison; it has the sense of "now" (samprati). Just as the word iha means "here", yet the sentence इहैव निधेहि (*ihaiva nidhehi*) means "put it now", so it should be understood. Therefore the phrase यावनात्रमुषसो न प्रतीकं (*yāvanātramuṣaso na pratīkaṃ*) ⟨NOTE:407⟩ means: for as long as, that is, for how long (only a short time) the dawn-time at the end of the night spreads, for just so long. The sentence सुपर्ण्यः सुपतना एता रात्रयो वसते मातरिश्वन (*suparṇyaḥ supatanā etā rātrayo vasate mātariśvana*) means: O Mātariśvan, the birds of fine wings, flying, hold the dawn-time. That is, "birds" here means the nights. The word suparṇyaḥ which indicates this, meaning "of various wings", conveys the sense of the various (fine) colours of the dawn-time. Therefore suparṇyaḥ means that when Uṣas rises at the end of the night, that Uṣas has various or beautiful colours. The extent of this dawn-time is very small. Since sunrise follows very quickly after the dawn-time, the dawn-time is very small in extent: the intention is, only for a very short time. The human hotṛ is inferior to Agni, the divine hotṛ; therefore the brāhmaṇa, the human hotṛ, seated in a place lower than Agni installed on the sacrificial altar, performs the hotṛ's work only for a very short time, by the grace of Agni, who is of special wisdom: this is the main intention. By this the smallness of man and the greatness of Agni become evident. Since this ṛk says that the brāhmaṇa, the human hotṛ, seated on the sacrificial altar, performs the hotṛ's work praising Agni, the divine hotṛ, it is clearly evident that here Vaiśvānara Agni means the earthly Agni who is praised, and not the Āditya.

होतृजपस्त्वनग्निर्वैश्वानरीयो भवति देव सवितरेतु त्वा वृणतेऽग्निं होत्राय सह पित्रा वैश्वानरेणेतीममेवाग्निं सवितारमाह सर्वस्य प्रसवितारं मध्यमं वोत्तमं वा पितरं । यस्तु सूक्तं भजते यस्मै हविर्निरुप्यतेयमेव सॊग्निर्वैश्वानरः । निसातमेवैते उत्तरे ज्योतिषी एतेन नामधेयेन भजेते भजेते ॥ (*hotṛjapastvanagnirvaiśvānarīyo bhavati deva savitaretu tvā vṛṇate 'gniṃ hotrāya saha pitrā vaiśvānareṇetīmamevāgniṃ savitāramāha sarvasya prasavitāraṃ madhyamaṃ vottamaṃ vā pitaraṃ | yastu sūktaṃ bhajate yasmai havirnirupyateyameva sògnirvaiśvānaraḥ | nisātamevaite uttare jyotiṣī etena nāmadheyena bhajete bhajete ‖*)

The japa-mantras and the like recited by the hotṛ in the sacrifice praise Vaiśvānara by addressing him. The mantra-japa (is that of) Agni: देवसवितरेतं त्वा वृणतेऽग्निं होत्राय सह पित्रा वैश्वानरेण (*devasavitaretaṃ tvā vṛṇate 'gniṃ hotrāya saha pitrā vaiśvānareṇa*) ⟨NOTE:408⟩. An explanation of the sentence "O shining god Savitṛ, the hotṛ has chosen you, that is, Agni, along with your father Vaiśvānara, for the praise" is necessary. Here the seer calls Agni himself Savitṛ. Here Savitṛ (the word savitṛ) means the producer of all things (or beings); the word is used here in this sense. He addresses as father either Vāyu, who belongs to the middle region, or the Āditya, who belongs to the highest (heavenly) place.
The god who is praised in the sūkta, and the god for whom (with whom in view) the oblation is offered, that Vaiśvānara is this earthly Agni.

As stated in sentences such as सूर्यो वैश्वानरः । अग्निर्वैश्वानरः । (*sūryo vaiśvānaraḥ | agnirvaiśvānaraḥ |*), the light of lightning-form in the middle region and the light of Āditya-form in heaven, both these lights, are spoken of by the one name Vaiśvānara. That is, the earthly Agni, spoken of by the word Vaiśvānara, shines in three forms: in heaven as Āditya, in the atmosphere as lightning, on earth as the earthly Agni: this is the main intention.
चतुर्थे मंडले प्रथमेऽनुवाके दश सूक्तानि । वैश्वानरायेति पंचदशर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं नामदेवस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं वैश्वानराग्नि देवताकं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । वैश्वानराय वैश्वानरीयमिति ॥ विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

In the fourth Maṇḍala, in the first anuvāka, there are ten sūktas. The fifth, beginning वैश्वानराय (*vaiśvānarāya*), has fifteen ṛks; its seer is नामदेवस्य (*nāmadevasya*) ⟨NOTE:410⟩; the metre is Triṣṭubh; the deity is Vaiśvānara Agni. The Anukramaṇikā says वैश्वानराय वैश्वानरीयमिति (*vaiśvānarāya vaiśvānarīyamiti*). The use in ritual (viniyoga) is laiṅgika, that is, by the indication of the text itself.

In the first anuvāka of the fourth maṇḍala there are ten sūktas. Of them this sūkta beginning "Vaiśvānarāya" is the fifth. It has fifteen ṛks. Vāmadeva is the seer of this sūkta; Vaiśvānara Agni is the deity; Triṣṭubh is the metre. The Anukramaṇikā says: "vaiśvānarāya vaiśvānarāyam" ⟨NOTE:411⟩. The use in ritual is laiṅgika.
Maṇḍala 4. Anuvāka 1. Sūkta 5. Aṣṭaka 3. Adhyāya 5. Vargas 1, 2, 3. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 15. Seer: Vāmadeva. Deity: Vaiśvānara. Metre: Triṣṭubh.
